For your own reference, on the page for everyone the rows of the first square are 6, 1, 8, then 7, 5, 3, then 2, 9, 4; the rows of the second square are 6, 7, 2, then 1, 5, 9, then 8, 3, 4.

blocks.title: Mirror Below the Line
blocks.instruction: The pictures lie on their side. Each one is only half done: color the squares below the line to make it symmetrical.

script.say: "Each picture on this page is only half done, and it lies on its side. The dashed line is a mirror. Color squares below the line so that the bottom half matches the top half exactly."
script.first: Do the first column of the first picture together. Count how many squares are colored in that column, starting at the dashed line and counting up. Color the same number of squares below the line, starting at the line again and counting down. Tell the children to work column by column from the left.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dashed line in one column and count the colored squares going up, then count the same number going down. A square that touches the line has its partner touching the line; a square far from the line has its partner just as far away.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: End of the Year, Day 1
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: End of the Year, Day 1
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for the end of the year in third grade: 8 review blocks in reading, writing, math, and science, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Machines
blocks.instruction: Each machine uses its rule on every number. Fill in the missing ones.

script.say: "Each number machine has a rule, printed at the top. A number goes in on the left, the machine uses its rule, and a new number comes out on the right. One machine multiplies, and one subtracts. Fill in the missing numbers. Watch out: sometimes the number that went in is the one that is missing."
script.first: Do the first machine together. Its rule is times 5. Ask, "6 goes in. What comes out?" Write 30. Then do the row where the box on the left is empty: "Something went in, the machine multiplied it by 5, and 35 came out. What went in?" Work backward: 35 divided by 5 is 7. Check it by putting 7 through the machine.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is the missing number before the arrow or after it?" After the arrow, the child uses the rule. Before the arrow, the child does the opposite (divide for times, add for minus) and then checks by putting the number through the machine. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the first machine gives 30, 60, 7, 50, and 2; the second gives 18, 15, 7, 27, and 9.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: Story 5
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence. When you finish, turn the page over and write three sentences that tell what happens next in the story."
script.first: Have the children read the story quietly to themselves, then read it aloud once to the class. The story says the children cannot go out for "break" and that the teacher opens the game "cupboard"; tell the class that this means recess and a cabinet. Do the first question together: read it, and ask which sentences in the story help us decide. Circle the answer. The children do the second question and the written answer on their own.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question: "The teacher opens the game cupboard because …" For your own reference, on the page for everyone the answers are "they are having fun" and "that they were no fun"; for question 3, any answer that says the children cannot go outside because of the rain is right.

blocks.title: Who Does It? The Person Word
blocks.instruction: Look at each person, read the word beside them and write the person word in the empty brick.

script.say: "Many words for people are made from a verb and an ending. Someone who teaches is a teacher. Look at each person, read the word next to them, and write the word for the person who does it in the empty brick."
script.first: Do the first two on the board. Ask, "Someone who runs is a …?" Write runner and point out the double n. Ask, "Someone who takes photographs is a …?" Write photographer. Tell the children that every person word on this page ends in -er.
script.stuck: Have the child say the sentence aloud: "Someone who ___ is a ___." For the spelling: a word that ends in e only adds an r, as in dance and dancer; run doubles its last letter. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the words are runner, photographer, dancer, gardener, teacher, baker, farmer, and singer.

blocks.title: Compare Two Animals: Same and Different
blocks.instruction: Read both fact files. For each fact, circle same or different. Then write two things that are the same and two that are different.

script.say: "Here are two fact files, one for a ladybug and one for an eagle. Each file gives four facts about its animal. Compare the facts one by one and circle same or different. Then write two things that are the same and two things that are different."
script.first: Read both fact files aloud together. Do the first fact together: "Animal group: the ladybug is an insect, and the eagle is a bird. Same or different?" Circle different. Write a sentence for it on the board: "Different: A ladybug is an insect, but an eagle is a bird." Tell the children to write whole sentences on the lines. The fact files use short words: "air" means that the animal flies, and "meat" means that it eats other animals (a ladybug eats tiny insects). If a child questions a fact, say that the job is to compare what the two files say.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a fact in the ladybug's file and one finger on the same line in the eagle's file and read both aloud. For the sentences, give the child a frame: "Both animals ___." and "The ladybug ___, but the eagle ___." For your own reference, on the page for everyone the animal group and the body covering are different; where the animals live and what they eat are the same.

blocks.title: Count the Squares
blocks.instruction: Count the squares in the rectangle. Finish the multiplication.

script.say: "Each rectangle on this page is made of squares. The number of squares is the area of the rectangle. Count the rows, and count how many squares are in one row. Then finish the multiplication to find how many squares there are in all."
script.first: Draw the first rectangle on the board: 3 rows of 5 squares. Count the rows, then count the squares in one row. Say, "3 rows of 5: 3 times 5 is 15." Count the squares one by one to check. Say the answer as a sentence: "The area is 15 squares."
script.stuck: Have the child run a finger down the left side to count the rows and along the top to count the squares in one row. A child who does not know the fact adds the rows, 5 plus 5 plus 5, or counts every square. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the answers are 15, 16, 20, and 27.

blocks.title: Division Word Problems: Sharing
blocks.instruction: Each story shares things out. Deal them into the boxes.

script.say: "These are division word problems about sharing. Read each story. Decide how many things there are and how many equal groups they go into. Write the division, and write the answer in the box. The picture is there if you want to check."
script.first: Read the first story aloud together: 5 children share 30 pens. Ask, "How many pens in all? How many children?" Write the division on the board: 30 divided by 5. Ask how the children can find the answer: by knowing that 5 times 6 is 30, or by dealing the pens into the five boxes. Write 6 in the answer box, and write the whole division, with its answer, on the lines. Then say the answer together in a whole sentence: "Each child gets 6 pens."
script.stuck: Have the child underline the two numbers in the story and say what each one counts. Then ask for the multiplication fact: "4 times what makes 24?" A child who does not know the fact deals the things into the boxes with dots, one for each box in turn. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the answers are 6 pens, 6 notebooks, and 4 rulers.

blocks.title: The Water Cycle: Label the Diagram
blocks.instruction: Read the four words in the bank and write each one on the line that has the same number as on the diagram.

script.say: "This is a science page about the water cycle: the way water travels from the sea up into the sky and back down again. The diagram has four numbers. Read the four words in the bank, and write each word on the line that has the same number as its place in the diagram."
script.first: Follow the arrows in the diagram together, starting at the sea: the Sun warms the water and it rises into the air; high up it cools and forms a cloud; it falls as rain; it runs back to the sea. Read the four words aloud and say each one in plain words: evaporation means water rises into the air, condensation means it turns into the tiny drops of a cloud, precipitation means rain or snow falls, and collection means the water gathers in rivers, lakes, and the sea. Do number 1 together.
script.stuck: Point to the number in the diagram and ask, "What is the water doing here: going up, making a cloud, falling, or gathering?" Then read the four words to the child again. For your own reference, on the page for everyone 1 is evaporation, 2 is condensation, 3 is precipitation, and 4 is collection.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates on a 10 × 10 Grid
blocks.instruction: Find each square on the big grid by its letter and number. Color it to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the lists name. Show how to find a square: put one finger on the letter at the top and one finger on the number at the side, and move them until they meet. Find the first square of the first list together and color it. Tell the children to cross out each code once its square is colored.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: End of the Year, Day 2
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: End of the Year, Day 2
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for the end of the year in third grade: 8 review blocks in reading, writing, math, and science, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Rounding to the Nearest 10 and 100
blocks.instruction: Round each number twice: to the nearest ten in the first box and to the nearest hundred in the second.

script.say: "Rounding means finding the nearest round number. On this page you round each number two times: first to the nearest ten, then to the nearest hundred. The box at the top shows how: look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to. If it is 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4, round down. If it is 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9, round up."
script.first: Read the example at the top together: 472 is about 470 to the nearest ten, and about 500 to the nearest hundred. The wavy equal sign means "is about." Do the first number on the board. For the nearest ten, underline the tens digit of 159 and look at the ones digit: it is 9, so round up to 160. For the nearest hundred, underline the hundreds digit and look at the tens digit: it is 5, so round up to 200. Tell the children to start from the number on the page both times.
script.stuck: Have the child say the two tens the number is between (150 and 160) and ask which one is closer; then the two hundreds (100 and 200). A 5 always rounds up. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the answers are 160 and 200; 490 and 500; 790 and 800; 310 and 300; 350 and 400; 540 and 500; 570 and 600; 560 and 600.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: Story 6
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence. When you finish, turn the page over and write three sentences that tell what happens next in the story."
script.first: Have the children read the story quietly to themselves, then read it aloud once to the class. Do the first question together: read it, and ask which sentence in the story helps us decide. (The sentences are numbered.) Circle the answer. The children do the second question and the written answer on their own.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question: "Ella wants to surprise Grandpa because …" For your own reference, on the page for everyone the answers are "a little nervous" and "Ella practiced all week"; for question 3, any answer that says it is Grandpa's birthday, or that he is turning seventy, is right.

blocks.title: Root Words: Sort by the Root
blocks.instruction: Read each word at the top and write it on a line of the wall that stands on its root word.

script.say: "The twelve words at the top come from three word families. Each family is built from one root word: joy, thought, or worth. Read each word, find the root word inside it, and write the word on a line of the wall that stands on its root word."
script.first: Read the twelve words aloud together. Do two words together: "enjoyment." Ask, "Which root word is inside it?" Write it on a line above joy. Then do "afterthought" the same way. Tell the children to cross out each word at the top once it is written on a wall; each wall gets four words.
script.stuck: Have the child look for the letters of joy, thought, or worth inside the word and underline them. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the joy wall gets joyless, enjoyment, joyous, and enjoyable; the thought wall gets thoughtless, thoughtful, afterthought, and thoughtfully; the worth wall gets worthwhile, worthlessness, worthlessly, and worthy.

blocks.title: Retell the Story with Starters
blocks.instruction: Write what happens in each picture on its lines, starting with the word printed on the first line.

script.say: "The four pictures tell a story from beginning to end. Write what happens in each picture on its lines. Use words that show the order, such as first, next, then, and finally. The box at the top gives you words you may need."
script.first: Look at the four pictures together and ask four volunteers to tell what happens in one picture each. Read the words in the box aloud. This page has no sentence starters, even though its title says "with Starters"; the order words do that job. Write First, Next, Then, Finally on the board. Say a sentence for the first picture together and write it on the board: "First, a whole banana stands on a plate." Tell the children to write two sentences for each picture and to end each one with a period. A child who finishes early writes one more sentence on the back of the page: who ate the banana?
script.stuck: Point to one picture and ask, "What is different from the picture before?" Have the child say the sentence aloud, starting with one of the order words on the board, before writing it. A word that is spelled by its sounds is fine.

blocks.title: Name That Fraction
blocks.instruction: Write the fraction the shaded parts show.

script.say: "Each shape on this page is cut into equal parts, and some of the parts are shaded. Write the fraction that the shaded parts show. The bottom number tells how many equal parts the whole shape has. The top number tells how many of them are shaded."
script.first: Draw the first shape on the board: a bar cut into four equal parts, with two of them shaded. Ask, "How many equal parts does the bar have in all?" Write 4 in the bottom box. Ask, "How many parts are shaded?" Write 2 in the top box. Read the fraction aloud: two fourths.
script.stuck: Have the child count all the parts first, shaded or not, and write that number at the bottom; then the child counts only the shaded parts for the top. The most common slip is to count only the parts that are not shaded for the bottom number.

blocks.title: Walk the Edge
blocks.instruction: Count the unit edges around each rectangle. Write the perimeter.

script.say: "The perimeter is the distance all the way around a shape, like a walk along its edge. Each rectangle on this page is made of squares. Count the edges of the small squares all the way around the outside of the rectangle. Write the perimeter in the box."
script.first: Draw the first rectangle on the board. Mark a starting corner with a dot. Count the edges along the top, down the side, along the bottom, and back up to the dot, making a small mark on each edge as you count it. Write the total in the box. Then show the shortcut: count each of the four sides and add the four numbers.
script.stuck: Have the child mark a starting corner and make a small mark on each edge as it is counted, so that no edge is skipped or counted twice. A child who counts the squares inside is finding the area; point to the outside edge. A square in a corner has two outside edges, and both count. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the perimeters are 20, 14, 20, and 22.

blocks.title: Butterfly and Frog Life Cycles Compared
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and put a check under the butterfly, the frog or both when it is true for that animal.

script.say: "This is a science page about two animals that change a great deal as they grow: the butterfly and the frog. Read each sentence. If it is true for the butterfly, put a check under the butterfly. If it is true for the frog, put a check under the frog. If it is true for both, check both."
script.first: Ask the children how each animal grows, and write the two chains on the board: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly; and egg, tadpole, young frog, frog. Do the first sentence together: "The grown-up catches insects to eat." That is true for the frog only, so only the frog gets a check. Tell the children that some sentences are true for both animals.
script.stuck: Read the sentence to the child and ask about each animal separately: "Is that true for the butterfly? Is it true for the frog?" Point to the two chains on the board. For your own reference, on the page for everyone the answers are, from top to bottom: frog, butterfly, both, frog, butterfly, frog, both, butterfly.

blocks.title: Bring the Crane Its Number
blocks.instruction: Start with the truck's number and, on your road, write the new number in each sign's box. Find the road that ends on the crane's number.

script.say: "The truck has to bring a number to the crane. The truck starts with 46, and the crane needs 54. There are several roads. Every sign on a road changes the number: plus 1, minus 10, and so on. Find the road that ends on the crane's number."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the truck with its number, the crane with its number, and one sign. Follow one road for two signs together and write the new number in the box of each sign: "46 plus 1 is 47." Tell the children to choose one road, write the new number in every box along it, and try another road if the last number is not 54.
script.stuck: Have the child write the new number in each sign's box before going on to the next sign. If a road ends on the wrong number, the child checks each step on that road first and then tries another road. Scrap paper is fine for the steps.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 1
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 1
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 1 of kindergarten: 7 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Loops, Eights and Spirals
blocks.instruction: Trace each line with your pencil. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrow.

script.say: "Today your pencil goes for a walk. Each line starts at an orange dot. Follow the arrow and stay on the line as well as you can."
script.first: Hold up the page and trace the first line with your finger, from the orange dot in the direction of the arrow. Have the children trace it in the air with a finger, then on the page with a finger, and only then with a pencil. Remind them to go slowly: this is not a race.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: Find the Letter
blocks.instruction: Circle every letter that matches the one in the box.

script.say: "Look at the letter in the box. Your job is to find every letter in the row that is the same, and circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to the letter in the box and say its name. Move your finger along the row and stop at each letter: "Is this one the same? Look closely." Circle the ones that match. Tell the children that some letters look almost alike, so they have to look closely.
script.stuck: Cover the row with a sheet of paper and uncover one letter at a time. Have the child hold a finger under the letter in the box and compare. If the child circles a letter that only looks similar, put the two side by side and ask what is different.

blocks.title: Draw It Twice as Big
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big.

script.say: "Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big."
script.first: Find the top-left colored square on the small grid together and count which row and which column it is in. Find the same row and column on the big grid and color that square. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: On, Under, Beside
blocks.instruction: Each card names a place: ON, UNDER, or BESIDE the box. Circle the picture that is there.

script.say: "Each card names a place: ON the box, UNDER the box, or BESIDE the box. Circle the shape that is in that place."
script.first: Put a book on a chair, then under it, then beside it, and have the class say the word each time. Read the words under each card aloud: ON the box, UNDER the box, BESIDE the box, UNDER the box. Do the first card together: "Which shape is ON the box?" Circle it.
script.stuck: Have the child show the word with a hand and the desk: "Put your hand ON the desk. Now UNDER the desk." Then go back to the picture and ask the child to point to the top of the box.

blocks.title: Draw 2D Shapes on Dot Paper
blocks.instruction: Read the shape name and connect the dots to draw it. Start at the thick line if there is one.

script.say: "Each box names a shape. Connect the dots with your pencil to draw that shape. If there is a thick line in the box, start there."
script.first: Read the name in each box aloud and draw that shape on the board: a triangle has 3 sides, a square has 4 sides that are all the same length, a rectangle has 4 sides with two long and two short. Draw the first shape together on the dot paper, going from dot to dot with straight lines.
script.stuck: Have the child count the sides of the shape on the board and put a finger on the dots where the corners will go. Then draw one side at a time from corner to corner.

blocks.title: Help the Hedgehog Reach the Apple Tree
blocks.instruction: Help the hedgehog get to the apple tree. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Find the way along the light path from the animal to its goal. Use your finger first, then your pencil."
script.first: Hold up the page and show where the path starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the beginning of the way with your finger and stop at the first place where the path splits: "Which way? Let's try one." Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: How Do You Feel? Circle the Face
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture, think how you would feel, and circle the face that matches.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Think about how it would make you feel. Then circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Look at the first picture together and ask what it shows. Ask, "How does that make you feel?" Let two or three children answer; they may not all feel the same, and that is fine. Each child circles the face that matches their own answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child what the picture shows and when they have seen one. Then point to each face and name the feeling it shows. There is no wrong answer on this page; any face the child can explain is right.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 2
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 2
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 2 of kindergarten: 7 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Find the Twins
blocks.instruction: Two pictures are exactly the same. Find them and circle both.

script.say: "On this page two pictures are exactly the same. Find the two twins and circle both."
script.first: Name the pictures together. Ask, "Do you see two that are the same?" Let the children look for a while; then show how to check: put a finger on each one and compare the colors and the parts.
script.stuck: Have the child name each picture; two pictures with the same name may be the twins.

blocks.title: Match the Shadow
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to its shadow.

script.say: "Each picture on the left has a shadow on the right. A shadow is dark and shows only the shape. Draw a line from each picture to its shadow."
script.first: Do the first one together: look at the outline of the first picture and ask, "Which shadow has the same shape?" Draw the line from dot to dot. Tell the children to look at the edges: the ears, the wheels, the tail.
script.stuck: Have the child trace the outside of the picture with a finger, then trace the shadows until one has the same shape.

blocks.title: Trace the Letter I i
blocks.instruction: Trace each letter, then write one on your own at the end of the line. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing letters. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace the letters first. Then write one all by yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Write the first letter of the page big on the board, saying where you start and which way you go. Have the children write it in the air with you. Then they trace the letters on the page. Walk around and watch where each child starts.
script.stuck: Put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here. Which way does the arrow point?" If the letter the child writes alone is far from the model, have the child trace one more and try again. Do not ask for a perfect letter.

blocks.title: Tall and Short
blocks.instruction: Circle the TALLEST one in each row.

script.say: "In each row, some things are tall and some are short. Look at all of them. Then circle the TALLEST one."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each picture and ask, "Is this the tallest? Is there a taller one?" Circle the tallest together. Remind the children to look at every picture in the row before they circle.
script.stuck: Have the child point to two pictures at a time and say which of the two is bigger, keeping a finger on the winner, until the row is done. The picture under the finger at the end gets the circle.

blocks.title: Find and Circle
blocks.instruction: Find every picture like the one in the box. Circle them all.

script.say: "Look at the picture in the box at the top. Find every picture on the page that is just like it, and circle them all."
script.first: Point to the picture in the box and name it together. Find one like it on the page together and circle it. Tell the children to look across the page row by row, like reading, so they do not miss any.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the page with a sheet of paper and slide it down slowly, looking at one row at a time.

blocks.title: What Is Missing?
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 empty places in the bottom picture where something from the top picture is missing, and check a box for each.

script.say: "The two pictures are the same, but three things are missing from the bottom picture. Find each empty place, circle it, and check a box for each one."
script.first: Hold up the page and compare the two pictures with the class, from the top down. Find one thing that is missing together and circle the empty place in the bottom picture. Check the first box.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the top picture and look for it in the bottom picture: "Is it there?" There are three missing things; the three boxes help them count.

blocks.title: Healthy and Not Healthy Foods
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes, Healthy and Not Healthy. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Is this good for our body every day, or is it a treat for once in a while?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. A treat is fine once in a while; the page only asks which foods to eat every day.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 3
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 3
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 3 of kindergarten: 7 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Advanced Pencil Paths
blocks.instruction: Trace each line with your pencil. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrow.

script.say: "Today your pencil goes for a walk. Each line starts at an orange dot. Follow the arrow and stay on the line as well as you can."
script.first: Hold up the page and trace the first line with your finger, from the orange dot in the direction of the arrow. Have the children trace it in the air with a finger, then on the page with a finger, and only then with a pencil. Remind them to go slowly: this is not a race.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: Sight Words: Read, Trace, Write
blocks.instruction: Read the word. Trace it. Then write it yourself on the empty line.

script.say: "These are words we see all the time. Read the word, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Do the first word together: read it, write it on the board, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more next to it. Tell the children to say the word each time they finish writing it.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: I Can: Check What You Can Do
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and check the things you can do. Then write one thing you want to learn.

script.say: "This page is about what YOU can do. Listen to each sentence. If you can do it, put a check in its box. At the bottom, write one thing you want to learn."
script.first: Read each sentence aloud while the children point to it: "I can paint a picture. I can brush my teeth…" After each one, pause so that every child can check the box or leave it empty. Tell them there is no wrong answer. For the last line, write "I want to learn to" on the board and let children say their ideas first.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask the child, "Can you do that?" For the last line, a child may draw the thing and write the first letter or one word with your help.

blocks.title: Smallest to Biggest
blocks.instruction: Number the pictures from 1 (smallest) to 5 (biggest).

script.say: "Each row has five pictures of the same thing in different sizes. Write 1 under the smallest, then 2, 3, 4, and 5 under the biggest."
script.first: Write 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 on the board. Do the first row together. Ask, "Which one is the smallest?" It gets the 1. "Which one is next?" It gets the 2. Go on until the biggest gets the 5.
script.stuck: Have the child find the smallest one left each time and cross it off lightly after writing its number.

blocks.title: Top, Middle, Bottom
blocks.instruction: Circle every picture in the MIDDLE row.

script.say: "The page has three rows: the top, the middle, and the bottom. Circle every picture in the MIDDLE row."
script.first: Point to the top row, the middle row, and the bottom row and have the class say each word. Find one picture in the middle row together and circle it.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on the top row and one on the bottom row: the middle is between the fingers.

blocks.title: AABB Patterns
blocks.instruction: Look at the pattern. Circle what comes next.

script.say: "A pattern is something that repeats, over and over. Say the pattern out loud. Then circle what comes next."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each picture and have the class say its name like a chant. On this page each picture comes two times, and then the next picture comes two times. Stop at the box with the question mark and ask, "What comes next?" Circle it among the choices.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Living and Non-living Things
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes, Living and Non-living. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Does it grow and need water and air? Then it is living." Plants are living too, even though they do not walk or run. Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 4
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 4
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 4 of kindergarten: 7 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Find the Twins
blocks.instruction: Two pictures are exactly the same. Find them and circle both.

script.say: "On this page two pictures are exactly the same. Find the two twins and circle both."
script.first: Name the pictures together. Ask, "Do you see two that are the same?" Let the children look for a while; then show how to check: put a finger on each one and compare the colors and the parts.
script.stuck: Have the child name each picture; two pictures with the same name may be the twins.

blocks.title: Find the Letter
blocks.instruction: Circle every letter that matches the one in the box.

script.say: "Look at the letter in the box. Your job is to find every letter in the row that is the same, and circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to the letter in the box and say its name. Move your finger along the row and stop at each letter: "Is this one the same? Look closely." Circle the ones that match. Tell the children that some letters look almost alike, so they have to look closely.
script.stuck: Cover the row with a sheet of paper and uncover one letter at a time. Have the child hold a finger under the letter in the box and compare. If the child circles a letter that only looks similar, put the two side by side and ask what is different.

blocks.title: Trace the Letter J j
blocks.instruction: Trace each letter, then write one on your own at the end of the line. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing letters. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace the letters first. Then write one all by yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Write the first letter of the page big on the board, saying where you start and which way you go. Have the children write it in the air with you. Then they trace the letters on the page. Walk around and watch where each child starts.
script.stuck: Put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here. Which way does the arrow point?" If the letter the child writes alone is far from the model, have the child trace one more and try again. Do not ask for a perfect letter.

blocks.title: Long and Short
blocks.instruction: Circle the LONGEST one in each row.

script.say: "In each row, some shapes are long and some are short. Look at all of them. Then circle the LONGEST one."
script.first: Do the first row together. Move your finger from one end of each shape to the other and ask, "Is this the longest? Is there a longer one?" Circle the longest together. Remind the children to look at every shape in the row before they circle.
script.stuck: Have the child point to two pictures at a time and say which of the two is bigger, keeping a finger on the winner, until the row is done. The picture under the finger at the end gets the circle.

blocks.title: Draw 2D Shapes on Dot Paper
blocks.instruction: Read the shape name and connect the dots to draw it. Start at the thick line if there is one.

script.say: "Each box names a shape. Connect the dots with your pencil to draw that shape. If there is a thick line in the box, start there."
script.first: Read the name in each box aloud and draw that shape on the board: a triangle has 3 sides, a square has 4 sides that are all the same length, a rectangle has 4 sides with two long and two short. Draw the first shape together on the dot paper, going from dot to dot with straight lines.
script.stuck: Have the child count the sides of the shape on the board and put a finger on the dots where the corners will go. Then draw one side at a time from corner to corner.

blocks.title: Help the Puppy Get to the Ball
blocks.instruction: Help the puppy get to the ball. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Help the animal get to its goal. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges."
script.first: Hold up the page, read its title aloud, and show where the road starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the road with your finger and stop at each place where it splits: "Which way leads to the goal?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Our Class Rules
blocks.instruction: Look at the two pictures in each row. Circle the picture that follows a class rule. Cross out the one that does not.

script.say: "Each row shows the same child two times. In one picture the child follows a class rule. Circle that picture, and put an X on the other one."
script.first: Do the first row together. Ask, "Which picture keeps everyone safe or helps us learn?" (walking in the hall, raising a hand, listening at story time, cleaning up the blocks). Have the children say the rule in their own words, then circle that picture and cross out the other.
script.stuck: Point to each picture and ask, "What is the child doing? Is that what we do in our class?" Say the rule for the child ("We walk in the hall.") and let the child find the picture that shows it.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 5
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 5
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 5 of kindergarten: 7 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Trace the Numbers 0 to 9
blocks.instruction: Trace each number. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing numbers. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace each number in the row."
script.first: Write the first number of the page big on the board and say where it starts and which way it goes. Have the children write it in the air with you. They trace the number on the page and then write their own.
script.stuck: Show the child where the number starts and guide the first stroke with your finger on the page. A number written backward is common at this age; show the right way once and move on.

blocks.title: Trace Your First Words
blocks.instruction: Trace the dashed word, then write it on the empty line.

script.say: "Each picture has its word next to it. Read the word, trace the dashed word, then write it on the empty line."
script.first: Name the pictures together and read each word aloud. Do the first word together: read it, trace it with your finger, and write it on the board once more, saying each letter.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: My Favorite Things: Circle and Write
blocks.instruction: In each row, circle your favorite picture and copy its word onto the line.

script.say: "In each row there are pictures of different things. Circle the one you like best. Then copy its word on the line."
script.first: Do the first row together: name the pictures, ask a few children which one they like best, and show how to circle one. Then show how to copy its word onto the line, letter by letter. Everyone circles their own favorite; there is no right answer.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger under the word and copy one letter at a time, moving the finger along. If the child cannot choose, say, "Pick the one you would like to have today."

blocks.title: Count and Circle
blocks.instruction: Count the pictures in each box. Circle the right number.

script.say: "Count the pictures in each box. Touch each one as you count. Then circle the number that tells how many."
script.first: Count the first box aloud together, touching each picture on your page as the class counts. Ask, "So how many are there?" Circle that number among the numbers in the box.
script.stuck: Have the child cross out each shape while counting it, so that none is counted twice. If the child does not know how to write the number, point to it on the board.

blocks.title: Short to Tall
blocks.instruction: Number the pictures from 1 (shortest) to 4 (tallest).

script.say: "Each row has four pictures of the same thing. Write 1 under the shortest, then 2 and 3, and 4 under the tallest."
script.first: Write 1, 2, 3, 4 on the board. Do the first row together. Ask, "Which one is the shortest?" It gets the 1. "Which one is next?" It gets the 2. Go on until the tallest gets the 4.
script.stuck: Have the child find the shortest one left each time and cross it off lightly after writing its number.

blocks.title: Complete the Pattern
blocks.instruction: A picture is missing. Circle what belongs in the empty box.

script.say: "Each row is a pattern, but one picture is missing. Find the empty box. Circle the picture that belongs in it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each shape and have the class say its name like a chant. Stop at the empty box and ask, "What goes here?" Say the pattern again with that shape and circle it among the choices at the end of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Taking Turns and Sharing
blocks.instruction: Look at each picture. Circle the friends who take turns, share or help. Cross out the pictures that are not kind.

script.say: "Look at each picture. If the friends are taking turns, sharing or helping, circle it. If someone is not being kind, put an X on it."
script.first: Do one picture together. Ask, "What is happening here? Is that kind?" Talk about what the child does, never about a bad child. If a picture shows grabbing, say: "Grabbing a toy is not kind. What could the child do instead?"
script.stuck: Ask how the other friend in the picture feels: a happy friend usually means a kind picture, a sad friend means someone was not kind. Some pages have more kind pictures than others, so look at each picture on its own.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 6
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 6
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 6 of kindergarten: 7 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Down Lines, Slants and Crosses
blocks.instruction: Trace each line with your pencil. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrow.

script.say: "Today your pencil goes for a walk. Each line starts at an orange dot. Follow the arrow and stay on the line as well as you can."
script.first: Hold up the page and trace the first line with your finger, from the orange dot in the direction of the arrow. Have the children trace it in the air with a finger, then on the page with a finger, and only then with a pencil. Remind them to go slowly: this is not a race.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: What Is It?
blocks.instruction: Only part of the picture is showing. Circle the whole picture it belongs to.

script.say: "In each row only a small part of a picture is showing. Which whole picture does it belong to? Circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together: look at the small part and ask, "What could this be? An ear, a tail, a head?" Look at the three whole pictures and circle the one the part belongs to.
script.stuck: Have the child find the part on each of the three pictures: "Does this one have it?"

blocks.title: Trace the Letter K k
blocks.instruction: Trace each letter, then write one on your own at the end of the line. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing letters. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace the letters first. Then write one all by yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Write the first letter of the page big on the board, saying where you start and which way you go. Have the children write it in the air with you. Then they trace the letters on the page. Walk around and watch where each child starts.
script.stuck: Put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here. Which way does the arrow point?" If the letter the child writes alone is far from the model, have the child trace one more and try again. Do not ask for a perfect letter.

blocks.title: Same Number?
blocks.instruction: Count each group and write how many. Do both groups have the same number? Circle ✓ for yes or ✗ for no.

script.say: "In each box there are two groups. Count each group and write how many. Then circle the check mark if the two groups have the same number, or the X if they do not."
script.first: Do the first box together: count the top group aloud, touching each picture, and write the number. Count the bottom group the same way. Ask, "Are the numbers the same?" Circle the check mark or the X. Tell the children that a group that is spread out can still have the same number as a group that is close together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a small dot on each picture while counting it, so that none is counted twice. Then compare the two numbers on the page: "Are they the same number?"

blocks.title: Inside and Outside
blocks.instruction: Circle every picture INSIDE the big shape.

script.say: "There is a big shape on the page. Circle every picture that is INSIDE the big shape."
script.first: Trace the edge of the big shape with your finger. Ask, "Which pictures are inside the line? Which are outside?" Find one inside together and circle it.
script.stuck: Have the child trace the edge of the shape with a finger: a picture inside the line gets a circle.

blocks.title: Picture Pairs: Find the Difference
blocks.instruction: Each row shows the same close-up twice; circle the one place that is different in the right picture and check the box of that row.

script.say: "Each row shows the same picture two times, but one place in the right picture is different. Circle it, and check the box of that row."
script.first: Do the first row together: compare the left and the right picture, part by part, and find the one difference. Circle it in the right picture and check the box of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child cover half of each picture with a hand and compare one half at a time.

blocks.title: Which Face Shows the Feeling?
blocks.instruction: Read the feeling word and circle the one face in the row that shows it.

script.say: "Each row has a feeling word and three faces. Circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Read every feeling word on the page aloud: tired, angry, happy, scared, surprised, sad. Make each face for the class. Do the first row together: read the word, look at the three faces, and circle the one that matches.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and make the face. Ask the child to point to the face on the page that looks like yours.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 7
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 7
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 7 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Trace the Number 0
blocks.instruction: Trace each number. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing numbers. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace each number in the row."
script.first: Write the first number of the page big on the board and say where it starts and which way it goes. Have the children write it in the air with you. They trace the number on the page and then write their own.
script.stuck: Show the child where the number starts and guide the first stroke with your finger on the page. A number written backward is common at this age; show the right way once and move on.

blocks.title: Family Members: Who Is Who?
blocks.instruction: Find each person on the family tree and write their number in the box next to their family word.

script.say: "This page shows a family tree. Each person has a number. Under the tree are family words. Write each person's number in the box next to their family word."
script.first: Look at the family tree together. The child with the star is the one the words are about: each word says who a person is to that child. Read the family words aloud. Do the first one together: ask, for example, "Which person is the mom?" Find her number on the tree and write it in the box next to the word.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and ask who that person is to the child with the star. If a child says their own family does not look like this one, say, "Every family is different. This page is about this child's family."

blocks.title: Rhyme or Not?
blocks.instruction: Say both pictures out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X.

script.say: "In each box there are two pictures. Say both names out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X."
script.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name the pictures together, two by two: cake and hand, boat and shirt, lock and sock, bag and duck, car and guitar, rug and brain, log and frog, hat and cat (the last animal is a cat). Do the first box together and circle the check mark or the X. For your own reference, these rhyme: lock and sock, car and guitar, log and frog, hat and cat; the other four do not.
script.stuck: Say the two words one after the other and stretch their endings. If the endings sound the same, they rhyme.

blocks.title: Trace and Write the Words
blocks.instruction: Say the picture word. Trace the dashed letters, then write the word yourself on the empty lines.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Its word is written next to it. Trace the dashed letters, then write the word yourself on the empty lines."
script.first: Name the pictures together and read each word aloud. Do the first word together: read it, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more on the board, saying each letter.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: Which Has Fewer?
blocks.instruction: Look at both groups. Circle the group that has FEWER.

script.say: "In each box there are two groups. Count both groups. Then circle the group that has FEWER."
script.first: Do the first box together: count one group aloud, then the other. Ask, "Which number is less?" Circle that group: it has fewer. Tell the children that fewer means not as many.
script.stuck: Have the child draw a line from each thing in one group to one thing in the other group. The group with things left over has more.

blocks.title: Count and Color
blocks.instruction: Color exactly as many pictures as the number shows.

script.say: "Look at the number at the start of each row. Color that many pictures in the row, no more and no fewer. Leave the other pictures white."
script.first: Read the first number together. Touch the pictures of that row one by one as the class counts aloud, and color one picture for each number said. Stop at the number. Count the colored pictures once more to check.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the first picture and say "one" while coloring it, then "two" on the next. Stop when the count reaches the number in the circle. If the child has colored too many, count the colored ones together and start a fresh row more slowly.

blocks.title: Sail the Boat to the Teddy Bear
blocks.instruction: Help the boat sail along the stream to the teddy bear on the dock. Draw a line through the water.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Draw a line along the blue water from the start to the goal, and stay inside the water."
script.first: Hold up the page, read its title aloud, and show where the water starts, at the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the water with your finger and stop at each place where it splits: "Which way leads to the goal?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Summer and Winter Clothes
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each item of clothing to the right group.

script.say: "At the top are clothes. At the bottom are two boxes: Summer and Winter. Draw a line from each piece of clothing to the season we wear it in."
script.first: Read the two boxes aloud and name every piece of clothing together. Do the first one together: ask, "Do we wear this when it is hot or when it is cold?" Draw the line to its box.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Would you wear this to the beach or in the snow?" Where you live, winter may not mean snow; let the child explain.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 8
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 8
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 8 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Find the Different Size
blocks.instruction: Look at each row. Circle the one that is a different size.

script.say: "In each row, the pictures are the same, but one is a different size. Find it and circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to the pictures one by one: "Same size… same size… this one is smaller!" Circle it together.
script.stuck: Have the child point to two pictures at a time and ask, "Are they the same size?"

blocks.title: This Is Me: Label the Face
blocks.instruction: Copy each word from the bank onto the line that points to that part of the face. Then draw your own face.

script.say: "This page is about your face. Each line points to a part of the face. Copy the right word from the box onto each line. Then draw your own face in the big box."
script.first: Read the words in the box aloud and have the children touch that part of their own body for each one. Do the first line together: follow it with your finger to the part it points to, say its name, find the word in the box, and copy it onto the line letter by letter.
script.stuck: Have the child touch the part on their own body and say its name. Then find the word in the box together; the first letter helps: "Eye starts with e. Where is the word that starts with e?" Eye and ear both start with e: eye ends with e, ear ends with r.

blocks.title: Sort by Syllables
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to its number of syllables.

script.say: "Words have beats, called syllables. Say the name of each picture and clap its beats. Draw a line to the box with that number: 1, 2, or 3."
script.first: Clap a few children's names together. Name the pictures together: acorn, sun, apron, airplane, dog, ambulance, cat, banana, astronaut. Clap the first word together and draw its line. For your own reference: 1 beat: sun, dog, cat; 2 beats: acorn, apron, airplane; 3 beats: ambulance, banana, astronaut.
script.stuck: Have the child put a hand under the chin and say the word at normal speed: the chin drops once for each syllable. If the child claps every sound, say the word together the way you would say it when talking.

blocks.title: My First Tracing
blocks.instruction: Start at the dot. Trace the big whale slowly, all the way around.

script.say: "Start at the dot on the whale. Trace the big whale slowly, all the way around, without lifting your pencil."
script.first: Hold up the page and trace the whale in the air with your finger, slowly, from the dot all the way around. Have the children trace it on the page with a finger first, then with a pencil. Remind them to go slowly: this is not a race.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: How Many? Quick!
blocks.instruction: Look quickly and circle how many you see.

script.say: "Look at each group very quickly, without counting one by one. How many do you see? Circle the number."
script.first: Hold up three fingers for a second and hide them: "How many?" Do the same with five. Then look at the first group on the page together for a moment and circle the number. Tell the children that it is fine to check by counting after they have guessed.
script.stuck: Have the child look for small groups inside the big one: "I see two and two. That makes four." Then count to check.

blocks.title: Top, Middle, Bottom
blocks.instruction: Circle every picture in the MIDDLE row.

script.say: "The page has three rows: the top, the middle, and the bottom. Circle every picture in the MIDDLE row."
script.first: Point to the top row, the middle row, and the bottom row and have the class say each word. Find one picture in the middle row together and circle it.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on the top row and one on the bottom row: the middle is between the fingers.

blocks.title: Big and Small Patterns
blocks.instruction: Look at the pattern. Circle what comes next.

script.say: "A pattern is something that repeats, over and over. Say the pattern out loud. Then circle what comes next."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each picture and say "big" or "small" like a chant: "big, small, big, small…" Stop at the box with the question mark and ask, "What comes next: a big one or a small one?" Circle it among the choices.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Feels Good or Feels Bad? Sort the Faces
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each face to the box that says whether the feeling feels good or bad.

script.say: "Each face shows a feeling. Some feelings feel good, and some feel bad. Draw a line from each face to the box Feels good or Feels bad."
script.first: Make each face on the page with your own face and let the class name the feeling: happy, sad, scared, and so on. Do the first one together: "Does that feeling feel good or bad?" Draw the line to its box.
script.stuck: Make the face yourself and ask the child to make it too. Ask, "When do you feel like this? Is it a nice feeling?"

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 9
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 9
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 9 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Find and Circle
blocks.instruction: Find every picture like the one in the box. Circle them all.

script.say: "Look at the picture in the box at the top. Find every picture on the page that is just like it, and circle them all."
script.first: Point to the picture in the box and name it together. Find one like it on the page together and circle it. Tell the children to look across the page row by row, like reading, so they do not miss any.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the page with a sheet of paper and slide it down slowly, looking at one row at a time.

blocks.title: Family Members: Who Is Who?
blocks.instruction: Find each person on the family tree and write their number in the box next to their family word.

script.say: "This page shows a family tree. Each person has a number. Under the tree are family words. Write each person's number in the box next to their family word."
script.first: Look at the family tree together. The child with the star is the one the words are about: each word says who a person is to that child. Read the family words aloud. Do the first one together: ask, for example, "Which person is the mom?" Find her number on the tree and write it in the box next to the word.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and ask who that person is to the child with the star. If a child says their own family does not look like this one, say, "Every family is different. This page is about this child's family."

blocks.title: Sort by Beginning Sound
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the letter it begins with.

script.say: "At the bottom are three boxes, each with a letter. Say the name of each picture and listen for its first sound. Draw a line from the picture to the letter it begins with."
script.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: star, cow, bus, cat, sun, banana, sock, ball, carrot. Do the first one together: "star. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to S. For your own reference: B: bus, banana, ball; C: cow, cat, carrot; S: star, sun, sock.
script.stuck: Say the word and stretch the first sound. Then say the sound of each letter on the boxes and ask which one matches.

blocks.title: I Can: Check What You Can Do
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and check the things you can do. Then write one thing you want to learn.

script.say: "This page is about what YOU can do. Listen to each sentence. If you can do it, put a check in its box. At the bottom, write one thing you want to learn."
script.first: Read each sentence aloud while the children point to it: "I can paint a picture. I can brush my teeth…" After each one, pause so that every child can check the box or leave it empty. Tell them there is no wrong answer. For the last line, write "I want to learn to" on the board and let children say their ideas first.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask the child, "Can you do that?" For the last line, a child may draw the thing and write the first letter or one word with your help.

blocks.title: 2D Shapes
blocks.instruction: Look at each shape, even the turned and skinny ones, and circle its name.

script.say: "Look at each shape. It may be turned or skinny, but it is still the same shape. Circle its name."
script.first: Draw a circle, a triangle, a square, and a rectangle on the board and name them. Do the first shape together: count its sides and read the three names next to it. Circle the right one.
script.stuck: Have the child count the sides with a finger: 3 sides is a triangle; 4 sides of the same length is a square; 4 sides, two long and two short, is a rectangle; round with no sides is a circle.

blocks.title: Short to Tall
blocks.instruction: Number the pictures from 1 (shortest) to 4 (tallest).

script.say: "Each row has four pictures of the same thing. Write 1 under the shortest, then 2 and 3, and 4 under the tallest."
script.first: Write 1, 2, 3, 4 on the board. Do the first row together. Ask, "Which one is the shortest?" It gets the 1. "Which one is next?" It gets the 2. Go on until the tallest gets the 4.
script.stuck: Have the child find the shortest one left each time and cross it off lightly after writing its number.

blocks.title: What Is Missing?
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 empty places in the bottom picture where something from the top picture is missing, and check a box for each.

script.say: "The two pictures are the same, but three things are missing from the bottom picture. Find each empty place, circle it, and check a box for each one."
script.first: Hold up the page and compare the two pictures with the class, from the top down. Find one thing that is missing together and circle the empty place in the bottom picture. Check the first box.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the top picture and look for it in the bottom picture: "Is it there?" There are three missing things; the three boxes help them count.

blocks.title: Pets and Wild Animals
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes for two kinds of animals. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the two boxes aloud, Pets and Wild Animals, and name every animal together. Do the first one together: ask, "Can this animal live in a house with people, or does it live in the wild?" Draw the line from the dot under it to its box. A rabbit can be a pet or wild; either box is right for it.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 10
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 10
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 10 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Circles, Squares and More Shapes
blocks.instruction: Trace each shape with your pencil. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrow.

script.say: "Today your pencil goes for a walk. Each line starts at an orange dot. Follow the arrow and stay on the line as well as you can."
script.first: Hold up the page and trace the first line with your finger, from the orange dot in the direction of the arrow. Have the children trace it in the air with a finger, then on the page with a finger, and only then with a pencil. Remind them to go slowly: this is not a race.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: Match Word to Picture
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each word to the picture it names.

script.say: "Read each word. Then draw a line from the word to its picture."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Name the pictures together: bus, can (a soup can), key, fig, fox, bun (the bread). Do the first word together and draw the line.
script.stuck: Have the child say the sound of each letter and then say the sounds faster. If that does not work, ask for the first sound only and look for the pictures that begin with it. Read the word for the child if they are still stuck.

blocks.title: Middle Sounds
blocks.instruction: Write the vowel you hear in the middle of each word.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture and listen for the sound in the MIDDLE. Write the vowel you hear: a, e, i, o, or u."
script.first: Write a, e, i, o, u on the board. Name the pictures together: bed, dog, fox, hen, cat, bus, fig, mug. Do the first one together: say "b-e-d" slowly and stretch the middle: "beeed." Ask, "Which vowel?" Write e. For your own reference: bed e, dog o, fox o, hen e, cat a, bus u, fig i, mug u.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and hold the middle sound. Then say each vowel sound on the board and ask which one matches.

blocks.title: Trace the Longer Words
blocks.instruction: These words are long. Trace each one, then write it yourself.

script.say: "These words are long. Read each word with me, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Name the pictures together and read each long word aloud, clapping its parts: "skate-board." Do the first word together: trace it with your finger and write it on the board, one part at a time.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: One More, One Less
blocks.instruction: Count the pictures. Look at the label: for “1 more” draw one in the empty box; for “1 less” cross one out. Write how many there are now.

script.say: "In each row, count the pictures. Then read the label. For one more, draw one more picture in the empty box. Write how many there are now."
script.first: Read the first label aloud: "1 more." Count the pictures together, then draw one more in the empty box (a circle is fine). Count again and write the new number after the arrow. Tell the children that one more is always the next number when we count.
script.stuck: Have the child count the pictures and then say the next number: "Four… then five." That is how many there are with one more.

blocks.title: Count and Trace
blocks.instruction: Count the pictures in each row. Trace the number that tells how many.

script.say: "Count the pictures in each row. The number that tells how many is at the end of the row. Trace it."
script.first: Count the pictures of the first row aloud together, touching each one. Say the number and point to it at the end of the row. Write it big on the board and show where it starts. Then the children trace it.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture while counting. For the tracing, put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here."

blocks.title: Growing Patterns
blocks.instruction: The pattern grows. Circle the group that comes next.

script.say: "These patterns grow: each box has one more than the box before. Count the boxes. Circle the group that comes next."
script.first: Do the first row together: count the pictures in each box aloud, "one, two, three." Ask, "So how many come next?" Count the groups at the end of the row and circle the one with four.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Long Ago and Today
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each thing from long ago to the thing we use today that does the same job.

script.say: "The pictures on the left are things from long ago. The pictures on the right are things we use today. Draw a line from each long-ago thing to the thing that does the same job today."
script.first: Name the long-ago things on your page together. Do the top one together: "What job does this do? Which thing on the right does that job today?"
script.stuck: Ask, "What job does this do?" (washing clothes, giving light at night, getting from place to place, talking to someone far away). Then have the child find the picture on the right that does the same job.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 11
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 11
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 11 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Left and Right
blocks.instruction: Circle every picture on the LEFT side of the line.

script.say: "There is a line down the middle of the page. Circle every picture on the LEFT side of the line."
script.first: Have the children hold up their left hand: the thumb and pointer finger make an L. Point to the left side of the page. Find one picture on the left together and circle it.
script.stuck: Have the child hold up the L hand and lay it next to the page on the left side. Everything on that side of the line gets a circle.

blocks.title: One and Many: First Words
blocks.instruction: One or many? Trace the word that names more than one.

script.say: "One means just one thing. Many means more than one. The word for one is written for you. Trace the word for many."
script.first: Read the first word aloud and show one finger. Then show two fingers and say the word for many. Point to the s at the end: "We add s when there is more than one." Trace the word for many together. Read each word on the page aloud with the class before they trace.
script.stuck: Read the word for one and the word for many for the child and have the child point to the part that is different. "Fox" gets -es: foxes. Then trace one letter at a time.

blocks.title: Missing Sound
blocks.instruction: Write the missing letter to finish each word.

script.say: "Each word on this page has a gap in the middle: one letter is missing. Say the picture's name, listen for the sound in the middle, and write its letter."
script.first: Name all the pictures together: fig, bun (the bread), jet, jam, lid, dog, cap, fox. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly, point to each letter as you say its sound, and stop at the empty space. Ask, "Which sound belongs here? Which letter makes it?" Write it in and read the word together.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and stretch the sound in the middle: "p-iii-g." The missing letter is always one of the vowels: a, e, i, o, or u. Write the five vowels on the board for the child to choose from.

blocks.title: Family Words: Trace and Write
blocks.instruction: Find the person with the same number on the tree, trace their family word and write it again on the line.

script.say: "This page shows a family. Each person on the family tree has a number. Find the person with the same number, trace the family word, and write it again on the line."
script.first: Look at the family tree together. The child with the star is the one the words are about. Read the family words on the page aloud. Do number 1 together: find the person with the 1 on the tree, find the word with the 1, trace it, and write it again on line 1.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the number next to the word and find the same number on the tree. Read the word for the child. If a child says their own family does not look like this one, say, "Every family is different. This page is about this child's family."

blocks.title: 2D Shapes
blocks.instruction: Look at each shape, even the turned and skinny ones, and circle its name.

script.say: "Look at each shape. It may be turned or skinny, but it is still the same shape. Circle its name."
script.first: Draw a circle, a triangle, a square, and a rectangle on the board and name them. Do the first shape together: count its sides and read the three names next to it. Circle the right one.
script.stuck: Have the child count the sides with a finger: 3 sides is a triangle; 4 sides of the same length is a square; 4 sides, two long and two short, is a rectangle; round with no sides is a circle.

blocks.title: Same Number?
blocks.instruction: Count each group and write how many. Do both groups have the same number? Circle ✓ for yes or ✗ for no.

script.say: "In each box there are two groups. Count each group and write how many. Then circle the check mark if the two groups have the same number, or the X if they do not."
script.first: Do the first box together: count the top group aloud, touching each picture, and write the number. Count the bottom group the same way. Ask, "Are the numbers the same?" Circle the check mark or the X. Tell the children that a group that is spread out can still have the same number as a group that is close together.
