script.stuck: Have the child put a small dot on each picture while counting it, so that none is counted twice. Then compare the two numbers on the page: "Are they the same number?"

blocks.title: Find the Pairs
blocks.instruction: Every picture has a twin. Draw a line to join the two pictures in each pair.

script.say: "Every picture on this page has a twin, a picture that looks just the same. Draw a line to join the two pictures of each pair."
script.first: Point to the first picture and ask, "Where is its twin?" Find it together and draw the line. Tell the children to cross off nothing: each picture is in one pair only.
script.stuck: Have the child name one picture and look for the same name somewhere else on the page.

blocks.title: Which Season Is It?
blocks.instruction: Look at the three pictures on each card and circle the season sign they belong to.

script.say: "Each card has three pictures that belong to one season. Under them are four signs: a snowflake for winter, a flower for spring, a sun for summer, and a leaf for fall. Circle the sign of the season."
script.first: Point to the four signs and name the seasons together. Do the first card together: name the three pictures and ask, "When do we see these?" Circle the sign.
script.stuck: Ask the child about one picture at a time: "Is it hot or cold then? Are there flowers or falling leaves?"

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 12
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 12
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 12 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Round and Round
blocks.instruction: Start at each dot and trace round and round, like the letter o.

script.say: "Start at each dot and trace round and round, like the letter o."
script.first: Draw a big circle on the board, starting at the top and going to the left, like the letter o. Have the children draw circles in the air. Then they trace each round picture on the page from its dot.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: Circle the Right Word: Four Pictures
blocks.instruction: Say each picture word, then circle the word that belongs with it.

script.say: "Under each picture are two little words: a and an. Say the name of the picture with a in front of it, then with an. Circle the one that sounds right."
script.first: Name the pictures together: elephant, pig, owl, fox. Do the first one together: "a elephant, an elephant. Which sounds right?" Circle an. Tell the children that an goes in front of words that start with a, e, i, o, or u. For your own reference: an elephant, a pig, an owl, a fox.
script.stuck: Say both choices for the child, slowly, and let the child hear which one is easier to say. Ask, "Does the word start with a, e, i, o, or u?"

blocks.title: Rhyming Pairs
blocks.instruction: Draw a line between the two pictures that rhyme.

script.say: "Rhyming words sound the same at the end, like cat and hat. Draw a line from each picture on the left to the picture on the right that rhymes with it."
script.first: Name all the pictures together, so that everyone uses the same words: on the left bed, bag, cat, dog, boat; on the right frog, goat, sled, hat, flag. Say the first picture on the left with each picture on the right: "bed, frog… bed, sled." Ask which pair sounds the same at the end. Draw that line together. For your own reference, the pairs are bed and sled, bag and flag, cat and hat, dog and frog, boat and goat.
script.stuck: Say the two words one after the other and stretch the ending: "c-AT, h-AT." If the endings sound the same, they rhyme. If the child does not know what a picture is called, tell them.

blocks.title: Trace the Letter L l
blocks.instruction: Trace each letter, then write one on your own at the end of the line. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing letters. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace the letters first. Then write one all by yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Write the first letter of the page big on the board, saying where you start and which way you go. Have the children write it in the air with you. Then they trace the letters on the page. Walk around and watch where each child starts.
script.stuck: Put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here. Which way does the arrow point?" If the letter the child writes alone is far from the model, have the child trace one more and try again. Do not ask for a perfect letter.

blocks.title: Count and Write: 11 to 20
blocks.instruction: Count all the pictures. Write how many there are in all.

script.say: "Count all the pictures in each box. There are between 11 and 20. Write how many there are in all."
script.first: Count the first box aloud together, touching each picture as the class counts. Ask, "So how many are there?" Write the number on the board. Then write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board and leave them there for children who need to copy them.
script.stuck: Have the child cross out each shape while counting it, so that none is counted twice. If the child does not know how to write the number, point to it on the board.

blocks.title: Color the Greater Number
blocks.instruction: Look at the two numbers in each box. Color the greater number.

script.say: "Each box has two numbers. Which number is greater, which one means more? Color the greater number."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board. Do the first box together: find both numbers on the board and ask, "Which one comes later when we count?" That one is greater. Color it.
script.stuck: Have the child count aloud from one and stop at the first of the two numbers that comes up; the other number is the greater one.

blocks.title: Help the Pig Reach the Mud Puddle
blocks.instruction: Help the hedgehog get to the apple tree. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Find the way along the light path from the animal to its goal. Use your finger first, then your pencil."
script.first: Hold up the page and show where the path starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the beginning of the way with your finger and stop at the first place where the path splits: "Which way? Let's try one." Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Community Helpers and Their Tools
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each helper to the tool they use.

script.say: "Each helper on the left uses one of the tools on the right. Draw a line from each helper to the tool they use."
script.first: Name each helper and each tool on your page together. Do the top helper together: "What does this helper do at work? Which tool helps with that job?" If there is one more tool than helpers, one tool belongs to no one on the page; it gets no line.
script.stuck: Ask, "What does this helper do at work? What do they hold to do it?" Let the child act it out, then find that tool.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 13
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 13
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 13 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Missing Numbers to 10
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 10 on the board. Count the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at the empty box: "one, two, (clap), four." Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Match Word to Picture
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each word to the picture it names.

script.say: "Read each word. Then draw a line from the word to its picture."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Name the pictures together: bag, dog, fan, bun (the bread), egg, key. Do the first word together and draw the line.
script.stuck: Have the child say the sound of each letter and then say the sounds faster. If that does not work, ask for the first sound only and look for the pictures that begin with it. Read the word for the child if they are still stuck.

blocks.title: Count the Syllables
blocks.instruction: Write how many syllables you hear in each word.

script.say: "Words have beats, like music. The beats are called syllables. Say the name of each picture, clap the beats, and write how many claps you made."
script.first: Clap a few children's names together: "Ma-ri-a, three claps." Name all the pictures together: domino, eraser, oval, ant, tomato, bat, baby, bed. The second picture is an eraser, not lipstick. Clap the first picture's word together and write the number on the board. For your own reference: domino 3, eraser 3, oval 2, ant 1, tomato 3, bat 1, baby 2, bed 1.
script.stuck: Have the child put a hand under the chin and say the word at normal speed: the chin drops once for each syllable. If the child claps every sound, say the word together the way you would say it when talking.

blocks.title: Singular and Plural
blocks.instruction: Read the word for one. Then trace the word for many and write it yourself on the empty line.

script.say: "The word for one is written for you. Read it with me. Then trace the word for many, and write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Read the first word aloud and show one finger. Then show two fingers and say the word for many. Point to the s at the end: "We add s when there is more than one." Trace the word for many together. Read each word on the page aloud with the class before they trace.
script.stuck: Read the word for one and the word for many for the child and have the child point to the part that is different. Then trace one letter at a time.

blocks.title: Tall and Short
blocks.instruction: Circle the TALLEST one in each row.

script.say: "In each row, some things are tall and some are short. Look at all of them. Then circle the TALLEST one."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each picture and ask, "Is this the tallest? Is there a taller one?" Circle the tallest together. Remind the children to look at every picture in the row before they circle.
script.stuck: Have the child point to two pictures at a time and say which of the two is bigger, keeping a finger on the winner, until the row is done. The picture under the finger at the end gets the circle.

blocks.title: Draw 2D Shapes on Dot Paper
blocks.instruction: Read the shape name and connect the dots to draw it. Start at the thick line if there is one.

script.say: "Each box names a shape. Connect the dots with your pencil to draw that shape. If there is a thick line in the box, start there."
script.first: Read the name in each box aloud and draw that shape on the board: a triangle has 3 sides, a square has 4 sides that are all the same length, a rectangle has 4 sides with two long and two short. Draw the first shape together on the dot paper, going from dot to dot with straight lines.
script.stuck: Have the child count the sides of the shape on the board and put a finger on the dots where the corners will go. Then draw one side at a time from corner to corner.

blocks.title: Match the Shadow
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to its shadow.

script.say: "Each picture on the left has a shadow on the right. A shadow is dark and shows only the shape. Draw a line from each picture to its shadow."
script.first: Do the first one together: look at the outline of the first picture and ask, "Which shadow has the same shape?" Draw the line from dot to dot. Tell the children to look at the edges: the ears, the wheels, the tail.
script.stuck: Have the child trace the outside of the picture with a finger, then trace the shadows until one has the same shape.

blocks.title: Wants and Needs
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "Draw a line from each picture to Needs or to Wants. Needs are things we must have to live. Wants are things that are nice to have."
script.first: Point to the words Needs and Wants and read them aloud. Do the first picture together: "Can we live without this? Then is it a need or a want?"
script.stuck: Ask, "Could you live without it?" Food, water, clothes and a home are needs; toys and treats are wants.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 14
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 14
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 14 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Inside and Outside
blocks.instruction: Circle every picture INSIDE the big shape.

script.say: "There is a big shape on the page. Circle every picture that is INSIDE the big shape."
script.first: Trace the edge of the big shape with your finger. Ask, "Which pictures are inside the line? Which are outside?" Find one inside together and circle it.
script.stuck: Have the child trace the edge of the shape with a finger: a picture inside the line gets a circle.

blocks.title: Circle the Right Word: Four Pictures
blocks.instruction: Say each picture word, then circle the word that belongs with it.

script.say: "Under each picture are two little words: a and an. Say the name of the picture with a in front of it, then with an. Circle the one that sounds right."
script.first: Name the pictures together: donut, taco, egg, iron (the iron for clothes). Do the first one together: "a donut, an donut. Which sounds right?" Circle a. Tell the children that an goes in front of words that start with a, e, i, o, or u. For your own reference: a donut, a taco, an egg, an iron.
script.stuck: Say both choices for the child, slowly, and let the child hear which one is easier to say. Ask, "Does the word start with a, e, i, o, or u?"

blocks.title: M or N? Hear the Difference
blocks.instruction: Say each picture. Circle the letter it begins with: m or n.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Does it begin with mmm or nnn? Circle m or n."
script.first: Say the sounds mmm and nnn together; feel the lips close for m. Name the pictures together: nest, necklace, moon, nose, medal, milk, nurse, mitten. Do the first one together: "nest. Does it start with mmm or nnn?" Circle n. For your own reference: n: nest, necklace, nose, nurse; m: moon, medal, milk, mitten.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word with a hand on the lips: for m the lips close, for n they stay open.

blocks.title: My Favorite Things: Circle and Write
blocks.instruction: In each row, circle your favorite picture and copy its word onto the line.

script.say: "In each row there are pictures of different things. Circle the one you like best. Then copy its word on the line."
script.first: Do the first row together: name the pictures, ask a few children which one they like best, and show how to circle one. Then show how to copy its word onto the line, letter by letter. Everyone circles their own favorite; there is no right answer.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger under the word and copy one letter at a time, moving the finger along. If the child cannot choose, say, "Pick the one you would like to have today."

blocks.title: Smallest to Biggest
blocks.instruction: Number the pictures from 1 (smallest) to 5 (biggest).

script.say: "Each row has five pictures of the same thing in different sizes. Write 1 under the smallest, then 2, 3, 4, and 5 under the biggest."
script.first: Write 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 on the board. Do the first row together. Ask, "Which one is the smallest?" It gets the 1. "Which one is next?" It gets the 2. Go on until the biggest gets the 5.
script.stuck: Have the child find the smallest one left each time and cross it off lightly after writing its number.

blocks.title: Stuck in the Middle
blocks.instruction: Write the number that comes between.

script.say: "Each row has two numbers with an empty box between them. Write the number that comes in the middle."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 in a row on the board. Do the first row together: find both numbers on the board and point to the one between them. Write it in the empty box.
script.stuck: Have the child count up from the first number: "Fourteen… fifteen." The number they say next is the one in the middle.

blocks.title: Picture Pairs: Find the Difference
blocks.instruction: Each row shows the same close-up twice; circle the one place that is different in the right picture and check the box of that row.

script.say: "Each row shows the same picture two times, but one place in the right picture is different. Circle it, and check the box of that row."
script.first: Do the first row together: compare the left and the right picture, part by part, and find the one difference. Circle it in the right picture and check the box of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child cover half of each picture with a hand and compare one half at a time.

blocks.title: Choosing One Thing
blocks.instruction: You can have only one thing in each row. Circle the one you choose. Put an X on the one you do not pick. There is no wrong answer.

script.say: "In each row you can have only one thing. Circle the one you choose and put an X on the one you do not pick. There is no wrong answer."
script.first: The small "1" at the start of a row is not a choice. Read the first row together and say what the 1 means: a hand with a coin, "You have one coin. You can buy one of these, not both."; a hand with a book, "You can take home one book."; just the 1, "Recess has time for one thing." Ask, "Which do you choose?" Two children who choose differently are both right.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which one would you like more?" Then help the child put an X on the other one: "That is the one you give up." Check only that every row has one circle and one X.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 15
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 15
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 15 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Missing Numbers to 10
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 10 on the board. Count the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at the empty box: "one, two, (clap), four." Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Find the Letter
blocks.instruction: Circle every letter that matches the one in the box.

script.say: "Look at the letter in the box. Your job is to find every letter in the row that is the same, and circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to the letter in the box and say its name. Move your finger along the row and stop at each letter: "Is this one the same? Look closely." Circle the ones that match. Tell the children that some letters look almost alike, so they have to look closely.
script.stuck: Cover the row with a sheet of paper and uncover one letter at a time. Have the child hold a finger under the letter in the box and compare. If the child circles a letter that only looks similar, put the two side by side and ask what is different.

blocks.title: Digraph Sort for Kindergarten: sh or ch
blocks.instruction: Say each picture's name. Draw a line from each picture to the letter team you hear.

script.say: "Two letters can make one sound. S and h say sh, like in shoe. C and h say ch, like in cheese. Say the name of each picture. Do you hear sh or ch? Draw a line to that side."
script.first: Say sh and ch together a few times. Name the pictures together: chocolate, shorts, wheelchair, cheese, shoe, shrimp. Do the first one together: say "chocolate" slowly and ask, "Do you hear sh or ch?" Draw the line to ch. For your own reference: ch: chocolate, wheelchair (the ch is in "chair"), cheese; sh: shorts, shoe, shrimp.
script.stuck: Say the word and stretch its first sound: "sh-sh-shoe." Then say "sh" and "ch" and ask which one it sounds like.

blocks.title: Trace and Write the Words
blocks.instruction: Say the picture word. Trace the dashed letters, then write the word yourself on the empty lines.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Its word is written next to it. Trace the dashed letters, then write the word yourself on the empty lines."
script.first: Name the pictures together and read each word aloud. Do the first word together: read it, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more on the board, saying each letter.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: Count the Array
blocks.instruction: Count all the pictures. Write how many there are in all.

script.say: "The pictures in each box stand in rows. Count all of them. Then write how many there are in all."
script.first: Count the first box aloud together, one row at a time, touching each picture as the class counts. Ask, "So how many are there in all?" Write the number on the board. Then write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board and leave them there for children who need to copy them.
script.stuck: Have the child cross out each shape while counting it, so that none is counted twice. If the child does not know how to write the number, point to it on the board.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot: Count On from 11
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Count on from 11 to 30 and connect the dots to finish the picture.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 11. Count on and draw a line to each next number, all the way to 30."
script.first: Count from 11 to 30 aloud together. Find the orange dot, number 11, together and put a finger on it. Find 12 and draw the first line together. The numbers 11 to 30 are printed at the bottom of the page to help.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and count one more; that is the number to look for. Point to the part of the page where the next dot is. If a line went to the wrong dot, leave it and go on from the right one.

blocks.title: Which Shape Is Different?
blocks.instruction: Look at each row. Circle the shape that does not belong.

script.say: "In each row the shapes are the same, but one shape does not belong. Find it and circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to the shapes one by one: "same… same… this one is different!" Ask a child to say what is different about it. Circle it.
script.stuck: Have the child name each shape in the row; the one with a different name gets the circle.

blocks.title: Healthy and Not Healthy Foods
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes, Healthy and Not Healthy. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Is this good for our body every day, or is it a treat for once in a while?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. A treat is fine once in a while; the page only asks which foods to eat every day.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 16
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 16
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 16 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Down, Across, Slanted
blocks.instruction: Look at the arrow above each column. Trace one column at a time: down, then across, then slanted.

script.say: "Each column has an arrow at the top. Trace the lines in that column the way the arrow points: down, then across, then slanted."
script.first: Point to the three arrows and show each way with your hand: down, across, slanted. Trace the first line of the first column in the air with the class, from the top down. Tell the children to do one column at a time.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: Parts of the Body
blocks.instruction: Copy each word from the bank onto the line that points to that part of the body.

script.say: "Look at the picture. Each line points to a part of the body. The words are in the box at the top. Copy the right word onto each line."
script.first: Read the words in the box aloud and have the children touch that part of their own body for each one. Do the first line together: follow it with your finger to the part it points to, say its name, find the word in the box, and copy it onto the line letter by letter.
script.stuck: Have the child touch the part on their own body and say its name. Then find the word in the box together; the first letter helps: "Eye starts with e. Where is the word that starts with e?" Eye and ear both start with e: eye ends with e, ear ends with r.

blocks.title: Build the Word
blocks.instruction: Use the letters to build the word for each picture.

script.say: "Next to each picture are the letters of its word, but they are mixed up. Say the word, listen to its sounds, and write the letters in the right order."
script.first: Name all the pictures together: fig, lid, bee, bus, cup, jam. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? The next sound? The last sound?" Write a letter for each sound and read the word together. "Bee" has two e's that make one sound.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word slowly and hold up one finger for each sound. Ask which of the letters makes the first sound, and cross each letter out when it is used. Then have the child read the word they wrote.

blocks.title: Family Words: Trace and Write
blocks.instruction: Find the person with the same number on the tree, trace their family word and write it again on the line.

script.say: "This page shows a family. Each person on the family tree has a number. Find the person with the same number, trace the family word, and write it again on the line."
script.first: Look at the family tree together. The child with the star is the one the words are about. Read the family words on the page aloud. Do number 1 together: find the person with the 1 on the tree, find the word with the 1, trace it, and write it again on line 1.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the number next to the word and find the same number on the tree. Read the word for the child. If a child says their own family does not look like this one, say, "Every family is different. This page is about this child's family."

blocks.title: Read the Tally
blocks.instruction: Count the tally marks. Write the number.

script.say: "Each box has tally marks. Count them and write the number."
script.first: Draw tally marks on the board while the class counts to five: four marks standing up and the fifth one across them. Do the first box together: count the marks and write the number. A bundle of five with a line across counts as five.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each mark and count. For a bundle with a line across, say "five" and count on from there: six, seven…

blocks.title: Count On from the Box
blocks.instruction: The number on the box tells how many are hidden inside. Start at that number and count on. Write how many there are in all.

script.say: "The number on each box tells how many are hidden inside. Start at that number and count on, one more for each picture next to the box. Write how many there are in all."
script.first: Do the first one together: put your hand on the box and say its number. Then touch each picture and count on aloud: "Six… seven." Write the number in the empty box. Tell the children not to count the box from one: they start at its number.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number on the box and then tap each picture while saying the next number. If the child starts again at one, say the box number together and go on from there.

blocks.title: AABB Patterns
blocks.instruction: Look at the pattern. Circle what comes next.

script.say: "A pattern is something that repeats, over and over. Say the pattern out loud. Then circle what comes next."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each picture and have the class say its name like a chant. On this page each picture comes two times, and then the next picture comes two times. Stop at the box with the question mark and ask, "What comes next?" Circle it among the choices.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Who Makes It? Who Does It?
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each worker to what they make or do.

script.say: "Each worker on the left makes something or does something. Draw a line from each worker to what they make or do."
script.first: Name the workers on your page together by what they wear and hold (a tall white hat and a rolling pin: a baker; a hard hat and a hammer: a builder; a striped pole, scissors and a comb: a barber; a cap and a bag of letters: a mail carrier). Do the top worker together: "What does this worker make or do?"
script.stuck: Ask, "What is this worker holding? What would they make or do with it?"

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 17
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 17
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 17 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Missing Days: Write the Week in Order
blocks.instruction: Some days are already written on the ladder. Copy the missing days from the word bank into the right places.

script.say: "The days of the week go down the ladder in order. Some days are already written. Find the missing days in the word box at the top and copy them onto the empty lines."
script.first: Say the days of the week together, starting with Sunday. Read the days already on the ladder aloud. Do the first empty line together: "Sunday, then…?" Find Monday in the word box and copy it letter by letter.
script.stuck: Say the days in order with the child, pointing down the ladder, and stop at the empty line. Help the child find the word in the box by its first letter.

blocks.title: Story Sequencing: Number the Pictures
blocks.instruction: Look at what changes in each story, then write the numbers in the boxes to put the pictures in order.

script.say: "Each row shows a little story in four pictures, but the pictures are out of order. Look at what changes. Write 1 under what happens first, then 2, 3, and 4."
script.first: Do the first story together. Ask a child to say what is happening in each picture. Ask, "Which one happens first? How do you know?" Write a 1 in the box under it, then find 2, 3, and 4 together. Have a child tell the whole story in order.
script.stuck: Ask the child to find the picture where the story starts, where nothing has happened yet. Then ask, "What happens after that?" Have the child tell the story aloud; if it makes sense, the order is right.

blocks.title: Rhyme or Not?
blocks.instruction: Say both pictures out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X.

script.say: "In each box there are two pictures. Say both names out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X."
script.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name the pictures together, two by two: hand and sand, balloon and raccoon, sheep and jeep, pan and chair, car and crane, hat and bat, letter (the envelope) and bread, shirt and map. Do the first box together and circle the check mark or the X. For your own reference, these rhyme: hand and sand, balloon and raccoon, sheep and jeep, hat and bat; the other four do not.
script.stuck: Say the two words one after the other and stretch their endings. If the endings sound the same, they rhyme.

blocks.title: Trace the Longer Words
blocks.instruction: These words are long. Trace each one, then write it yourself.

script.say: "These words are long. Read each word with me, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Name the pictures together and read each long word aloud, clapping its parts: "skate-board." Do the first word together: trace it with your finger and write it on the board, one part at a time.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: Color the Greater Number
blocks.instruction: Look at the two numbers in each box. Color the greater number.

script.say: "Each box has two numbers. Which number is greater, which one means more? Color the greater number."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board. Do the first box together: find both numbers on the board and ask, "Which one comes later when we count?" That one is greater. Color it.
script.stuck: Have the child count aloud from one and stop at the first of the two numbers that comes up; the other number is the greater one.

blocks.title: Count and Trace
blocks.instruction: Count the pictures in each row. Trace the number that tells how many.

script.say: "Count the pictures in each row. The number that tells how many is at the end of the row. Trace it."
script.first: Count the pictures of the first row aloud together, touching each one. Say the number and point to it at the end of the row. Write it big on the board and show where it starts. Then the children trace it.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture while counting. For the tracing, put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here."

blocks.title: Help the Kitten Get to the Milk
blocks.instruction: Help the puppy get to the ball. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Help the animal get to its goal. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges."
script.first: Hold up the page, read its title aloud, and show where the road starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the road with your finger and stop at each place where it splits: "Which way leads to the goal?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Living and Non-living Things
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes, Living and Non-living. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Does it grow and need water and air? Then it is living." Plants are living too, even though they do not walk or run. Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 18
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 18
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 18 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Left and Right
blocks.instruction: Circle every picture on the LEFT side of the line.

script.say: "There is a line down the middle of the page. Circle every picture on the LEFT side of the line."
script.first: Have the children hold up their left hand: the thumb and pointer finger make an L. Point to the left side of the page. Find one picture on the left together and circle it.
script.stuck: Have the child hold up the L hand and lay it next to the page on the left side. Everything on that side of the line gets a circle.

blocks.title: Match Word to Picture
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each word to the picture it names.

script.say: "Read each word. Then draw a line from the word to its picture."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Name the pictures together: cap, fan, bee, hen, hot (the hot sun), jam. Do the first word together and draw the line.
script.stuck: Have the child say the sound of each letter and then say the sounds faster. If that does not work, ask for the first sound only and look for the pictures that begin with it. Read the word for the child if they are still stuck.

blocks.title: Sort by Beginning Sound
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the letter it begins with.

script.say: "At the bottom are three boxes, each with a letter. Say the name of each picture and listen for its first sound. Draw a line from the picture to the letter it begins with."
script.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: cow, can (a soup can), sink, seal, salt (the salt shaker), bat, cat, bun, bus. Do the first one together: "cow. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to C. For your own reference: B: bat, bun, bus; C: cow, can, cat; S: sink, seal, salt.
script.stuck: Say the word and stretch the first sound. Then say the sound of each letter on the boxes and ask which one matches.

blocks.title: I Can: Check What You Can Do
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and check the things you can do. Then write one thing you want to learn.

script.say: "This page is about what YOU can do. Listen to each sentence. If you can do it, put a check in its box. At the bottom, write one thing you want to learn."
script.first: Read each sentence aloud while the children point to it: "I can paint a picture. I can brush my teeth…" After each one, pause so that every child can check the box or leave it empty. Tell them there is no wrong answer. For the last line, write "I want to learn to" on the board and let children say their ideas first.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask the child, "Can you do that?" For the last line, a child may draw the thing and write the first letter or one word with your help.

blocks.title: How Many Altogether?
blocks.instruction: Count both groups together. Write how many in all.

script.say: "In each box there are two groups. Count all the things in both groups together, and write how many there are in all."
script.first: Do the first box together: count the first group aloud and keep counting through the second group without starting over. Ask, "How many in all?" Write the number on the board.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture while counting and keep going from the first group into the second. If the child starts again at one for the second group, count with them once.

blocks.title: Quick Look!
blocks.instruction: Do not count one by one! Look quickly and circle how many.

script.say: "Look at each group very quickly, without counting one by one. How many do you see? Circle the number."
script.first: Hold up three fingers for a second and hide them: "How many?" Do the same with five. Then look at the first group on the page together for a moment and circle the number. Tell the children that it is fine to check by counting after they have guessed.
script.stuck: Have the child look for small groups inside the big one: "I see two and two. That makes four." Then count to check.

blocks.title: Find the Pairs
blocks.instruction: Every picture has a twin. Draw a line to join the two pictures in each pair.

script.say: "Every picture on this page has a twin, a picture that looks just the same. Draw a line to join the two pictures of each pair."
script.first: Point to the first picture and ask, "Where is its twin?" Find it together and draw the line. Tell the children to cross off nothing: each picture is in one pair only.
script.stuck: Have the child name one picture and look for the same name somewhere else on the page.

blocks.title: Our Flag
blocks.instruction: Color the flag like the small flag: red and white stripes, red at the top and the bottom. Color the box blue around the stars. Leave the stars white.

script.say: "This is the flag of our country, the United States. If your flag has red dots, color the stripes with the dots red. Color it like the small flag: red and white stripes, red at the top and the bottom. Color the box blue around the stars, and leave the stars white."
script.first: Look at the small colored flag together and name the stripes from the top: red, white, red. Each child needs a red crayon and a blue one; the white stripes and the stars stay white.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on a stripe of the small flag and find the same stripe on the big one. A stripe colored by mistake is fine; go on to the next stripe together.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 19
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 19
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 19 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Missing Days: Write the Week in Order
blocks.instruction: Some days are already written on the ladder. Copy the missing days from the word bank into the right places.

script.say: "The days of the week go down the ladder in order. Some days are already written. Find the missing days in the word box at the top and copy them onto the empty lines."
script.first: Say the days of the week together, starting with Sunday. Read the days already on the ladder aloud. Do the first empty line together: "Sunday, then…?" Find Monday in the word box and copy it letter by letter.
script.stuck: Say the days in order with the child, pointing down the ladder, and stop at the empty line. Help the child find the word in the box by its first letter.

blocks.title: Story Sequencing: Number the Pictures
blocks.instruction: Look at what changes in each story, then write the numbers in the boxes to put the pictures in order.

script.say: "Each row shows a little story in four pictures, but the pictures are out of order. Look at what changes. Write 1 under what happens first, then 2, 3, and 4."
script.first: Do the first story together. Ask a child to say what is happening in each picture. Ask, "Which one happens first? How do you know?" Write a 1 in the box under it, then find 2, 3, and 4 together. Have a child tell the whole story in order.
script.stuck: Ask the child to find the picture where the story starts, where nothing has happened yet. Then ask, "What happens after that?" Have the child tell the story aloud; if it makes sense, the order is right.

blocks.title: Missing Sound
blocks.instruction: Write the missing letter to finish each word.

script.say: "Each word on this page has a gap in the middle: one letter is missing. Say the picture's name, listen for the sound in the middle, and write its letter."
script.first: Name all the pictures together: dog, bag, bed, leg, jug, bus, bat, fig. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly, point to each letter as you say its sound, and stop at the empty space. Ask, "Which sound belongs here? Which letter makes it?" Write it in and read the word together.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and stretch the sound in the middle: "p-iii-g." The missing letter is always one of the vowels: a, e, i, o, or u. Write the five vowels on the board for the child to choose from.

blocks.title: Trace the Letter M m
blocks.instruction: Trace each letter, then write one on your own at the end of the line. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing letters. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace the letters first. Then write one all by yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Write the first letter of the page big on the board, saying where you start and which way you go. Have the children write it in the air with you. Then they trace the letters on the page. Walk around and watch where each child starts.
script.stuck: Put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here. Which way does the arrow point?" If the letter the child writes alone is far from the model, have the child trace one more and try again. Do not ask for a perfect letter.

blocks.title: Take Away on the Ten-Frame
blocks.instruction: Count the dots. The crossed-out dots are taken away. Write how many are left.

script.say: "Count the dots in each ten-frame. Some dots are crossed out: they are taken away. Write how many are left."
script.first: Do the first one together: count all the dots, then count the crossed-out ones. Read the number sentence aloud: "Ten take away one." Count the dots that are not crossed out and write the number after the equals sign.
script.stuck: Have the child cover each crossed-out dot with a finger and count only the dots that can still be seen.

blocks.title: Count and Color
blocks.instruction: Color exactly as many pictures as the number shows.

script.say: "Look at the number at the start of each row. Color that many pictures in the row, no more and no fewer. Leave the other pictures white."
script.first: Read the first number together. Touch the pictures of that row one by one as the class counts aloud, and color one picture for each number said. Stop at the number. Count the colored pictures once more to check.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the first picture and say "one" while coloring it, then "two" on the next. Stop when the count reaches the number in the circle. If the child has colored too many, count the colored ones together and start a fresh row more slowly.

blocks.title: What Is Missing?
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 empty places in the bottom picture where something from the top picture is missing, and check a box for each.

script.say: "The two pictures are the same, but three things are missing from the bottom picture. Find each empty place, circle it, and check a box for each one."
script.first: Hold up the page and compare the two pictures with the class, from the top down. Find one thing that is missing together and circle the empty place in the bottom picture. Check the first box.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the top picture and look for it in the bottom picture: "Is it there?" There are three missing things; the three boxes help them count.

blocks.title: How Do You Feel? Circle the Face
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture, think how you would feel, and circle the face that matches.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Think about how it would make you feel. Then circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Look at the first picture together and ask what it shows. Ask, "How does that make you feel?" Let two or three children answer; they may not all feel the same, and that is fine. Each child circles the face that matches their own answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child what the picture shows and when they have seen one. Then point to each face and name the feeling it shows. There is no wrong answer on this page; any face the child can explain is right.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 20
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 20
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 20 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Loops, Eights and Spirals
blocks.instruction: Trace each line with your pencil. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrow.

script.say: "Today your pencil goes for a walk. Each line starts at an orange dot. Follow the arrow and stay on the line as well as you can."
script.first: Hold up the page and trace the first line with your finger, from the orange dot in the direction of the arrow. Have the children trace it in the air with a finger, then on the page with a finger, and only then with a pencil. Remind them to go slowly: this is not a race.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: Sight Words: Read, Trace, Write
blocks.instruction: Read the word. Trace it. Then write it yourself on the empty line.

script.say: "These are words we see all the time. Read the word, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Do the first word together: read it, write it on the board, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more next to it. Tell the children to say the word each time they finish writing it.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: Rhyming Pairs
blocks.instruction: Draw a line between the two pictures that rhyme.

script.say: "Rhyming words sound the same at the end, like cat and hat. Draw a line from each picture on the left to the picture on the right that rhymes with it."
script.first: Name all the pictures together, so that everyone uses the same words: on the left sun, cat, boat, star, bed; on the right car, goat, bun (the bread), sled, hat. Say the first picture on the left with each picture on the right: "sun, car… sun, bun." Ask which pair sounds the same at the end. Draw that line together. For your own reference, the pairs are sun and bun, cat and hat, boat and goat, star and car, bed and sled.
script.stuck: Say the two words one after the other and stretch the ending: "c-AT, h-AT." If the endings sound the same, they rhyme. If the child does not know what a picture is called, tell them.

blocks.title: Singular and Plural
blocks.instruction: Read the word for one. Then trace the word for many and write it yourself on the empty line.

script.say: "The word for one is written for you. Read it with me. Then trace the word for many, and write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Read the first word aloud and show one finger. Then show two fingers and say the word for many. Point to the s at the end: "We add s when there is more than one." Trace the word for many together. Read each word on the page aloud with the class before they trace.
script.stuck: Read the word for one and the word for many for the child and have the child point to the part that is different. "Octopus" gets -es: octopuses. Then trace one letter at a time.

blocks.title: 2D Shapes Around Us
blocks.instruction: Look at each picture and color the shape it has: the circle or the rectangle.

script.say: "Each picture is something we see every day. Is its shape a circle or a rectangle? Color the shape it has."
script.first: Draw a circle and a rectangle on the board and name them. Name the first picture together and ask, "Is it round like a circle, or does it have four sides like a rectangle?" Color that shape in the box next to the picture.
script.stuck: Have the child trace the outside of the picture with a finger: round all the way around is a circle; four straight sides are a rectangle.

blocks.title: Before and After
blocks.instruction: Write the number that comes before and the one that comes after.

script.say: "Each number has a neighbor before it and a neighbor after it. Write the number that comes just before and the number that comes just after."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 in a row on the board and leave them there. Do the first one together: find the number on the board, point to the number before it and the number after it, and write them on the page.
script.stuck: Walk to the board with the child and have the child put a finger on the number: one step to the left is the number before, one step to the right is the number after.

blocks.title: What Is It?
blocks.instruction: Only part of the picture is showing. Circle the whole picture it belongs to.

script.say: "In each row only a small part of a picture is showing. Which whole picture does it belong to? Circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together: look at the small part and ask, "What could this be? An ear, a tail, a head?" Look at the three whole pictures and circle the one the part belongs to.
script.stuck: Have the child find the part on each of the three pictures: "Does this one have it?"

blocks.title: Fair for Everyone
blocks.instruction: Look at the two pictures in each row. They show the same moment. Circle the picture that is fair to everyone.

script.say: "The two pictures in each row show the same moment. Circle the picture that is fair to everyone."
script.first: Do the first row together. Ask, "In which picture does everyone get a turn, or the same?" Talk about what the children do (keeping the swing, sharing the crackers, letting a friend play), never about a bad child.
script.stuck: Ask how each child in the picture feels. In the fair picture everyone can smile; in the other one someone is left out, still waiting, or has none.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 21
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 21
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 21 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Missing Numbers to 10
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 10 on the board. Count the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at the empty box: "one, two, (clap), four." Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Find the Action Word
blocks.instruction: Read the three words in each row. Circle the action word.

script.say: "Each row has three words. One of them is something you can DO, like hop or run. That is the action word. Circle it."
script.first: Read the three words of the first row aloud and have the class read them with you: hop, egg, hat. Ask, "Which one can you do?" Have everyone hop once. Circle hop. Read each row aloud with the class before they choose.
script.stuck: Read the three words for the child and ask about each one: "Can you ___?" The word that makes sense is the action word.

blocks.title: Build the Word
blocks.instruction: Use the letters to build the word for each picture.

script.say: "Next to each picture are the letters of its word, but they are mixed up. Say the word, listen to its sounds, and write the letters in the right order."
script.first: Name all the pictures together: ham, jar, egg, hot (the hot sun), ant, jet. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? The next sound? The last sound?" Write a letter for each sound and read the word together. "Egg" ends with two g's.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word slowly and hold up one finger for each sound. Ask which of the letters makes the first sound, and cross each letter out when it is used. Then have the child read the word they wrote.

blocks.title: Family Words: Trace and Write
blocks.instruction: Find the person with the same number on the tree, trace their family word and write it again on the line.

script.say: "This page shows a family. Each person on the family tree has a number. Find the person with the same number, trace the family word, and write it again on the line."
script.first: Look at the family tree together. The child with the star is the one the words are about. Read the family words on the page aloud. Do number 1 together: find the person with the 1 on the tree, find the word with the 1, trace it, and write it again on line 1.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the number next to the word and find the same number on the tree. Read the word for the child. If a child says their own family does not look like this one, say, "Every family is different. This page is about this child's family."

blocks.title: Number Bonds to 10
blocks.instruction: Look at each number bond. Write the missing number in the dashed circle.

script.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
script.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
script.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

blocks.title: Count the Array
blocks.instruction: Count all the pictures. Write how many there are in all.

script.say: "The pictures in each box stand in rows. Count all of them. Then write how many there are in all."
script.first: Count the first box aloud together, one row at a time, touching each picture as the class counts. Ask, "So how many are there in all?" Write the number on the board. Then write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board and leave them there for children who need to copy them.
script.stuck: Have the child cross out each shape while counting it, so that none is counted twice. If the child does not know how to write the number, point to it on the board.

blocks.title: Complete the Pattern
blocks.instruction: A picture is missing. Circle what belongs in the empty box.

script.say: "Each row is a pattern, but one picture is missing. Find the empty box. Circle the picture that belongs in it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each shape and have the class say its name like a chant. Stop at the empty box and ask, "What goes here?" Say the pattern again with that shape and circle it among the choices at the end of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Summer and Winter Clothes
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each item of clothing to the right group.

script.say: "At the top are clothes. At the bottom are two boxes: Summer and Winter. Draw a line from each piece of clothing to the season we wear it in."
script.first: Read the two boxes aloud and name every piece of clothing together. Do the first one together: ask, "Do we wear this when it is hot or when it is cold?" Draw the line to its box.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Would you wear this to the beach or in the snow?" Where you live, winter may not mean snow; let the child explain.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 22
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 22
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 22 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Find the Different Size
blocks.instruction: Look at each row. Circle the one that is a different size.

script.say: "In each row, the pictures are the same, but one is a different size. Find it and circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to the pictures one by one: "Same size… same size… this one is smaller!" Circle it together.
script.stuck: Have the child point to two pictures at a time and ask, "Are they the same size?"

blocks.title: Fix the First Letter
blocks.instruction: Circle the sentence that starts with a capital letter. Then write that capital letter in the box.

script.say: "Each box has the same sentence two times. One starts with a capital letter, and one does not. Circle the sentence that starts the right way. Then write that capital letter in the box."
script.first: Read the two sentences of the first box aloud while you point to them. Ask, "Which one starts with a big letter, a capital?" Circle it together and copy the capital letter into the box. Remind the children that every sentence starts with a capital letter.
script.stuck: Cover all but the first letter of each sentence with your finger and ask, "Which one is the big letter?" A child who is not sure may look for the same letter on the classroom alphabet.

blocks.title: Sort by Beginning Sound
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the letter it begins with.

script.say: "At the bottom are three boxes, each with a letter. Say the name of each picture and listen for its first sound. Draw a line from the picture to the letter it begins with."
script.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: bed, sock, bat, car, cup, sun, cake, bus, spoon. Do the first one together: "bed. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to B. For your own reference: B: bed, bat, bus; C: car, cup, cake; S: sock, sun, spoon.
script.stuck: Say the word and stretch the first sound. Then say the sound of each letter on the boxes and ask which one matches.

blocks.title: My Favorite Things: Circle and Write
blocks.instruction: In each row, circle your favorite picture and copy its word onto the line.

script.say: "In each row there are pictures of different things. Circle the one you like best. Then copy its word on the line."
script.first: Do the first row together: name the pictures, ask a few children which one they like best, and show how to circle one. Then show how to copy its word onto the line, letter by letter. Everyone circles their own favorite; there is no right answer.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger under the word and copy one letter at a time, moving the finger along. If the child cannot choose, say, "Pick the one you would like to have today."

blocks.title: Take Away on the Ten-Frame
blocks.instruction: Count the dots. The crossed-out dots are taken away. Write how many are left.

script.say: "Count the dots in each ten-frame. Some dots are crossed out: they are taken away. Write how many are left."
script.first: Do the first one together: count all the dots, then count the crossed-out ones. Read the number sentence aloud: "Ten take away one." Count the dots that are not crossed out and write the number after the equals sign.
script.stuck: Have the child cover each crossed-out dot with a finger and count only the dots that can still be seen.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot 1 to 20
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Connect the dots in number order to finish the picture.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 1. Draw a line to 2, then to 3, and keep counting until you get to 20."
script.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Find the orange dot together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 1?" Find 2 and draw the first line together. The numbers 1 to 20 are printed at the bottom of the page to help.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and count one more; that is the number to look for. Point to the part of the page where the next dot is. If a line went to the wrong dot, leave it and go on from the right one.

blocks.title: Paddle the Kayak to the Cabin
blocks.instruction: Help the boat sail along the stream to the teddy bear on the dock. Draw a line through the water.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Draw a line along the blue water from the start to the goal, and stay inside the water."
script.first: Hold up the page, read its title aloud, and show where the water starts, at the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the water with your finger and stop at each place where it splits: "Which way leads to the goal?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Fruits and Vegetables
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each food to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes, Fruits and Vegetables. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Is this a fruit or a vegetable?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. If a food can be called both, either box is right when the child can say why.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 23
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 23
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 23 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Trace the Number 1
blocks.instruction: Trace each number. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing numbers. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace each number in the row."
script.first: Write the first number of the page big on the board and say where it starts and which way it goes. Have the children write it in the air with you. They trace the number on the page and then write their own.
script.stuck: Show the child where the number starts and guide the first stroke with your finger on the page. A number written backward is common at this age; show the right way once and move on.

blocks.title: A Period or a Question Mark?
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence. Does it tell or ask? Write a period or a question mark in the box.

script.say: "Some sentences tell us something. Some sentences ask us something. A telling sentence ends with a period. An asking sentence ends with a question mark. Write the right mark in each box."
script.first: Draw a period and a question mark on the board. Read the first sentence aloud: "The car is green." Ask, "Does it tell or ask?" It tells, so write a period. Read every sentence aloud to the class and let them decide before they write.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask, "Could you answer it with yes or no?" If you can, it asks, and it gets a question mark.

blocks.title: Rhyme or Not?
blocks.instruction: Say both pictures out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X.

script.say: "In each box there are two pictures. Say both names out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X."
script.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name the pictures together, two by two: bat and cat, moose and deer, cap and map, snail and nail, train and balloon, nest and swing, bed and rake, pear and chair. Do the first box together and circle the check mark or the X. For your own reference, these rhyme: bat and cat, cap and map, snail and nail, pear and chair; the other four do not.
script.stuck: Say the two words one after the other and stretch their endings. If the endings sound the same, they rhyme.

blocks.title: Trace and Write the Words
blocks.instruction: Say the picture word. Trace the dashed letters, then write the word yourself on the empty lines.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Its word is written next to it. Trace the dashed letters, then write the word yourself on the empty lines."
script.first: Name the pictures together and read each word aloud. Do the first word together: read it, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more on the board, saying each letter.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: Number Bonds Within 10
blocks.instruction: Look at each number bond. Write the missing number in the dashed circle.

script.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
script.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
script.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

blocks.title: Same Number?
blocks.instruction: Count each group and write how many. Do both groups have the same number? Circle ✓ for yes or ✗ for no.

script.say: "In each box there are two groups. Count each group and write how many. Then circle the check mark if the two groups have the same number, or the X if they do not."
script.first: Do the first box together: count the top group aloud, touching each picture, and write the number. Count the bottom group the same way. Ask, "Are the numbers the same?" Circle the check mark or the X. Tell the children that a group that is spread out can still have the same number as a group that is close together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a small dot on each picture while counting it, so that none is counted twice. Then compare the two numbers on the page: "Are they the same number?"

blocks.title: Picture Pairs: Find the Difference
blocks.instruction: Each row shows the same close-up twice; circle the one place that is different in the right picture and check the box of that row.

script.say: "Each row shows the same picture two times, but one place in the right picture is different. Circle it, and check the box of that row."
script.first: Do the first row together: compare the left and the right picture, part by part, and find the one difference. Circle it in the right picture and check the box of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child cover half of each picture with a hand and compare one half at a time.

blocks.title: Animal Babies
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each grown-up animal to its baby.

script.say: "On the left are grown-up animals. On the right are their babies, but they are mixed up. Draw a line from each grown-up animal to its own baby."
script.first: Name the grown-up animals together, then the babies. Do the first one together: point to the first grown-up animal and ask, "Which baby belongs to it? How do you know?" Draw the line from dot to dot. Some babies look very different from their parents, like a caterpillar and a butterfly.
script.stuck: Point to one baby and ask what kind of animal it will be when it grows up. If the child does not know, say what the baby is called: a calf is a baby cow, a foal is a baby horse, a chick is a baby hen.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 24
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 24
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 24 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Advanced Pencil Paths
blocks.instruction: Trace each line with your pencil. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrow.

script.say: "Today your pencil goes for a walk. Each line starts at an orange dot. Follow the arrow and stay on the line as well as you can."
script.first: Hold up the page and trace the first line with your finger, from the orange dot in the direction of the arrow. Have the children trace it in the air with a finger, then on the page with a finger, and only then with a pencil. Remind them to go slowly: this is not a race.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: Choose the Position Word
blocks.instruction: Look at each picture. Circle the word that fits in the sentence.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Where is the small picture? Circle the word that fits in the sentence."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud with a hum for the gap: "The apple is hmm the circle." Read the three words below it. Ask, "Where is the apple?" Read the sentence with each word and circle the one that is true.
script.stuck: Have the child show the place word with a pencil and a book: "Put the pencil under the book. Now next to it." Then look at the picture again.

blocks.title: Missing Sound
blocks.instruction: Write the missing letter to finish each word.

script.say: "Each word on this page has a gap in the middle: one letter is missing. Say the picture's name, listen for the sound in the middle, and write its letter."
script.first: Name all the pictures together: lid, bed, dog, bus, fan, fox, fig, bun (the bread). Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly, point to each letter as you say its sound, and stop at the empty space. Ask, "Which sound belongs here? Which letter makes it?" Write it in and read the word together.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and stretch the sound in the middle: "p-iii-g." The missing letter is always one of the vowels: a, e, i, o, or u. Write the five vowels on the board for the child to choose from.

blocks.title: Family Words: Trace and Write
blocks.instruction: Find the person with the same number on the tree, trace their family word and write it again on the line.

script.say: "This page shows a family. Each person on the family tree has a number. Find the person with the same number, trace the family word, and write it again on the line."
script.first: Look at the family tree together. The child with the star is the one the words are about. Read the family words on the page aloud. Do number 1 together: find the person with the 1 on the tree, find the word with the 1, trace it, and write it again on line 1.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the number next to the word and find the same number on the tree. Read the word for the child. If a child says their own family does not look like this one, say, "Every family is different. This page is about this child's family."

blocks.title: 2D Shapes
blocks.instruction: Look at each shape, even the turned and skinny ones, and circle its name.

script.say: "Look at each shape. It may be turned or skinny, but it is still the same shape. Circle its name."
script.first: Draw a circle, a triangle, a square, and a rectangle on the board and name them. Do the first shape together: count its sides and read the three names next to it. Circle the right one.
script.stuck: Have the child count the sides with a finger: 3 sides is a triangle; 4 sides of the same length is a square; 4 sides, two long and two short, is a rectangle; round with no sides is a circle.

blocks.title: Color the Greater Number
blocks.instruction: Look at the two numbers in each box. Color the greater number.

script.say: "Each box has two numbers. Which number is greater, which one means more? Color the greater number."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 20 on the board. Do the first box together: find both numbers on the board and ask, "Which one comes later when we count?" That one is greater. Color it.
script.stuck: Have the child count aloud from one and stop at the first of the two numbers that comes up; the other number is the greater one.

blocks.title: Big and Small Patterns
blocks.instruction: Look at the pattern. Circle what comes next.

script.say: "A pattern is something that repeats, over and over. Say the pattern out loud. Then circle what comes next."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each picture and say "big" or "small" like a chant: "big, small, big, small…" Stop at the box with the question mark and ask, "What comes next: a big one or a small one?" Circle it among the choices.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Farm and Wild Animals
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes for two kinds of animals. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the two boxes aloud, Farm Animals and Wild Animals, and name every animal together. Do the first one together: ask, "Does this animal live on a farm, or in the wild?" Draw the line from the dot under it to its box.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 25
