packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 25
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 25 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count On from Any Number
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. The strips on this page start at big numbers. Read the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Fix the First Letter
blocks.instruction: Circle the sentence that starts with a capital letter. Then write that capital letter in the box.

script.say: "Each box has the same sentence two times. One starts with a capital letter, and one does not. Circle the sentence that starts the right way. Then write that capital letter in the box."
script.first: Read the two sentences of the first box aloud while you point to them. Ask, "Which one starts with a big letter, a capital?" Circle it together and copy the capital letter into the box. Remind the children that every sentence starts with a capital letter.
script.stuck: Cover all but the first letter of each sentence with your finger and ask, "Which one is the big letter?" A child who is not sure may look for the same letter on the classroom alphabet.

blocks.title: Sort by Beginning Sound
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the letter it begins with.

script.say: "At the bottom are three boxes, each with a letter. Say the name of each picture and listen for its first sound. Draw a line from the picture to the letter it begins with."
script.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: seal, bag, sock, bee, cup, cake, car, bus, sink. Do the first one together: "seal. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to S. For your own reference: B: bag, bee, bus; C: cup, cake, car; S: seal, sock, sink.
script.stuck: Say the word and stretch the first sound. Then say the sound of each letter on the boxes and ask which one matches.

blocks.title: Trace the Letter N n
blocks.instruction: Trace each letter, then write one on your own at the end of the line. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows.

script.say: "Now we practice writing letters. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrows. Trace the letters first. Then write one all by yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Write the first letter of the page big on the board, saying where you start and which way you go. Have the children write it in the air with you. Then they trace the letters on the page. Walk around and watch where each child starts.
script.stuck: Put your finger on the orange dot: "Start here. Which way does the arrow point?" If the letter the child writes alone is far from the model, have the child trace one more and try again. Do not ask for a perfect letter.

blocks.title: Teen Numbers on Two Ten-Frames
blocks.instruction: Count what is in the two ten-frames. Write the number, then finish the number sentence.

script.say: "A teen number is ten and some more. One ten-frame holds ten. Count what is in the two ten-frames and write the number. Then finish the number sentence: ten plus how many more."
script.first: Do the first one together: point to the full ten-frame and say, "That is ten." Count on with the second frame: "eleven, twelve…" Write the number. Then read the sentence: "Twelve equals ten plus…" and write how many are in the second frame.
script.stuck: Have the child start at ten for the full frame and count on, touching each dot in the second frame.

blocks.title: Draw 2D Shapes on Dot Paper
blocks.instruction: Read the shape name and connect the dots to draw it. Start at the thick line if there is one.

script.say: "Each box names a shape. Connect the dots with your pencil to draw that shape. If there is a thick line in the box, start there."
script.first: Read the name in each box aloud and draw that shape on the board: a triangle has 3 sides, a square has 4 sides that are all the same length, a rectangle has 4 sides with two long and two short. Draw the first shape together on the dot paper, going from dot to dot with straight lines.
script.stuck: Have the child count the sides of the shape on the board and put a finger on the dots where the corners will go. Then draw one side at a time from corner to corner.

blocks.title: Help the Boy on the Bike Reach the Slide
blocks.instruction: Help the hedgehog get to the apple tree. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Find the way along the light path from the animal to its goal. Use your finger first, then your pencil."
script.first: Hold up the page and show where the path starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the beginning of the way with your finger and stop at the first place where the path splits: "Which way? Let's try one." Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Day and Night
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes, Day and Night. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Do we see this in the day or at night?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. Some things can be seen in the day and at night, like the moon; let the child choose and say why.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 26
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 26
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 26 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Find the Different Size
blocks.instruction: Look at each row. Circle the one that is a different size.

script.say: "In each row, the pictures are the same, but one is a different size. Find it and circle it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to the pictures one by one: "Same size… same size… this one is smaller!" Circle it together.
script.stuck: Have the child point to two pictures at a time and ask, "Are they the same size?"

blocks.title: Circle the Right Word: Four Pictures
blocks.instruction: Say each picture word, then circle the word that belongs with it.

script.say: "Under each picture are two little words: a and an. Say the name of the picture with a in front of it, then with an. Circle the one that sounds right."
script.first: Name the pictures together: cup, bed, umbrella, bottle. Do the first one together: "a cup, an cup. Which sounds right?" Circle a. Tell the children that an goes in front of words that start with a, e, i, o, or u. For your own reference: a cup, a bed, an umbrella, a bottle.
script.stuck: Say both choices for the child, slowly, and let the child hear which one is easier to say. Ask, "Does the word start with a, e, i, o, or u?"

blocks.title: Build the Word
blocks.instruction: Use the letters to build the word for each picture.

script.say: "Next to each picture are the letters of its word, but they are mixed up. Say the word, listen to its sounds, and write the letters in the right order."
script.first: Name all the pictures together: can, jet, cup, bun (the bread), lid, cat. Do the first word on the board: say the word slowly and ask, "What is the first sound? The next sound? The last sound?" Write a letter for each sound and read the word together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word slowly and hold up one finger for each sound. Ask which of the letters makes the first sound, and cross each letter out when it is used. Then have the child read the word they wrote.

blocks.title: Trace the Longer Words
blocks.instruction: These words are long. Trace each one, then write it yourself.

script.say: "These words are long. Read each word with me, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Name the pictures together and read each long word aloud, clapping its parts: "skate-board." Do the first word together: trace it with your finger and write it on the board, one part at a time.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: Tally Match
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each number to its tally marks.

script.say: "On the left are numbers. On the right are tally marks. Draw a line from each number to its tally marks."
script.first: Draw a bundle of five tally marks on the board. Count the first group of marks together and find its number on the left. Draw the line.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each mark and count. For a bundle with a line across, say "five" and count on from there: six, seven…

blocks.title: Blast Off! 10, 9, 8…
blocks.instruction: Count backward. Write each missing number.

script.say: "This is a countdown, like for a rocket: 10, 9, 8 and down to 1. Some numbers are missing. Write each missing number."
script.first: Count down from 10 to 1 together, with a quiet "blast off" at the end. Do the first strip together, pointing to each box, and say the number at each empty box.
script.stuck: Have the child say the countdown from 10 while touching each box; the number they say at an empty box is the one to write.

blocks.title: Growing Patterns
blocks.instruction: The pattern grows. Circle the group that comes next.

script.say: "These patterns grow: each box has one more than the box before. Count the boxes. Circle the group that comes next."
script.first: Do the first row together: count the pictures in each box aloud, "one, two, three." Ask, "So how many come next?" Count the groups at the end of the row and circle the one with four.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Things That Fly
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are labeled boxes. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Where does this go? Does it fly?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 27
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 27
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 27 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Down Lines, Slants and Crosses
blocks.instruction: Trace each line with your pencil. Start at the orange dot and follow the arrow.

script.say: "Today your pencil goes for a walk. Each line starts at an orange dot. Follow the arrow and stay on the line as well as you can."
script.first: Hold up the page and trace the first line with your finger, from the orange dot in the direction of the arrow. Have the children trace it in the air with a finger, then on the page with a finger, and only then with a pencil. Remind them to go slowly: this is not a race.
script.stuck: Check the grip: the pencil is pinched between the thumb and the pointer finger and rests on the middle finger. If a child starts at the wrong end, put your finger on the orange dot and say, "Start here." A wobbly line is fine; do not have the child erase.

blocks.title: Parts of the Body
blocks.instruction: Copy each word from the bank onto the line that points to that part of the body.

script.say: "Look at the picture. Each line points to a part of the body. The words are in the box at the top. Copy the right word onto each line."
script.first: Read the words in the box aloud and have the children touch that part of their own body for each one. Do the first line together: follow it with your finger to the part it points to, say its name, find the word in the box, and copy it onto the line letter by letter.
script.stuck: Have the child touch the part on their own body and say its name. Then find the word in the box together; the first letter helps: "Hand starts with h. Where is the word that starts with h?"

blocks.title: Rhyme or Not?
blocks.instruction: Say both pictures out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X.

script.say: "In each box there are two pictures. Say both names out loud. If the two words rhyme, circle the check mark. If they do not rhyme, circle the X."
script.first: Say "cat, hat" and "cat, dog" and ask which pair rhymes. Name the pictures together, two by two: nest and vest, can and coat, lock and elf, glass and truck, jeep and sheep, bat and hat, map and cap, log and sled. Do the first box together and circle the check mark or the X. For your own reference, these rhyme: nest and vest, jeep and sheep, bat and hat, map and cap; the other four do not.
script.stuck: Say the two words one after the other and stretch their endings. If the endings sound the same, they rhyme.

blocks.title: I Can: Check What You Can Do
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and check the things you can do. Then write one thing you want to learn.

script.say: "This page is about what YOU can do. Listen to each sentence. If you can do it, put a check in its box. At the bottom, write one thing you want to learn."
script.first: Read each sentence aloud while the children point to it: "I can paint a picture. I can brush my teeth…" After each one, pause so that every child can check the box or leave it empty. Tell them there is no wrong answer. For the last line, write "I want to learn to" on the board and let children say their ideas first.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask the child, "Can you do that?" For the last line, a child may draw the thing and write the first letter or one word with your help.

blocks.title: Draw the Number on Two Ten-Frames
blocks.instruction: Read the number. Draw that many dots in the two ten-frames. Fill the first ten-frame before you start the second.

script.say: "Read the number in each row. Draw that many dots in the two ten-frames. Fill the first ten-frame all the way before you start the second one."
script.first: Do the first one together: read the number, for example 13. Fill the first ten-frame with ten dots while counting aloud, then count on in the second frame: "eleven, twelve, thirteen." Stop when you reach the number.
script.stuck: Have the child fill the first frame and say "ten", then draw one dot at a time in the second frame while counting on.

blocks.title: Count On from the Box
blocks.instruction: The number on the box tells how many are hidden inside. Start at that number and count on. Write how many there are in all.

script.say: "The number on each box tells how many are hidden inside. Start at that number and count on, one more for each picture next to the box. Write how many there are in all."
script.first: Do the first one together: put your hand on the box and say its number. Then touch each picture and count on aloud: "Six… seven." Write the number in the empty box. Tell the children not to count the box from one: they start at its number.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number on the box and then tap each picture while saying the next number. If the child starts again at one, say the box number together and go on from there.

blocks.title: Match the Shadow
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to its shadow.

script.say: "Each picture on the left has a shadow on the right. A shadow is dark and shows only the shape. Draw a line from each picture to its shadow."
script.first: Do the first one together: look at the outline of the first picture and ask, "Which shadow has the same shape?" Draw the line from dot to dot. Tell the children to look at the edges: the ears, the wheels, the tail.
script.stuck: Have the child trace the outside of the picture with a finger, then trace the shadows until one has the same shape.

blocks.title: Natural and Man-made
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are two boxes, Natural and Man-made. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Did people make this, or is it found in nature?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? Where?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Kindergarten Sub Plans: Week 28
packs.metaTitle: Kindergarten Emergency Sub Plans: Week 28
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 28 of kindergarten: 8 review blocks in letters and sounds, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count On from Any Number
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. The strips on this page start at big numbers. Read the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Story Sequencing: Number the Pictures
blocks.instruction: Look at what changes in each story, then write the numbers in the boxes to put the pictures in order.

script.say: "Each row shows a little story in four pictures, but the pictures are out of order. Look at what changes. Write 1 under what happens first, then 2, 3, and 4."
script.first: Do the first story together. Ask a child to say what is happening in each picture. Ask, "Which one happens first? How do you know?" Write a 1 in the box under it, then find 2, 3, and 4 together. Have a child tell the whole story in order.
script.stuck: Ask the child to find the picture where the story starts, where nothing has happened yet. Then ask, "What happens after that?" Have the child tell the story aloud; if it makes sense, the order is right.

blocks.title: Sort by Beginning Sound
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the letter it begins with.

script.say: "At the bottom are three boxes, each with a letter. Say the name of each picture and listen for its first sound. Draw a line from the picture to the letter it begins with."
script.first: Read the letters on the boxes aloud, B, C, and S, and say their sounds. Name the pictures together: cake, cow, sink, bat, bee, bed, cat, sock, salt (the salt shaker). Do the first one together: "cake. What is the first sound?" Draw a line to C. For your own reference: B: bat, bee, bed; C: cake, cow, cat; S: sink, sock, salt.
script.stuck: Say the word and stretch the first sound. Then say the sound of each letter on the boxes and ask which one matches.

blocks.title: Singular and Plural
blocks.instruction: Read the word for one. Then trace the word for many and write it yourself on the empty line.

script.say: "The word for one is written for you. Read it with me. Then trace the word for many, and write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Read the first word aloud and show one finger. Then show two fingers and say the word for many. Point to the s at the end: "We add s when there is more than one." Trace the word for many together. Read each word on the page aloud with the class before they trace.
script.stuck: Read the word for one and the word for many for the child and have the child point to the part that is different. Then trace one letter at a time.

blocks.title: Long and Short
blocks.instruction: Circle the LONGEST one in each row.

script.say: "In each row, some shapes are long and some are short. Look at all of them. Then circle the LONGEST one."
script.first: Do the first row together. Move your finger from one end of each shape to the other and ask, "Is this the longest? Is there a longer one?" Circle the longest together. Remind the children to look at every shape in the row before they circle.
script.stuck: Have the child point to two pictures at a time and say which of the two is bigger, keeping a finger on the winner, until the row is done. The picture under the finger at the end gets the circle.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot 11 to 20
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Connect the dots from 11 to 20 to finish the picture.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 11. Draw a line to 12, then to 13, and keep counting until you get to 20."
script.first: Count from 11 to 20 aloud together. Find the orange dot, number 11, together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 11?" Find 12 and draw the first line together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and count one more; that is the number to look for. Point to the part of the page where the next dot is. If a line went to the wrong dot, leave it and go on from the right one.

blocks.title: What Is Missing?
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 empty places in the bottom picture where something from the top picture is missing, and check a box for each.

script.say: "The two pictures are the same, but three things are missing from the bottom picture. Find each empty place, circle it, and check a box for each one."
script.first: Hold up the page and compare the two pictures with the class, from the top down. Find one thing that is missing together and circle the empty place in the bottom picture. Check the first box.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the top picture and look for it in the bottom picture: "Is it there?" There are three missing things; the three boxes help them count.

blocks.title: Hot Places, Cold Places
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each thing to the place where people would use it.

script.say: "One big picture is a snowy, cold place and the other is a hot beach. Draw a line from each thing to the place where people would use it."
script.first: Name the two places together and ask what the weather is like in each. Do the first thing together: "Would people use this in the snow or at the beach? Why?"
script.stuck: Ask, "Would this keep you warm, or help you stay cool?" Things for cold, snowy days go with the snowy place; things for hot, sunny days go with the beach.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 1
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 1
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 1 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count On from Any Number
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. The strips on this page start at big numbers. Read the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Match Word to Picture
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each word to the picture it names.

script.say: "Read each word. Then draw a line from the word to its picture."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Name the pictures together: bus, can (a soup can), key, fig, fox, bun (the bread). Do the first word together and draw the line.
script.stuck: Have the child say the sound of each letter and then say the sounds faster. If that does not work, ask for the first sound only and look for the pictures that begin with it. Read the word for the child if they are still stuck.

blocks.title: Rhyming Words: Rhyme and Write
blocks.instruction: Say the first picture. Circle the picture that rhymes with it, then write its word on the line.

script.say: "Rhyming words sound the same at the end, like cat and hat. On this page you find the picture that rhymes, then you write its word."
script.first: Name the pictures of each row together, so that everyone uses the same words (they are below). Do the first row together: say the first picture with each of the others and ask which one rhymes. Circle it and write its word on the line. Spelling it the way it sounds is fine.
script.stuck: Say the first picture with each choice and stretch the endings. For your own reference, the rows are glass (grass, chair, rock), hat (mouse, van, cat), plate (sweater, gate, train), shelf (crane, drum, elf), shirt (skirt, cap, whale), cart (clock, heart, nail); the rhymes are grass, cat, gate, elf, skirt, heart.

blocks.title: Picture Words
blocks.instruction: Trace the picture. Say its name. Trace the word under it.

script.say: "These are words we see all the time. Read the word, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Do the first word together: read it, write it on the board, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more next to it. Tell the children to say the word each time they finish writing it.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: Domino Math
blocks.instruction: Count both sides of the domino. Write the sum.

script.say: "Each domino has dots on two sides. Count the dots on both sides and write how many there are altogether. That number is called the sum."
script.first: Draw the first domino on the board. Count the dots on the left side, then keep counting on the right side. Write the two numbers and the sum. Show the children how to start with the bigger side and count on from it.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each dot while counting. If the child counts one side, starts over at one for the other side, and writes that second number, count across both sides with them once without stopping.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot 1 to 20
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Connect the dots in number order to finish the picture.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 1. Draw a line to 2, then to 3, and keep counting until you get to 20."
script.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Find the orange dot together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 1?" Find 2 and draw the first line together. The numbers 1 to 20 are printed at the bottom of the page to help.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and count one more; that is the number to look for. Point to the part of the page where the next dot is. If a line went to the wrong dot, leave it and go on from the right one.

blocks.title: Help the Rabbit Find the Cabbage
blocks.instruction: Look at the whole maze first. Then draw the orangutan's way to the banana tree.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 2
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 2
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 2 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Bonds to 10
blocks.instruction: Look at each number bond. Write the missing number in the dashed circle.

script.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
script.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
script.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

blocks.title: Word Family Carpet: Read and Color
blocks.instruction: Read every word on the carpet out loud. Then find each picture's word on the carpet and color that word in the picture's color.

script.say: "The carpet at the top has rows of words. Each row is a word family: the words end the same. Read every word out loud. Then find each picture's word on the carpet and color it."
script.first: Read the carpet aloud together, one row at a time. Name the pictures together: log, fan, jug, cat, can, clock. Find the first picture's word together and color it.
script.stuck: Have the child name the picture and say its first sound, then look for the word that begins with that letter. If two words begin the same way, have the child read both to the end.

blocks.title: Sound Strip: How Many Sounds?
blocks.instruction: Say the word slowly. Write one sound in each box, starting from the left. Leave the boxes you do not need empty.

script.say: "Say the word for each picture slowly, like a turtle. Write one sound in each box, starting on the left. If the word has fewer sounds than boxes, leave the last boxes empty."
script.first: Name the pictures together: swan, jet, rocket, duck, seagull, balloon. Do "jet" on the board: say j-e-t, one finger for each sound, and write one sound in each box. Leave the boxes you do not need empty. Some sounds take two letters, like ck in duck.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word slowly and push a finger forward for each sound. Two letters that make one sound, such as sh, go in one box together. A child who fills every box, whether the word needs them all or not, is spelling letter by letter and not listening for sounds; say the word together again and tap one box for each sound.

blocks.title: I Can: Check What You Can Do
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and check the things you can do. Then write one thing you want to learn.

script.say: "This page is about what YOU can do. Listen to each sentence. If you can do it, put a check in its box. At the bottom, write one thing you want to learn."
script.first: Read each sentence aloud while the children point to it: "I can paint a picture. I can brush my teeth…" After each one, pause so that every child can check the box or leave it empty. Tell them there is no wrong answer. For the last line, write "I want to learn to" on the board and let children say their ideas first.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask the child, "Can you do that?" For the last line, a child may draw the thing and write the first letter or one word with your help.

blocks.title: Picture Subtraction
blocks.instruction: Some pictures are crossed out. Write how many are left.

script.say: "In each box, some pictures are crossed out. They are gone. Count the pictures that are left and write that number."
script.first: Do the first box together: count all the pictures, then count the crossed-out ones. Read the number sentence aloud. Count the pictures that are not crossed out and write the number after the equals sign.
script.stuck: Have the child circle each picture that is not crossed out while counting it. If the child counts every picture, cover the crossed-out ones with a finger.

blocks.title: Count On!
blocks.instruction: Start at the dot. Hop forward and write where you land.

script.say: "Each number line has a dot where you start, and little arcs that show the hops. Count the hops forward from the dot, and write the number where the last hop lands."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Put your finger on the starting dot and say its number. Follow the arcs one at a time and count on aloud: "fifteen… sixteen, seventeen, eighteen." Write the number where the last arc lands. Point out that the line is numbered by twos: each small mark between two numbers is the number in between.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dot, say its number, and move one mark for each arc while counting on. If the child cannot tell which number the dot is on, count the marks from the last printed number together.

blocks.title: Complete the Pattern
blocks.instruction: A picture is missing. Circle what belongs in the empty box.

script.say: "Each row is a pattern, but one picture is missing. Find the empty box. Circle the picture that belongs in it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each shape and have the class say its name like a chant. Stop at the empty box and ask, "What goes here?" Say the pattern again with that shape and circle it among the choices at the end of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: How Do You Feel? Circle the Face
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture, think how you would feel, and circle the face that matches.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Think about how it would make you feel. Then circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Look at the first picture together and ask what it shows. Ask, "How does that make you feel?" Let two or three children answer; they may not all feel the same, and that is fine. Each child circles the face that matches their own answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child what the picture shows and when they have seen one. Then point to each face and name the feeling it shows. There is no wrong answer on this page; any face the child can explain is right.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 3
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 3
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 3 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Missing Number Problems to 10
blocks.instruction: Work out the missing number in your head. Write it in the box.

script.say: "In each problem one number is missing. Work out the missing number in your head and write it in the box."
script.first: Write 6 + __ = 10 on the board. Ask, "Six and how many more make ten?" Count on from 6 with fingers to 10: four. Write 4. Then do one with take away: 8 − __ = 5.
script.stuck: Have the child say the problem aloud with a hum for the box. Count on or back with fingers from the first number to the answer, and count the fingers.

blocks.title: Match Word to Picture
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each word to the picture it names.

script.say: "Read each word. Then draw a line from the word to its picture."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Name the pictures together: bag, dog, fan, bun (the bread), egg, key. Do the first word together and draw the line.
script.stuck: Have the child say the sound of each letter and then say the sounds faster. If that does not work, ask for the first sound only and look for the pictures that begin with it. Read the word for the child if they are still stuck.

blocks.title: Sort the Rhymes
blocks.instruction: Say each picture in the bank. Find the big picture it rhymes with and write its word on a line under that picture.

script.say: "Rhyming words sound the same at the end, like cat and hat. At the top of the page are small pictures. Say each one, find the big picture it rhymes with, and write its word on a line under that big picture."
script.first: Name the big pictures and the small pictures in the bank together, so that everyone uses the same words (they are below). Take the first small picture: say it with each big picture and ask which one rhymes. Write its word on a line under that big picture.
script.stuck: Say the small picture with each big picture and stretch the endings. For your own reference, the rhyming families are hat, bat, cat; balloon, spoon, raccoon; jar, star, guitar.

blocks.title: Write the Word: The First Letter Is Given
blocks.instruction: Say the name of each picture. Find the word in the word bank and finish it after the first letter.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Find its word in the word bank. The first letter is already there; you write the rest of the word."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together: bread, cheese, donut, fish, pizza, taco. Name the pictures together. Do the first one together on the board: find its word in the bank and finish it after the first letter.
script.stuck: Have the child say the picture word and listen for its first sound, then look in the word bank for a word that starts with the letter that is already written. Read the words in the word bank for a child who cannot read them.

blocks.title: Fact Family Houses
blocks.instruction: Use the three numbers on the roof. Complete the four related facts.

script.say: "The three numbers on the roof are a family. They make four facts: two adding and two taking away. Use the three numbers to finish all four facts in each house."
script.first: Draw a house on the board with 3, 7, and 10 on the roof. Write the four facts together: 3 + 7 = 10, 7 + 3 = 10, 10 − 3 = 7, 10 − 7 = 3. Point out that the biggest number is the whole: it comes after the equals sign when we add and first when we take away.
script.stuck: Have the child find the biggest number on the roof and circle it: that is the whole. The other two are the parts. Adding the parts makes the whole; taking a part away from the whole leaves the other part.

blocks.title: Teen Numbers on Two Ten-Frames
blocks.instruction: Count what is in the two ten-frames. Write the number, then finish the number sentence.

script.say: "A teen number is ten and some more. One ten-frame holds ten. Count what is in the two ten-frames and write the number. Then finish the number sentence: ten plus how many more."
script.first: Do the first one together: point to the full ten-frame and say, "That is ten." Count on with the second frame: "eleven, twelve…" Write the number. Then read the sentence: "Twelve equals ten plus…" and write how many are in the second frame.
script.stuck: Have the child start at ten for the full frame and count on, touching each dot in the second frame.

blocks.title: Help the Hedgehog Reach the Apple Tree
blocks.instruction: Help the hedgehog get to the apple tree. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Find the way along the light path from the animal to its goal. Use your finger first, then your pencil."
script.first: Hold up the page and show where the path starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the beginning of the way with your finger and stop at the first place where the path splits: "Which way? Let's try one." Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Sort by Food Group
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each food to its food group.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Fruits, Vegetables, Grains, and Protein. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Is this a fruit, a vegetable, a grain like bread or pasta, or a protein like eggs, meat, or fish?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. If a food fits two groups, either box is right when the child can say why.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 4
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 4
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 4 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Mental Math to 10
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: adding and taking away with numbers up to 10. Do the ones you know first. If you need your fingers for the others, that is fine."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board. Ask how the children got their answers and accept every way that gives the right answer: fingers, counting on, or just knowing it.
script.stuck: Let the child use fingers or draw dots; that is fine even where the page says to solve the problems in your head. Read a problem with an empty box as a question, for example: "Four plus what number makes nine?"

blocks.title: Read Digraph Words and Match the Pictures
blocks.instruction: Read each word. The letter team is marked. Draw a line to the picture the word names.

script.say: "Read each word. Its letter team is marked. Draw a line from the word to the picture it names."
script.first: Write sh, ch, and th on the board and say each sound with the class. Read the first word together, sound by sound, and find its picture. Tell the children to read the letter team as one sound.
script.stuck: Cover the word with a finger and uncover it a part at a time: "ben… ch… bench." Then find the picture together.

blocks.title: Sound Strip: How Many Sounds?
blocks.instruction: Say the word slowly. Write one sound in each box, starting from the left. Leave the boxes you do not need empty.

script.say: "Say the word for each picture slowly, like a turtle. Write one sound in each box, starting on the left. If the word has fewer sounds than boxes, leave the last boxes empty."
script.first: Name the pictures together: boat, swing, robot, scooter, rocket, train. Do "boat" on the board: say b-oa-t, one finger for each sound, and write one sound in each box: oa is one sound. Leave the boxes you do not need empty.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word slowly and push a finger forward for each sound. Two letters that make one sound, such as sh, go in one box together. A child who fills every box, whether the word needs them all or not, is spelling letter by letter and not listening for sounds; say the word together again and tap one box for each sound.

blocks.title: Picture Words
blocks.instruction: Trace the picture. Say its name. Trace the word under it.

script.say: "These are words we see all the time. Read the word, trace it, and then write it yourself on the empty line."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and have the class read each one after you. Do the first word together: read it, write it on the board, trace over it with your finger, and write it once more next to it. Tell the children to say the word each time they finish writing it.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and have the child say it back while pointing to it. For the writing, have the child copy one letter at a time and keep the letters close together.

blocks.title: Picture Addition
blocks.instruction: Count both groups. Write how many altogether.

script.say: "In each row there are two groups of pictures. Count both groups. Write how many there are altogether after the equals sign."
script.first: Do the first row together: count the first group, then keep counting into the second group. Write the number after the equals sign. Show the children how to start with the bigger group and count on.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each dot while counting. If the child counts one side, starts over at one for the other side, and writes that second number, count across both sides with them once without stopping.

blocks.title: Count Back!
blocks.instruction: Start at the dot. Hop backward and write where you land.

script.say: "Each number line has a dot where you start, and arcs that show the hops back. Count back one mark for each hop, and write the number where the last hop lands."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Put your finger on the starting dot and say its number. Follow the arcs back one at a time and count back aloud. Write where the last arc lands. Point out that the line is numbered by twos: each small mark between two numbers is the number in between.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dot, say its number, and move one mark for each arc while counting on. If the child cannot tell which number the dot is on, count the marks from the last printed number together.

blocks.title: What Is Missing?
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 empty places in the bottom picture where something from the top picture is missing, and check a box for each.

script.say: "The two pictures are the same, but three things are missing from the bottom picture. Find each empty place, circle it, and check a box for each one."
script.first: Hold up the page and compare the two pictures with the class, from the top down. Find one thing that is missing together and circle the empty place in the bottom picture. Check the first box.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the top picture and look for it in the bottom picture: "Is it there?" There are three missing things; the three boxes help them count.

blocks.title: Rules in Different Places
blocks.instruction: Read each rule. Draw a line from the rule to the place where it belongs.

script.say: "Each rule belongs to a place. Read each rule with me. Then draw a line from the rule to the place where it belongs."
script.first: Read the names of the places aloud and point to each picture. Do the first rule together: read it, ask, "Where do people need this rule?" and draw the line together. If your page also asks you to write a rule, say one together first: "We take turns on the slide so that everyone gets a turn."
script.stuck: Read the rule with the child and ask, "Where would someone say this to you?" Point to each place in turn and ask, "Here?" Then ask why the rule is there: to keep us safe, to let everyone hear, or to be fair.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 5
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 5
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 5 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Bonds Within 10
blocks.instruction: Look at each number bond. Write the missing number in the dashed circle.

script.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
script.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
script.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

blocks.title: Word Families with Blends
blocks.instruction: Read every word on the carpet out loud. Say each picture word, find it on the carpet, then write the two letters it starts with on the line.

script.say: "Read every word on the carpet out loud. Say each picture word, find it on the carpet, and write the two letters it starts with on the line."
script.first: Read the carpet aloud together. Name the pictures together: truck, drum, clock, swan, flag, frog. Do the first one together: find "truck" and write tr on the line.
script.stuck: Have the child name the picture and say its first sound, then look for the word that begins with that letter. If two words begin the same way, have the child read both to the end.

blocks.title: Sort by Syllables
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to its number of syllables.

script.say: "Words have beats, called syllables. Say the name of each picture and clap its beats. Draw a line to the box with that number: 1, 2, or 3."
script.first: Clap a few children's names together. Name the pictures together: acorn, sun, apron, airplane, dog, ambulance, cat, banana, astronaut. Clap the first word together and draw its line. For your own reference: 1 beat: sun, dog, cat; 2 beats: acorn, apron, airplane; 3 beats: ambulance, banana, astronaut.
script.stuck: Have the child put a hand under the chin and say the word at normal speed: the chin drops once for each syllable. If the child claps every sound, say the word together the way you would say it when talking.

blocks.title: Word Bank and Letter Boxes
blocks.instruction: Find the word in the bank. Write one letter in each box.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Find its word in the word bank, and write it in the letter boxes, one letter in each box."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together and name the pictures. Do the first one together: find the word, count its letters and the boxes, and write one letter in each box.
script.stuck: Have the child say the picture word and listen for its first sound, then look in the word bank for a word that starts with the letter that is already written. Read the words in the word bank for a child who cannot read them.

blocks.title: Doubles and Halves with Pictures to 20
blocks.instruction: Some cards ask for the double, others for the half. Write each answer in the box.

script.say: "A double is a number added to itself, like 4 + 4. A half is one of two equal parts. Some cards ask for the double, others for the half. Write each answer in the box."
script.first: Hold up 4 fingers on each hand: "4 and 4 is 8. Eight is the double of four." Then hold up 8 fingers and split them into two equal parts: "Half of 8 is 4." Read the word on the first card, double or half, and do it together.
script.stuck: For a double, have the child count the pictures and then count them again on from the first number. For a half, have the child share the pictures in two groups, one for you and one for the child, until none are left.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot 1 to 20
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Connect the dots in number order to finish the picture.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 1. Draw a line to 2, then to 3, and keep counting until you get to 20."
script.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Find the orange dot together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 1?" Find 2 and draw the first line together. The numbers 1 to 20 are printed at the bottom of the page to help.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and count one more; that is the number to look for. Point to the part of the page where the next dot is. If a line went to the wrong dot, leave it and go on from the right one.

blocks.title: Copy the Picture Using Letters and Numbers
blocks.instruction: Use the letter and number of each square to copy the picture.

script.say: "Use the letter and number of each square to copy the picture onto the empty grid."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Find one colored square together, say its letter and number, and color the same square on the empty grid. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Being a Good Citizen
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Circle what a good citizen does. Then circle the word that tells how.

script.say: "Each box tells a short story. Circle what a good citizen does. Then circle the word that tells how."
script.first: Read the words on the page aloud and say what each one means: honest, you tell the truth; kind, you are nice to others; fair, everyone gets a turn or a share; responsible, you do the job you said you would do. Read the first story and both choices aloud, then ask, "Which one is what a good citizen does?" Circle it together, then circle the word that tells how.
script.stuck: Read the story again and ask, "What did the child do: tell the truth, help someone, share, or do a job?" Then read the two words beside it and let the child choose. If the child has a good reason for the other word, say, "Yes, that is true too," and ask which word fits best.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 6
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 6
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 6 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Mental Math to 20
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: adding and taking away with numbers up to 20. Do the ones you know first. Then go back to the others."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board. Ask how the children got their answers and accept every way that gives the right answer: fingers, counting on, or just knowing it.
script.stuck: Let the child use fingers or draw dots; that is fine even where the page says to solve the problems in your head. Read a problem with an empty box as a question, for example: "Four plus what number makes nine?"

blocks.title: Read and Color
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence carefully. Then color exactly the pictures it tells you to.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read each sentence, then do exactly what it says."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud together, pointing to each word. Ask: "What does the sentence tell us to do?" Do it together. Then the children read the other sentences on their own.
script.stuck: Point to the word the child cannot read and say its first sound; if that is not enough, read the word. Then have the child read the whole sentence again and tell you what it asks for before starting.

blocks.title: Blends
blocks.instruction: Say the name of each picture. Write the two letters the word starts with.

script.say: "Each word starts with two letters that you can hear together, like s and l in sled. Say the name of each picture. Write the two letters it starts with."
script.first: Say "sled" slowly: "s-l-ed. Two sounds at the start: s and l." Name the pictures together: swan, train, sled, snail, spatula, stove, broom, flag. Do the first one together: "swan, s-w." Write sw. For your own reference: sw, tr, sl, sn, sp, st, br, fl.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and stretch the start: "ssslll-ed." Ask the child to say the first sound, then the second sound, and write both letters.

blocks.title: I Can: Check What You Can Do
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and check the things you can do. Then write one thing you want to learn.

script.say: "This page is about what YOU can do. Listen to each sentence. If you can do it, put a check in its box. At the bottom, write one thing you want to learn."
script.first: Read each sentence aloud while the children point to it: "I can paint a picture. I can brush my teeth…" After each one, pause so that every child can check the box or leave it empty. Tell them there is no wrong answer. For the last line, write "I want to learn to" on the board and let children say their ideas first.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask the child, "Can you do that?" For the last line, a child may draw the thing and write the first letter or one word with your help.

blocks.title: Fact Family Houses to 20
blocks.instruction: Use the three numbers on the roof. Complete the four related facts.

script.say: "The three numbers on the roof are a family. They make four facts: two adding and two taking away. Use the three numbers to finish all four facts in each house."
script.first: Draw a house on the board with 3, 7, and 10 on the roof. Write the four facts together: 3 + 7 = 10, 7 + 3 = 10, 10 − 3 = 7, 10 − 7 = 3. Point out that the biggest number is the whole: it comes after the equals sign when we add and first when we take away.
script.stuck: Have the child find the biggest number on the roof and circle it: that is the whole. The other two are the parts. Adding the parts makes the whole; taking a part away from the whole leaves the other part.

blocks.title: Hop Along the Line!
blocks.instruction: Start at the dot. Count the hops. Write the addition answer.

script.say: "Each number line shows a number sentence. Start at the dot, count the hops forward, and write the answer of the addition."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Read the number sentence aloud. Put your finger on the starting dot and follow the hops: "two… three, four, five." Write the answer. Point out that the line is numbered by twos: each small mark between two numbers is the number in between.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dot, say its number, and move one mark for each arc while counting on. If the child cannot tell which number the dot is on, count the marks from the last printed number together.

blocks.title: Help the Earthworm Reach the Leaf
blocks.instruction: Help the ant go down and up through the tunnels to the raspberry. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Leaders and Their Jobs
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each leader to what that leader leads. Then circle the leader who says each sentence.

script.say: "Draw a line from each leader to what that leader leads."
script.first: Say what each leader does: the principal leads a school, the mayor leads a town or a city, the governor leads a state, and the president leads our whole country. Name the pictures on the page together. Do the first line together. If your page asks "Who says it?", read each sentence aloud and let the children circle the leader.
script.stuck: Ask, "Who leads our school? Our town? Our state? Our whole country?" Go from the smallest place, the school, to the biggest, the whole country.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 7
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 7
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 7 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count On from Any Number
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. The strips on this page start at big numbers. Read the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Fill-in-the-Blank Sentences
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Find the word that fits the sentence in the word bank and write it in the box.

script.say: "Each sentence is missing a word. The words are in the word bank at the top, and each sentence has a picture. Find the word that fits and write it in the box."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together. Read the first sentence aloud and say "blank" at the gap. Look at its picture and ask, "Which word fits?" Write it in the box together.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with the child, one word at a time, and say "blank" at the gap. Look at the picture together and find its word in the bank.

blocks.title: Digraphs sh, ch and th: Which Letter Team Do You Hear?
blocks.instruction: Say the name of each picture. Circle the letter team you hear.

script.say: "Two letters can make one sound: sh, ch, and th. Say the name of each picture. Circle the letter team you hear in it."
script.first: Write sh, ch, and th on the board and say each sound with the class. Name the pictures together: mushroom, shrimp, chair, chocolate, jellyfish, thumb, bench, feather. Do the first one together: "mushroom: sh." Circle sh. For your own reference: sh: mushroom, shrimp, jellyfish; ch: chair, chocolate, bench; th: thumb, feather.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and stop at the letter team: "mu-sh-room." Then say sh, ch, and th and ask which one it sounds like.

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence: With Clues
blocks.instruction: Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line. The capital letter and the end mark show where it begins and ends.

script.say: "The words of each sentence are mixed up. The word with the capital letter comes first, and the word with the end mark comes last. Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: True or False?
blocks.instruction: Is each equation true? Circle the check mark if it is true and the X if it is false.

script.say: "Is each number sentence true? If both sides are the same amount, it is true: circle the check mark. If not, it is false: circle the X."
script.first: Write 10 − 2 = 8 on the board and ask, "Is ten take away two eight? Yes: true." Write 9 = 5 + 6 and ask, "Is five and six nine? No: false." Remind the children that the equals sign means "the same as" and can be on either side.
script.stuck: Have the child work out the side with the plus or minus sign and then compare it with the number on the other side.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot 1 to 20
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Connect the dots in number order to finish the picture.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 1. Draw a line to 2, then to 3, and keep counting until you get to 20."
script.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Find the orange dot together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 1?" Find 2 and draw the first line together. The numbers 1 to 20 are printed at the bottom of the page to help.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and count one more; that is the number to look for. Point to the part of the page where the next dot is. If a line went to the wrong dot, leave it and go on from the right one.

blocks.title: Growing Patterns
blocks.instruction: The pattern grows. Circle the group that comes next.

script.say: "These patterns grow: each box has one more than the box before. Count the boxes. Circle the group that comes next."
script.first: Do the first row together: count the pictures in each box aloud, "one, two, three." Ask, "So how many come next?" Count the groups at the end of the row and circle the one with four.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Family Generations: Oldest to Youngest
blocks.instruction: In each row, write 1, 2 and 3 in the boxes to put the family words in order from the oldest generation to the youngest.

script.say: "In each row there are family words. Write 1, 2, and 3 to put them in order, from the oldest generation to the youngest."
script.first: Talk about a family: grandparents are the oldest generation, then parents, aunts, and uncles, then children like brothers, sisters, and cousins. Read the first row aloud together and ask, "Who is the oldest?" Write 1 under that word, then 2 and 3.
script.stuck: Ask the child about each word: "Is that a grandparent, a parent, or a child?" Grandparents get 1, parents 2, children 3. Every family is different; this page is about the words.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 8
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 8
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 8 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Addition Practice to 20
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: adding with numbers up to 20. Do the ones you know first. Then go back to the others."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board. Ask how the children got their answers and accept every way that gives the right answer: counting on from the bigger number, making ten, or just knowing it.
script.stuck: Have the child start at the bigger number and count on the smaller one with fingers: for 13 + 6, say "13" and count on six more. Drawing dots is fine, too, even though the page says to solve the problems in your head.

blocks.title: Story Sequencing Sentences: Match the Pictures
blocks.instruction: Number each story's sentences in order in the boxes, then draw a line from every sentence to its picture.

script.say: "Each story on this page is told in four sentences, but the sentences are out of order. Read them. Number them 1 to 4 in the order things happen. Then draw a line from each sentence to its picture."
script.first: Read the four sentences of the first story aloud. Ask, "What happens first? How do you know?" Write 1 next to it, then 2, 3, and 4 together. Then draw a line from each sentence to its picture.
script.stuck: Read the sentences to the child and ask which one could be the beginning. Have the child tell the story aloud in the order of the numbers; if it makes sense, the order is right. The pictures help: look at what changes from one to the next.

blocks.title: Blends
blocks.instruction: Say the name of each picture. Write the two letters the word starts with.

script.say: "Each word starts with two letters that you can hear together, like s and l in sled. Say the name of each picture. Write the two letters it starts with."
script.first: Say "sled" slowly: "s-l-ed. Two sounds at the start: s and l." Name the pictures together: dress, snowflake, flamingo, swing, stool, glass, slide, spatula. Do the first one together: "dress, d-r." Write dr. For your own reference: dr, sn, fl, sw, st, gl, sl, sp.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and stretch the start: "ssslll-ed." Ask the child to say the first sound, then the second sound, and write both letters.

blocks.title: Fill In the Question Word
blocks.instruction: Read the answer and find the highlighted words. Write the question word from the bank in the box.

script.say: "Read each answer. Look at the highlighted words. Which question asks for them: who, what, where, when, or how many? Write that question word in the box."
script.first: Read the question words in the bank aloud. Read the first answer and its question aloud and look at the highlighted words. Ask, "Which question word asks for these words?" Write it in the box together. Do the rest of the page by reading each answer aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Ask the child: "Is the highlighted part a person? Then who. A thing? What. A place? Where. A time? When. A number? How many."

blocks.title: Number Walls
blocks.instruction: Each brick is the sum of the two bricks under it. Fill in the missing numbers.

script.say: "This is a number wall. Each brick is the sum of the two bricks right under it. Start at the bottom and build every wall to the top."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks that sit side by side in the bottom row and to the brick that rests on both of them: "Three plus two is five. Five goes on top." Fill in that wall together.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers with fingers or dots. If the child writes the sum next to the bricks and not above them, point to the brick that touches both.

blocks.title: Stories with Three Numbers
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Draw it in the box. Write the three numbers. Look for two numbers that make ten, then add.

script.say: "Each story has three numbers. Read the story, draw it in the box, and write the three numbers in the number sentence. Look for two numbers that make ten. Then write how many in all."
script.first: Read the first story aloud while the children follow. Ask, "What are the three numbers?" Write them on the board with plus signs. Draw quick circles for them. Look for two numbers that make ten together, add them first, then add the third.
script.stuck: Read the story with the child, one sentence at a time, and underline each number. Have the child draw circles for each number and count them all.

blocks.title: Help the Puppy Get to the Ball
blocks.instruction: Help the puppy get to the ball. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Help the animal get to its goal. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges."
script.first: Hold up the page, read its title aloud, and show where the road starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the road with your finger and stop at each place where it splits: "Which way leads to the goal?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Which Face Shows the Feeling?
blocks.instruction: Read the feeling word and circle the one face in the row that shows it.

script.say: "Each row has a feeling word and three faces. Circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Read every feeling word on the page aloud: tired, angry, happy, scared, surprised, sad. Make each face for the class. Do the first row together: read the word, look at the three faces, and circle the one that matches.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and make the face. Ask the child to point to the face on the page that looks like yours.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 9
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 9
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 9 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Bonds to 10
blocks.instruction: Look at each number bond. Write the missing number in the dashed circle.

script.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
script.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
script.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

blocks.title: Find the Answer in the Story
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then finish the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then finish the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: M or N? Hear the Difference
blocks.instruction: Say each picture. Circle the letter it begins with: m or n.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Does it begin with mmm or nnn? Circle m or n."
script.first: Say the sounds mmm and nnn together; feel the lips close for m. Name the pictures together: nest, necklace, moon, nose, medal, milk, nurse, mitten. Do the first one together: "nest. Does it start with mmm or nnn?" Circle n. For your own reference: n: nest, necklace, nose, nurse; m: moon, medal, milk, mitten.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word with a hand on the lips: for m the lips close, for n they stay open.

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence: No Clues
blocks.instruction: There is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line.

script.say: "The words of each sentence are mixed up, and there is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence with a capital letter and a period."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: True or False?
blocks.instruction: Is each equation true? Circle the check mark if it is true and the X if it is false.

script.say: "Is each number sentence true? If both sides are the same amount, it is true: circle the check mark. If not, it is false: circle the X."
script.first: Write 10 − 2 = 8 on the board and ask, "Is ten take away two eight? Yes: true." Write 9 = 5 + 6 and ask, "Is five and six nine? No: false." Remind the children that the equals sign means "the same as" and can be on either side.
script.stuck: Have the child work out the side with the plus or minus sign and then compare it with the number on the other side.

blocks.title: Odd and Even Numbers: Odd House, Even House
blocks.instruction: Write each number in the house where it belongs, the odd house or the even house. Three numbers have moved in already and show their pairs.

script.say: "Even numbers can be shared in pairs with none left over. Odd numbers always have one left over. Write each number in the house where it belongs: the odd house or the even house."
script.first: Count by twos together: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10: these are even. Write them on the board. The numbers in between, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, are odd. Tell the children that a number ending in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8 is even. Do the first number together.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the last digit of the number and check it against the list of even numbers on the board. For a small number, draw dots in pairs.

blocks.title: Picture Pairs: Find the Difference
