blocks.instruction: Each row shows the same close-up twice; circle the one place that is different in the right picture and check the box of that row.

script.say: "Each row shows the same picture two times, but one place in the right picture is different. Circle it, and check the box of that row."
script.first: Do the first row together: compare the left and the right picture, part by part, and find the one difference. Circle it in the right picture and check the box of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child cover half of each picture with a hand and compare one half at a time.

blocks.title: Sort by Food Group
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each food to its food group.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Fruits, Vegetables, Grains, and Protein. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Is this a fruit, a vegetable, a grain like bread or pasta, or a protein like eggs, meat, or fish?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. A tomato can be called a fruit or a vegetable; either box is right for it.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 10
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 10
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 10 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Missing Number Problems to 20
blocks.instruction: Work out the missing number in your head. Write it in the box.

script.say: "In each problem one number is missing. Work out the missing number in your head and write it in the box."
script.first: Write 6 + __ = 10 on the board. Ask, "Six and how many more make ten?" Count on from 6 with fingers to 10: four. Write 4. Then do one with take away: 8 − __ = 5.
script.stuck: Have the child say the problem aloud with a hum for the box. Count on or back with fingers from the first number to the answer, and count the fingers.

blocks.title: Characters, Setting, and Events
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write who is in it, where it takes place, and what happens.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write who is in it, where it takes place, and what happens."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Rhyme Strings
blocks.instruction: Say each picture. Find the two words in the bank that rhyme with it and write them on its lines. Some words fit nowhere.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Find the two words in the bank that rhyme with it and write them on its lines. Some words in the bank fit nowhere."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together and name the pictures: dog, car, hat, sock. Do the first picture together: "dog… which words in the bank sound like dog at the end?" Write them on its lines. For your own reference: dog: frog, log; car: guitar, star; hat: bat, cat; sock: lock, rock. Pool, sheep, nail, and plate fit nowhere.
script.stuck: Say the picture word and each word of the bank one after the other. If the endings sound the same, it rhymes.

blocks.title: Fill In the Question Word
blocks.instruction: Read the answer and find the highlighted words. Write the question word from the bank in the box.

script.say: "Read each answer. Look at the highlighted words. Which question asks for them: who, what, where, when, or how many? Write that question word in the box."
script.first: Read the question words in the bank aloud. Read the first answer and its question aloud and look at the highlighted words. Ask, "Which question word asks for these words?" Write it in the box together. Do the rest of the page by reading each answer aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Ask the child: "Is the highlighted part a person? Then who. A thing? What. A place? Where. A time? When. A number? How many."

blocks.title: Number Walls: Build Every Row
blocks.instruction: Add each pair of bricks next to each other and write the sum in the brick above them. Keep going up to the top.

script.say: "Add each pair of bricks next to each other and write the sum in the brick above them. Keep going up until the wall reaches the top."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks that sit side by side in the bottom row and to the brick that rests on both of them: "Three plus two is five. Five goes on top." Fill in that wall together.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers with fingers or dots. If the child writes the sum next to the bricks and not above them, point to the brick that touches both.

blocks.title: Picture Word Problems
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Use the pictures to help you. Write the answer in the box.

script.say: "Each problem on this page is a short story with numbers. I will read each story aloud. Listen, look at the picture, and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Read the first story aloud while the children follow with a finger. Ask, "What do we know? What do we need to find out?" Count the pictures together or count on, and write the answer in the box. Then read each story aloud for the class, one at a time.
script.stuck: Read the story to the child again and ask them to tell it back in their own words. Let them touch and count the pictures, or draw dots.

blocks.title: Help the Rabbit Pick Up Every Carrot
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

blocks.title: School and Play Long Ago and Today
blocks.instruction: Circle long ago or today for each picture and for each thing a child said.

script.say: "Look at each picture and read each sentence. Is it from long ago or today? Circle long ago or today."
script.first: Ask the class, "How did children go to school and play long ago, when your great-grandparents were little?" Read the words under the first picture aloud and ask, "Do children do that today?" Circle together. Read the sentences aloud for the children who need it. If the page asks which school the child would like, any answer with a reason is right.
script.stuck: Ask, "Have you seen one of these at school or at home?" Something children use today is today; something we see only in old pictures is long ago.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 11
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 11
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 11 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Subtraction Practice to 20
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: subtracting with numbers up to 20. Do the ones you know first. Then go back to the others."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board together and think aloud: "Nine take away five. I count back from nine: eight, seven, six, five, four." Then the children work on their own; tell them to skip a hard one and come back to it.
script.stuck: Have the child count up from the smaller number to the bigger one on fingers: for 17 minus 9, say "9" and count up to 17. Drawing dots and crossing them out is fine, too.

blocks.title: Retell the Story and Tell Its Lesson
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end. Use the word bank. Then circle the lesson.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, using the word bank. Then circle the lesson of the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Sound Strip: How Many Sounds?
blocks.instruction: Say the word slowly. Write one sound in each box, starting from the left. Leave the boxes you do not need empty.

script.say: "Say the word for each picture slowly, like a turtle. Write one sound in each box, starting on the left. If the word has fewer sounds than boxes, leave the last boxes empty."
script.first: Name the pictures together: fish, chair, sailboat, seagull, hat, bucket. Do "fish" on the board: say f-i-sh, one finger for each sound, and write one sound in each box: sh is one sound. Leave the boxes you do not need empty.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word slowly and push a finger forward for each sound. Two letters that make one sound, such as sh, go in one box together. A child who fills every box, whether the word needs them all or not, is spelling letter by letter and not listening for sounds; say the word together again and tap one box for each sound.

blocks.title: Write the Word: Every Clue
blocks.instruction: Write each word using the bank, the boxes and the first letter.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Use every clue to write its word: the word bank, the letter boxes, and the first letter."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together and name the pictures. Do the first one together: find the word in the bank, check its first letter, and write one letter in each box.
script.stuck: Have the child say the picture word and listen for its first sound, then look in the word bank for a word that starts with the letter that is already written. Read the words in the word bank for a child who cannot read them.

blocks.title: Domino Math
blocks.instruction: Count both sides of the domino. Write the sum.

script.say: "Each domino has dots on two sides. Count the dots on both sides and write how many there are altogether. That number is called the sum."
script.first: Draw the first domino on the board. Count the dots on the left side, then keep counting on the right side. Write the two numbers and the sum. Show the children how to start with the bigger side and count on from it.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each dot while counting. If the child counts one side, starts over at one for the other side, and writes that second number, count across both sides with them once without stopping.

blocks.title: Count On!
blocks.instruction: Start at the dot. Hop forward and write where you land.

script.say: "Each number line has a dot where you start, and little arcs that show the hops. Count the hops forward from the dot, and write the number where the last hop lands."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Put your finger on the starting dot and say its number. Follow the arcs one at a time and count on aloud: "fifteen… sixteen, seventeen, eighteen." Write the number where the last arc lands. Point out that the line is numbered by twos: each small mark between two numbers is the number in between.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dot, say its number, and move one mark for each arc while counting on. If the child cannot tell which number the dot is on, count the marks from the last printed number together.

blocks.title: Count Along with the Train to the Cabin
blocks.instruction: Help the train get to the cabin. At every fork, go to the next number from 1 to 20.

script.say: "Read the title with me: it tells you who is going where. At every fork, take the road to the next number when you count: 1, 2, 3, all the way to 20."
script.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Put your finger on the start and find 1. Ask, "What comes next? Which road goes to 2?" Draw the first part together. Tell the children to say each number as they reach it.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 12
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 12
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 12 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count On from Any Number
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. The strips on this page start at big numbers. Read the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Find the Answer in the Story
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then finish the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then finish the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Long or Short Vowel?
blocks.instruction: Say each word. Is the colored vowel sound long or short? Circle the line if it is long. Circle the curve if it is short.

script.say: "Say each word. Listen to the colored vowel. Does it say its name, like the a in rake? That is a long vowel: circle the line. Does it make its short sound, like the a in bag? Circle the curve."
script.first: Write rake and bag on the board and say both: "rake, a says its name: long. bag, a says /a/: short." Read the words on the page aloud together. Do the first one together and circle the line or the curve.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and hold the vowel. Then say the letter's name: if the word says the name, it is long. For your own reference: long: rake, nose, stove, slide; short: chick, bag, fish, nest.

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence
blocks.instruction: The words are mixed up. Put them in order and write the sentence on the line with a capital letter and an end mark.

script.say: "The words of these sentences got mixed up. Your job is to put them back in order and write the sentence. Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with an end mark: a period, a question mark, or an exclamation point."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: Picture Subtraction
blocks.instruction: Some pictures are crossed out. Write how many are left.

script.say: "In each box, some pictures are crossed out. They are gone. Count the pictures that are left and write that number."
script.first: Do the first box together: count all the pictures, then count the crossed-out ones. Read the number sentence aloud. Count the pictures that are not crossed out and write the number after the equals sign.
script.stuck: Have the child circle each picture that is not crossed out while counting it. If the child counts every picture, cover the crossed-out ones with a finger.

blocks.title: Addition Word Problems
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Use the pictures to help you. Write the answer in the box.

script.say: "Each problem on this page is a short story with numbers. I will read each story aloud. Listen, look at the picture, and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Read the first story aloud while the children follow with a finger. Ask, "Are things put together? Then we add." Use the pictures to count all, and write the answer in the box. Then read each story aloud for the class, one at a time.
script.stuck: Read the story to the child again and ask them to tell it back in their own words. Let them touch and count the pictures, or draw dots.

blocks.title: Complete the Pattern
blocks.instruction: A picture is missing. Circle what belongs in the empty box.

script.say: "Each row is a pattern, but one picture is missing. Find the empty box. Circle the picture that belongs in it."
script.first: Do the first row together. Point to each shape and have the class say its name like a chant. Stop at the empty box and ask, "What goes here?" Say the pattern again with that shape and circle it among the choices at the end of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Beginning, Middle and End of a Story
blocks.instruction: Look at the beginning and the end of each story and draw what happens in the middle frame.

script.say: "Each story on this page has a beginning and an end, but the middle is missing. Look at what is different between the first picture and the last one. Then draw what happens in the middle."
script.first: Do the first story together: look at the first picture and the last one and ask, "What changed? What must have happened in between?" Let two or three children say their ideas. Each child draws their own middle picture; many drawings can be right.
script.stuck: Ask the child: "What is here at the beginning? What is different at the end? What did someone do to make that happen?" Any drawing that leads from the first picture to the last is right; it does not have to be neat.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 13
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 13
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 13 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Bonds Within 10
blocks.instruction: Look at each number bond. Write the missing number in the dashed circle.

script.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
script.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
script.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

blocks.title: Retell the Story and Tell Its Lesson
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end. Use the word bank. Then circle the lesson.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, using the word bank. Then circle the lesson of the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Missing Digraphs: Write sh, ch or th
blocks.instruction: Say each picture word. Write the missing letter team from the top in the dashed space.

script.say: "Each picture word is missing its letter team: sh, ch, or th. Say the word and write the missing letter team in the dashed space."
script.first: Write sh, ch, and th on the board and say each sound with the class. Name the pictures together: bench, thermometer, chocolate, thumb, shoe, chair, jellyfish, wreath. Do the first one together: "ben…ch." Write ch in the dashed space. For your own reference: ch, th, ch, th, sh, ch, sh, th.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and stop at the letter team: "mu-sh-room." Then say sh, ch, and th and ask which one it sounds like.

blocks.title: Write the Word: The First Letter Is Given
blocks.instruction: Say the name of each picture. Find the word in the word bank and finish it after the first letter.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Find its word in the word bank. The first letter is already there; you write the rest of the word."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together and name the pictures: hat, mask, scarf, wallet, medal, vest. Do the first one together on the board: find its word in the bank and finish it after the first letter.
script.stuck: Have the child say the picture word and listen for its first sound, then look in the word bank for a word that starts with the letter that is already written. Read the words in the word bank for a child who cannot read them.

blocks.title: Count the Tens: 10 to 90
blocks.instruction: Count the ten-rods. Write how many tens there are. Then write the number.

script.say: "Each picture shows ten-rods. Each rod is ten. Count the tens, write how many tens there are, and then write the number."
script.first: Draw three rods on the board and count by tens: "10, 20, 30. Three tens is thirty." Do the first one on the page together: count the rods, write the number of tens, then the number.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each rod and count by tens: 10, 20, 30. The number of rods is the number of tens, and the number ends in 0.

blocks.title: Teen Numbers on Two Ten-Frames
blocks.instruction: Count what is in the two ten-frames. Write the number, then finish the number sentence.

script.say: "A teen number is ten and some more. One ten-frame holds ten. Count what is in the two ten-frames and write the number. Then finish the number sentence: ten plus how many more."
script.first: Do the first one together: point to the full ten-frame and say, "That is ten." Count on with the second frame: "eleven, twelve…" Write the number. Then read the sentence: "Twelve equals ten plus…" and write how many are in the second frame.
script.stuck: Have the child start at ten for the full frame and count on, touching each dot in the second frame.

blocks.title: Treasure Hunt: Follow the Steps
blocks.instruction: Start at the flag. Follow the steps. Circle the picture where you land.

script.say: "Start at the flag on the grid. Follow the steps, one at a time: each step says which way to move and how many squares. Circle the picture where you land."
script.first: Put your finger on the flag and read the first step aloud: "Move 1 square right." Move the finger together and stop. Read the next step and move again. Tell the children to count the squares, not the lines, and to keep the finger on the page until the last step.
script.stuck: Have the child say each step aloud and point with a finger. Check right and left: "Which hand is your right hand? Move that way."

blocks.title: How Do You Feel? Circle the Face
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture, think how you would feel, and circle the face that matches.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Think about how it would make you feel. Then circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Look at the first picture together and ask what it shows. Ask, "How does that make you feel?" Let two or three children answer; they may not all feel the same, and that is fine. Each child circles the face that matches their own answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child what the picture shows and when they have seen one. Then point to each face and name the feeling it shows. There is no wrong answer on this page; any face the child can explain is right.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 14
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 14
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 14 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: ABC Order: Number the Words
blocks.instruction: Number the four cards to put the words in ABC order.

script.say: "We are going to put words in ABC order, the order of the alphabet."
script.first: Point to the alphabet strip at the top of the page. Read the four words on the cards aloud with the class. Ask, "Which word starts with the letter that comes first in the alphabet?" Write a 1 on its card together. Tell the children to number the other cards 2, 3, and 4.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the alphabet strip and slide along it, stopping at the first letter that starts one of the words. That word is next. Cross out each word once it has a number.

blocks.title: Read and Circle
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence. Find the picture or pictures it names in the row and draw a circle around them. Then check the little box.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. At the top is a row of animals. Each sentence tells you which animals to circle in that row. Read the sentence, circle exactly what it says, and check the little box when you are done."
script.first: Name the animals in the row together. Read the first sentence aloud together. Ask: "Which animals does it name? Is it one, or all of them?" Circle them together and check the box.
script.stuck: Point to the word the child cannot read and say its first sound; if that is not enough, read the word. Remind the child that "all" means every one of that animal in the row, and that some animals are in the row more than once.

blocks.title: Nouns and Verbs: Two Bins
blocks.instruction: Read each word. Is it a noun or a verb? Write it in the right bin.

script.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing, like dog or school. A verb is something you can do, like run or sing. Read each word and write it in the right bin: noun or verb."
script.first: Read the ten words aloud together. Take the first word and try two test sentences: "I can see a ___" for a noun, and "I can ___" for a verb. Decide together and write the word in its bin. Cross it out in the list.
script.stuck: Read the word to the child and have the child try both test sentences aloud: "I can see a jump. I can jump." The one that sounds right tells the bin. A word that can be both, such as "paint," is right in either bin if the child can use it in a sentence.

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence: With Clues
blocks.instruction: Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line. The capital letter and the end mark show where it begins and ends.

script.say: "The words of each sentence are mixed up. The word with the capital letter comes first, and the word with the end mark comes last. Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: Halves to 12
blocks.instruction: Every card cuts a group in half. Write the two equal parts.

script.say: "Every card cuts a group in half: two equal parts. Write the two equal parts."
script.first: Hold up 4 fingers on each hand: "4 and 4 is 8. Eight is the double of four." Then hold up 8 fingers and split them into two equal parts: "Half of 8 is 4." Read the word on the first card, double or half, and do it together.
script.stuck: For a double, have the child count the pictures and then count them again on from the first number. For a half, have the child share the pictures in two groups, one for you and one for the child, until none are left.

blocks.title: Number Words to 20
blocks.instruction: Read the number. Circle the word that matches it.

script.say: "Each number has a word that we read and write. Read the number and circle the word that matches it."
script.first: Write 1 to 20 on the board and the words for a few of them. Do the first one together: read the number, read the three words, and circle the matching one.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number aloud and listen to its first sound; find the word that starts with that letter. Read the words with the child.

blocks.title: Copy the Picture on an 8 × 8 Grid
blocks.instruction: A bigger grid: find each square by its letter and number, then copy.

script.say: "A bigger grid: find each square by its letter and number, and copy the picture onto the empty grid."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Find one colored square together, say its letter and number, and color the same square on the empty grid. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: City, Suburb and Small Town
blocks.instruction: Look at the places. Read each sentence. Write the letter of the place it tells about.

script.say: "Each picture shows a place, and each place has a letter. Read each sentence and write the letter of the place it tells about."
script.first: Look at the places on your page together and ask the children what they see in each one: tall buildings and a subway in the city, houses with garages near a shopping center in the suburb, fields and a silo in the farm town. Read the first sentence aloud and ask, "Which picture shows that?" Write the letter together. If the page asks where the child lives and gets food, any true answer is right.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask, "What is it about?" Then find that thing in the pictures together and write the letter of that place.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 15
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 15
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 15 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number of the Day
blocks.instruction: Look at the big number. Fill in every box on the page for that number.

script.say: "Look at the big number on the page. It is the number of the day. Every box on the page asks something about that number. Fill in all the boxes."
script.first: Read the number of the day aloud together. Go around the page and read the label of each box aloud, so that the children know what each one asks for. Fill in the tens and ones box together: "How many tens are in this number? How many ones?" The children do the other boxes on their own.
script.stuck: Read the label of the box to the child again. Have the child build the number with ten fingers and some more, or draw a row of ten dots and the extra ones. A child who cannot finish every box should do the ones they know.

blocks.title: Word Family Carpet: Read and Color
blocks.instruction: Read every word on the carpet out loud. Then find each picture's word on the carpet and color that word in the picture's color.

script.say: "The carpet at the top has rows of words. Each row is a word family: the words end the same. Read every word out loud. Then find each picture's word on the carpet and color it."
script.first: Read the carpet aloud together, one row at a time. Name the pictures together: bat, mug, jug, log, rock, van. Find the first picture's word together and color it.
script.stuck: Have the child name the picture and say its first sound, then look for the word that begins with that letter. If two words begin the same way, have the child read both to the end.

blocks.title: Long or Short Vowel?
blocks.instruction: Say each word. Is the colored vowel sound long or short? Circle the line if it is long. Circle the curve if it is short.

script.say: "Say each word. Listen to the colored vowel. Does it say its name, like the a in rake? That is a long vowel: circle the line. Does it make its short sound, like the a in bag? Circle the curve."
script.first: Write rake and bag on the board and say both: "rake, a says its name: long. bag, a says /a/: short." Read the words on the page aloud together. Do the first one together and circle the line or the curve.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and hold the vowel. Then say the letter's name: if the word says the name, it is long. For your own reference: long: tape, stove, globe, beet; short: shrimp, nest, leg, sled.

blocks.title: Personal Pronouns
blocks.instruction: Look at the person and read the name. Circle the word we use instead of the name.

script.say: "Look at each person and read the name. Which word do we use instead of the name: he, she, or they? Circle it."
script.first: Write he, she, and they on the board. Read the first name aloud and look at the picture together. Ask, "Is it one boy, one girl, or more than one person?" Circle the word. For two names, it is always they.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the picture and say how many people it shows. One boy is he, one girl is she, and two or more people are they.

blocks.title: Teen Numbers: One Ten and Some Ones
blocks.instruction: Look at the ten-rod and the ones. Write how many ones there are. Then write the number.

script.say: "Each picture shows one ten-rod and some ones. Write how many ones there are, and then write the number: ten and some more."
script.first: Draw one rod and three small cubes on the board: "One ten and three ones: thirteen." Do the first one on the page together: count the ones, write the number of ones, then the number.
script.stuck: Have the child say "ten" for the rod and count on by ones for each cube: eleven, twelve, thirteen. The number starts with 1 and ends with the number of ones.

blocks.title: Hop Back and Subtract
blocks.instruction: Follow the hops backward. Write the subtraction answer.

script.say: "Each number line shows a take-away sentence. Follow the hops backward and write the answer."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Read the number sentence aloud. Put your finger on the starting number and follow the hops back, counting back aloud. Write where you land. Point out that the line is numbered by twos: each small mark between two numbers is the number in between.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dot, say its number, and move one mark for each arc while counting on. If the child cannot tell which number the dot is on, count the marks from the last printed number together.

blocks.title: Bring the Polar Bear Home Safely
blocks.instruction: Help the polar bear get to the igloo. Do not take a road with a walrus or a hole in the ice.

script.say: "Help the animal get home safely. Look at the whole maze first. Do not take a road with one of the dangers the page names."
script.first: Read the title aloud and show the start and the goal. Point to the dangers on the page and say that a road with a danger is closed. Trace a way with your finger and stop at each fork: "Is there a danger on this road?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Sort the Animals
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Mammals, Birds, and Reptiles. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Does it have fur, feathers, or scales? Does it lay eggs or feed its babies milk?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. Mammals have fur or hair, birds have feathers, and reptiles have dry scales.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 16
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 16
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 16 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: ABC Order: Number Them, Then Write Them
blocks.instruction: Number the cards, then copy the words onto the lines in order.

script.say: "We are going to put words in ABC order, the order of the alphabet."
script.first: Point to the alphabet strip at the top of the page. Read the four words on the cards aloud with the class. Ask, "Which word starts with the letter that comes first in the alphabet?" Write a 1 on its card together. The children number the other cards and then copy the words onto the lines in that order.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the alphabet strip and slide along it, stopping at the first letter that starts one of the words. That word is next. Cross out each word once it has a number.

blocks.title: Match the Sentence to the Picture
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence. Which picture fills the blank? Draw a line from the sentence to that picture.

script.say: "Each sentence has a gap, and one of the pictures belongs in it. Read the sentence, find the picture that makes sense, and draw a line from the sentence to that picture."
script.first: Name all the pictures together. Read the first sentence aloud together and say "blank" at the gap. Try a picture word in the gap: "Does that make sense?" Draw the line together. Then the children read the other sentences on their own.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with the child, one word at a time, and say "blank" at the gap. Then say the sentence with each picture word in turn and ask which one makes sense.

blocks.title: Nouns and Adjectives: Two Bins
blocks.instruction: Read each word. Is it a noun or an adjective? Write it in the right bin.

script.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing. An adjective tells what something is like, like big or red. Read each word and write it in the right bin."
script.first: Read all the words on the page aloud with the class. Do the first two words together: "Is it a thing, or does it tell what something is like?" Write each in its bin.
script.stuck: Read the word to the child and have the child try both test sentences aloud: "I can see a jump. I can jump." The one that sounds right tells the bin. A word that can be both, such as "paint," is right in either bin if the child can use it in a sentence.

blocks.title: Joining Words: and, but, so, because
blocks.instruction: A joining word puts two sentences together. Circle the one that fits best in each sentence. Then join two sentences and write them as one.

script.say: "A joining word puts two sentences together. And adds one more thing. But tells something you did not expect. So tells what happened because of it. Circle the joining word that fits best in each sentence."
script.first: Read the box with the three joining words aloud. Read the first sentence aloud three times, once with each joining word, and ask which one makes the most sense. Circle it. For the last part, read the two sentences together and join them on the lines.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with each joining word for the child and ask, "Which one sounds right?" For but, ask, "Is the second part a surprise?"

blocks.title: Jump to the Ten First
blocks.instruction: Jump to the ten first, then jump the rest. Fill in the boxes.

script.say: "Each problem has a number line. Jump to the ten first, then jump the rest. Fill in the boxes."
script.first: Do 9 + 2 on the board: "From 9, one jump makes 10. One more is 11." Write 9 + 1 + 1 = 11. Show that 2 was split into 1 and 1. Do a take-away one the same way: from 13 back to 10, then the rest.
script.stuck: Ask, "How many to get to ten?" Write that part first, then ask how much is left of the number to add or take away.

blocks.title: Hundreds Chart Puzzle Pieces: Fill In the Numbers
blocks.instruction: One number is printed on each piece. Write every missing number: 1 more to the right, 1 less to the left, 10 more below, 10 less above.

script.say: "Each puzzle piece is a part of a hundreds chart. One number is printed on each piece. Write every missing number: 1 more to the right, 1 less to the left, 10 more below, 10 less above."
script.first: Draw a small piece on the board with 76 in it. Ask, "What is right of 76? One more: 77. Left? 75. Below? Ten more: 86. Above? 66." Fill the boxes together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the rule for the box: right is one more, left is one less, down is ten more, up is ten less.

blocks.title: What Is Missing?
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 empty places in the bottom picture where something from the top picture is missing, and check a box for each.

script.say: "The two pictures are the same, but three things are missing from the bottom picture. Find each empty place, circle it, and check a box for each one."
script.first: Hold up the page and compare the two pictures with the class, from the top down. Find one thing that is missing together and circle the empty place in the bottom picture. Check the first box.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the top picture and look for it in the bottom picture: "Is it there?" There are three missing things; the three boxes help them count.

blocks.title: Work That Fits the Land
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each worker to the land where the work is done.

script.say: "Draw a line from each worker to the land where the work is done."
script.first: Name the pictures of the land together: a forest, the ocean coast, and on some pages flat farmland and snowy mountains. Read the workers aloud. Do the first one together: "A person who fishes. Which land is by the ocean?" Draw the line. If the page asks for sentences about one place, the child picks any place on the page.
script.stuck: Ask, "What does this worker need for the job: trees, the ocean, snow, or a big flat field? Which picture has it?"

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 17
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 17
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 17 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 1 More, 1 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 1 less and the number that is 1 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 1 less. On the right, write the number that is 1 more."
script.first: Write 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. Do the first one together: find the number, step one back for 1 less and one on for 1 more.
script.stuck: Have the child count aloud up to the number and say the next one: that is 1 more. The one said just before it is 1 less.

blocks.title: Story Sequencing: What Happens Next?
blocks.instruction: Look at each story's three pictures, then circle the picture below them that belongs in the ? frame.

script.say: "Each row is a little story in three pictures, and a question mark shows the picture that comes next. Look at what changes. Circle the picture below the story that belongs in the question-mark frame."
script.first: Do the first story together: ask a child to say what happens in each picture. Ask, "What happens next?" Look at the three choices below and circle the one that goes on the story.
script.stuck: Have the child tell the story aloud with each choice at the end; the choice that makes sense is the right one.

blocks.title: Rhyming Words: Rhyme and Write
blocks.instruction: Say the first picture. Circle the picture that rhymes with it, then write its word on the line.

script.say: "Rhyming words sound the same at the end, like cat and hat. On this page you find the picture that rhymes, then you write its word."
script.first: Name the pictures of each row together, so that everyone uses the same words (they are below). Do the first row together: say the first picture with each of the others and ask which one rhymes. Circle it and write its word on the line. Spelling it the way it sounds is fine.
script.stuck: Say the first picture with each choice and stretch the endings. For your own reference, the rows are hat (nail, cat, shelf), bear (car, pear, crane), boat (coat, plate, mouse), rake (lamp, cake, log), nose (rose, rock, star), shirt (guitar, pan, skirt); the rhymes are cat, pear, coat, cake, rose, skirt.

blocks.title: Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow
blocks.instruction: A verb tells when: yesterday I walked, today I walk, tomorrow I will walk. Write the missing verbs. Then circle the verb that fits.

script.say: "A verb tells when something happens: yesterday I walked, today I walk, tomorrow I will walk. Write the missing verbs. Then circle the verb that fits the time word in each sentence."
script.first: Write walked, walk, will walk under Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow on the board. Do the first row on the page together. For the second part, read the first sentence aloud and look for the time word: yesterday, today, or tomorrow.
script.stuck: Ask, "Did it happen already, is it happening now, or will it happen later?" Already: add -ed. Later: will.

blocks.title: Fact Family Houses
blocks.instruction: Use the three numbers on the roof. Complete the four related facts.

script.say: "The three numbers on the roof are a family. They make four facts: two adding and two taking away. Use the three numbers to finish all four facts in each house."
script.first: Draw a house on the board with 3, 7, and 10 on the roof. Write the four facts together: 3 + 7 = 10, 7 + 3 = 10, 10 − 3 = 7, 10 − 7 = 3. Point out that the biggest number is the whole: it comes after the equals sign when we add and first when we take away.
script.stuck: Have the child find the biggest number on the roof and circle it: that is the whole. The other two are the parts. Adding the parts makes the whole; taking a part away from the whole leaves the other part.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 0 to 10
blocks.instruction: Write the number each arrow points to, from 0 to 10.

script.say: "Each arrow points to a mark on the number line. Count on from the number before it and write the number the arrow points to."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Count the marks with the class from 0, one by one, up to the arrow. Write that number. Tell the children that not every mark has its number written; they count the marks between.
script.stuck: Have the child find the last printed number before the arrow, put a finger on it, and count each mark up to the arrow.

blocks.title: Help the Pig Reach the Mud Puddle
blocks.instruction: Help the hedgehog get to the apple tree. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Find the way along the light path from the animal to its goal. Use your finger first, then your pencil."
script.first: Hold up the page and show where the path starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the beginning of the way with your finger and stop at the first place where the path splits: "Which way? Let's try one." Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Where Do Animals Live?
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to where it lives.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Land, Water, and Air. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Where does this animal spend most of its time: on land, in the water, or in the air?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. An animal that flies lives on land too, so Air and Land are both right for it, and a crab lives in the water and on land, so Water and Land are both right for it, when the child can say why.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 18
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 18
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 18 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count by Tens
blocks.instruction: Skip count by 10. Write each missing number.

script.say: "On this page we count by tens: 10, 20, 30. Some numbers are missing. Count by tens and write each missing number."
script.first: Count by tens to 100 together, clapping on each number. Read the first row aloud together and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. Tell the children that a row does not always start at 10.
script.stuck: Have the child whisper the count by tens from the first number of the row, one box at a time: each number is ten more than the one before it.

blocks.title: Read and Check: True or False
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and look at the row of pictures. Is the sentence true or false? Circle the right word.

script.say: "Read each sentence and look at the row of pictures. Is the sentence true or false? Circle the right word."
script.first: Point to the row of pictures and name them together from left to right. Read the first sentence aloud and check it on the row together, counting the pictures from the left. Circle true or false.
script.stuck: Point to the word the child cannot read and say its first sound; if that is not enough, read the word. Then have the child read the whole sentence again and tell you what it asks for before starting.

blocks.title: Blends
blocks.instruction: Say the name of each picture. Write the two letters the word starts with.

script.say: "Each word starts with two letters that you can hear together, like s and l in sled. Say the name of each picture. Write the two letters it starts with."
script.first: Say "sled" slowly: "s-l-ed. Two sounds at the start: s and l." Name the pictures together: spider, dragon, flute, stove, crib, glove, plunger, snorkel. Do the first one together: "spider, s-p." Write sp. For your own reference: sp, dr, fl, st, cr, gl, pl, sn.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and stretch the start: "ssslll-ed." Ask the child to say the first sound, then the second sound, and write both letters.

blocks.title: Capital Letter or Small Letter?
blocks.instruction: Names and the days of the week start with a capital letter. Other words do not, unless they start the sentence.

script.say: "Names of people and pets, and the days of the week, start with a capital letter. Other words do not, unless they start the sentence. In each sentence, circle the word that is written the right way."
script.first: Write "Monday" and "monday" on the board and ask which is right. Read the first sentence aloud with both choices: "On Monday, or monday, we have a test." Circle Monday together. Read each sentence aloud with the class before they choose. Then read the second part of the page together.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is this word a name, a day, or a month? Does it start the sentence?" If yes, it gets a capital letter.

blocks.title: Number Walls
blocks.instruction: Each brick is the sum of the two bricks under it. Fill in the missing numbers.

script.say: "This is a number wall. Each brick is the sum of the two bricks right under it. Start at the bottom and build every wall to the top."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks that sit side by side in the bottom row and to the brick that rests on both of them: "Three plus two is five. Five goes on top." Fill in that wall together.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers with fingers or dots. If the child writes the sum next to the bricks and not above them, point to the brick that touches both.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot 1 to 20
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Connect the dots in number order to finish the picture.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot. Start at the orange dot, at number 1. Draw a line to 2, then to 3, and keep counting until you get to 20."
script.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Find the orange dot together and put a finger on it. Ask, "What comes after 1?" Find 2 and draw the first line together. The numbers 1 to 20 are printed at the bottom of the page to help.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and count one more; that is the number to look for. Point to the part of the page where the next dot is. If a line went to the wrong dot, leave it and go on from the right one.

blocks.title: Growing Patterns
blocks.instruction: The pattern grows. Circle the group that comes next.

script.say: "These patterns grow: each box has one more than the box before. Count the boxes. Circle the group that comes next."
script.first: Do the first row together: count the pictures in each box aloud, "one, two, three." Ask, "So how many come next?" Count the groups at the end of the row and circle the one with four.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each picture and say its name aloud from the start of the row, then say the next word before looking at the choices. If the child cannot name a picture, give it a simple name.

blocks.title: Caring for Our Park
blocks.instruction: Circle the 5 things people changed in picture 2. In picture 3, circle every person who helps.

script.say: "The first picture shows a park in the morning. The next picture shows the same park in the evening. Circle the things people changed."
script.first: Look at the morning picture together and name what is there: the flowers, the pond, the bench, the trash can, the tree. Then look at the evening picture and ask, "What is different? Did a person do that?" Find the first change together. The page says how many changes to find. If there is a clean-up-day picture, circle each person who is helping; someone just walking a dog is visiting, not helping. If the page asks how our class can help, any helpful idea is right.
script.stuck: Point to one thing in the morning picture, the pond for example, and ask, "Is it the same in the evening?" Go through the park one thing at a time.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 19
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 19
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 19 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 10 More, 10 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 10 less and the number that is 10 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 10 less. On the right, write the number that is 10 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "Ten more: which digit changes, the tens or the ones?" Show that only the tens digit changes, one more ten for ten more and one less ten for ten less. Count by tens from another number together, for example 7, 17, 27, 37.
script.stuck: If the classroom has a hundreds chart, have the child find the number on it: the number straight above is 10 less, and the number straight below is 10 more. Without a chart, have the child cover the ones digit and change the tens digit by one.

blocks.title: Characters, Setting, and Events
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write who is in it, where it takes place, and what happens.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write who is in it, where it takes place, and what happens."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Opposites: Write the Opposite Word
blocks.instruction: Read the word on each card. Find its opposite in the word bank and write it on the line.

script.say: "Read the word on each card. Find its opposite in the word bank and write it on the line."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud. Read the first card together and ask, "What is the opposite of day?" Find night in the bank and write it on the line.
script.stuck: Act the word out for the child, or ask, "What is the other end of this word?"

blocks.title: Plan a True Story
blocks.instruction: Time words like first, next, and last tell the order of a story.

script.say: "Time words like first, next, and last tell the order of a story. First read the little story and circle its time words. Then plan your own true story in the boxes."
script.first: Read the story on the page aloud and circle the time words together: first, then, last. Do the numbering part together. For the plan, let a few children say an idea: a rainy day, something new they learned. Each child draws and writes a few words in each box: First, Next, Last, and how they felt.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "What did you do first? And then?" Write one word for the child to copy, or let the child draw and label.

blocks.title: Mental Math to 100
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Think of the tens and the ones. Write the answer in the box.

script.say: "Solve each problem in your head. Think of the tens and the ones. Write the answer in the box."
script.first: Write 36 + 6 on the board. Say, "36 is 3 tens and 6 ones. 6 and 6 make 12, so we get one more ten: 42." Do one taking away ten: 46 − 10 = 36: "only the tens change." Then the children work on their own.
script.stuck: Have the child say the tens and the ones of the first number. For adding or taking away tens, only the tens digit changes; for ones, count on or back from the number.

blocks.title: Subtraction Word Problems
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Use the pictures to help you. Write the answer in the box.

script.say: "Each problem on this page is a short story with numbers. I will read each story aloud. Listen, look at the picture, and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Read the first story aloud while the children follow with a finger. Ask, "Are some taken away? Then we subtract." Use the pictures: cover the ones that go away and count the rest. Write the answer in the box. Then read each story aloud for the class.
script.stuck: Read the story to the child again and ask them to tell it back in their own words. Let them touch and count the pictures, or draw dots.

blocks.title: Help the Tortoise Find the Watermelon
blocks.instruction: Look at the whole maze first. Then draw the orangutan's way to the banana tree.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Symbols of the United States
blocks.instruction: Read about each symbol. Write its name from the word box.

script.say: "Each picture shows a symbol of the United States. Read about it. Then trace or write its name."
script.first: Name the symbols on your page together: the flag, the bald eagle, the Statue of Liberty, the Liberty Bell. Read each sentence aloud for the children who need it. Do the first one together. On some pages the names are in a word box at the top. If the page asks for a symbol for our class, any drawing with what it stands for is right.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask, "Which picture does that tell about?" Then find its name in the word box, or trace the name under the picture.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 20
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 20
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 20 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number of the Day: Ten More, Ten Less
blocks.instruction: Find ten more and ten less than the number of the day.

script.say: "Look at the big number: it is the number of the day. Every box asks something about it: its word, the numbers before and after, ten more and ten less. Fill in all the boxes."
script.first: Read the number of the day aloud together. Go around the page and read the label of each box aloud, so that the children know what each one asks for. Fill in the tens and ones box together: "How many tens are in this number? How many ones?" The children do the other boxes on their own.
script.stuck: Read the label of the box to the child again. Have the child build the number with ten fingers and some more, or draw a row of ten dots and the extra ones. A child who cannot finish every box should do the ones they know.

blocks.title: Word Families with Blends
blocks.instruction: Read every word on the carpet out loud. Say each picture word, find it on the carpet, then write the two letters it starts with on the line.

script.say: "Read every word on the carpet out loud. Say each picture word, find it on the carpet, and write the two letters it starts with on the line."
script.first: Read the carpet aloud together. Name the pictures together: glass, brush, swing, stamp, truck, crib. Do the first one together: find "glass" and write gl on the line.
script.stuck: Have the child name the picture and say its first sound, then look for the word that begins with that letter. If two words begin the same way, have the child read both to the end.

blocks.title: Shades of Meaning: From a Little to a Lot
blocks.instruction: Read the three words in each row and write 1, 2 and 3 in the boxes, from the weakest word to the strongest.

script.say: "Each row has three words that mean almost the same thing, but some are stronger. Write 1 for the weakest word, 2 for the middle one, and 3 for the strongest."
script.first: Act out the first row: tap the desk softly, knock, then bang. Ask which is the weakest and which is the strongest. Write 1, 2, 3 together. Read every row aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Act the words out with the child or say them with your voice, from a little to a lot.

blocks.title: Word Bank and Letter Boxes
blocks.instruction: Find the word in the bank. Write one letter in each box.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Find its word in the word bank, and write it in the letter boxes, one letter in each box."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together and name the pictures. Do the first one together: find the word, count its letters and the boxes, and write one letter in each box.
script.stuck: Have the child say the picture word and listen for its first sound, then look in the word bank for a word that starts with the letter that is already written. Read the words in the word bank for a child who cannot read them.

blocks.title: Add Three Numbers
blocks.instruction: Add the three numbers. Look for two numbers that make ten and add them first.

script.say: "Each problem adds three numbers. Look for two numbers that make ten, add them first, and then add the third number."
script.first: Write 9 + 1 + 8 on the board. Ask, "Which two numbers make ten?" Circle 9 and 1: "Ten. Ten and eight more is eighteen." Write 18. Tell the children that if no two numbers make ten, they may add in any order.
script.stuck: Have the child look at each pair of numbers and ask, "Do these two make ten?" If no pair does, add the first two, then count on the third with fingers.

blocks.title: Odd and Even Numbers: Odd House, Even House
blocks.instruction: Write each number in the house where it belongs, the odd house or the even house. Three numbers have moved in already and show their pairs.

script.say: "Even numbers can be shared in pairs with none left over. Odd numbers always have one left over. Write each number in the house where it belongs: the odd house or the even house."
script.first: Count by twos together: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10: these are even. Write them on the board. The numbers in between, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, are odd. Tell the children that a number ending in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8 is even. Do the first number together.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the last digit of the number and check it against the list of even numbers on the board. For a small number, draw dots in pairs.

blocks.title: Picture Pairs: Find the Difference
blocks.instruction: Each row shows the same close-up twice; circle the one place that is different in the right picture and check the box of that row.

script.say: "Each row shows the same picture two times, but one place in the right picture is different. Circle it, and check the box of that row."
script.first: Do the first row together: compare the left and the right picture, part by part, and find the one difference. Circle it in the right picture and check the box of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child cover half of each picture with a hand and compare one half at a time.

blocks.title: Family Tree: Read the Clues
blocks.instruction: Read the clues and write each name in the right name box on the family tree.

script.say: "Read each clue. It tells you who someone is in the family. Write each name in the right name box on the family tree."
script.first: Read the names on the tree and the first clue aloud. Find the child the clues are about on the tree. Ask, "If Leo is Jack's brother, where does he go on the tree?" Write Leo in that box together.
script.stuck: Read the clue with the child and point to Jack on the tree. Ask, "Is a brother next to Jack, above him, or two rows up?" Brothers and sisters are next to him, parents above, grandparents at the top.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 21
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 21
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 21 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Missing Number Problems to 10
blocks.instruction: Work out the missing number in your head. Write it in the box.

script.say: "In each problem one number is missing. Work out the missing number in your head and write it in the box."
script.first: Write 6 + __ = 10 on the board. Ask, "Six and how many more make ten?" Count on from 6 with fingers to 10: four. Write 4. Then do one with take away: 8 − __ = 5.
script.stuck: Have the child say the problem aloud with a hum for the box. Count on or back with fingers from the first number to the answer, and count the fingers.

blocks.title: Digraphs: sh, ch, and th
blocks.instruction: Read each word and draw a line to its picture. Two words have no picture. Then write each word under sh or ch, and cross it out.

script.say: "First read each word and draw a line to its picture; two words have no picture. Then read the words in the second part and write each one under sh or ch."
script.first: Write sh and ch on the board and say each sound with the class. Read the words of the first part aloud together: hip, shelf, chick, chips, ship, kick. Find the first picture together and draw its line. For the second part, read the first word together and ask, "sh or ch?"
script.stuck: Read the word for the child, slowly, and stop at the letter team. Then ask which letter team makes that sound.

blocks.title: Synonyms with Pictures: Two Words, One Picture
blocks.instruction: Look at each picture and circle the two words under it that mean the same and tell about the picture.

script.say: "Synonyms are words that mean the same thing, like big and large. Under each picture there are words. Circle the two words that mean the same and tell about the picture."
script.first: Write big and large on the board: "They mean the same." Look at the first picture together and read its words aloud. Ask, "Which two mean the same and fit the picture?" Circle them.
script.stuck: Read the words with the child and ask, "Which word could you put in place of this one?"

blocks.title: Sort the Names: He, She or They
blocks.instruction: Read each name card. Write the name under the word we use for that person.

script.say: "Read each name card. Write the name under the word we use for that person: he, she, or they."
script.first: Write he, she, and they on the board. Read the first name card aloud and ask, "Would we say he, she, or they?" Write the name under that word together. Two names on one card go under they.
script.stuck: Read the name card with the child. One boy is he, one girl is she, and two or more people are they: two names on one card go under they.

blocks.title: Picture Addition
blocks.instruction: Count both groups. Write how many altogether.

script.say: "In each row there are two groups of pictures. Count both groups. Write how many there are altogether after the equals sign."
script.first: Do the first row together: count the first group, then keep counting into the second group. Write the number after the equals sign. Show the children how to start with the bigger group and count on.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each dot while counting. If the child counts one side, starts over at one for the other side, and writes that second number, count across both sides with them once without stopping.

blocks.title: Number Line to 50: Counting by Fives
blocks.instruction: Count by fives from 0, 25 or 50 to each arrow. Write the number.

script.say: "On each number line the marks count by fives. Count by fives from the printed numbers to each arrow, and write the number it points to."
script.first: Count by fives to 50 together. Draw the first line on the board, start at 0, and count each mark: "5, 10, 15." Stop at the arrow and write that number.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the printed number before the arrow and count on by fives, one mark at a time.

blocks.title: Draw It Twice as Big
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big.

script.say: "Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big."
script.first: Find the top-left colored square on the small grid together and count which row and which column it is in. Find the same row and column on the big grid and color that square. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 22
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 22
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 22 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Bonds to 10
blocks.instruction: Look at each number bond. Write the missing number in the dashed circle.

script.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
script.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
script.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

blocks.title: Read the Facts
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the answer to each question. Finish the sentence.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write the answer to each question by finishing the sentence."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Opposite or the Same? Circle the Opposite
blocks.instruction: Read the word. One of the three words under it means the opposite. Circle it, not the one that means the same.

script.say: "Read the word. One of the three words under it means the opposite. Circle it, not the one that means the same."
script.first: Read the first word and its three choices aloud. Ask, "Which one means the opposite?" Point out that one choice means almost the same as the word: that is the trap. Circle the opposite.
script.stuck: Read each choice and ask, "Does it mean the same, or the opposite?"

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence: No Clues
blocks.instruction: There is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line.

script.say: "The words of each sentence are mixed up, and there is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence with a capital letter and a period."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
