script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: On the Hour
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour. Circle the time that matches the clock."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board showing 3:00 and say, "The long hand is on the 12, so it is something o'clock. The short hand points to 3: three o'clock." Do the first clock on the page together. Some choices end in :30; check where the long hand points.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

blocks.title: Color the Counting Path
blocks.instruction: Two boxes are colored to start you off. Color every number in the same counting pattern.

script.say: "Two boxes on the chart are colored to start you off. Find the counting pattern and color every number that comes in it."
script.first: Point to the two colored boxes and read them: for example 5 and 10. Ask, "How do we get from 5 to 10? We count by fives." Color 15 together and say the next one: 20. The children go on to the end of the chart.
script.stuck: Have the child count on from the last colored number by the same jump, touching each box.

blocks.title: Help the Kitten Get to the Milk
blocks.instruction: Help the puppy get to the ball. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Help the animal get to its goal. Draw a line along the wide road and stay between its edges."
script.first: Hold up the page, read its title aloud, and show where the road starts, at the animal with the arrow, and where it ends. Trace the road with your finger and stop at each place where it splits: "Which way leads to the goal?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: School and Play Long Ago and Today
blocks.instruction: Circle long ago or today for each picture and for each thing a child said.

script.say: "Look at each picture and read each sentence. Is it from long ago or today? Circle long ago or today."
script.first: Ask the class, "How did children go to school and play long ago, when your great-grandparents were little?" Read the words under the first picture aloud and ask, "Do children do that today?" Circle together. Read the sentences aloud for the children who need it. If the page asks which school the child would like, any answer with a reason is right.
script.stuck: Ask, "Have you seen one of these at school or at home?" Something children use today is today; something we see only in old pictures is long ago.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 23
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 23
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 23 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: The Month Before and After
blocks.instruction: One month is given in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it.

script.say: "Each box has one month in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it."
script.first: Say the months of the year aloud together, twice, and write them on the board in order. Do the first box together: find the month on the board and read the month on its left and on its right. Write them.
script.stuck: Have the child find the month on the board and put a finger on it: one step back is before, one step on is after. After December comes January again.

blocks.title: Main Topic and Key Details
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the main topic. Then write two key details from the text.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write what the whole text is about, the main topic, and two key details: facts the text tells about it."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Shades of Meaning: From a Little to a Lot
blocks.instruction: Read the three words in each row and write 1, 2 and 3 in the boxes, from the weakest word to the strongest.

script.say: "Each row has three words that mean almost the same thing, but some are stronger. Write 1 for the weakest word, 2 for the middle one, and 3 for the strongest."
script.first: Act out the first row: tap the desk softly, knock, then bang. Ask which is the weakest and which is the strongest. Write 1, 2, 3 together. Read every row aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Act the words out with the child or say them with your voice, from a little to a lot.

blocks.title: Fill In the Question Word
blocks.instruction: Read the answer and find the highlighted words. Write the question word from the bank in the box.

script.say: "Read each answer. Look at the highlighted words. Which question asks for them: who, what, where, when, or how many? Write that question word in the box."
script.first: Read the question words in the bank aloud. Read the first answer and its question aloud and look at the highlighted words. Ask, "Which question word asks for these words?" Write it in the box together. Do the rest of the page by reading each answer aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Ask the child: "Is the highlighted part a person? Then who. A thing? What. A place? Where. A time? When. A number? How many."

blocks.title: True or False?
blocks.instruction: Is each equation true? Circle the check mark if it is true and the X if it is false.

script.say: "Is each number sentence true? If both sides are the same amount, it is true: circle the check mark. If not, it is false: circle the X."
script.first: Write 10 − 2 = 8 on the board and ask, "Is ten take away two eight? Yes: true." Write 9 = 5 + 6 and ask, "Is five and six nine? No: false." Remind the children that the equals sign means "the same as" and can be on either side.
script.stuck: Have the child work out the side with the plus or minus sign and then compare it with the number on the other side.

blocks.title: Count Back!
blocks.instruction: Start at the dot. Hop backward and write where you land.

script.say: "Each number line has a dot where you start, and arcs that show the hops back. Count back one mark for each hop, and write the number where the last hop lands."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Put your finger on the starting dot and say its number. Follow the arcs back one at a time and count back aloud. Write where the last arc lands. Point out that the line is numbered by twos: each small mark between two numbers is the number in between.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dot, say its number, and move one mark for each arc while counting on. If the child cannot tell which number the dot is on, count the marks from the last printed number together.

blocks.title: Treasure Hunt: Follow the Steps
blocks.instruction: Start at the flag. Follow the steps. Circle the picture where you land.

script.say: "Start at the flag on the grid. Follow the steps, one at a time: each step says which way to move and how many squares. Circle the picture where you land."
script.first: Put your finger on the flag and read the first step aloud: "Move 1 square right." Move the finger together and stop. Read the next step and move again. Tell the children to count the squares, not the lines, and to keep the finger on the page until the last step.
script.stuck: Have the child say each step aloud and point with a finger. Check right and left: "Which hand is your right hand? Move that way."

blocks.title: How Do You Feel? Circle the Face
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture, think how you would feel, and circle the face that matches.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Think about how it would make you feel. Then circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Look at the first picture together and ask what it shows. Ask, "How does that make you feel?" Let two or three children answer; they may not all feel the same, and that is fine. Each child circles the face that matches their own answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child what the picture shows and when they have seen one. Then point to each face and name the feeling it shows. There is no wrong answer on this page; any face the child can explain is right.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 24
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 24
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 24 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count On from Any Number
blocks.instruction: Count along the strip. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Some numbers on these number strips are missing. Count along the strip and write each number that is missing."
script.first: Write the numbers 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. The strips on this page start at big numbers. Read the first strip aloud together, pointing to each box, and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. The children do the other strips the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child read the first number of the strip and count on aloud from it, touching each box; the number they say at the empty box is the one to write. A child who does not know how to write a number may copy it from the board.

blocks.title: Read the Facts
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the answer to each question. Finish the sentence.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write the answer to each question by finishing the sentence."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Sound Strip: How Many Sounds?
blocks.instruction: Say the word slowly. Write one sound in each box, starting from the left. Leave the boxes you do not need empty.

script.say: "Say the word for each picture slowly, like a turtle. Write one sound in each box, starting on the left. If the word has fewer sounds than boxes, leave the last boxes empty."
script.first: Name the pictures together: fish, fox, hat, vest, bear, raccoon. Do "hat" on the board: say h-a-t, one finger for each sound, and write one sound in each box. Leave the boxes you do not need empty.
script.stuck: Have the child say the word slowly and push a finger forward for each sound. Two letters that make one sound, such as sh, go in one box together. A child who fills every box, whether the word needs them all or not, is spelling letter by letter and not listening for sounds; say the word together again and tap one box for each sound.

blocks.title: Write the Word: Every Clue
blocks.instruction: Write each word using the bank, the boxes and the first letter.

script.say: "Say the name of each picture. Use every clue to write its word: the word bank, the letter boxes, and the first letter."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together and name the pictures. Do the first one together: find the word in the bank, check its first letter, and write one letter in each box.
script.stuck: Have the child say the picture word and listen for its first sound, then look in the word bank for a word that starts with the letter that is already written. Read the words in the word bank for a child who cannot read them.

blocks.title: Time in Words
blocks.instruction: Read the time in words. Draw a line from each clock to the words that tell its time.

script.say: "Read the times in words. Draw a line from each clock to the words that tell its time."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board at half past three and say, "The long hand is on the 6: half past. The short hand is just past the 3: half past three." Read the words on the page aloud together and match the first clock together. Quarter past means the long hand is on the 3.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

blocks.title: Which Place? Write the Ordinal Number
blocks.instruction: Find each small picture in its line and write which place it stands in, counting from the flag.

script.say: "Each row of pictures starts at a flag. Find the small picture in the row and write which place it stands in, counting from the flag: first, second, third, and so on."
script.first: Write 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th on the board and read them. Do the first one together: start at the flag, touch each picture and count: "first, second, third." Stop at the small picture and write its place.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger next to the flag and move to the right one picture at a time, saying the places aloud.

blocks.title: Help the Gerbil Reach the Blueberry
blocks.instruction: Help the ant go down and up through the tunnels to the raspberry. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Goods and Services
blocks.instruction: Goods are things people make or grow. Services are work someone does for you. Color the box yellow for goods and green for services.

script.say: "Goods are things people make or grow. Services are work someone does for you. Color the box yellow for goods and green for services."
script.first: Hold up a pencil: "Someone made this. It is a good." Then say, "When someone does work for you, that is a service." Name each picture on the page together and do the first one together. If your page has a town map, read the labels aloud: a good from a place on the map is from our town; a good grown far away is not.
script.stuck: Ask, "Is it a thing someone made or grew, or is it work someone does for you?" Bananas are a good; a haircut is a service.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 25
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 25
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 25 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Mental Math to 10
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: adding and taking away with numbers up to 10. Do the ones you know first. If you need your fingers for the others, that is fine."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board. Ask how the children got their answers and accept every way that gives the right answer: fingers, counting on, or just knowing it.
script.stuck: Let the child use fingers or draw dots; that is fine even where the page says to solve the problems in your head. Read a problem with an empty box as a question, for example: "Four plus what number makes nine?"

blocks.title: Main Topic and Key Details
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the main topic. Then write two key details from the text.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write what the whole text is about, the main topic, and two key details: facts the text tells about it."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Write the Word in Syllables
blocks.instruction: Read the word beside each picture. Copy it on the line and write a small dash between its syllables.

script.say: "Read the word beside each picture. Copy it on the line and write a small dash between its syllables, its beats."
script.first: Clap a long word together: "el-e-phant, three claps." Write el-e-phant on the board with dashes. Read the first word on the page together, clap it, and copy it with dashes.
script.stuck: Have the child put a hand under the chin and say the word: each time the chin drops is a syllable. Write the word one syllable at a time.

blocks.title: Joining Words: and, but, so, because
blocks.instruction: A joining word puts two sentences together. Circle the one that fits best in each sentence. Then join two sentences and write them as one.

script.say: "A joining word puts two sentences together. And adds one more thing. But tells something you did not expect. So tells what happened because of it. Circle the joining word that fits best in each sentence."
script.first: Read the box with the three joining words aloud. Read the first sentence aloud three times, once with each joining word, and ask which one makes the most sense. Circle it. For the last part, read the two sentences together and join them on the lines.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with each joining word for the child and ask, "Which one sounds right?" For but, ask, "Is the second part a surprise?"

blocks.title: Counting Money: All the Coins
blocks.instruction: Count the coins. Write how much money there is in all.

script.say: "Each box has coins in it. The number on a coin tells you how many cents it is worth. Count how much money is in each box and write the amount."
script.first: Draw the four coins on the board with their value: a quarter is 25 cents, a dime is 10, a nickel is 5, and a penny is 1. Do the first box together: start with the coin that is worth the most and count on: "25, 50… 55, 60." Write the amount in the box in front of the cent sign.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each coin, biggest number first, and say the running total. A child who counts the coins and not the cents (three coins are "3") should read the number on each coin aloud first. If the classroom has play coins, let the child lay them out.

blocks.title: Write the Number Words
blocks.instruction: Find the matching word in the word bank. Write it on the line.

script.say: "Find the word for each number in the word bank at the top. Write it on the line."
script.first: Read the words in the word bank aloud together. Do the first one together: read the number, find its word in the bank, and copy it letter by letter.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number aloud and listen to its first sound; find the word that starts with that letter. Read the words with the child.

blocks.title: What Is Missing?
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 empty places in the bottom picture where something from the top picture is missing, and check a box for each.

script.say: "The two pictures are the same, but three things are missing from the bottom picture. Find each empty place, circle it, and check a box for each one."
script.first: Hold up the page and compare the two pictures with the class, from the top down. Find one thing that is missing together and circle the empty place in the bottom picture. Check the first box.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in the top picture and look for it in the bottom picture: "Is it there?" There are three missing things; the three boxes help them count.

blocks.title: Sink or Float?
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each object to the group you think it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Float and Sink. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "If we put this in water, would it float on top or sink to the bottom?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. This page asks what the children think; a child who can say why has done the page well.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 26
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 26
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 26 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: ABC Order: Number the Words
blocks.instruction: Number the four cards to put the words in ABC order.

script.say: "We are going to put words in ABC order, the order of the alphabet."
script.first: Point to the alphabet strip at the top of the page. Read the four words on the cards aloud with the class. Ask, "Which word starts with the letter that comes first in the alphabet?" Write a 1 on its card together. Tell the children to number the other cards 2, 3, and 4.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the alphabet strip and slide along it, stopping at the first letter that starts one of the words. That word is next. Cross out each word once it has a number.

blocks.title: Fill-in-the-Blank Sentences
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Find the word that fits the sentence in the word bank and write it in the box.

script.say: "Each sentence is missing a word. The words are in the word bank at the top, and each sentence has a picture. Find the word that fits and write it in the box."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together. Read the first sentence aloud and say "blank" at the gap. Look at its picture and ask, "Which word fits?" Write it in the box together.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with the child, one word at a time, and say "blank" at the gap. Look at the picture together and find its word in the bank.

blocks.title: Nouns and Verbs: Two Bins
blocks.instruction: Read each word. Is it a noun or a verb? Write it in the right bin.

script.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing, like dog or school. A verb is something you can do, like run or sing. Read each word and write it in the right bin: noun or verb."
script.first: Read the ten words aloud together. Take the first word and try two test sentences: "I can see a ___" for a noun, and "I can ___" for a verb. Decide together and write the word in its bin. Cross it out in the list.
script.stuck: Read the word to the child and have the child try both test sentences aloud: "I can see a jump. I can jump." The one that sounds right tells the bin. A word that can be both, such as "paint," is right in either bin if the child can use it in a sentence.

blocks.title: Personal Pronouns
blocks.instruction: Look at the person and read the name. Circle the word we use instead of the name.

script.say: "Look at each person and read the name. Which word do we use instead of the name: he, she, or they? Circle it."
script.first: Write he, she, and they on the board. Read the first name aloud and look at the picture together. Ask, "Is it one boy, one girl, or more than one person?" Circle the word. For two names, it is always they.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the picture and say how many people it shows. One boy is he, one girl is she, and two or more people are they.

blocks.title: 2D Shapes: Write the Names
blocks.instruction: Look at each shape and write its name on the line, using the names in the box.

script.say: "Look at each shape. Count its sides and corners. Write its name on the line, using the names in the box."
script.first: Draw a circle, a triangle, a square, and a rectangle on the board and read their names in the box. Do the first shape together: count the sides and choose the name.
script.stuck: Have the child count the sides with a finger: 3 sides is a triangle; 4 equal sides is a square; 4 sides, two long and two short, is a rectangle; no sides is a circle.

blocks.title: Word Problems Within 10
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Use the pictures to help you. Write the answer in the box.

script.say: "Each problem on this page is a short story with numbers. I will read each story aloud. Listen, look at the picture, and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Read the first story aloud while the children follow with a finger. Ask, "Do we add or take away?" Use the pictures to count, and write the answer in the box. Then read each story aloud for the class, one at a time.
script.stuck: Read the story to the child again and ask them to tell it back in their own words. Let them touch and count the pictures, or draw dots.

blocks.title: Count Along with the Elephant to the Watermelon
blocks.instruction: Help the train get to the cabin. At every fork, go to the next number from 1 to 20.

script.say: "Read the title with me: it tells you who is going where. At every fork, take the road to the next number when you count: 1, 2, 3, all the way to 20."
script.first: Count from 1 to 20 aloud together. Put your finger on the start and find 1. Ask, "What comes next? Which road goes to 2?" Draw the first part together. Tell the children to say each number as they reach it.
script.stuck: Tell the child that a dead end is part of every maze: go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way. Starting from the goal and working backward also helps.

blocks.title: Jobs and Earning Money
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each sentence to the worker who says it. Then circle what a family can spend its pay on.

script.say: "Draw a line from each sentence to the worker who says it. Then circle what a family can spend its pay on."
script.first: Say, "People work at jobs and get paid money. Then they can buy what they need." Read each sentence aloud and name the workers in the pictures together. Do the first line together. Then point to each picture of the last part and ask, "Can a family buy this with money?" The sun, a hug, and a rainbow cannot be bought. If the page asks for a job the child would like, any job is right.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with the child and ask, "Who does that work?" Point to each worker and ask what that person does.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 27
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 27
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 27 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number of the Day: Up to 99
blocks.instruction: Show a two-digit number in tens and ones, then fill every box.

script.say: "Look at the big number: it is the number of the day. Show it in tens and ones, and fill in every box on the page."
script.first: Read the number of the day aloud together. Go around the page and read the label of each box aloud, so that the children know what each one asks for. Fill in the tens and ones box together: "How many tens are in this number? How many ones?" The children do the other boxes on their own.
script.stuck: Read the label of the box to the child again. Have the child build the number with ten fingers and some more, or draw a row of ten dots and the extra ones. A child who cannot finish every box should do the ones they know.

blocks.title: Story Sequencing Sentences: Match the Pictures
blocks.instruction: Number each story's sentences in order in the boxes, then draw a line from every sentence to its picture.

script.say: "Each story on this page is told in four sentences, but the sentences are out of order. Read them. Number them 1 to 4 in the order things happen. Then draw a line from each sentence to its picture."
script.first: Read the four sentences of the first story aloud. Ask, "What happens first? How do you know?" Write 1 next to it, then 2, 3, and 4 together. Then draw a line from each sentence to its picture.
script.stuck: Read the sentences to the child and ask which one could be the beginning. Have the child tell the story aloud in the order of the numbers; if it makes sense, the order is right. The pictures help: look at what changes from one to the next.

blocks.title: Syllable Division
blocks.instruction: Say each picture word and clap its parts. Draw one scoop under every syllable you hear.

script.say: "Words have parts called syllables. Say each picture word and clap its parts. Then draw one scoop under the word for every syllable you hear."
script.first: Name all the pictures together. Clap the first word together and count the claps. Show on the board how to draw a scoop, a little curved line, under each part of the word.
script.stuck: Have the child put a hand under the chin and say the word at normal speed: the chin drops once for each syllable. The number of drops is the number of scoops.

blocks.title: Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow
blocks.instruction: A verb tells when: yesterday I walked, today I walk, tomorrow I will walk. Write the missing verbs. Then circle the verb that fits.

script.say: "A verb tells when something happens: yesterday I walked, today I walk, tomorrow I will walk. Write the missing verbs. Then circle the verb that fits the time word in each sentence."
script.first: Write walked, walk, will walk under Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow on the board. Do the first row on the page together. For the second part, read the first sentence aloud and look for the time word: yesterday, today, or tomorrow.
script.stuck: Ask, "Did it happen already, is it happening now, or will it happen later?" Already: add -ed. Later: will.

blocks.title: Square by Square
blocks.instruction: Each object sits on unit squares. Count them and write the length.

script.say: "Each picture sits on a row of squares. Count the squares from one end of the picture to the other, and write the length."
script.first: Do the first one together: put a finger on the square under the start of the picture and count each square to the end. Write the number in the box. Tell the children to count only the squares under the picture.
script.stuck: Have the child make a small mark in each square while counting it.

blocks.title: Teen Numbers on Two Ten-Frames
blocks.instruction: Count what is in the two ten-frames. Write the number, then finish the number sentence.

script.say: "A teen number is ten and some more. One ten-frame holds ten. Count what is in the two ten-frames and write the number. Then finish the number sentence: ten plus how many more."
script.first: Do the first one together: point to the full ten-frame and say, "That is ten." Count on with the second frame: "eleven, twelve…" Write the number. Then read the sentence: "Twelve equals ten plus…" and write how many are in the second frame.
script.stuck: Have the child start at ten for the full frame and count on, touching each dot in the second frame.

blocks.title: Help the Bee Pick Up Every Sunflower
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

blocks.title: Prices at the Market
blocks.instruction: Look at each price tag. Circle the coins that pay the price exactly. Then circle the one in each pair that costs more.

script.say: "Each thing at the market has a price tag. Circle the coins that pay the price exactly. Then circle the one that costs more."
script.first: Look at the coins at the top together and name each coin and what it is worth: a penny is 1 cent, a nickel 5 cents, a dime 10 cents, a quarter 25 cents. Do the first thing together: read its price, start with the biggest coin that fits, and count on aloud as you circle each coin. Some coins are left over. Then read the two prices in "Which costs more?" and circle the bigger one.
script.stuck: Have the child find each coin of the tray in the coins at the top. Start with the biggest coin that fits, add the next coin that still fits, and count on aloud until you reach the price.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 28
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 28
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 28 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 1 More, 1 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 1 less and the number that is 1 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 1 less. On the right, write the number that is 1 more."
script.first: Write 1 to 100 in rows of ten on the board, or point to the class hundred chart. Do the first one together: find the number, step one back for 1 less and one on for 1 more.
script.stuck: Have the child count aloud up to the number and say the next one: that is 1 more. The one said just before it is 1 less.

blocks.title: Read and Color
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence carefully. Then color exactly the pictures it tells you to.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read each sentence, then do exactly what it says."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud together, pointing to each word. Ask: "What does the sentence tell us to do?" Do it together. Then the children read the other sentences on their own.
script.stuck: Point to the word the child cannot read and say its first sound; if that is not enough, read the word. Then have the child read the whole sentence again and tell you what it asks for before starting.

blocks.title: Sort the Rhymes
blocks.instruction: Say each picture in the bank. Find the big picture it rhymes with and write its word on a line under that picture.

script.say: "Rhyming words sound the same at the end, like cat and hat. At the top of the page are small pictures. Say each one, find the big picture it rhymes with, and write its word on a line under that big picture."
script.first: Name the big pictures and the small pictures in the bank together, so that everyone uses the same words (they are below). Take the first small picture: say it with each big picture and ask which one rhymes. Write its word on a line under that big picture.
script.stuck: Say the small picture with each big picture and stretch the endings. For your own reference, the rhyming families are pie, tie, eye; bear, pear, chair; bat, hat, cat.

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence
blocks.instruction: The words are mixed up. Put them in order and write the sentence on the line with a capital letter and an end mark.

script.say: "The words of these sentences got mixed up. Your job is to put them back in order and write the sentence. Every sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with an end mark: a period, a question mark, or an exclamation point."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: Which Purse Has More?
blocks.instruction: Count the money in both purses. Circle the purse that has more.

script.say: "Each row has two purses. Count the money in each purse. Circle the purse that has more."
script.first: Draw the four coins on the board with their value: a quarter is 25 cents, a dime is 10, a nickel is 5, and a penny is 1. Do the first row together: count each purse, biggest coin first, and write the two amounts next to it. Circle the purse with more.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each coin, biggest number first, and say the running total. A child who counts the coins and not the cents (three coins are "3") should read the number on each coin aloud first. If the classroom has play coins, let the child lay them out.

blocks.title: Number Line to 100: Counting by Tens
blocks.instruction: The tick marks count by tens. Count by tens to each arrow and write the number.

script.say: "On this page we count by fives: 5, 10, 15, 20. Some numbers are missing. Count by fives and write each missing number. Be careful: the rows do not all start at 5."
script.first: Count by fives to 100 aloud together, twice. Do the first row on the board: read the first number, count on by fives, and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number comes here?" Write it in.
script.stuck: Have the child whisper the count by fives from the first number of the row. Numbers you say when you count by fives end in 5 or in 0; if the child's number ends in something else, count the row together.

blocks.title: Draw It Twice as Big
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big.

script.say: "Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big."
script.first: Find the top-left colored square on the small grid together and count which row and which column it is in. Find the same row and column on the big grid and color that square. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Animal Coverings
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to its body covering.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Fur, Feathers, and Scales. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "What covers this animal's body: fur, feathers, or scales?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. Fur is soft hair, feathers have a stem with soft sides, and scales are small, hard plates on the skin.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 29
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 29
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 29 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: The Month Before and After
blocks.instruction: One month is given in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it.

script.say: "Each box has one month in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it."
script.first: Say the months of the year aloud together, twice, and write them on the board in order. Do the first box together: find the month on the board and read the month on its left and on its right. Write them.
script.stuck: Have the child find the month on the board and put a finger on it: one step back is before, one step on is after. After December comes January again.

blocks.title: Find the Answer in the Story
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then finish the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then finish the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Long or Short Vowel?
blocks.instruction: Say each word. Is the colored vowel sound long or short? Circle the line if it is long. Circle the curve if it is short.

script.say: "Say each word. Listen to the colored vowel. Does it say its name, like the a in rake? That is a long vowel: circle the line. Does it make its short sound, like the a in bag? Circle the curve."
script.first: Write rake and bag on the board and say both: "rake, a says its name: long. bag, a says /a/: short." Read the words on the page aloud together. Do the first one together and circle the line or the curve.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and hold the vowel. Then say the letter's name: if the word says the name, it is long. For your own reference: long: flute, goat, cube, face; short: rock, sack, hen, shrimp.

blocks.title: Capital Letter or Small Letter?
blocks.instruction: Names and the days of the week start with a capital letter. Other words do not, unless they start the sentence.

script.say: "Names of people and pets, and the days of the week, start with a capital letter. Other words do not, unless they start the sentence. In each sentence, circle the word that is written the right way."
script.first: Write "Monday" and "monday" on the board and ask which is right. Read the first sentence aloud with both choices: "On Monday, or monday, we have a test." Circle Monday together. Read each sentence aloud with the class before they choose. Then read the second part of the page together.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is this word a name, a day, or a month? Does it start the sentence?" If yes, it gets a capital letter.

blocks.title: The Tallest Bar
blocks.instruction: Look at the bars. Circle the one with the most.

script.say: "Look at the bars. A taller bar means more. Circle the one with the most."
script.first: Hold up the page and point to each bar. Ask, "Which bar is the tallest?" Put a finger on its top and read its number on the side. Circle the picture of that bar together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the top of the bar and move it straight across to the numbers. The child may also count the boxes in the bar from the bottom up.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 0 to 30
blocks.instruction: Count on to 30. Write the number each arrow points to.

script.say: "Each arrow points to a mark on the number line. Count on from the number before it and write the number the arrow points to."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Count the marks with the class from 0, one by one, up to the arrow. Write that number. Tell the children that not every mark has its number written; they count the marks between.
script.stuck: Have the child find the last printed number before the arrow, put a finger on it, and count each mark up to the arrow.

blocks.title: Picture Pairs: Find the Difference
blocks.instruction: Each row shows the same close-up twice; circle the one place that is different in the right picture and check the box of that row.

script.say: "Each row shows the same picture two times, but one place in the right picture is different. Circle it, and check the box of that row."
script.first: Do the first row together: compare the left and the right picture, part by part, and find the one difference. Circle it in the right picture and check the box of the row.
script.stuck: Have the child cover half of each picture with a hand and compare one half at a time.

blocks.title: Saving for a Goal
blocks.instruction: Color one part of the jar for each week the child saves. Write how many weeks it takes. Circle why the child saved.

script.say: "The child in the story saves one dollar each week. Color one part of the jar for each week until the jar is full. Then answer the questions and circle why the child saved."
script.first: Read the story aloud and ask, "How much does the child save each week? How much does the thing cost?" Color one part together and say, "One week, one dollar." Count the weeks aloud as you color. The number of colored parts is the number of weeks. If the page asks for the child's own goal, it costs $20 or less, and any goal is right.
script.stuck: Color one part with the child and say, "One week, one dollar." Keep going, one part at a time, until the jar is full. Then count the colored parts together.

packs.title: First Grade Sub Plans: Week 30
packs.metaTitle: First Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 30
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 30 of first grade: 8 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Bonds Within 10
blocks.instruction: Look at each number bond. Write the missing number in the dashed circle.

script.say: "A number bond shows a number and the two parts that make it. The whole is on top, and the two parts are below. One number is missing. Find it and write it in the dashed circle."
script.first: Draw the first number bond on the board. Point to the top circle and say, "This is the whole." Point to the two circles below: "These are the two parts." Show it with fingers: "The whole is 5. One part is 2. How many are in the other part?" Write the answer in the dashed circle.
script.stuck: Have the child draw dots: as many as the whole. Cross out as many as the part that is shown and count what is left. If the whole is the number that is missing, count both parts together.

blocks.title: Word Family Carpet: Read and Color
blocks.instruction: Read every word on the carpet out loud. Then find each picture's word on the carpet and color that word in the picture's color.

script.say: "The carpet at the top has rows of words. Each row is a word family: the words end the same. Read every word out loud. Then find each picture's word on the carpet and color it."
script.first: Read the carpet aloud together, one row at a time. Name the first picture and find its word together. Color it. Tell the children to say the picture word, then look in the row whose words end the same way.
script.stuck: Have the child name the picture and say its first sound, then look for the word that begins with that letter. If two words begin the same way, have the child read both to the end.

blocks.title: Opposites: Write the Opposite Word
blocks.instruction: Read the word on each card. Find its opposite in the word bank and write it on the line.

script.say: "Read the word on each card. Find its opposite in the word bank and write it on the line."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud. Read the first card together and ask, "What is the opposite of day?" Find night in the bank and write it on the line.
script.stuck: Act the word out for the child, or ask, "What is the other end of this word?"

blocks.title: Plan a True Story
blocks.instruction: Time words like first, next, and last tell the order of a story.

script.say: "Time words like first, next, and last tell the order of a story. First read the little story and circle its time words. Then plan your own true story in the boxes."
script.first: Read the story on the page aloud and circle the time words together: first, then, last. Do the numbering part together. For the plan, let a few children say an idea: a rainy day, something new they learned. Each child draws and writes a few words in each box: First, Next, Last, and how they felt.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "What did you do first? And then?" Write one word for the child to copy, or let the child draw and label.

blocks.title: Square by Square
blocks.instruction: Each object sits on unit squares. Count them and write the length.

script.say: "Each picture sits on a row of squares. Count the squares from one end of the picture to the other, and write the length."
script.first: Do the first one together: put a finger on the square under the start of the picture and count each square to the end. Write the number in the box. Tell the children to count only the squares under the picture.
script.stuck: Have the child make a small mark in each square while counting it.

blocks.title: Where Does the Piece Go?
blocks.instruction: Read the numbers on each piece, find its place on the empty chart and write them in.

script.say: "Each puzzle piece is cut from a hundreds chart. Read the numbers on each piece, find where it fits on the empty chart, and write the numbers in."
script.first: Point to the empty chart and read the numbers that are printed on it. Take the first piece together: read its numbers and ask, "Where is 28 on the chart?" Count along the row to find it and write the numbers of the piece in.
script.stuck: Have the child find the tens of the number first: 28 is in the row of the 20s. Then count along the row.

blocks.title: Bring the Fish to the Coral Safely
blocks.instruction: Help the polar bear get to the igloo. Do not take a road with a walrus or a hole in the ice.

script.say: "Help the animal get home safely. Look at the whole maze first. Do not take a road with one of the dangers the page names."
script.first: Read the title aloud and show the start and the goal. Point to the dangers on the page and say that a road with a danger is closed. Trace a way with your finger and stop at each fork: "Is there a danger on this road?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: What Animals Eat
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Plant Eaters and Meat Eaters. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "What does this animal eat: plants or other animals?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 1
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 1
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 1 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Addition Practice to 20
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: adding with numbers up to 20. Do the ones you know first. Then go back to the others."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board. Ask how the children got their answers and accept every way that gives the right answer: counting on from the bigger number, making ten, or just knowing it.
script.stuck: Have the child start at the bigger number and count on the smaller one with fingers: for 13 + 6, say "13" and count on six more. Drawing dots is fine, too, even though the page says to solve the problems in your head.

blocks.title: Read and Do: Two-Step Instructions
blocks.instruction: Each sentence tells you two things to do. Read it to the end before you start, then do both steps in the row of pictures.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read each sentence, then do exactly what it says."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud together, pointing to each word. Ask: "What does the sentence tell us to do?" Do it together. Then the children read the other sentences on their own.
script.stuck: Point to the word the child cannot read and say its first sound; if that is not enough, read the word. Then have the child read the whole sentence again and tell you what it asks for before starting.

blocks.title: Digraphs in Sentences: Circle and Count sh
blocks.instruction: Read the sentences. Circle every sh. Write how many you found in each sentence in its box.

script.say: "Read the sentences. Circle every letter team the title names. Write how many you found in each sentence in its box."
script.first: Read the letter team in the title aloud and say its sound. Read the first sentence aloud together and circle every one of that letter team; count them and write the number in the box.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger under each word and look for the two letters of the title right next to each other. Read the sentence to a child who cannot read it; the task is to find the letters. One of the two letters alone does not count.

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence: No Clues
blocks.instruction: There is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line.

script.say: "The words of each sentence are mixed up, and there is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence with a capital letter and a period."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: Number Walls
blocks.instruction: Each brick is the sum of the two bricks under it. Fill in the missing numbers.

script.say: "This is a number wall. Each brick is the sum of the two bricks right under it. Start at the bottom and build every wall to the top."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks that sit side by side in the bottom row and to the brick that rests on both of them: "Three plus two is five. Five goes on top." Fill in that wall together.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers with fingers or dots. If the child writes the sum next to the bricks and not above them, point to the brick that touches both.

blocks.title: Find the Missing Part: Story Problems
blocks.instruction: Read each story. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the missing part. Write an equation. Then write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the missing part. Then write the equation and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "Do we know the whole? Which part do we know?" Write the numbers in the bar together and a question mark in the missing part. Solve it together.
script.stuck: Draw the bar with the child: the whole on top, the parts below. Put the numbers of the story where they belong.

blocks.title: Road Safety Quiz: Which Sign Fits?
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and circle the one road sign that fits it.

script.say: "Read each sentence. Circle the one road sign that fits it."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud and look at the three signs next to it. Ask, "Which sign tells drivers about this?" Circle it together. Read each sentence aloud for children who need it.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and name the three signs; ask which one would help in that place.

blocks.title: Find 10 Differences: In the Park
blocks.instruction: Circle the 10 differences, 5 in each pair of pictures, and check a box under the pair for every one you find.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle with two pairs of pictures. In each pair, the picture on the right is different in 5 places. Circle each difference, and check a box under the pair for every one you find."
script.first: Find one difference in the top pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Circle it in the picture on the right and check off one box.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom. Things can be missing, added, or changed.

blocks.title: Which Face Shows the Feeling?
blocks.instruction: Read the feeling word and circle the one face in the row that shows it.

script.say: "Each row has a feeling word and three faces. Circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Read every feeling word on the page aloud: tired, angry, happy, scared, surprised, sad. Make each face for the class. Do the first row together: read the word, look at the three faces, and circle the one that matches.
script.stuck: Read the word for the child and make the face. Ask the child to point to the face on the page that looks like yours.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 2
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 2
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 2 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number of the Day: Up to 99
blocks.instruction: Show a two-digit number in tens and ones, then fill every box.

script.say: "Look at the big number: it is the number of the day. Show it in tens and ones, and fill in every box on the page."
script.first: Read the number of the day aloud together. Go around the page and read the label of each box aloud, so that the children know what each one asks for. Fill in the tens and ones box together: "How many tens are in this number? How many ones?" The children do the other boxes on their own.
script.stuck: Read the label of the box to the child again. Have the child build the number with ten fingers and some more, or draw a row of ten dots and the extra ones. A child who cannot finish every box should do the ones they know.

blocks.title: Fill-in-the-Blank Sentences
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Find the word that fits the sentence in the word bank and write it in the box.

script.say: "Each sentence is missing a word. The words are in the word bank at the top, and each sentence has a picture. Find the word that fits and write it in the box."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together. Read the first sentence aloud and say "blank" at the gap. Look at its picture and ask, "Which word fits?" Write it in the box together.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with the child, one word at a time, and say "blank" at the gap. Look at the picture together and find its word in the bank.

blocks.title: Vowel Teams for Long a, e, and o
blocks.instruction: ai and ay spell long a. ee and ea spell long e. oa and ow spell long o.

script.say: "Two vowels together can make one long sound. Ai and ay spell long a, ee and ea spell long e, oa and ow spell long o. Read each word and write it under its vowel sound."
script.first: Write rain, play, feet, eat, boat, and snow on the board and read them. Read the first word on the page together, find its vowel team, and write it under its sound.
script.stuck: Have the child find the two vowels together and say the long sound they make.

blocks.title: Joining Words: and, but, so, because
blocks.instruction: A joining word puts two sentences together. Circle the one that fits best in each sentence. Then join two sentences and write them as one.

script.say: "A joining word puts two sentences together. And adds one more thing. But tells something you did not expect. So tells what happened because of it. Circle the joining word that fits best in each sentence."
script.first: Read the box with the three joining words aloud. Read the first sentence aloud three times, once with each joining word, and ask which one makes the most sense. Circle it. For the last part, read the two sentences together and join them on the lines.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with each joining word for the child and ask, "Which one sounds right?" For but, ask, "Is the second part a surprise?"

blocks.title: Fact Family Houses to 20
blocks.instruction: Use the three numbers on the roof. Complete the four related facts.

script.say: "The three numbers on the roof are a family. They make four facts: two adding and two taking away. Use the three numbers to finish all four facts in each house."
script.first: Draw a house on the board with 3, 7, and 10 on the roof. Write the four facts together: 3 + 7 = 10, 7 + 3 = 10, 10 − 3 = 7, 10 − 7 = 3. Point out that the biggest number is the whole: it comes after the equals sign when we add and first when we take away.
script.stuck: Have the child find the biggest number on the roof and circle it: that is the whole. The other two are the parts. Adding the parts makes the whole; taking a part away from the whole leaves the other part.

blocks.title: Hundreds Chart Puzzle Pieces: Fill In the Numbers
blocks.instruction: One number is printed on each piece. Write every missing number: 1 more to the right, 1 less to the left, 10 more below, 10 less above.

script.say: "Each puzzle piece is a part of a hundreds chart. One number is printed on each piece. Write every missing number: 1 more to the right, 1 less to the left, 10 more below, 10 less above."
script.first: Draw a small piece on the board with 76 in it. Ask, "What is right of 76? One more: 77. Left? 75. Below? Ten more: 86. Above? 66." Fill the boxes together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the rule for the box: right is one more, left is one less, down is ten more, up is ten less.

blocks.title: Laws in Our Community
blocks.instruction: Read each law. Write the letter of the problem the law stops. Use each letter one time.

script.say: "Each law stops a problem: read each law and write the letter of the problem it stops."
script.first: Say, "A law is a rule for everyone in a community." Read the problems in the box at the top aloud, with their letters. Read the first law aloud and look at its picture together: it shows people keeping the law. Ask, "What could happen if no one kept this law?" Find that problem in the box and write its letter together. If your page says "Use each letter one time," each problem goes with one law. If your page asks why our community needs one law, any true reason is right.
script.stuck: Read the law with the child and ask, "What could go wrong if no one kept this law?" Then read the problems one at a time and ask, "Is it this one?"

blocks.title: Help the Orangutan Find the Banana Tree
blocks.instruction: Look at the whole maze first. Then draw the orangutan's way to the banana tree.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Beginning, Middle and End of a Story
blocks.instruction: Look at the beginning and the end of each story and draw what happens in the middle frame.

script.say: "Each story on this page has a beginning and an end, but the middle is missing. Look at what is different between the first picture and the last one. Then draw what happens in the middle."
script.first: Do the first story together: look at the first picture and the last one and ask, "What changed? What must have happened in between?" Let two or three children say their ideas. Each child draws their own middle picture; many drawings can be right.
script.stuck: Ask the child: "What is here at the beginning? What is different at the end? What did someone do to make that happen?" Any drawing that leads from the first picture to the last is right; it does not have to be neat.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 3
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 3
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 3 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 10 More, 10 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 10 less and the number that is 10 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 10 less. On the right, write the number that is 10 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "Ten more: which digit changes, the tens or the ones?" Show that only the tens digit changes, one more ten for ten more and one less ten for ten less. Count by tens from another number together, for example 7, 17, 27, 37.
script.stuck: If the classroom has a hundreds chart, have the child find the number on it: the number straight above is 10 less, and the number straight below is 10 more. Without a chart, have the child cover the ones digit and change the tens digit by one.

blocks.title: Find the Answer in the Story
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then finish the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then finish the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Nouns, Verbs, and Adjectives
blocks.instruction: Read every word. Is it a noun (naming word), a verb (action word), or an adjective (describing word)? Write it in the right bin.

script.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing. A verb is something you can do. An adjective tells what something is like. Read every word and write each one in the right bin."
script.first: Read all the words on the page aloud with the class. Do the first two words together: "Is it a naming word, an action word, or a describing word?" Write each in its bin.
script.stuck: Read the word to the child and try three test sentences aloud: "I see a ___." (a noun), "I can ___." (a verb), "It is ___." (an adjective). The one that sounds right tells the bin. For your own reference, on this page the nouns are skateboard, girl, dinosaur, and ball; the verbs swim, throw, sit, and jump; the adjectives blue, wet, tall, and fast.

blocks.title: Fix the Sentence: Capital and End Mark
blocks.instruction: Rewrite each sentence with a capital letter and the right end mark.

script.say: "Each sentence lost its capital letter and its end mark. Write it again with a capital letter at the start and the right end mark: a period or a question mark."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud. Ask, "Does it tell or ask?" Write it on the board with a capital letter and the right end mark together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the first word, then on every name, then on the end of the sentence, and ask at each place, "Capital letter? End mark?" The three small pictures above the first sentence show the three things to check.

blocks.title: More Than Nine of a Kind
blocks.instruction: Count the blocks. Ten ones make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Write the number.

script.say: "Count the blocks in each picture. Ten small cubes make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Write the number they show."
script.first: Draw a flat (a hundred), two rods, and four small cubes on the board. Count together: "one hundred, one hundred ten, one hundred twenty, and four more: one hundred twenty-four." Tell the children that when there are ten or more cubes of one kind, they bundle ten into the next place. Do the first picture together.
script.stuck: Have the child count each kind first: hundreds, tens, ones. If there are more than nine ones, circle ten of them: that is one more ten.

blocks.title: Number Line to 100: Counting by Fives
blocks.instruction: The tick marks count by fives, up to 100. Write the number each arrow points to.

script.say: "The tick marks count by fives, up to 100. Write the number each arrow points to."
script.first: Count by fives to 100 together. Draw the first line on the board and count the marks from the nearest printed number: "50, 55, 60." Write the number at the arrow.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the printed number before the arrow and count on by fives, one mark at a time.

blocks.title: Local, State and National Government
blocks.instruction: Read each leader card. Write each leader in the right box: local, state or national.

script.say: "Write each leader in the right box: local, state, or national."
script.first: Read the sentence at the top and the names of the three boxes aloud: our country, our state, our town or city. The boxes sit inside each other, so write each leader in the smallest box it fits. Say, "The mayor leads a town or city. The governor leads a state. The president leads our whole country." Do the first leader card together. On the line "Our state is," the children write the name of our state. If your page has the city council and Congress, say, "Both are groups of people who make laws: the city council for a town or city, Congress for our whole country." If the page asks for one job of each level, any true job is right.
script.stuck: Read the leader card with the child and ask, "Does this leader lead a town or city, a state, or the whole country?" Then point to the box with that name.

blocks.title: Copy the Picture Using Letters and Numbers
blocks.instruction: Use the letter and number of each square to copy the picture.

script.say: "Use the letter and number of each square to copy the picture onto the empty grid."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Find one colored square together, say its letter and number, and color the same square on the empty grid. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 4
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 4
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 4 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot: Count by Fives
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Count by fives from 5 to 50 and connect the dots. Part of the picture is already drawn.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot, and you count by fives. Start at the orange dot at 5. Draw a line to 10, then to 15, and keep going to 50."
script.first: Count by fives from 5 to 50 together. Find the orange dot at 5 together and draw the line to 10. Part of the picture is already drawn; the dots finish it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and add five; that is the dot to look for. The numbers in the row at the bottom can be crossed off one by one.

blocks.title: Characters, Setting, and Events
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write who is in it, where it takes place, and what happens.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write who is in it, where it takes place, and what happens."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Short or Long Vowel?
blocks.instruction: A short vowel says its sound: hop. A long vowel says its name: hope.

script.say: "A short vowel says its sound: hop. A long vowel says its name: hope. Read each word and write it under short vowel or long vowel."
script.first: Write hop and hope on the board and read them. Point out the e at the end and the two vowels together that often make a long sound, like ee and ay. Read the first word on the page together and decide.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and hold the vowel. Then say the letter's name: if the word says the name, it is long.

blocks.title: Match the Verb to Its Past Tense
blocks.instruction: Read each verb on the left. Draw a line to its past tense (the yesterday form) on the right — one line for each verb.

script.say: "Read each verb on the left. Draw a line to its past tense, the yesterday form, on the right."
script.first: Write jump and jumped on the board: "Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped." Read the first verb aloud and find its yesterday form together. Some verbs change: sing, sang.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud with the verb and listen. If the sentence has "yesterday," the verb tells about the past (jumped). With one person and "today" or "every day," the verb gets an s (runs, sings).

blocks.title: Mental Math to 100
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Think of the tens and the ones. Write the answer in the box.

script.say: "Solve each problem in your head. Think of the tens and the ones. Write the answer in the box."
script.first: Write 36 + 6 on the board. Say, "36 is 3 tens and 6 ones. 6 and 6 make 12, so we get one more ten: 42." Do one taking away ten: 46 − 10 = 36: "only the tens change." Then the children work on their own.
script.stuck: Have the child say the tens and the ones of the first number. For adding or taking away tens, only the tens digit changes; for ones, count on or back from the number.

blocks.title: Counting Money: All the Coins
blocks.instruction: Count the coins. Write how much money there is in all.

script.say: "Each box has coins in it. The number on a coin tells you how many cents it is worth. Count how much money is in each box and write the amount."
script.first: Draw the four coins on the board with their value: a quarter is 25 cents, a dime is 10, a nickel is 5, and a penny is 1. Do the first box together: start with the coin that is worth the most and count on: "25, 50… 55, 60." Write the amount in the box in front of the cent sign.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each coin, biggest number first, and say the running total. A child who counts the coins and not the cents (three coins are "3") should read the number on each coin aloud first. If the classroom has play coins, let the child lay them out.

blocks.title: Services Our Government Provides
blocks.instruction: Circle every service of the government in the town. Then write who two of them help.

script.say: "Circle every government service in the town: work the town, the state, or the country does for everyone."
script.first: Read the sentence at the top aloud. Look at the town together and read its signs. A school, a park, a library, a fire station, road work, and a mail carrier are government services; a store that sells things is a business, so it gets no circle, and the house gets no circle either. Ask about the first place, "Is it for everyone, or does it sell things?" and circle together. If your page asks who a service helps, any true answer is right, such as "The library helps kids who want books."
script.stuck: Point to one place at a time and ask, "Can everyone use it, or does it sell things to make money?" If your page shows a mail carrier, point to it: it has no sign.

blocks.title: Treasure Hunt: Follow the Steps
blocks.instruction: Start at the flag. Follow the steps. Circle the picture where you land.

script.say: "Start at the flag on the grid. Follow the steps, one at a time: each step says which way to move and how many squares. Circle the picture where you land."
script.first: Put your finger on the flag and read the first step aloud: "Move 1 square right." Move the finger together and stop. Read the next step and move again. Tell the children to count the squares, not the lines, and to keep the finger on the page until the last step.
