script.stuck: Have the child say each step aloud and point with a finger. Check right and left: "Which hand is your right hand? Move that way."

blocks.title: The Month Before and After
blocks.instruction: One month is given in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it.

script.say: "Each box has one month in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it."
script.first: Say the months of the year aloud together, twice, and write them on the board in order. Do the first box together: find the month on the board and read the month on its left and on its right. Write them.
script.stuck: Have the child find the month on the board and put a finger on it: one step back is before, one step on is after. After December comes January again.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 5
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 5
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 5 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: ABC Order: Number Them, Then Write Them
blocks.instruction: Number the cards, then copy the words onto the lines in order.

script.say: "We are going to put words in ABC order, the order of the alphabet."
script.first: Point to the alphabet strip at the top of the page. Read the four words on the cards aloud with the class. Ask, "Which word starts with the letter that comes first in the alphabet?" Write a 1 on its card together. The children number the other cards and then copy the words onto the lines in that order.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the alphabet strip and slide along it, stopping at the first letter that starts one of the words. That word is next. Cross out each word once it has a number.

blocks.title: Retell the Story and Tell Its Lesson
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end. Use the word bank. Then circle the lesson.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, using the word bank. Then circle the lesson of the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Parts of Speech: Sort Twelve Words
blocks.instruction: No pictures to help. Read each word and sort it into a bin.

script.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing. A verb is something you can do. An adjective tells what something is like. Read the twelve words and write each one in the right bin."
script.first: Read all twelve words aloud with the class. Do the first two words together: "Is it a noun, a verb, or an adjective?" Write each in its bin.
script.stuck: Read the word to the child and try three test sentences aloud: "I see a ___." (a noun), "I can ___." (a verb), "It is ___." (an adjective). The one that sounds right tells the bin. For your own reference, on this page the nouns are persimmon, kiwi, blueberry, and raspberry; the verbs run, climb, read, and catch; the adjectives hot, brave, shiny, and purple.

blocks.title: Who Is He? Pronouns in Sentences
blocks.instruction: Read the sentences. Draw a line from each word in a box to the name it stands for.

script.say: "Read the sentences. A pronoun like he, she, or they takes the place of a name. Draw a line from each word in a box to the name it stands for."
script.first: Read the first sentences aloud together. Point to the first word in a box and ask, "Who is she?" Draw the line to that name.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence again with the name in place of the word in the box. He goes to a boy's name, she to a girl's, and they to two or more names; if the sentence still makes sense, the line is right.

blocks.title: Expanded Form Both Ways
blocks.instruction: Put the parts together, or break each number into hundreds, tens and ones. Write the numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Every digit in a number is worth something. In 479, the 4 is worth 400, the 7 is worth 70, and the 9 is worth 9. This page goes both ways. When the parts are printed, put them together and write the number in the box. When the number is printed, break it into its hundreds, its tens, and its ones."
script.first: Write 257 on the board and break it up together: 200 + 50 + 7. Then go the other way: 400 + 30 + 2 = 432. Point out that some problems put the parts together and others break the number up. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the number aloud slowly and write what each part says: "two hundred" is 200, "forty" is 40, "two" is 2. A child who writes 2 + 4 + 2 for 242 has copied the digits; point to the first 2 and ask, "Is this 2 ones or 2 hundreds?" The right three parts in another order are still correct.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 0 to 50
blocks.instruction: Count on to each arrow and write its number. Every tenth number is printed to help you.

script.say: "Each arrow points to a mark on the number line. Count on from the number before it and write the number the arrow points to."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Count the marks with the class from 0, one by one, up to the arrow. Write that number. Tell the children that not every mark has its number written; they count the marks between.
script.stuck: Have the child find the last printed number before the arrow, put a finger on it, and count each mark up to the arrow.

blocks.title: Sort the Animals
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Mammals, Birds, and Reptiles. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Does it have fur, feathers, or scales? Does it lay eggs or feed its babies milk?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. Mammals have fur or hair, birds have feathers, and reptiles have dry scales.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

blocks.title: On the Hour
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour. Circle the time that matches the clock."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board showing 3:00 and say, "The long hand is on the 12, so it is something o'clock. The short hand points to 3: three o'clock." Do the first clock on the page together. Some choices end in :30; check where the long hand points.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 6
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 6
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 6 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 100 More, 100 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 100 less and the number that is 100 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 100 less. On the right, write the number that is 100 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "A hundred more: which digit changes? Which two stay the same?" Show that only the hundreds digit changes. Count by hundreds from another number together.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens and the ones with a finger and look only at the hundreds digit: one less for 100 less, one more for 100 more. The two covered digits are copied as they are.

blocks.title: Read the Facts
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the answer to each question. Finish the sentence.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write the answer to each question by finishing the sentence."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Bossy r: ar and or
blocks.instruction: Bossy r changes the vowel sound: ar says the sound in park, and or says the sound in storm.

script.say: "When r comes after a vowel, it bosses the vowel and changes its sound. A-r says ar, like in park. O-r says or, like in storm. Read each word and write it under ar or or."
script.first: Write park and storm on the board and read them with the class. Read the first word on the page aloud together, listen for ar or or, and write it under its heading. Then read the second part of the page aloud together.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the letter before the r: a-r is ar, o-r is or. Read the word together slowly.

blocks.title: Ask About the Picture: Why and How
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Finish each question. Start with the word already on the line.

script.say: "Look at the four pictures at the top of the page. You are going to ask questions about them. Each line already starts with a question word: Who, What, Where, When, Why, How. Finish each question, and end it with a question mark."
script.first: Name the four pictures together. Make up a question for the first line aloud and write it on the board with its question mark. Ask two children for a question that starts with What. Tell the class that any question that fits one of the pictures and starts with the printed word is right, and that nobody has to answer the questions.
script.stuck: Point to one picture and ask the child what they would like to know about it. Then help the child say it as a question that starts with the printed word: "Who is this? Where is this place? What is it doing?"

blocks.title: More Than Nine of a Kind
blocks.instruction: Count the blocks. Ten ones make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Write the number.

script.say: "Count the blocks in each picture. Ten small cubes make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Write the number they show."
script.first: Draw a flat (a hundred), two rods, and four small cubes on the board. Count together: "one hundred, one hundred ten, one hundred twenty, and four more: one hundred twenty-four." Tell the children that when there are ten or more cubes of one kind, they bundle ten into the next place. Do the first picture together.
script.stuck: Have the child count each kind first: hundreds, tens, ones. If there are more than nine ones, circle ten of them: that is one more ten.

blocks.title: Tens in Words: 10 to 100
blocks.instruction: Read the number. Circle the word that matches it.

script.say: "Each number has a word that we read and write. Read the number and circle the word that matches it."
script.first: Write 1 to 20 on the board and the words for a few of them. Do the first one together: read the number, read the three words, and circle the matching one.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number aloud and listen to its first sound; find the word that starts with that letter. Read the words with the child.

blocks.title: Where Do Animals Live?
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to where it lives.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Land, Water, and Air. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Where does this animal spend most of its time: on land, in the water, or in the air?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. An animal that flies lives on land too, so Air and Land are both right for it, and a crab lives in the water and on land, so Water and Land are both right for it, when the child can say why.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Help the Bee Pick Up Every Sunflower
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

blocks.title: How Do You Feel? Circle the Face
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture, think how you would feel, and circle the face that matches.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Think about how it would make you feel. Then circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Look at the first picture together and ask what it shows. Ask, "How does that make you feel?" Let two or three children answer; they may not all feel the same, and that is fine. Each child circles the face that matches their own answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child what the picture shows and when they have seen one. Then point to each face and name the feeling it shows. There is no wrong answer on this page; any face the child can explain is right.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 7
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 7
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 7 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Subtraction Practice to 20
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: subtracting with numbers up to 20. Do the ones you know first. Then go back to the others."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board together and think aloud: "Nine take away five. I count back from nine: eight, seven, six, five, four." Then the children work on their own; tell them to skip a hard one and come back to it.
script.stuck: Have the child count up from the smaller number to the bigger one on fingers: for 17 minus 9, say "9" and count up to 17. Drawing dots and crossing them out is fine, too.

blocks.title: Main Topic and Key Details
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the main topic. Then write two key details from the text.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write what the whole text is about, the main topic, and two key details: facts the text tells about it."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: er, ir, and ur: One Sound, Three Spellings
blocks.instruction: er, ir, and ur say the same sound: her, first, turn.

script.say: "Er, ir, and ur all say the same sound, like in her, first, and turn. Read each word and write it under er, ir, or ur."
script.first: Write her, first, and turn on the board and read them with the class. Read the first word on the page together and look at its letters: which spelling does it use? Write it under that heading. Read the second part of the page aloud together.
script.stuck: Point out that the sound is the same, so the child looks at the letters, not the sound: is it e-r, i-r, or u-r?

blocks.title: The Irregular Verbs: be, have, do, go
blocks.instruction: These verbs change a lot. Write the today form and the yesterday form of each one in the dashed boxes.

script.say: "Be, have, do, and go change a lot. Write the today form and the yesterday form of each one in the dashed boxes. Then finish the sentences."
script.first: Say the verbs with the class: go, goes, went; have, has, had; be, is, was; do, does, did. Do the first row together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud with the verb and listen. If the sentence has "yesterday," the verb tells about the past (jumped). With one person and "today" or "every day," the verb gets an s (runs, sings).

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 40 to 60
blocks.instruction: This line does not start at zero. Count on from the nearest printed number and write the number each arrow points to.

script.say: "These number lines do not start at zero. They start at 40 and go to 60. Each arrow points to a number. Find out which number it is and write it in the box."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Point out that it does not start at zero. Count the small marks from the nearest printed number to the arrow and write the number.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the nearest printed number and count the small marks one by one to the arrow, saying the numbers. An answer such as 3 means the child wrote the number of steps, not the number on the line; an answer that is too small means the child counted from the left end as if it were zero.

blocks.title: What Happened in the Middle? Story Problems
blocks.instruction: Read each story. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the missing number. Write an equation. Then write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Something happened in the middle. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the missing number. Then solve."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "How many at the start? How many at the end? What changed?" Write the numbers in the bar together and solve.
script.stuck: Act the story out with fingers: start with the first number, and ask how many went away or came to make the last number.

blocks.title: North, East, South, West: Label the Four Directions
blocks.instruction: The orange tip on each compass rose points north; write the three missing letters in the empty boxes.

script.say: "The four directions are north, east, south, and west. On these compass roses the orange tip always points north, even when it does not point up. Write the three missing letters in the empty boxes."
script.first: Draw a compass rose on the board: N at the top, S at the bottom, E on the right, W on the left. Say "Never Eat Soggy Waffles" going around clockwise from N. On the page, north is wherever the orange tip points, and on some roses it points down, left, or right. Do the first rose together: put a finger on the orange tip, say "north," then go around clockwise and say east, south, west, writing each missing letter where it falls.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the orange tip and say north, then go around clockwise: east, south, west.

blocks.title: Find 10 Differences: In the Forest
blocks.instruction: Circle the 10 differences, 5 in each pair of pictures, and check a box under the pair for every one you find.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle with two pairs of pictures. In each pair, the picture on the right is different in 5 places. Circle each difference, and check a box under the pair for every one you find."
script.first: Find one difference in the top pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Circle it in the picture on the right and check off one box.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom. Things can be missing, added, or changed.

blocks.title: Beginning, Middle and End of a Story
blocks.instruction: Look at the beginning and the end of each story and draw what happens in the middle frame.

script.say: "Each story on this page has a beginning and an end, but the middle is missing. Look at what is different between the first picture and the last one. Then draw what happens in the middle."
script.first: Do the first story together: look at the first picture and the last one and ask, "What changed? What must have happened in between?" Let two or three children say their ideas. Each child draws their own middle picture; many drawings can be right.
script.stuck: Ask the child: "What is here at the beginning? What is different at the end? What did someone do to make that happen?" Any drawing that leads from the first picture to the last is right; it does not have to be neat.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 8
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 8
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 8 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number of the Day: Ten More, Ten Less
blocks.instruction: Find ten more and ten less than the number of the day.

script.say: "Look at the big number: it is the number of the day. Every box asks something about it: its word, the numbers before and after, ten more and ten less. Fill in all the boxes."
script.first: Read the number of the day aloud together. Go around the page and read the label of each box aloud, so that the children know what each one asks for. Fill in the tens and ones box together: "How many tens are in this number? How many ones?" The children do the other boxes on their own.
script.stuck: Read the label of the box to the child again. Have the child build the number with ten fingers and some more, or draw a row of ten dots and the extra ones. A child who cannot finish every box should do the ones they know.

blocks.title: Read and Check: True or False
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and look at the row of pictures. Is the sentence true or false? Circle the right word.

script.say: "Read each sentence and look at the row of pictures. Is the sentence true or false? Circle the right word."
script.first: Point to the row of pictures and name them together from left to right. Read the first sentence aloud and check it on the row together, counting the pictures from the left. Circle true or false.
script.stuck: Point to the word the child cannot read and say its first sound; if that is not enough, read the word. Then have the child read the whole sentence again and tell you what it asks for before starting.

blocks.title: Bossy r: ar and or
blocks.instruction: Bossy r changes the vowel sound: ar says the sound in park, and or says the sound in storm.

script.say: "When r comes after a vowel, it bosses the vowel and changes its sound. A-r says ar, like in park. O-r says or, like in storm. Read each word and write it under ar or or."
script.first: Write park and storm on the board and read them with the class. Read the first word on the page aloud together, listen for ar or or, and write it under its heading. Then read the second part of the page aloud together.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the letter before the r: a-r is ar, o-r is or. Read the word together slowly.

blocks.title: Possessive Pronouns
blocks.instruction: Look at who owns the thing. Circle the word that shows it belongs to that person.

script.say: "Words like his, her, and their tell who something belongs to. Look at who owns the thing in each row. Read the sentence and circle the word that fits: his, her, or their."
script.first: Read the first row aloud and look at who owns the thing. Ask, "Is it a boy's, a girl's, or more than one person's?" Circle his, her, or their together. Read each row aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Have the child count the people in the little picture: one boy takes his, one girl takes her, and two or more people take their, whether they are boys or girls.

blocks.title: Jump Puzzles: Follow the Arrows
blocks.instruction: Start at the number and follow the arrows: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, right is 1 more. Write where you land.

script.say: "Each puzzle starts at a number and has three arrows. Every arrow changes the number: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, and right is 1 more. Follow the arrows and write the number where you land."
script.first: Point to the key at the top of the page and read it aloud together. Do the first puzzle on the board, one arrow at a time, and write the number after each arrow: for example, "30, one less is 29, ten more is 39, one less is 38."
script.stuck: Have the child write the new number above each arrow before going on to the next one. If the classroom has a hundreds chart, the child can put a finger on the starting number and move one square for each arrow.

blocks.title: True or False?
blocks.instruction: Is each equation true? Circle the check mark if it is true and the X if it is false.

script.say: "Is each number sentence true? If both sides are the same amount, it is true: circle the check mark. If not, it is false: circle the X."
script.first: Write 10 − 2 = 8 on the board and ask, "Is ten take away two eight? Yes: true." Write 9 = 5 + 6 and ask, "Is five and six nine? No: false." Remind the children that the equals sign means "the same as" and can be on either side.
script.stuck: Have the child work out the side with the plus or minus sign and then compare it with the number on the other side.

blocks.title: Label the Continents
blocks.instruction: Write the name of each numbered continent on its line. Use the names in the box.

script.say: "The map shows the seven continents, each with a number. Write the name of each continent on its line. If your page has a box of names, use it."
script.first: Say the seven names together: North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania, Antarctica (if your page has a box of names, read them from it). Point to North America on the map: "This is where the United States is." Find its number together and write North America on that line. The children do the rest; with a box, they cross out each name when they use it.
script.stuck: Give clues: "Antarctica is the icy one at the bottom. South America is under North America. Africa is the big one in the middle." Let the child find each one on the map.

blocks.title: Bring the Polar Bear Home Safely
blocks.instruction: Help the polar bear get to the igloo. Do not take a road with a walrus or a hole in the ice.

script.say: "Help the animal get home safely. Look at the whole maze first. Do not take a road with one of the dangers the page names."
script.first: Read the title aloud and show the start and the goal. Point to the dangers on the page and say that a road with a danger is closed. Trace a way with your finger and stop at each fork: "Is there a danger on this road?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 9
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 9
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 9 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot: Count by Tens
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Count by tens from 10 to 100 and connect the dots. Part of the picture is already drawn.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot, and you count by tens. Start at the orange dot at 10. Draw a line to 20, then to 30, and keep going to 100."
script.first: Count by tens from 10 to 100 together. Find the orange dot at 10 together and draw the line to 20. Part of the picture is already drawn; the dots finish it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and add ten; that is the dot to look for. The numbers in the row at the bottom can be crossed off one by one.

blocks.title: Fill-in-the-Blank Sentences
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Find the word that fits the sentence in the word bank and write it in the box.

script.say: "Each sentence is missing a word. The words are in the word bank at the top, and each sentence has a picture. Find the word that fits and write it in the box."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together. Read the first sentence aloud and say "blank" at the gap. Look at its picture and ask, "Which word fits?" Write it in the box together.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with the child, one word at a time, and say "blank" at the gap. Look at the picture together and find its word in the bank.

blocks.title: Split the Compound: Find the Two Words
blocks.instruction: The whole word is printed letter by letter next to its picture. Draw one line where the second word starts.

script.say: "A compound word is made of two smaller words, like sun and flower in sunflower. Each word on this page is printed letter by letter. Draw one line where the second word starts."
script.first: Read every word on the page aloud with the class. Then read the first word again and look at its picture. Ask, "Which two words make it?" Draw one line where the second word starts, together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the whole word and clap once for each of the two small words, then cover the end of the word with a finger and move it until a real word shows.

blocks.title: Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow
blocks.instruction: A verb tells when: yesterday I walked, today I walk, tomorrow I will walk. Write the missing verbs. Then circle the verb that fits.

script.say: "A verb tells when something happens: yesterday I walked, today I walk, tomorrow I will walk. Write the missing verbs. Then circle the verb that fits the time word in each sentence."
script.first: Write walked, walk, will walk under Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow on the board. Do the first row on the page together. For the second part, read the first sentence aloud and look for the time word: yesterday, today, or tomorrow.
script.stuck: Ask, "Did it happen already, is it happening now, or will it happen later?" Already: add -ed. Later: will.

blocks.title: Label the Number Line
blocks.instruction: Use the numbers you see to find what the line counts by. Write the missing numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Use the numbers you see to find what the line counts by. Then write the missing numbers in the boxes."
script.first: Draw the first line on the board. Ask, "How far is it from one printed number to the next? How many marks are in between?" Find the step together, then count on to each box.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the nearest printed number and count the small marks one by one to the arrow. An answer such as 3 or 7 means the child counted from the left end as if it were zero; point to the 40.

blocks.title: Find the Mistakes
blocks.instruction: Check each answer. If it is wrong, put an X in the small box and write the right answer in the big box. If it is right, leave both boxes empty.

script.say: "Someone has already solved these problems, but some answers are wrong. Check each one. If it is wrong, put an X in the small box and write the right answer in the big box. If it is right, leave both boxes empty."
script.first: Do the first problem on the board together: solve it yourself and compare with the answer that is printed. "Is it the same? Then leave both boxes empty. If not, an X and the right answer." Tell the children to solve each problem first and only then look at the printed answer.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the printed answer, solve the problem with fingers or a drawing, and then uncover the answer and compare.

blocks.title: How Places Change
blocks.instruction: Circle who changed each place: nature or people. Then write why it changed.

script.say: "Each pair of pictures shows one place before and after: circle who changed it, nature or people."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud and look at its two pictures together. Ask, "What is different? Did people do it, or did nature do it, like the weather or the seasons?" Circle together. Building and planting are things people do. If your page asks why it changed, the sentence tells what happened, so use it to write the reason together. If it asks for a place near our school, any real change the child has seen is right.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and ask, "Would this happen if no people were there?" If yes, nature changed it; if people had to do it, people changed it.

blocks.title: Copy the Picture on an 8 × 8 Grid
blocks.instruction: A bigger grid: find each square by its letter and number, then copy.

script.say: "A bigger grid: find each square by its letter and number, and copy the picture onto the empty grid."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Find one colored square together, say its letter and number, and color the same square on the empty grid. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Half Past What?
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Every clock on this page shows a time that is half past the hour. Read each clock and circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board that shows half past two. Say: "The long hand points to the 6. That means half past. The short hand tells the hour. It has gone past the 2 and is halfway to the 3, so the time is half past two, or 2:30." Do the first clock on the page together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 10
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 10
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 10 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Walls with Two-Digit Answers
blocks.instruction: The numbers go past 20. Add each pair of bricks and write the sum in the brick above.

script.say: "This is a number wall. Each brick is the sum of the two bricks right under it. Start at the bottom and build every wall to the top. The numbers get bigger than twenty, so you may add on paper."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks next to each other at the bottom and add them aloud, tens and ones; write the sum in the brick above them. Tell the children to work up the wall one row at a time.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers on scrap paper, tens and ones. A wrong brick lower down makes every brick above it wrong, so check the rows from the bottom up.

blocks.title: Find the Answer in the Story
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then finish the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then finish the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Find the Root Word
blocks.instruction: Circle the part the three words share and write that root word in the empty stone.

script.say: "The three words on each card are a word family: they are all built from one small word, the root word. Circle the part that all three words share. Then write the root word in the empty stone."
script.first: Read the three words of the first stone aloud. Ask, "Which part do all three words share?" Circle it in each word and write that root word in the empty stone together.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the beginnings and the endings of the words with a finger until a small real word shows. The root word must be a word by itself.

blocks.title: Capital Letter or Small Letter?
blocks.instruction: Names and the days of the week start with a capital letter. Other words do not, unless they start the sentence.

script.say: "Names of people and pets, and the days of the week, start with a capital letter. Other words do not, unless they start the sentence. In each sentence, circle the word that is written the right way."
script.first: Write "Monday" and "monday" on the board and ask which is right. Read the first sentence aloud with both choices: "On Monday, or monday, we have a test." Circle Monday together. Read each sentence aloud with the class before they choose. Then read the second part of the page together.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is this word a name, a day, or a month? Does it start the sentence?" If yes, it gets a capital letter.

blocks.title: Column Addition and Subtraction
blocks.instruction: Add or subtract one place at a time. Start with the ones.

script.say: "Add or subtract one place at a time. Start with the ones, then the tens. Look at the sign of each problem first."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board, one number under the other. Point to the sign: add or take away? Work the ones column first, then the tens, and write each digit under its column.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens column with a finger and add only the ones, then cover the ones and add the tens. Fingers or dots are fine for the small sums.

blocks.title: Bar Models
blocks.instruction: Look at each bar. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "Each bar shows a whole and its two parts. One number is missing. Write the missing number in the box."
script.first: Draw a bar on the board split into two parts, with 60 on top as the whole and 20 in one part. Ask, "What goes with 20 to make 60?" Count on by tens together: 30, 40, 50, 60: forty. Write it in the empty part. Tell the children to check whether the missing number is a part or the whole.
script.stuck: Ask, "Is the whole missing? Then add the two parts. Is a part missing? Then take the other part away from the whole."

blocks.title: Sort by Food Group
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each food to its food group.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Fruits, Vegetables, Grains, and Protein. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Is this a fruit, a vegetable, a grain like bread or pasta, or a protein like eggs, meat, or fish?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. If a food fits two groups, either box is right when the child can say why.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

blocks.title: The Month Before and After
blocks.instruction: One month is given in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it.

script.say: "Each box has one month in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it."
script.first: Say the months of the year aloud together, twice, and write them on the board in order. Do the first box together: find the month on the board and read the month on its left and on its right. Write them.
script.stuck: Have the child find the month on the board and put a finger on it: one step back is before, one step on is after. After December comes January again.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 11
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 11
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 11 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 10 More, 10 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 10 less and the number that is 10 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 10 less. On the right, write the number that is 10 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "Ten more: which digit changes, the tens or the ones?" Show that only the tens digit changes, one more ten for ten more and one less ten for ten less. Count by tens from another number together, for example 7, 17, 27, 37.
script.stuck: If the classroom has a hundreds chart, have the child find the number on it: the number straight above is 10 less, and the number straight below is 10 more. Without a chart, have the child cover the ones digit and change the tens digit by one.

blocks.title: Read and Do: Two-Step Instructions
blocks.instruction: Each sentence tells you two things to do. Read it to the end before you start, then do both steps in the row of pictures.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read each sentence, then do exactly what it says."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud together, pointing to each word. Ask: "What does the sentence tell us to do?" Do it together. Then the children read the other sentences on their own.
script.stuck: Point to the word the child cannot read and say its first sound; if that is not enough, read the word. Then have the child read the whole sentence again and tell you what it asks for before starting.

blocks.title: Synonyms: Circle the Word That Means the Same
blocks.instruction: Read the big word on each card and circle the word under it that means the same.

script.say: "Synonyms are words that mean the same thing, or almost the same, like big and large. Read the big word on each card. Then circle the word under it that means the same."
script.first: Read the big word on the first card and the words under it aloud. Ask, "Which one means the same?" Circle it together. Read the cards aloud with the class before they start.
script.stuck: Read the words of the card to the child and have the child put each one into the same short sentence. The word that keeps the meaning of the sentence is the one to circle.

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence: No Clues
blocks.instruction: There is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line.

script.say: "The words of each sentence are mixed up, and there is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence with a capital letter and a period."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: How Far Apart? Count the Jumps
blocks.instruction: Count how many jumps down and how many jumps right take you from the first number to the second. Write both numbers.

script.say: "Count how many jumps down and how many jumps right take you from the first number to the second. Write both numbers."
script.first: Point to the key: down is 10 more, right is 1 more. Do the first one on the board: from 4 to 35, count the tens: 14, 24, 34: three jumps down; then 35: one jump right.
script.stuck: Have the child count by tens first until the tens digit matches, then by ones.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 0 to 120
blocks.instruction: This line goes past 100. Count by tens to each arrow and write the number.

script.say: "This line goes past 100. Count by tens to each arrow and write the number."
script.first: Count by tens to 120 together. Draw the first line on the board, start at the nearest printed number, and count each mark by ten to the arrow.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the printed number before the arrow and count on by tens, one mark at a time.

blocks.title: Sink or Float?
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each object to the group you think it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Float and Sink. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "If we put this in water, would it float on top or sink to the bottom?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. This page asks what the children think; a child who can say why has done the page well.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Help the Rabbit Find the Cabbage
blocks.instruction: Look at the whole maze first. Then draw the orangutan's way to the banana tree.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: How Do You Feel? Circle the Face
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture, think how you would feel, and circle the face that matches.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Think about how it would make you feel. Then circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Look at the first picture together and ask what it shows. Ask, "How does that make you feel?" Let two or three children answer; they may not all feel the same, and that is fine. Each child circles the face that matches their own answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child what the picture shows and when they have seen one. Then point to each face and name the feeling it shows. There is no wrong answer on this page; any face the child can explain is right.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 12
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 12
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 12 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: ABC Order: When Words Start the Same
blocks.instruction: Two pairs start with the same letter. Use the second letter to order them.

script.say: "Put the words in ABC order. Two pairs of words start with the same letter: then look at the second letter to decide."
script.first: Point to the alphabet strip at the top. Read the six words aloud with the class. Find two words that start with the same letter together and ask, "Which second letter comes first in the alphabet?" Number the words 1 to 6 together, then the children write them in order.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the alphabet strip and slide along it, stopping at the first letter that starts one of the words. That word is next. Cross out each word once it has a number.

blocks.title: Characters, Setting, and Events
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write who is in it, where it takes place, and what happens.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write who is in it, where it takes place, and what happens."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Suffixes -ful, -less, and -ly
blocks.instruction: -ful means full of, and -less means without.

script.say: "A suffix is a word part at the end. -ful means full of, -less means without, and -ly tells how. Circle the base word in each word and underline the suffix. Then match each word to its meaning."
script.first: Write playful on the board: circle play, underline -ful. Ask, "What does playful mean? Full of play." Do the same with toothless. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then add the suffix and ask what the whole word means.

blocks.title: Fix the Sentence: Choose the End Mark
blocks.instruction: Fix the capital letters and the names, and choose the right end mark.

script.say: "These sentences have lost their capital letters and their end marks, and some of them are questions. Write each sentence again on the lines, the right way. Choose the end mark: a period for a sentence that tells something, a question mark for a sentence that asks something."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud. Ask, "Does it tell, ask, or show strong feeling?" Write it on the board with a capital letter at the start, capitals for names, and the right end mark together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud and listen: does it ask something? Then it needs a question mark. Then the child puts a finger on the first word, on every name, and on the end of the sentence, and checks each place.

blocks.title: 2-Digit Column Subtraction
blocks.instruction: Subtract one place at a time. Start with the ones.

script.say: "These subtraction problems are written one number under the other. Subtract one place at a time. Start on the right with the ones. Then subtract the tens."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board, one number under the other. Subtract the ones first, then the tens, and write each digit under its column. Tell the children to check the sign before they start.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens column with a finger and subtract only the ones, then cover the ones and subtract the tens. Counting back on fingers is fine for the small differences.

blocks.title: Story Problems Within 100: Question, Equation, Answer
blocks.instruction: Read each story. If the question is missing, write a question that fits. Then write the equation and the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Write the question if it is missing, then the equation and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "What do we need to find out?" Write the equation on the board together and solve it with tens and ones. Then the children read the other stories on their own.
script.stuck: Read the story with the child and underline the numbers. Ask, "Are things put together, or taken away?" Draw a quick bar to show the parts and the whole.

blocks.title: Family Generations: Oldest to Youngest
blocks.instruction: In each row, write 1, 2 and 3 in the boxes to put the family words in order from the oldest generation to the youngest.

script.say: "In each row there are family words. Write 1, 2, and 3 to put them in order, from the oldest generation to the youngest."
script.first: Talk about a family: grandparents are the oldest generation, then parents, aunts, and uncles, then children like brothers, sisters, and cousins. Read the first row aloud together and ask, "Who is the oldest?" Write 1 under that word, then 2 and 3.
script.stuck: Ask the child about each word: "Is that a grandparent, a parent, or a child?" Grandparents get 1, parents 2, children 3. Every family is different; this page is about the words.

blocks.title: Treasure Hunt: Follow the Steps
blocks.instruction: Start at the flag. Follow the steps. Circle the picture where you land.

script.say: "Start at the flag on the grid. Follow the steps, one at a time: each step says which way to move and how many squares. Circle the picture where you land."
script.first: Put your finger on the flag and read the first step aloud: "Move 1 square right." Move the finger together and stop. Read the next step and move again. Tell the children to count the squares, not the lines, and to keep the finger on the page until the last step.
script.stuck: Have the child say each step aloud and point with a finger. Check right and left: "Which hand is your right hand? Move that way."

blocks.title: Time in Words
blocks.instruction: Read the time in words. Draw a line from each clock to the words that tell its time.

script.say: "Read the times in words. Draw a line from each clock to the words that tell its time."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board at half past three and say, "The long hand is on the 6: half past. The short hand is just past the 3: half past three." Read the words on the page aloud together and match the first clock together. Quarter past means the long hand is on the 3.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 13
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 13
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 13 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 100 More, 100 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 100 less and the number that is 100 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 100 less. On the right, write the number that is 100 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "A hundred more: which digit changes? Which two stay the same?" Show that only the hundreds digit changes. Count by hundreds from another number together.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens and the ones with a finger and look only at the hundreds digit: one less for 100 less, one more for 100 more. The two covered digits are copied as they are.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: The Sandcastle
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. Then read each question and circle the best answer. The answers are in the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Circle the answer together.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask them to put a finger on the sentence in the story that tells the answer. If the child cannot read the story alone, read it with them.

blocks.title: Describing Words in Real Life
blocks.instruction: Describing words tell what real things are like: a warm hat, a cold drink.

script.say: "Describing words tell what real things are like: hot soup, a soft blanket. Read each sentence and do what the page asks."
script.first: Read the first part of the page aloud with the class and do its first item together. Ask, "What is this thing really like? Which word fits?"
script.stuck: Ask the child to think of a real one: "Have you touched one? Is it hard or soft, hot or cold?"

blocks.title: Choose the Right Verb Form
blocks.instruction: Read the sentence. Three forms of the verb are printed under it. Circle the one that fits.

script.say: "Read each sentence. Three forms of the verb are printed under it. Circle the one that fits."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud with each form. Look for a time word like yesterday or every day. Circle the form that fits together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud with the verb and listen. If the sentence has "yesterday," the verb tells about the past (jumped). With one person and "today" or "every day," the verb gets an s (runs, sings).

blocks.title: Number Walls: Start at the Top
blocks.instruction: The top brick is given this time. Work downwards and subtract.

script.say: "The top brick of each wall is given this time. Work downward: the two bricks under a brick add up to it, so take away to find the missing one."
script.first: Draw a small wall on the board with 17 on top and 9 below it. Ask, "9 and what make 17?" Write 8. Tell the children to start where only one brick is missing.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers with fingers or dots. If the child writes the sum next to the bricks and not above them, point to the brick that touches both.

blocks.title: Where Does the Piece Go?
blocks.instruction: Read the numbers on each piece, find its place on the empty chart and write them in.

script.say: "Each puzzle piece is cut from a hundreds chart. Read the numbers on each piece, find where it fits on the empty chart, and write the numbers in."
script.first: Point to the empty chart and read the numbers that are printed on it. Take the first piece together: read its numbers and ask, "Where is 28 on the chart?" Count along the row to find it and write the numbers of the piece in.
script.stuck: Have the child find the tens of the number first: 28 is in the row of the 20s. Then count along the row.

blocks.title: Where Does It Come From?
blocks.instruction: Read each label. Find the country on the map, circle it and draw a line from it to the star.

script.say: "Find the country of each label on the map, circle it, and draw a line from it to the star, the United States."
script.first: Read each thing and its label aloud. Show the star on the map: it is the United States, our country. Do the first label together: find the country's name on the map, follow its short line to the land if it has one, and circle the land, not the name. Then draw a line from that country to the star. If your page asks for one thing in our classroom, first find one or two things together whose label names a country, such as a box of crayons, and read the label aloud; any child who finds no other label uses that one.
script.stuck: Read the label with the child and find the country's name on the map together. Point from the name to the land, then circle the land.

blocks.title: Help the Crab Pick Up Every Shell
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

blocks.title: Beginning, Middle and End of a Story
blocks.instruction: Look at the beginning and the end of each story and draw what happens in the middle frame.

script.say: "Each story on this page has a beginning and an end, but the middle is missing. Look at what is different between the first picture and the last one. Then draw what happens in the middle."
script.first: Do the first story together: look at the first picture and the last one and ask, "What changed? What must have happened in between?" Let two or three children say their ideas. Each child draws their own middle picture; many drawings can be right.
script.stuck: Ask the child: "What is here at the beginning? What is different at the end? What did someone do to make that happen?" Any drawing that leads from the first picture to the last is right; it does not have to be neat.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 14
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 14
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 14 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Addition Practice to 20
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: adding with numbers up to 20. Do the ones you know first. Then go back to the others."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board. Ask how the children got their answers and accept every way that gives the right answer: counting on from the bigger number, making ten, or just knowing it.
script.stuck: Have the child start at the bigger number and count on the smaller one with fingers: for 13 + 6, say "13" and count on six more. Drawing dots is fine, too, even though the page says to solve the problems in your head.

blocks.title: Fill in the Blank Story
blocks.instruction: Read the whole story. The three pictures show the missing words. Write each word from the bank in its box.

script.say: "This page has three short stories with missing words. The three little pictures above each story show the words that are missing. Find each word in the word bank at the top and write it in the box where it makes sense."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud. Read the whole first story aloud with the class and say "blank" at each gap. Look at its pictures and decide together which word goes in each box.
script.stuck: Have the child name the pictures of the story, then read each sentence aloud and try each word in the gap. The spelling is copied from the word bank.

blocks.title: Adjective or Adverb?
blocks.instruction: An adjective tells about a noun. An adverb tells about a verb: how it is done.

script.say: "An adjective tells about a noun: a brave dog. An adverb tells how something is done: the dog ran bravely. Many adverbs end in -ly. Circle the word that fits each sentence, then draw an arrow to the word it tells about."
script.first: Write "a quick fox" and "the fox ran quickly" on the board. Ask which word tells about the fox and which tells how it ran. Read the first sentence on the page aloud with both choices and circle the one that fits together. Read the rule box about words ending in y aloud.
script.stuck: Ask, "Does the word tell about a thing, or about how someone does something?" A thing gets the adjective; how someone does something gets the -ly word.

blocks.title: Ask About the Picture: Why and How
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Finish each question. Start with the word already on the line.

script.say: "Look at the four pictures at the top of the page. You are going to ask questions about them. Each line already starts with a question word: Who, What, Where, When, Why, How. Finish each question, and end it with a question mark."
script.first: Name the four pictures together. Make up a question for the first line aloud and write it on the board with its question mark. Ask two children for a question that starts with What. Tell the class that any question that fits one of the pictures and starts with the printed word is right, and that nobody has to answer the questions.
script.stuck: Point to one picture and ask the child what they would like to know about it. Then help the child say it as a question that starts with the printed word: "Who is this? Where is this place? What is it doing?"

blocks.title: Expanded Form Both Ways
blocks.instruction: Put the parts together, or break each number into hundreds, tens and ones. Write the numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Every digit in a number is worth something. In 479, the 4 is worth 400, the 7 is worth 70, and the 9 is worth 9. This page goes both ways. When the parts are printed, put them together and write the number in the box. When the number is printed, break it into its hundreds, its tens, and its ones."
script.first: Write 257 on the board and break it up together: 200 + 50 + 7. Then go the other way: 400 + 30 + 2 = 432. Point out that some problems put the parts together and others break the number up. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the number aloud slowly and write what each part says: "two hundred" is 200, "forty" is 40, "two" is 2. A child who writes 2 + 4 + 2 for 242 has copied the digits; point to the first 2 and ask, "Is this 2 ones or 2 hundreds?" The right three parts in another order are still correct.

blocks.title: Counting Money: All the Coins
blocks.instruction: Count the coins. Write how much money there is in all.

script.say: "Each box has coins in it. The number on a coin tells you how many cents it is worth. Count how much money is in each box and write the amount."
script.first: Draw the four coins on the board with their value: a quarter is 25 cents, a dime is 10, a nickel is 5, and a penny is 1. Do the first box together: start with the coin that is worth the most and count on: "25, 50… 55, 60." Write the amount in the box in front of the cent sign.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each coin, biggest number first, and say the running total. A child who counts the coins and not the cents (three coins are "3") should read the number on each coin aloud first. If the classroom has play coins, let the child lay them out.

blocks.title: Made Here, Sold There
blocks.instruction: Read each card. Write each thing in the right arrow.

script.say: "Write each thing in the right arrow: made in other countries and sold here, or made here and sold in other countries."
script.first: Read the two arrows aloud and point: one goes into the United States, the other goes out to other countries. Read the first card and its fact aloud and ask, "Is it grown or made in the United States, or in another country?" Write its name in the right arrow together. If your page asks you to finish two sentences, any thing from the right arrow is right.
script.stuck: Read the fact on the card again and ask, "Does it say the United States, or another country?" Made in the United States goes out; made in another country comes in.

blocks.title: Find 10 Differences in the Garden
blocks.instruction: Circle the 10 differences, 5 in each pair of pictures, and check a box under the pair for every one you find.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle with two pairs of pictures. In each pair, the picture on the right is different in 5 places. Circle each difference, and check a box under the pair for every one you find."
script.first: Find one difference in the top pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Circle it in the picture on the right and check off one box.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom. Things can be missing, added, or changed.

blocks.title: The Month Before and After
blocks.instruction: One month is given in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it.

script.say: "Each box has one month in the middle. Write the month that comes before it and the month that comes after it."
script.first: Say the months of the year aloud together, twice, and write them on the board in order. Do the first box together: find the month on the board and read the month on its left and on its right. Write them.
script.stuck: Have the child find the month on the board and put a finger on it: one step back is before, one step on is after. After December comes January again.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 15
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 15
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 15 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number of the Day: Up to 99
blocks.instruction: Show a two-digit number in tens and ones, then fill every box.

script.say: "Look at the big number: it is the number of the day. Show it in tens and ones, and fill in every box on the page."
script.first: Read the number of the day aloud together. Go around the page and read the label of each box aloud, so that the children know what each one asks for. Fill in the tens and ones box together: "How many tens are in this number? How many ones?" The children do the other boxes on their own.
script.stuck: Read the label of the box to the child again. Have the child build the number with ten fingers and some more, or draw a row of ten dots and the extra ones. A child who cannot finish every box should do the ones they know.

blocks.title: How a Character Meets a Challenge
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then write the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Ask the class, "What is the character's problem? What does the character do about it?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Describing Words in Real Life
blocks.instruction: Describing words tell what real things are like: a warm hat, a cold drink.

script.say: "Describing words tell what real things are like: hot soup, a soft blanket. Read each sentence and do what the page asks."
script.first: Read the first part of the page aloud with the class and do its first item together. Ask, "What is this thing really like? Which word fits?"
script.stuck: Ask the child to think of a real one: "Have you touched one? Is it hard or soft, hot or cold?"

blocks.title: Joining Words: and, but, so, because
blocks.instruction: A joining word puts two sentences together. Circle the one that fits best in each sentence. Then join two sentences and write them as one.

script.say: "A joining word puts two sentences together. And adds one more thing. But tells something you did not expect. So tells what happened because of it. Circle the joining word that fits best in each sentence."
script.first: Read the box with the three joining words aloud. Read the first sentence aloud three times, once with each joining word, and ask which one makes the most sense. Circle it. For the last part, read the two sentences together and join them on the lines.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with each joining word for the child and ask, "Which one sounds right?" For but, ask, "Is the second part a surprise?"

blocks.title: Subtract with Regrouping: Tens-and-Ones Mat
blocks.instruction: The first number is drawn on the mat. Are there enough ones to take away? Mark yes or no. If there are not enough, cross out one stick and draw ten dots for it. Cross out what is taken away and write what is left.

script.say: "The first number is drawn on the tens-and-ones mat. Are there enough ones to take away? Mark yes or no. If there are not enough, trade one ten for ten ones. Then subtract and write the answer."
script.first: Do the first problem on the board: draw the tens and ones of the first number. Ask, "Can we take away the ones?" If not, cross out one ten and draw ten more ones. Then cross out the ones and tens to take away and count what is left.
script.stuck: Have the child compare the ones: "Do we have more ones than we take away?" If not, trade a ten. Count the leftover tens and ones together.

blocks.title: How Many at the Start? Story Problems
blocks.instruction: Read each story. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the missing number. Write an equation. Then write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. We do not know how many there were at the start. Write the two numbers you know and a question mark in the bar model. Then solve."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "What do we know? The change and the end. What is missing? The start." Write the numbers in the bar together and solve.
script.stuck: Have the child count back from the end, or think: "What number and the change make the end?"

blocks.title: Why Countries Trade
blocks.instruction: Draw an arrow from the island that has each thing to the island that needs it. Then finish the sentence.

script.say: "Draw an arrow from the island that has a thing to the island that needs it."
script.first: Read the line for each island aloud and point to the person's thought bubble on each island: it shows what that island needs. Do the first one together: "Sunny Island has fruit and needs fish. Which island has fish?" Draw the arrow from that island to Sunny Island. Each island gives one thing and gets one thing. Then any true ending for "Countries trade because" is right, such as "they need things other countries have."
script.stuck: Ask, "What does this island need? Which island has it?" Find the line that says that island has it, and draw the arrow from there.

blocks.title: Draw It Twice as Big
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big.

script.say: "Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big."
script.first: Find the top-left colored square on the small grid together and count which row and which column it is in. Find the same row and column on the big grid and color that square. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.
