script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 16
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 16
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 16 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot: Count by Fives
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Count by fives from 5 to 50 and connect the dots. Part of the picture is already drawn.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot, and you count by fives. Start at the orange dot at 5. Draw a line to 10, then to 15, and keep going to 50."
script.first: Count by fives from 5 to 50 together. Find the orange dot at 5 together and draw the line to 10. Part of the picture is already drawn; the dots finish it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and add five; that is the dot to look for. The numbers in the row at the bottom can be crossed off one by one.

blocks.title: What Is the Lesson?
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write its lesson. Then write what a character does that shows the lesson.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write its lesson, the thing a reader learns from it, and what a character does that shows the lesson."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. After reading, ask, "What does the story teach us?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Opposite or the Same? Circle the Opposite
blocks.instruction: Read the word. One of the three words under it means the opposite. Circle it, not the one that means the same.

script.say: "Read the word. One of the three words under it means the opposite. Circle it, not the one that means the same."
script.first: Read the first word and its three choices aloud. Ask, "Which one means the opposite?" Point out that one choice means almost the same as the word: that is the trap. Circle the opposite.
script.stuck: Read each choice and ask, "Does it mean the same, or the opposite?"

blocks.title: Write About the Picture
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Use the word bank to help you write about what you see.

script.say: "Look at the picture. Use the words in the word bank to help you write about what you see. The sentence starters help you begin."
script.first: Look at the picture together and read the word bank and the sentence starters aloud. Say one sentence together using the first starter, and write it on the board. Tell the children to finish each sentence with their own words and to end it with a period.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "What do you see? What is happening?" Have the child say the sentence aloud before writing it. A child who finishes early writes one more sentence on the last lines.

blocks.title: Fact Family Houses to 20
blocks.instruction: Use the three numbers on the roof. Complete the four related facts.

script.say: "The three numbers on the roof are a family. They make four facts: two adding and two taking away. Use the three numbers to finish all four facts in each house."
script.first: Draw a house on the board with 3, 7, and 10 on the roof. Write the four facts together: 3 + 7 = 10, 7 + 3 = 10, 10 − 3 = 7, 10 − 7 = 3. Point out that the biggest number is the whole: it comes after the equals sign when we add and first when we take away.
script.stuck: Have the child find the biggest number on the roof and circle it: that is the whole. The other two are the parts. Adding the parts makes the whole; taking a part away from the whole leaves the other part.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 0 to 50
blocks.instruction: Count on to each arrow and write its number. Every tenth number is printed to help you.

script.say: "Each arrow points to a mark on the number line. Count on from the number before it and write the number the arrow points to."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Count the marks with the class from 0, one by one, up to the arrow. Write that number. Tell the children that not every mark has its number written; they count the marks between.
script.stuck: Have the child find the last printed number before the arrow, put a finger on it, and count each mark up to the arrow.

blocks.title: Road Safety Quiz: Which Sign Fits?
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and circle the one road sign that fits it.

script.say: "Read each sentence. Circle the one road sign that fits it."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud and look at the three signs next to it. Ask, "Which sign tells drivers about this?" Circle it together. Read each sentence aloud for children who need it.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and name the three signs; ask which one would help in that place.

blocks.title: Bring the Fish to the Coral Safely
blocks.instruction: Help the polar bear get to the igloo. Do not take a road with a walrus or a hole in the ice.

script.say: "Help the animal get home safely. Look at the whole maze first. Do not take a road with one of the dangers the page names."
script.first: Read the title aloud and show the start and the goal. Point to the dangers on the page and say that a road with a danger is closed. Trace a way with your finger and stop at each fork: "Is there a danger on this road?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: On the Hour
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour. Circle the time that matches the clock."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board showing 3:00 and say, "The long hand is on the 12, so it is something o'clock. The short hand points to 3: three o'clock." Do the first clock on the page together. Some choices end in :30; check where the long hand points.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 17
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 17
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 17 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Walls with Two-Digit Answers
blocks.instruction: The numbers go past 20. Add each pair of bricks and write the sum in the brick above.

script.say: "This is a number wall. Each brick is the sum of the two bricks right under it. Start at the bottom and build every wall to the top. The numbers get bigger than twenty, so you may add on paper."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks next to each other at the bottom and add them aloud, tens and ones; write the sum in the brick above them. Tell the children to work up the wall one row at a time.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers on scrap paper, tens and ones. A wrong brick lower down makes every brick above it wrong, so check the rows from the bottom up.

blocks.title: What Happens and Why
blocks.instruction: Read the story. A cause makes something happen. An effect is what happens. Write the effect of each cause.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Ask the class, "What is the character's problem? What does the character do about it?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Shades of Meaning: From a Little to a Lot
blocks.instruction: Read the three words in each row and write 1, 2 and 3 in the boxes, from the weakest word to the strongest.

script.say: "Each row has three words that mean almost the same thing, but some are stronger. Write 1 for the weakest word, 2 for the middle one, and 3 for the strongest."
script.first: Act out the first row: tap the desk softly, knock, then bang. Ask which is the weakest and which is the strongest. Write 1, 2, 3 together. Read every row aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Act the words out with the child or say them with your voice, from a little to a lot.

blocks.title: Plan Your True Story
blocks.instruction: A plan tells who, where, when, and what happened.

script.say: "A true story tells what really happened, in order. Read the parts of a true story at the top, then do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud: beginning, middle with time words, and an ending. Do the first task together. For a plan, let a few children say their idea first.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words the way they sound. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Subtract with Regrouping: Tens-and-Ones Mat
blocks.instruction: The first number is drawn on the mat. Are there enough ones to take away? Mark yes or no. If there are not enough, cross out one stick and draw ten dots for it. Cross out what is taken away and write what is left.

script.say: "The first number is drawn on the tens-and-ones mat. Are there enough ones to take away? Mark yes or no. If there are not enough, trade one ten for ten ones. Then subtract and write the answer."
script.first: Do the first problem on the board: draw the tens and ones of the first number. Ask, "Can we take away the ones?" If not, cross out one ten and draw ten more ones. Then cross out the ones and tens to take away and count what is left.
script.stuck: Have the child compare the ones: "Do we have more ones than we take away?" If not, trade a ten. Count the leftover tens and ones together.

blocks.title: Tens in Words: 10 to 100
blocks.instruction: Read the number. Circle the word that matches it.

script.say: "Each number has a word that we read and write. Read the number and circle the word that matches it."
script.first: Write 1 to 20 on the board and the words for a few of them. Do the first one together: read the number, read the three words, and circle the matching one.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number aloud and listen to its first sound; find the word that starts with that letter. Read the words with the child.

blocks.title: Laws in Our Community
blocks.instruction: Read each law. Write the letter of the problem the law stops. Use each letter one time.

script.say: "Each law stops a problem: read each law and write the letter of the problem it stops."
script.first: Say, "A law is a rule for everyone in a community." Read the problems in the box at the top aloud, with their letters. Read the first law aloud and look at its picture together: it shows people keeping the law. Ask, "What could happen if no one kept this law?" Find that problem in the box and write its letter together. If your page says "Use each letter one time," each problem goes with one law. If your page asks why our community needs one law, any true reason is right.
script.stuck: Read the law with the child and ask, "What could go wrong if no one kept this law?" Then read the problems one at a time and ask, "Is it this one?"

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

blocks.title: How Do You Feel? Circle the Face
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture, think how you would feel, and circle the face that matches.

script.say: "Look at each picture. Think about how it would make you feel. Then circle the face that shows that feeling."
script.first: Look at the first picture together and ask what it shows. Ask, "How does that make you feel?" Let two or three children answer; they may not all feel the same, and that is fine. Each child circles the face that matches their own answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child what the picture shows and when they have seen one. Then point to each face and name the feeling it shows. There is no wrong answer on this page; any face the child can explain is right.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 18
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 18
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 18 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: ABC Order: Number Them, Then Write Them
blocks.instruction: Number the cards, then copy the words onto the lines in order.

script.say: "We are going to put words in ABC order, the order of the alphabet."
script.first: Point to the alphabet strip at the top of the page. Read the four words on the cards aloud with the class. Ask, "Which word starts with the letter that comes first in the alphabet?" Write a 1 on its card together. The children number the other cards and then copy the words onto the lines in that order.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the alphabet strip and slide along it, stopping at the first letter that starts one of the words. That word is next. Cross out each word once it has a number.

blocks.title: Retell the Story and Tell Its Lesson
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end. Use the word bank. Then circle the lesson.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, using the word bank. Then circle the lesson of the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Nouns, Verbs, and Adjectives
blocks.instruction: Read every word. Is it a noun (naming word), a verb (action word), or an adjective (describing word)? Write it in the right bin.

script.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing. A verb is something you can do. An adjective tells what something is like. Read every word and write each one in the right bin."
script.first: Read all the words on the page aloud with the class. Do the first two words together: "Is it a naming word, an action word, or a describing word?" Write each in its bin.
script.stuck: Read the word to the child and try three test sentences aloud: "I see a ___." (a noun), "I can ___." (a verb), "It is ___." (an adjective). The one that sounds right tells the bin. For your own reference, on this page the nouns are scale, mailbox, package, and envelope; the verbs sleep, hide, sing, and climb; the adjectives fast, cold, tall, and quiet.

blocks.title: Write About the Picture: What You See
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture and write about what you see. The sentence starters help you begin, and the word bank names everything.

script.say: "Look at the picture. You are going to write three sentences about it. The beginning of each sentence is already on the line. The word bank names everything in the picture."
script.first: Look at the picture together and read the word bank and the sentence starters aloud. Say one sentence together using the first starter, and write it on the board. Tell the children to finish each sentence with their own words and to end it with a period.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "What do you see? What is happening?" Have the child say the sentence aloud before writing it. A child who finishes early writes one more sentence on the last lines.

blocks.title: Add and Subtract Tens
blocks.instruction: Add or take away tens in your head. Only the tens change. Write the answer in the box.

script.say: "Add or take away tens in your head. Only the tens change. Write the answer in the box."
script.first: Write 34 − 10 on the board and count back by ten together: "34, 24." Ask, "What changed? The tens. The ones stayed 4." Do 56 − 30 together: three tens back: 46, 36, 26.
script.stuck: Have the child say the tens and the ones of the first number. For adding or taking away tens, only the tens digit changes; for ones, count on or back from the number.

blocks.title: Number Line to 100: Counting by Fives
blocks.instruction: The tick marks count by fives, up to 100. Write the number each arrow points to.

script.say: "The tick marks count by fives, up to 100. Write the number each arrow points to."
script.first: Count by fives to 100 together. Draw the first line on the board and count the marks from the nearest printed number: "50, 55, 60." Write the number at the arrow.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the printed number before the arrow and count on by fives, one mark at a time.

blocks.title: Family Relationships: Riddles
blocks.instruction: Read each riddle and write the right family word from the box on the line; one word can fit more than one riddle.

script.say: "Now it is time to read and think. Each sentence is a riddle about one child's family. Read the riddle and work it out step by step. Then write the right family word from the box on the line. Some words fit more than one riddle."
script.first: Draw a family tree on the board with stick people: the child the riddles are about at the bottom; the mom and the dad above the child; a grandma and a grandpa above each parent; an aunt or an uncle beside each parent; and a cousin under the aunt. Read the first riddle aloud and follow it on the tree together, one step at a time, and write the word. Keep to the family on the page, not the children's own families.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the end of the riddle and say who its first part names ("the dad"), then add the last word ("his brother"). Following the riddle on the tree on the board helps. The children of an aunt or an uncle are cousins.

blocks.title: Help the Tortoise Find the Watermelon
blocks.instruction: Look at the whole maze first. Then draw the orangutan's way to the banana tree.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Half Past What?
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Every clock on this page shows a time that is half past the hour. Read each clock and circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board that shows half past two. Say: "The long hand points to the 6. That means half past. The short hand tells the hour. It has gone past the 2 and is halfway to the 3, so the time is half past two, or 2:30." Do the first clock on the page together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 19
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 19
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 19 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 10 More, 10 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 10 less and the number that is 10 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 10 less. On the right, write the number that is 10 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "Ten more: which digit changes, the tens or the ones?" Show that only the tens digit changes, one more ten for ten more and one less ten for ten less. Count by tens from another number together, for example 7, 17, 27, 37.
script.stuck: If the classroom has a hundreds chart, have the child find the number on it: the number straight above is 10 less, and the number straight below is 10 more. Without a chart, have the child cover the ones digit and change the tens digit by one.

blocks.title: What the Diagram Shows
blocks.instruction: Read the text and study the diagram. Write each answer. Questions 1 to 3 ask about the diagram. Questions 4 and 5 ask about the text and the diagram.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then use the diagram to answer the questions. Questions 1 to 3 ask about the diagram; the others ask about the text."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Show the children how to follow the arrows of the diagram from the first picture to the last.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Digraphs in Sentences: Circle and Count ng
blocks.instruction: Read the sentences. Circle every sh. Write how many you found in each sentence in its box.

script.say: "Read the sentences. Circle every letter team the title names. Write how many you found in each sentence in its box."
script.first: Read the letter team in the title aloud and say its sound. Read the first sentence aloud together and circle every one of that letter team; count them and write the number in the box.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger under each word and look for the two letters of the title right next to each other. Read the sentence to a child who cannot read it; the task is to find the letters. One of the two letters alone does not count.

blocks.title: Plan Your True Story
blocks.instruction: A plan tells who, where, when, and what happened.

script.say: "A true story tells what really happened, in order. Read the parts of a true story at the top, then do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud: beginning, middle with time words, and an ending. Do the first task together. For a plan, let a few children say their idea first.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words the way they sound. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: What Time Is It?
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour, and the long hand shows the minutes: count by fives. Circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Count by fives around the numbers with the class: 5, 10, 15… Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, count the minutes by fives, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then have the child count by fives from the 12 to the long hand: 5, 10, 15.

blocks.title: True or False?
blocks.instruction: Is each equation true? Circle the check mark if it is true and the X if it is false.

script.say: "Is each number sentence true? If both sides are the same amount, it is true: circle the check mark. If not, it is false: circle the X."
script.first: Write 10 − 2 = 8 on the board and ask, "Is ten take away two eight? Yes: true." Write 9 = 5 + 6 and ask, "Is five and six nine? No: false." Remind the children that the equals sign means "the same as" and can be on either side.
script.stuck: Have the child work out the side with the plus or minus sign and then compare it with the number on the other side.

blocks.title: Animal Coverings
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to its body covering.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Fur, Feathers, and Scales. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "What covers this animal's body: fur, feathers, or scales?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. Fur is soft hair, feathers have a stem with soft sides, and scales are small, hard plates on the skin.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Treasure Hunt: Follow the Steps
blocks.instruction: Start at the flag. Follow the steps. Circle the picture where you land.

script.say: "Start at the flag on the grid. Follow the steps, one at a time: each step says which way to move and how many squares. Circle the picture where you land."
script.first: Put your finger on the flag and read the first step aloud: "Move 1 square right." Move the finger together and stop. Read the next step and move again. Tell the children to count the squares, not the lines, and to keep the finger on the page until the last step.
script.stuck: Have the child say each step aloud and point with a finger. Check right and left: "Which hand is your right hand? Move that way."

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 20
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 20
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 20 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Read the Calendar
blocks.instruction: Look at the calendar. Use it to answer every question.

script.say: "This is a calendar page for one month. The questions under it ask you to find things on the calendar. Read each question and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the month and the days of the week across the top. Read the first question aloud and find the answer on the calendar together: put one finger on the date and slide up the column to its day.
script.stuck: For a question about a day of the week, have the child find the date and move a finger straight up its column to the day's name. For a question about a picture, the child looks for the little picture inside the calendar.

blocks.title: Steps in Order
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the four steps in order. The first word of each step is given.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write the four steps in order. The first word of each step is given."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Ask the class to look for the words first, then, next, and last in the text.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Split the Compound: Find the Two Words
blocks.instruction: The whole word is printed letter by letter next to its picture. Draw one line where the second word starts.

script.say: "A compound word is made of two smaller words, like sun and flower in sunflower. Each word on this page is printed letter by letter. Draw one line where the second word starts."
script.first: Read every word on the page aloud with the class. Then read the first word again and look at its picture. Ask, "Which two words make it?" Draw one line where the second word starts, together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the whole word and clap once for each of the two small words, then cover the end of the word with a finger and move it until a real word shows.

blocks.title: Who Is He? Pronouns in Sentences
blocks.instruction: Read the sentences. Draw a line from each word in a box to the name it stands for.

script.say: "Read the sentences. A pronoun like he, she, or they takes the place of a name. Draw a line from each word in a box to the name it stands for."
script.first: Read the first sentences aloud together. Point to the first word in a box and ask, "Who is she?" Draw the line to that name.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence again with the name in place of the word in the box. He goes to a boy's name, she to a girl's, and they to two or more names; if the sentence still makes sense, the line is right.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 40 to 60
blocks.instruction: This line does not start at zero. Count on from the nearest printed number and write the number each arrow points to.

script.say: "These number lines do not start at zero. They start at 40 and go to 60. Each arrow points to a number. Find out which number it is and write it in the box."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Point out that it does not start at zero. Count the small marks from the nearest printed number to the arrow and write the number.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the nearest printed number and count the small marks one by one to the arrow, saying the numbers. An answer such as 3 means the child wrote the number of steps, not the number on the line; an answer that is too small means the child counted from the left end as if it were zero.

blocks.title: Hundreds Chart Puzzle Pieces: Fill In the Numbers
blocks.instruction: One number is printed on each piece. Write every missing number: 1 more to the right, 1 less to the left, 10 more below, 10 less above.

script.say: "Each puzzle piece is a part of a hundreds chart. One number is printed on each piece. Write every missing number: 1 more to the right, 1 less to the left, 10 more below, 10 less above."
script.first: Draw a small piece on the board with 76 in it. Ask, "What is right of 76? One more: 77. Left? 75. Below? Ten more: 86. Above? 66." Fill the boxes together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the rule for the box: right is one more, left is one less, down is ten more, up is ten less.

blocks.title: Parts of a Plant We Eat
blocks.instruction: Look at each food. Circle the part of the plant that we eat.

script.say: "We eat different parts of plants: roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds. Look at each food and circle the part of the plant we eat."
script.first: Draw a plant on the board and label its parts. Name the first food on the page together and ask, "Does it grow under the ground, is it the stem, a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or a seed?" Circle the word.
script.stuck: Ask the child where the food grows: under the ground (roots), the long part that holds the plant up (stem), the flat green part (leaf), the part bees visit (flower), the part with seeds inside (fruit), or the seed itself. Let the child choose and say why.

blocks.title: Draw It Twice as Big
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big.

script.say: "Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big."
script.first: Find the top-left colored square on the small grid together and count which row and which column it is in. Find the same row and column on the big grid and color that square. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Help the Ant Reach Its Raspberry
blocks.instruction: Help the ant go down and up through the tunnels to the raspberry. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 21
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 21
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 21 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Subtraction Practice to 20
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: subtracting with numbers up to 20. Do the ones you know first. Then go back to the others."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board together and think aloud: "Nine take away five. I count back from nine: eight, seven, six, five, four." Then the children work on their own; tell them to skip a hard one and come back to it.
script.stuck: Have the child count up from the smaller number to the bigger one on fingers: for 17 minus 9, say "9" and count up to 17. Drawing dots and crossing them out is fine, too.

blocks.title: What the Diagram Shows
blocks.instruction: Read the text and study the diagram. Write each answer. Questions 1 to 3 ask about the diagram. Questions 4 and 5 ask about the text and the diagram.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then use the diagram to answer the questions. Questions 1 to 3 ask about the diagram; the others ask about the text."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Show the children how to follow the arrows of the diagram from the first picture to the last.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Synonym Pairs: Match the Words That Mean the Same
blocks.instruction: Draw a line to link each word on the left with the word on the right that means the same.

script.say: "Synonyms are words that mean the same thing, or almost the same, like big and large. Each word on the left has a partner on the right that means the same. Draw a line from each word to its partner."
script.first: Read all the words on the page aloud with the class. Do the first word on the left together: "Which word on the right means the same?" Draw the line.
script.stuck: Read the word to the child and have the child put it into a short sentence. Then the child tries the words on the right in the same sentence; the one that keeps the meaning is its partner.

blocks.title: Fix the Sentence: Where Does It End?
blocks.instruction: Two sentences ran together. Write them as two sentences.

script.say: "Two sentences ran together. Find where the first one ends and write them as two sentences, each with a capital letter and a period."
script.first: Read the first line aloud and stop where the first idea ends. Write it on the board as two sentences together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the first word, then on every name, then on the end of the sentence, and ask at each place, "Capital letter? End mark?" The three small pictures above the first sentence show the three things to check.

blocks.title: Shopping Math: Two Stories
blocks.instruction: Read each story and use the shelf prices to answer it.

script.say: "Read each story and use the prices on the shelf to answer it."
script.first: Read the prices on the shelf aloud. Read the first story aloud and find the prices of the things in it; add them together on the board.
script.stuck: Have the child circle the two things on the shelf that the question shows, then write the two prices one under the other and add the ones first. Coins or drawn dimes and pennies help a child who cannot add the numbers yet.

blocks.title: Write the Question: Story Problems Within 20
blocks.instruction: Read each story. If the question is missing, write a question you can answer by adding or subtracting. Then write the equation and the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. If the question is missing, write a question you can answer by adding or subtracting. Then write the equation and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "What could we ask about it?" Let a few children say a question, write one on the board, and solve it together.
script.stuck: Give the child the start of a question: "How many … in all?" or "How many … are left?"

blocks.title: Questions About an Old Photograph
blocks.instruction: Look closely at the old photograph. Write two things you see, what you think, and two questions you wonder about.

script.say: "Look closely at this picture of a main street long ago, about 1910, and then do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the caption aloud. Look at the picture together and name a few things: the HARDWARE and BANK signs, the streetcar on its rails, the horse and wagon, the old car, the people in hats. Ask, "What is different from a street today?" If your page has a list of five things, find the first one together and circle it. Then say a question together, such as "I wonder why people rode in a wagon," and let each child write their own. If the page asks how we could find out, the child might ask an older person or look in a book.
script.stuck: Point to one thing in the picture and ask, "Do we see this on a street today?" Then help the child start a question: "I wonder why …"

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

blocks.title: Quarter Hours
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Every clock on this page shows a quarter hour: something o'clock, quarter past, half past, or quarter to. Read each clock and circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Show quarter past (the long hand on 3), half past (on 6), and quarter to (on 9). Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, the minutes from the long hand, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then look at the long hand: on the 12 is o'clock, on the 3 quarter past, on the 6 half past, on the 9 quarter to.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 22
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 22
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 22 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 100 More, 100 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 100 less and the number that is 100 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 100 less. On the right, write the number that is 100 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "A hundred more: which digit changes? Which two stay the same?" Show that only the hundreds digit changes. Count by hundreds from another number together.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens and the ones with a finger and look only at the hundreds digit: one less for 100 less, one more for 100 more. The two covered digits are copied as they are.

blocks.title: Steps in Order
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the four steps in order. The first word of each step is given.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write the four steps in order. The first word of each step is given."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Ask the class to look for the words first, then, next, and last in the text.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Find the Root Word
blocks.instruction: Circle the part the three words share and write that root word in the empty stone.

script.say: "The three words on each card are a word family: they are all built from one small word, the root word. Circle the part that all three words share. Then write the root word in the empty stone."
script.first: Read the three words of the first stone aloud. Ask, "Which part do all three words share?" Circle it in each word and write that root word in the empty stone together.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the beginnings and the endings of the words with a finger until a small real word shows. The root word must be a word by itself.

blocks.title: Unscramble the Sentence: No Clues
blocks.instruction: There is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence on the line.

script.say: "The words of each sentence are mixed up, and there is no capital letter and no period to help you. Put the words in order and write the sentence with a capital letter and a period."
script.first: Write the mixed-up words of the first sentence on the board. Read them aloud with the class. Ask: "Which word could start the sentence?" Try the children's ideas aloud until one order sounds right. Write the sentence on the board, and point out the capital letter at the start and the end mark.
script.stuck: Have the child read every word aloud, then try a first word and read on: "Does that sound like something you would say?" If the child cannot read a word, read it for them. Cross out each word once it is used.

blocks.title: Graph Detective
blocks.instruction: Use the graph to solve both picture questions.

script.say: "Use the bar graph to answer both questions. One asks you to add, and one asks you to take away."
script.first: Read the graph together: find each bar and read its number on the side. Read the first question aloud and write its number sentence together.
script.stuck: Have the child write the number next to each tally first: five for each bundle, then the single marks. For the bar, the child puts a finger on that number at the side of the graph and colors up to its line.

blocks.title: Find the Mistakes
blocks.instruction: Check each answer. If it is wrong, put an X in the small box and write the right answer in the big box. If it is right, leave both boxes empty.

script.say: "Someone has already solved these problems, but some answers are wrong. Check each one. If it is wrong, put an X in the small box and write the right answer in the big box. If it is right, leave both boxes empty."
script.first: Do the first problem on the board together: solve it yourself and compare with the answer that is printed. "Is it the same? Then leave both boxes empty. If not, an X and the right answer." Tell the children to solve each problem first and only then look at the printed answer.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the printed answer, solve the problem with fingers or a drawing, and then uncover the answer and compare.

blocks.title: What Animals Eat
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Plant Eaters and Meat Eaters. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "What does this animal eat: plants or other animals?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Help the Lemur Pick Up Every Banana
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

blocks.title: Time in Words
blocks.instruction: Read the time in words. Draw a line from each clock to the words that tell its time.

script.say: "Read the times in words. Draw a line from each clock to the words that tell its time."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board at half past three and say, "The long hand is on the 6: half past. The short hand is just past the 3: half past three." Read the words on the page aloud together and match the first clock together. Quarter past means the long hand is on the 3.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 23
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 23
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 23 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number of the Day: Ten More, Ten Less
blocks.instruction: Find ten more and ten less than the number of the day.

script.say: "Look at the big number: it is the number of the day. Every box asks something about it: its word, the numbers before and after, ten more and ten less. Fill in all the boxes."
script.first: Read the number of the day aloud together. Go around the page and read the label of each box aloud, so that the children know what each one asks for. Fill in the tens and ones box together: "How many tens are in this number? How many ones?" The children do the other boxes on their own.
script.stuck: Read the label of the box to the child again. Have the child build the number with ten fingers and some more, or draw a row of ten dots and the extra ones. A child who cannot finish every box should do the ones they know.

blocks.title: Fill-in-the-Blank Sentences
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Find the word that fits the sentence in the word bank and write it in the box.

script.say: "Each sentence is missing a word. The words are in the word bank at the top, and each sentence has a picture. Find the word that fits and write it in the box."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud together. Read the first sentence aloud and say "blank" at the gap. Look at its picture and ask, "Which word fits?" Write it in the box together.
script.stuck: Read the sentence with the child, one word at a time, and say "blank" at the gap. Look at the picture together and find its word in the bank.

blocks.title: Vowel Teams for Long a, e, and o
blocks.instruction: ai and ay spell long a. ee and ea spell long e. oa and ow spell long o.

script.say: "Two vowels together can make one long sound. Ai and ay spell long a, ee and ea spell long e, oa and ow spell long o. Read each word and write it under its vowel sound."
script.first: Write rain, play, feet, eat, boat, and snow on the board and read them. Read the first word on the page together, find its vowel team, and write it under its sound.
script.stuck: Have the child find the two vowels together and say the long sound they make.

blocks.title: Parts of an Informative Piece
blocks.instruction: An informative piece has a topic sentence, facts, and a closing sentence.

script.say: "An informative piece teaches facts. It has a topic sentence that tells what it is about, facts, and a closing sentence. Read the parts at the top, then do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box with the parts of an informative piece aloud. Do the first task of the page together: find the topic sentence, a fact, or the closing sentence. Then the children go on.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words the way they sound. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Read the Line Plot
blocks.instruction: Count the X marks above each number. Write how many.

script.say: "A line plot shows how many with X marks above each number. Count the X marks above each number and write how many."
script.first: Draw a short number line on the board with a few X marks above the numbers. Count the X marks above one number together and write the count. Do the first question on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the number and count the X marks straight above it, from the bottom up.

blocks.title: Bar Models
blocks.instruction: Look at each bar. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "Each bar shows a whole and its two parts. One number is missing. Write the missing number in the box."
script.first: Draw a bar on the board split into two parts, with 60 on top as the whole and 20 in one part. Ask, "What goes with 20 to make 60?" Count on by tens together: 30, 40, 50, 60: forty. Write it in the empty part. Tell the children to check whether the missing number is a part or the whole.
script.stuck: Ask, "Is the whole missing? Then add the two parts. Is a part missing? Then take the other part away from the whole."

blocks.title: Label the Butterfly Life Cycle
blocks.instruction: Write the four stage names from the word bank on the lines under their pictures, then cross out the name that does not belong.

script.say: "A butterfly grows in four stages. Write the four stage names from the word bank on the lines under their pictures. Then cross out the name that is not part of a butterfly's life."
script.first: Read the word bank aloud together. Ask, "What does a butterfly start as?" An egg. Find the egg picture and write egg under it together. Talk through the order: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A tadpole is a baby frog.
script.stuck: Have the child follow the arrows from the egg and name what each picture shows.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates
blocks.instruction: Find each square by its letter and number, like B2. Color it with the color of its group to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Read the first square, for example B2: go across to B and down to 2. Color it in its color together. Tell the children to cross off each square on the list as they color it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

blocks.title: What Time Is It?
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour, and the long hand shows the minutes: count by fives. Circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Count by fives around the numbers with the class: 5, 10, 15… Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, count the minutes by fives, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then have the child count by fives from the 12 to the long hand: 5, 10, 15.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 24
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 24
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 24 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot: Count by Tens
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Count by tens from 10 to 100 and connect the dots. Part of the picture is already drawn.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot, and you count by tens. Start at the orange dot at 10. Draw a line to 20, then to 30, and keep going to 100."
script.first: Count by tens from 10 to 100 together. Find the orange dot at 10 together and draw the line to 20. Part of the picture is already drawn; the dots finish it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and add ten; that is the dot to look for. The numbers in the row at the bottom can be crossed off one by one.

blocks.title: Two Versions of One Tale: Sort the Facts
blocks.instruction: Two versions of a tale can have different characters and settings.

script.say: "Two versions of one tale can have different characters and settings. Read both versions. Sort each fact: is it in version 1, version 2, or both?"
script.first: Read the two versions aloud while the children follow. Then read the first fact aloud and ask, "Which version tells this?" Write it in the right place together.
script.stuck: Read the fact with the child and look for it in each version, one at a time.

blocks.title: Short or Long Vowel?
blocks.instruction: A short vowel says its sound: hop. A long vowel says its name: hope.

script.say: "A short vowel says its sound: hop. A long vowel says its name: hope. Read each word and write it under short vowel or long vowel."
script.first: Write hop and hope on the board and read them. Point out the e at the end and the two vowels together that often make a long sound, like ee and ay. Read the first word on the page together and decide.
script.stuck: Say the word slowly and hold the vowel. Then say the letter's name: if the word says the name, it is long.

blocks.title: Match the Verb to Its Past Tense
blocks.instruction: Read each verb on the left. Draw a line to its past tense (the yesterday form) on the right — one line for each verb.

script.say: "Read each verb on the left. Draw a line to its past tense, the yesterday form, on the right."
script.first: Write jump and jumped on the board: "Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped." Read the first verb aloud and find its yesterday form together. Some verbs change: sing, sang.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud with the verb and listen. If the sentence has "yesterday," the verb tells about the past (jumped). With one person and "today" or "every day," the verb gets an s (runs, sings).

blocks.title: Shopping Math: Four Questions
blocks.instruction: Answer the shopping question on each of the four cards.

script.say: "Answer the shopping question on each of the four cards. Use the prices on the shelf."
script.first: Read the prices on the shelf aloud. Read the first card aloud and solve it on the board together. Two quarters are 50 cents.
script.stuck: Have the child circle the two things on the shelf that the question shows, then write the two prices one under the other and add the ones first. Coins or drawn dimes and pennies help a child who cannot add the numbers yet.

blocks.title: Find the Start: Story Problems Within 100
blocks.instruction: Read each story. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the number you need. Write an equation. Then write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the number you need. Then solve."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "Do we know the start? The change? The end?" Write the two numbers you know in the bar and a question mark where the missing number goes. Solve it together.
script.stuck: Read the story with the child and underline the numbers. Ask, "Are things put together, or taken away?" Draw a quick bar to show the parts and the whole.

blocks.title: Tools and Skills for the Job
blocks.instruction: Color the box blue for each tool or machine and orange for each skill.

script.say: "Color the box blue for each tool or machine a worker uses, and orange for each skill a worker knows."
script.first: The children need a blue and an orange crayon. Read the key at the top aloud. Read the first card aloud and look at its picture: is the worker holding a thing, or thinking, with a thought bubble? A thing the worker uses is a tool or machine: blue. Something the worker knows, in the bubble, is a skill: orange. Color the first box together. If your page asks how a machine helps the baker make more bread, any true reason is right, such as "it works faster than hands."
script.stuck: Read the card with the child and ask, "Is the worker using this thing, or thinking about something they know?" Using a thing is blue; knowing is orange.

blocks.title: Bring the Butterfly to the Rose Safely
blocks.instruction: Help the polar bear get to the igloo. Do not take a road with a walrus or a hole in the ice.

script.say: "Help the animal get home safely. Look at the whole maze first. Do not take a road with one of the dangers the page names."
script.first: Read the title aloud and show the start and the goal. Point to the dangers on the page and say that a road with a danger is closed. Trace a way with your finger and stop at each fork: "Is there a danger on this road?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 25
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 25
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 25 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Odd or Even? Write Two Equal Addends
blocks.instruction: Circle the dots two by two. Then write the number as two equal parts and write what is left over in the small box.

script.say: "Circle the dots two by two. Then write the number as two equal parts, and write what is left over in the small box."
script.first: Draw 7 dots on the board and circle them in pairs: three pairs and one left over. Write 7 = 3 + 3 + 1 left over. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child circle the dots two by two and count the pairs: that is each equal part. A dot left over goes in the small box, and the number is odd; no dot left over means it is even.

blocks.title: Read and Check: True or False
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and look at the row of pictures. Is the sentence true or false? Circle the right word.

script.say: "Read each sentence and look at the row of pictures. Is the sentence true or false? Circle the right word."
script.first: Point to the row of pictures and name them together from left to right. Read the first sentence aloud and check it on the row together, counting the pictures from the left. Circle true or false.
script.stuck: Point to the word the child cannot read and say its first sound; if that is not enough, read the word. Then have the child read the whole sentence again and tell you what it asks for before starting.

blocks.title: er, ir, and ur: One Sound, Three Spellings
blocks.instruction: er, ir, and ur say the same sound: her, first, turn.

script.say: "Er, ir, and ur all say the same sound, like in her, first, and turn. Read each word and write it under er, ir, or ur."
script.first: Write her, first, and turn on the board and read them with the class. Read the first word on the page together and look at its letters: which spelling does it use? Write it under that heading. Read the second part of the page aloud together.
script.stuck: Point out that the sound is the same, so the child looks at the letters, not the sound: is it e-r, i-r, or u-r?

blocks.title: Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow
blocks.instruction: A verb tells when: yesterday I walked, today I walk, tomorrow I will walk. Write the missing verbs. Then circle the verb that fits.

script.say: "A verb tells when something happens: yesterday I walked, today I walk, tomorrow I will walk. Write the missing verbs. Then circle the verb that fits the time word in each sentence."
script.first: Write walked, walk, will walk under Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow on the board. Do the first row on the page together. For the second part, read the first sentence aloud and look for the time word: yesterday, today, or tomorrow.
script.stuck: Ask, "Did it happen already, is it happening now, or will it happen later?" Already: add -ed. Later: will.

blocks.title: Tally to Graph
blocks.instruction: Read the tally chart. Color one bar for each count.

script.say: "Read the tally chart. Color one box of the bar graph for each tally mark."
script.first: Count the tally marks of the first row together: a bundle with a line across is five. Color that many boxes in its bar, from the bottom up.
script.stuck: Have the child write the number next to each tally first: five for each bundle, then the single marks. For the bar, the child puts a finger on that number at the side of the graph and colors up to its line.

blocks.title: Counting Money: All the Coins
blocks.instruction: Count the coins. Write how much money there is in all.

script.say: "Each box has coins in it. The number on a coin tells you how many cents it is worth. Count how much money is in each box and write the amount."
script.first: Draw the four coins on the board with their value: a quarter is 25 cents, a dime is 10, a nickel is 5, and a penny is 1. Do the first box together: start with the coin that is worth the most and count on: "25, 50… 55, 60." Write the amount in the box in front of the cent sign.
script.stuck: Have the child touch each coin, biggest number first, and say the running total. A child who counts the coins and not the cents (three coins are "3") should read the number on each coin aloud first. If the classroom has play coins, let the child lay them out.

blocks.title: My Habitat Report
blocks.instruction: In the picture, draw three animals that live there, write their names and a plant that grows there, and circle the word that fits this habitat.

script.say: "This is your habitat report. In the picture, draw three animals that live there and write their names. Then write a plant that grows there, and circle whether the habitat is wet or dry."
script.first: Read the name of the habitat on the page aloud and talk about it: "What animals live in the ocean?" Let a few children say ideas. Each child draws and labels three animals.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Which animals have you seen at an aquarium, in a book, or in a movie about the sea?" Any animal that lives in the ocean is right, and the drawing does not have to be neat. Point to the board for the spelling.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates
blocks.instruction: Find each square by its letter and number, like B2. Color it with the color of its group to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Read the first square, for example B2: go across to B and down to 2. Color it in its color together. Tell the children to cross off each square on the list as they color it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

blocks.title: Draw It Twice as Big
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big.

script.say: "Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big."
script.first: Find the top-left colored square on the small grid together and count which row and which column it is in. Find the same row and column on the big grid and color that square. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 26
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 26
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 26 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: ABC Order: When Words Start the Same
blocks.instruction: Two pairs start with the same letter. Use the second letter to order them.

script.say: "Put the words in ABC order. Two pairs of words start with the same letter: then look at the second letter to decide."
script.first: Point to the alphabet strip at the top. Read the six words aloud with the class. Find two words that start with the same letter together and ask, "Which second letter comes first in the alphabet?" Number the words 1 to 6 together, then the children write them in order.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the alphabet strip and slide along it, stopping at the first letter that starts one of the words. That word is next. Cross out each word once it has a number.

blocks.title: Two Versions of One Tale: Sort the Facts
blocks.instruction: Two versions of a tale can have different characters and settings.

script.say: "Two versions of one tale can have different characters and settings. Read both versions. Sort each fact: is it in version 1, version 2, or both?"
script.first: Read the two versions aloud while the children follow. Then read the first fact aloud and ask, "Which version tells this?" Write it in the right place together.
script.stuck: Read the fact with the child and look for it in each version, one at a time.

blocks.title: Suffixes -ful, -less, and -ly
blocks.instruction: -ful means full of, and -less means without.

script.say: "A suffix is a word part at the end. -ful means full of, -less means without, and -ly tells how. Circle the base word in each word and underline the suffix. Then match each word to its meaning."
script.first: Write playful on the board: circle play, underline -ful. Ask, "What does playful mean? Full of play." Do the same with toothless. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then add the suffix and ask what the whole word means.

blocks.title: Parts of a Friendly Letter
blocks.instruction: A friendly letter has a date, a greeting, a body, a closing, and a signature.

script.say: "A friendly letter has five parts: the date, the greeting, the body, the closing, and the signature. Write the name of each part on its line, using the word bank."
script.first: Read the five parts in the word bank aloud and find each one in the letter on the page together: the date at the top, "Dear…" is the greeting, the long middle is the body, "Your friend" is the closing, and the name at the end is the signature. Do the first one together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Where does a letter start? Who is it to? Who wrote it?" Point to each part as you ask.

blocks.title: Rows and Columns
blocks.instruction: Count the rows and columns. Finish the multiplication sentence.

script.say: "Count the rows and the columns of each array. Finish the multiplication sentence: rows times columns."
script.first: Draw an array of 3 rows of 4 dots on the board. Count the rows and the columns together, then add the rows: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Show that 3 × 4 means 3 rows of 4. Do the first picture on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child run a finger along each row of an array and count the rows first, then count the things in the top row. On this page the first number is the number of rows and the second number is how many are in each row.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 0 to 120
blocks.instruction: This line goes past 100. Count by tens to each arrow and write the number.

script.say: "This line goes past 100. Count by tens to each arrow and write the number."
script.first: Count by tens to 120 together. Draw the first line on the board, start at the nearest printed number, and count each mark by ten to the arrow.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the printed number before the arrow and count on by tens, one mark at a time.

blocks.title: What Does It Cost to Make?
blocks.instruction: Circle what the children must buy and add the costs. Write what 10 cups bring in at each price. Circle the lowest price that brings in more than they must pay.

script.say: "Circle what the children must buy, add the costs, and find the lowest price per cup that brings in more than they must pay."
script.first: Read the story aloud: it says what the children need. Read the price list together; some things on it are not needed. Circle the first needed thing together and write its price in the first box, then add all the prices. For the prices per cup, say, "10 cups at $1 a cup bring in $10." At 50 cents a cup, 2 cups make a dollar, so 10 cups bring in $5; at 20 cents, count by 20s to 200 cents: $2. Circle the lowest price that brings in more than the total. If your page asks you to choose a price, any price that brings in more, with a reason, is right.
script.stuck: Ask, "Do they need this to make or sell lemonade?" For a price per cup, count with the child, one cup at a time, until you reach 10 cups.

blocks.title: Treasure Hunt: Follow the Steps
blocks.instruction: Start at the flag. Follow the steps. Circle the picture where you land.

script.say: "Start at the flag on the grid. Follow the steps, one at a time: each step says which way to move and how many squares. Circle the picture where you land."
script.first: Put your finger on the flag and read the first step aloud: "Move 1 square right." Move the finger together and stop. Read the next step and move again. Tell the children to count the squares, not the lines, and to keep the finger on the page until the last step.
script.stuck: Have the child say each step aloud and point with a finger. Check right and left: "Which hand is your right hand? Move that way."

blocks.title: Help the Foal Pick Up Every Apple
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 27
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 27
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 27 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count by Threes
blocks.instruction: Skip count by 3. Write each missing number.

script.say: "On this page we count by threes: 3, 6, 9, 12. Some numbers are missing. Count by threes and write each missing number. The rows do not start at 3."
script.first: Count by threes together to 60. Read the first row aloud and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. Tell the children that a row does not always start at 3.
script.stuck: Have the child add three to the number before the gap with fingers: say the number, then count three more. To check, the next printed number must be three more than the number the child wrote.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: Story 3
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. Then read each question and circle the best answer. The answers are in the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Circle the answer together.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask them to put a finger on the sentence in the story that tells the answer. If the child cannot read the story alone, read it with them.

blocks.title: Opposite or the Same? Circle the Opposite
blocks.instruction: Read the word. One of the three words under it means the opposite. Circle it, not the one that means the same.
