script.say: "Read the word. One of the three words under it means the opposite. Circle it, not the one that means the same."
script.first: Read the first word and its three choices aloud. Ask, "Which one means the opposite?" Point out that one choice means almost the same as the word: that is the trap. Circle the opposite.
script.stuck: Read each choice and ask, "Does it mean the same, or the opposite?"

blocks.title: Write Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Tell your opinion, give your reasons, and end with a closing sentence.

script.say: "Today you write an opinion piece: what you think and why. Circle one question. Write your opinion, give your reasons, and end with a closing sentence."
script.first: Read both questions aloud and let a few children say their opinion and one reason. Write the parts on the board: I think … because … Also … That is why … Each child circles one question and writes.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words the way they sound. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: 3-Digit Numbers in Columns
blocks.instruction: Add or subtract one place at a time. Start with the ones.

script.say: "Add or subtract one place at a time: ones, then tens, then hundreds. Look at the sign of each problem first."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board, one number under the other. Point to the sign. Work the ones column first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Tell the children to check the sign of every problem, because the page mixes them.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens column with a finger and add only the ones, then cover the ones and add the tens. Fingers or dots are fine for the small sums.

blocks.title: Draw, Solve, Answer: Story Problems Within 20
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Draw it in the box. Write the equation. Then write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Draw it in the box. Write the equation. Then write the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud and draw it quickly on the board with circles. Write the equation under the drawing together and the answer with a word: "12 sandwiches."
script.stuck: Have the child draw one circle for each thing in the story, cross out the ones that go away, and count.

blocks.title: What Banks Do
blocks.instruction: Read the sentences. Write the right sentence next to each picture.

script.say: "A bank keeps money safe, pays savers a little extra called interest, and lends money: write the right sentence next to each picture."
script.first: Read the sentences at the top aloud. Say what each picture on your page shows. A child giving money to the bank, with a big round vault door behind, shows that the bank keeps money safe. The savings paper where the bank added $1 shows that the bank pays savers interest. A banker holding money out to a parent, who is thinking about their house, shows that the bank lends money. Do the first picture together and copy its sentence. If your page asks why a family might borrow money, any real need is right, such as fixing a roof.
script.stuck: Point to the picture and ask, "Is someone putting money in the bank, getting a little extra, or borrowing money?" Then find the sentence that says that.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates
blocks.instruction: Find each square by its letter and number, like B2. Color it with the color of its group to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Read the first square, for example B2: go across to B and down to 2. Color it in its color together. Tell the children to cross off each square on the list as they color it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

blocks.title: Quarter Hours
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Every clock on this page shows a quarter hour: something o'clock, quarter past, half past, or quarter to. Read each clock and circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Show quarter past (the long hand on 3), half past (on 6), and quarter to (on 9). Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, the minutes from the long hand, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then look at the long hand: on the 12 is o'clock, on the 3 quarter past, on the 6 half past, on the 9 quarter to.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 28
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 28
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 28 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Walls with Two-Digit Answers
blocks.instruction: The numbers go past 20. Add each pair of bricks and write the sum in the brick above.

script.say: "This is a number wall. Each brick is the sum of the two bricks right under it. Start at the bottom and build every wall to the top. The numbers get bigger than twenty, so you may add on paper."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks next to each other at the bottom and add them aloud, tens and ones; write the sum in the brick above them. Tell the children to work up the wall one row at a time.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers on scrap paper, tens and ones. A wrong brick lower down makes every brick above it wrong, so check the rows from the bottom up.

blocks.title: Read the Facts
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the answer to each question. Finish the sentence.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write the answer to each question by finishing the sentence."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Parts of Speech: Sort Twelve Words
blocks.instruction: No pictures to help. Read each word and sort it into a bin.

script.say: "A noun names a person, an animal, a place, or a thing. A verb is something you can do. An adjective tells what something is like. Read the twelve words and write each one in the right bin."
script.first: Read all twelve words aloud with the class. Do the first two words together: "Is it a noun, a verb, or an adjective?" Write each in its bin.
script.stuck: Read the word to the child and try three test sentences aloud: "I see a ___." (a noun), "I can ___." (a verb), "It is ___." (an adjective). The one that sounds right tells the bin. For your own reference, on this page the nouns are eyebrow, heel, nose, and face; the verbs pull, eat, catch, and jump; the adjectives big, happy, fluffy, and loud. Face can be a verb too ("face the board"): it is right in either bin when the child can say a sentence that uses it that way.

blocks.title: Parts of a Friendly Letter
blocks.instruction: A friendly letter has a date, a greeting, a body, a closing, and a signature.

script.say: "A friendly letter has five parts: the date, the greeting, the body, the closing, and the signature. Write the name of each part on its line, using the word bank."
script.first: Read the five parts in the word bank aloud and find each one in the letter on the page together: the date at the top, "Dear…" is the greeting, the long middle is the body, "Your friend" is the closing, and the name at the end is the signature. Do the first one together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Where does a letter start? Who is it to? Who wrote it?" Point to each part as you ask.

blocks.title: Half and Half
blocks.instruction: Color one half of each shape.

script.say: "Each shape is cut into equal parts. Color the fraction the row shows."
script.first: Draw a circle cut into two equal parts and color one: "one half." Do the first shape on the page together: read the fraction, count the parts, and color.
script.stuck: Have the child count the parts of the shape and then color exactly one of them, all the way to its edges. It does not matter which of the two parts is colored. A child who colors the whole shape counts the parts again with you.

blocks.title: Where Does the Piece Go?
blocks.instruction: Read the numbers on each piece, find its place on the empty chart and write them in.

script.say: "Each puzzle piece is cut from a hundreds chart. Read the numbers on each piece, find where it fits on the empty chart, and write the numbers in."
script.first: Point to the empty chart and read the numbers that are printed on it. Take the first piece together: read its numbers and ask, "Where is 28 on the chart?" Count along the row to find it and write the numbers of the piece in.
script.stuck: Have the child find the tens of the number first: 28 is in the row of the 20s. Then count along the row.

blocks.title: Cardinal Directions on a Map
blocks.instruction: Start at the first picture on the map, look the way the word says, and circle the one of the three pictures that lies that way.

script.say: "Look at the map. Start at the first picture of each question, look the way the word says, and circle the picture you see in that direction."
script.first: Find the compass rose on the map together, or the north arrow if your page has only that, and say the four directions: north is the way it points, south the other way, east to the right of north, and west to the left. Read the first question aloud, put a finger on its first picture, and move the finger the way the word says. Circle the picture you reach. Use the map key to name the pictures.
script.stuck: Have the child show the direction on the compass rose or the north arrow first, then move a finger the same way across the map.

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

blocks.title: On the Hour
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour. Circle the time that matches the clock."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board showing 3:00 and say, "The long hand is on the 12, so it is something o'clock. The short hand points to 3: three o'clock." Do the first clock on the page together. Some choices end in :30; check where the long hand points.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That number is the hour. A child who names the next number is looking at where the short hand is going, not at where it has been.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 29
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 29
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 29 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Read the Calendar: Days of the Week
blocks.instruction: Read down the columns to answer the questions about the days.

script.say: "This is a calendar page for one month. The questions under it ask you to find things on the calendar. Read each question and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the month and the days of the week across the top. Read the first question aloud: put a finger on the date and slide up the column to read its day. Read down a column to find all the dates of one day.
script.stuck: For a question about a day of the week, have the child find the day's name at the top and move a finger straight down its column. For one date, the child moves up from the date to the day's name.

blocks.title: Beginning, Middle, and End
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then retell it: write what happens at the beginning, in the middle, and at the end.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write its lesson, the thing a reader learns from it, and what a character does that shows the lesson."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. After reading, ask, "What does the story teach us?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Adjective or Adverb?
blocks.instruction: An adjective tells about a noun. An adverb tells about a verb: how it is done.

script.say: "An adjective tells about a noun: a brave dog. An adverb tells how something is done: the dog ran bravely. Many adverbs end in -ly. Circle the word that fits each sentence, then draw an arrow to the word it tells about."
script.first: Write "a quick fox" and "the fox ran quickly" on the board. Ask which word tells about the fox and which tells how it ran. Read the first sentence on the page aloud with both choices and circle the one that fits together. Read the rule box about words ending in y aloud.
script.stuck: Ask, "Does the word tell about a thing, or about how someone does something?" A thing gets the adjective; how someone does something gets the -ly word.

blocks.title: Write Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Tell your opinion, give your reasons, and end with a closing sentence.

script.say: "Today you write an opinion piece: what you think and why. Circle one question. Write your opinion, give your reasons, and end with a closing sentence."
script.first: Read both questions aloud and let a few children say their opinion and one reason. Write the parts on the board: I think … because … Also … That is why … Each child circles one question and writes.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words the way they sound. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Share the Set
blocks.instruction: Circle the fraction of the pictures. Write how many that is.

script.say: "Each row shows a group of pictures and a fraction. Circle that part of the group, and write how many that is."
script.first: Draw 8 circles on the board. Say, "One half means two equal groups. Half of 8 is 4." Circle 4. For one fourth, make four equal groups and circle one group. Do the first row together.
script.stuck: Have the child share the pictures into as many equal groups as the bottom number says, one picture at a time. Then circle as many groups as the top number says.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 0 to 50
blocks.instruction: Count on to each arrow and write its number. Every tenth number is printed to help you.

script.say: "Each arrow points to a mark on the number line. Count on from the number before it and write the number the arrow points to."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Count the marks with the class from 0, one by one, up to the arrow. Write that number. Tell the children that not every mark has its number written; they count the marks between.
script.stuck: Have the child find the last printed number before the arrow, put a finger on it, and count each mark up to the arrow.

blocks.title: Family Tree: Read the Clues
blocks.instruction: Read the clues and write each name in the right name box on the family tree.

script.say: "Read each clue. It tells you who someone is in the family. Write each name in the right name box on the family tree."
script.first: Read the names on the tree and the first clue aloud. Find the child the clues are about on the tree. Ask, "If Leo is Jack's brother, where does he go on the tree?" Write Leo in that box together.
script.stuck: Read the clue with the child and point to Jack on the tree. Ask, "Is a brother next to Jack, above him, or two rows up?" Brothers and sisters are next to him, parents above, grandparents at the top.

blocks.title: Help the Seagull Find the Boat
blocks.instruction: Look at the whole maze first. Then draw the orangutan's way to the banana tree.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates on a 6 × 6 Grid
blocks.instruction: Find each square by its letter and number. Color it to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the lists name. Show how to find a square: put one finger on the letter at the top and one finger on the number at the side, and move them until they meet. Find the first square of the first list together and color it. Tell the children to cross out each code once its square is colored.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 30
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 30
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 30 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 10 More, 10 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 10 less and the number that is 10 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 10 less. On the right, write the number that is 10 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "Ten more: which digit changes, the tens or the ones?" Show that only the tens digit changes, one more ten for ten more and one less ten for ten less. Count by tens from another number together, for example 7, 17, 27, 37.
script.stuck: If the classroom has a hundreds chart, have the child find the number on it: the number straight above is 10 less, and the number straight below is 10 more. Without a chart, have the child cover the ones digit and change the tens digit by one.

blocks.title: Main Topic and Key Details
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the main topic. Then write two key details from the text.

script.say: "Read the story at the top of the page. Then write what the whole text is about, the main topic, and two key details: facts the text tells about it."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud to the class while the children follow with a finger. Then read the first question aloud and ask, "Where in the story does it tell us?" Find the sentence together and finish the first answer together. The children read the story again on their own before they do the rest.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its words in the story together. Point to the sentence that has the answer and have the child read it aloud. The answer may be a few words; it does not need to be a long sentence.

blocks.title: Synonyms: Circle the Word That Means the Same
blocks.instruction: Read the big word on each card and circle the word under it that means the same.

script.say: "Synonyms are words that mean the same thing, or almost the same, like big and large. Read the big word on each card. Then circle the word under it that means the same."
script.first: Read the big word on the first card and the words under it aloud. Ask, "Which one means the same?" Circle it together. Read the cards aloud with the class before they start.
script.stuck: Read the words of the card to the child and have the child put each one into the same short sentence. The word that keeps the meaning of the sentence is the one to circle.

blocks.title: Ask About the Picture: Why and How
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Finish each question. Start with the word already on the line.

script.say: "Look at the four pictures at the top of the page. You are going to ask questions about them. Each line already starts with a question word: Who, What, Where, When, Why, How. Finish each question, and end it with a question mark."
script.first: Name the four pictures together. Make up a question for the first line aloud and write it on the board with its question mark. Ask two children for a question that starts with What. Tell the class that any question that fits one of the pictures and starts with the printed word is right, and that nobody has to answer the questions.
script.stuck: Point to one picture and ask the child what they would like to know about it. Then help the child say it as a question that starts with the printed word: "Who is this? Where is this place? What is it doing?"

blocks.title: Thirds and Quarters
blocks.instruction: Color the fraction of each shape.

script.say: "Each shape is cut into equal parts. Read the fraction and color that many parts."
script.first: Draw a rectangle cut into four equal parts on the board and color three: "three fourths: three of four equal parts." Do the first shape on the page together: read the fraction, count the parts, and color.
script.stuck: Have the child count the equal parts of the shape and color as many as the top number of the fraction says: any parts, all the way to their edges. A child who colors the whole shape counts the parts again with you.

blocks.title: Tens in Words: 10 to 100
blocks.instruction: Read the number. Circle the word that matches it.

script.say: "Each number has a word that we read and write. Read the number and circle the word that matches it."
script.first: Write 1 to 20 on the board and the words for a few of them. Do the first one together: read the number, read the three words, and circle the matching one.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number aloud and listen to its first sound; find the word that starts with that letter. Read the words with the child.

blocks.title: Family Relationships: Riddles
blocks.instruction: Read each riddle and write the right family word from the box on the line; one word can fit more than one riddle.

script.say: "Now it is time to read and think. Each sentence is a riddle about one child's family. Read the riddle and work it out step by step. Then write the right family word from the box on the line. Some words fit more than one riddle."
script.first: Draw a family tree on the board with stick people: the child the riddles are about at the bottom; the mom and the dad above the child; a grandma and a grandpa above each parent; an aunt or an uncle beside each parent; and a cousin under the aunt. Read the first riddle aloud and follow it on the tree together, one step at a time, and write the word. Keep to the family on the page, not the children's own families.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the end of the riddle and say who its first part names ("the dad"), then add the last word ("his brother"). Following the riddle on the tree on the board helps. The children of an aunt or an uncle are cousins.

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

blocks.title: What Time Is It?
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour, and the long hand shows the minutes: count by fives. Circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Count by fives around the numbers with the class: 5, 10, 15… Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, count the minutes by fives, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then have the child count by fives from the 12 to the long hand: 5, 10, 15.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 31
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 31
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 31 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Addition Practice to 20
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem in your head. Write the missing number in the box.

script.say: "This is math you already know: adding with numbers up to 20. Do the ones you know first. Then go back to the others."
script.first: Do the first two problems on the board. Ask how the children got their answers and accept every way that gives the right answer: counting on from the bigger number, making ten, or just knowing it.
script.stuck: Have the child start at the bigger number and count on the smaller one with fingers: for 13 + 6, say "13" and count on six more. Drawing dots is fine, too, even though the page says to solve the problems in your head.

blocks.title: Fill in the Blank Story
blocks.instruction: Read the whole story. The three pictures show the missing words. Write each word from the bank in its box.

script.say: "This page has three short stories with missing words. The three little pictures above each story show the words that are missing. Find each word in the word bank at the top and write it in the box where it makes sense."
script.first: Read the words in the bank aloud. Read the whole first story aloud with the class and say "blank" at each gap. Look at its pictures and decide together which word goes in each box.
script.stuck: Have the child name the pictures of the story, then read each sentence aloud and try each word in the gap. The spelling is copied from the word bank.

blocks.title: Shades of Meaning: From a Little to a Lot
blocks.instruction: Read the three words in each row and write 1, 2 and 3 in the boxes, from the weakest word to the strongest.

script.say: "Each row has three words that mean almost the same thing, but some are stronger. Write 1 for the weakest word, 2 for the middle one, and 3 for the strongest."
script.first: Act out the first row: tap the desk softly, knock, then bang. Ask which is the weakest and which is the strongest. Write 1, 2, 3 together. Read every row aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Act the words out with the child or say them with your voice, from a little to a lot.

blocks.title: Write About the Picture
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Use the word bank to help you write about what you see.

script.say: "Look at the picture. Use the words in the word bank to help you write about what you see. The sentence starters help you begin."
script.first: Look at the picture together and read the word bank and the sentence starters aloud. Say one sentence together using the first starter, and write it on the board. Tell the children to finish each sentence with their own words and to end it with a period.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "What do you see? What is happening?" Have the child say the sentence aloud before writing it. A child who finishes early writes one more sentence on the last lines.

blocks.title: Find the Symmetric Picture
blocks.instruction: Circle the picture that is the same on both sides.

script.say: "Circle the picture in each row that is the same on both sides."
script.first: Draw a heart with a line down the middle: "Both sides match." Look at the first row together and ask which picture would match if you folded it in the middle.
script.stuck: Have the child cover one side of each picture with a hand, look at the other side, and then switch. The picture whose two sides match is the one to circle.

blocks.title: Two-Step Story Problems Within 100
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Do the first step, then the second step. Write the numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Each story has two steps. Do the first step, then the second step. Write the numbers in the boxes."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "What happens first? What happens next?" Do step a together, then step b with the answer of step a.
script.stuck: Read the story with the child and underline the numbers. Ask, "Are things put together, or taken away?" Draw a quick bar to show the parts and the whole.

blocks.title: Two Stories of the Same Day
blocks.instruction: Read both stories. Underline what both stories say in blue and what only one story says in orange.

script.say: "Two people tell about the same day: underline in blue what both stories say, and in orange what only one story says."
script.first: The children need a blue and an orange crayon. Read both stories aloud while the children follow. Read the first sentence of the first story and ask, "Does the other story say this too, maybe in other words?" If yes, underline it in blue; if only one story says it, in orange. Do the first sentence together. If your page asks for only one of each, find one blue and one orange. Say, "Neither person is wrong. Each one tells what they saw and did."
script.stuck: Read one sentence with the child, then look for the same fact in the other story together. The words can be different and still tell the same thing. If the page asks why they noticed different things, ask, "What was each person doing that day?"

blocks.title: Bring the Toy Car to the Garage Safely
blocks.instruction: Help the polar bear get to the igloo. Do not take a road with a walrus or a hole in the ice.

script.say: "Help the animal get home safely. Look at the whole maze first. Do not take a road with one of the dangers the page names."
script.first: Read the title aloud and show the start and the goal. Point to the dangers on the page and say that a road with a danger is closed. Trace a way with your finger and stop at each fork: "Is there a danger on this road?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates: Write the Codes
blocks.instruction: The picture is colored in. Write the code of each square in the list for its color.

script.say: "This grid already has a picture colored in. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. Write the name of each colored square in the list for its color."
script.first: Show how to name a square: go straight up from the square to its letter and straight to the side to its number, and write the letter first. Do the first colored square together and write its code in the first box of the list. Tell the children to put a small dot on each square once its code is written.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on the square and move it straight up to read the letter, then straight to the left to read the number. The order of the codes in the list does not matter, as long as every colored square is there once.

packs.title: Second Grade Sub Plans: Week 32
packs.metaTitle: Second Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 32
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 32 of second grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Odd Number Hunt
blocks.instruction: Circle every ODD number. Look at the last digit to decide.

script.say: "Even numbers can be split into two equal groups. Odd numbers always have one left over. You only need to look at the last digit. If a number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9, it is odd. Circle every odd number."
script.first: Write 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 on the board and leave it there. Do the first few numbers together: point to the last digit and ask, "Is it on our list?" Circle the number if it is: it is odd.
script.stuck: Have the child cover every digit but the last one with a finger and check it against the list on the board.

blocks.title: How a Character Meets a Challenge
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then write the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Ask the class, "What is the character's problem? What does the character do about it?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Split the Compound: Find the Two Words
blocks.instruction: The whole word is printed letter by letter next to its picture. Draw one line where the second word starts.

script.say: "A compound word is made of two smaller words, like sun and flower in sunflower. Each word on this page is printed letter by letter. Draw one line where the second word starts."
script.first: Read every word on the page aloud with the class. Then read the first word again and look at its picture. Ask, "Which two words make it?" Draw one line where the second word starts, together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the whole word and clap once for each of the two small words, then cover the end of the word with a finger and move it until a real word shows.

blocks.title: Possessive Pronouns
blocks.instruction: Look at who owns the thing. Circle the word that shows it belongs to that person.

script.say: "Words like his, her, and their tell who something belongs to. Look at who owns the thing in each row. Read the sentence and circle the word that fits: his, her, or their."
script.first: Read the first row aloud and look at who owns the thing. Ask, "Is it a boy's, a girl's, or more than one person's?" Circle his, her, or their together. Read each row aloud with the class.
script.stuck: Have the child count the people in the little picture: one boy takes his, one girl takes her, and two or more people take their, whether they are boys or girls.

blocks.title: Share the Set
blocks.instruction: Circle the fraction of the pictures. Write how many that is.

script.say: "Each row shows a group of pictures and a fraction. Circle that part of the group, and write how many that is."
script.first: Draw 8 circles on the board. Say, "One half means two equal groups. Half of 8 is 4." Circle 4. For one fourth, make four equal groups and circle one group. Do the first row together.
script.stuck: Have the child share the pictures into as many equal groups as the bottom number says, one picture at a time. Then circle as many groups as the top number says.

blocks.title: True or False?
blocks.instruction: Is each equation true? Circle the check mark if it is true and the X if it is false.

script.say: "Is each number sentence true? If both sides are the same amount, it is true: circle the check mark. If not, it is false: circle the X."
script.first: Write 10 − 2 = 8 on the board and ask, "Is ten take away two eight? Yes: true." Write 9 = 5 + 6 and ask, "Is five and six nine? No: false." Remind the children that the equals sign means "the same as" and can be on either side.
script.stuck: Have the child work out the side with the plus or minus sign and then compare it with the number on the other side.

blocks.title: Parts of a Plant We Eat
blocks.instruction: Look at each food. Circle the part of the plant that we eat.

script.say: "We eat different parts of plants: roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds. Look at each food and circle the part of the plant we eat."
script.first: Draw a plant on the board and label its parts. Name the first food on the page together and ask, "Does it grow under the ground, is it the stem, a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or a seed?" Circle the word.
script.stuck: Ask the child where the food grows: under the ground (roots), the long part that holds the plant up (stem), the flat green part (leaf), the part bees visit (flower), the part with seeds inside (fruit), or the seed itself. Let the child choose and say why.

blocks.title: Treasure Hunt: Follow the Steps
blocks.instruction: Start at the flag. Follow the steps. Circle the picture where you land.

script.say: "Start at the flag on the grid. Follow the steps, one at a time: each step says which way to move and how many squares. Circle the picture where you land."
script.first: Put your finger on the flag and read the first step aloud: "Move 1 square right." Move the finger together and stop. Read the next step and move again. Tell the children to count the squares, not the lines, and to keep the finger on the page until the last step.
script.stuck: Have the child say each step aloud and point with a finger. Check right and left: "Which hand is your right hand? Move that way."

blocks.title: The Other Half
blocks.instruction: Trace the dashed half so both sides of each picture look the same.

script.say: "Each picture is the same on both sides of the line, but one side is dashed. Trace the dashed half so both sides look the same."
script.first: Fold a sheet of paper in half and show that both halves match. Point to the dashed half of the first picture and trace a few dashes together, slowly.
script.stuck: Have the child trace one part of the dashed half at a time and compare it with the same part on the solid side: the two must look like a picture and its reflection.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 1
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 1
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 1 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Walls with Two-Digit Answers
blocks.instruction: The numbers go past 20. Add each pair of bricks and write the sum in the brick above.

script.say: "This is a number wall. Each brick is the sum of the two bricks right under it. Start at the bottom and build every wall to the top. The numbers get bigger than twenty, so you may add on paper."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks next to each other at the bottom and add them aloud, tens and ones; write the sum in the brick above them. Tell the children to work up the wall one row at a time.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers on scrap paper, tens and ones. A wrong brick lower down makes every brick above it wrong, so check the rows from the bottom up.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: The Sandcastle
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence. When you finish, turn the page over and write three sentences that tell what happens next in the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow; then they read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Which sentence helps us?" Circle the answer together. Question 3 asks the children to write their own answer on the lines: tell them to use a full sentence.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question.

blocks.title: Closed and Open Syllables
blocks.instruction: An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name: ro | bot.

script.say: "A closed syllable ends with a consonant, and its vowel is short: rab in rabbit. An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name: ro in robot. Read each word, draw a line between its syllables, and write C or O for each one."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write robot and rabbit on the board, split them together (ro|bot, rab|bit), and mark each part C or O. Read the first word on the page together and do it.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the letters between the two vowels. Two consonants: split between them. One consonant: split after the first vowel and say it long; if that is not a word, split after the consonant and say it short. A part that ends with a vowel is open, a part that ends with a consonant is closed. For your own reference, on this page the splits are hu|mid, e|mu, pro|gram, ra|ven, la|bel, ten|nis, so|lo, pu|pil, ha|lo, mi|nus, po|lo, bi|son, lo|go, pup|pet, hu|man, and pen|cil; a part that ends with a vowel gets O, a part that ends with a consonant gets C. The sentences take silo, unit, music, bacon, hotel, and photo.

blocks.title: Write About the Picture
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Use the word bank to help you write about what you see.

script.say: "Look at the picture. Use the words in the word bank to help you write about what you see. The sentence starters help you begin."
script.first: Look at the picture together and read the word bank and the sentence starters aloud. Say one sentence together using the first starter, and write it on the board. Tell the children to finish each sentence with their own words and to end it with a period.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "What do you see? What is happening?" Have the child say the sentence aloud before writing it. A child who finishes early writes one more sentence on the last lines.

blocks.title: 2-Digit Column Subtraction
blocks.instruction: Subtract one place at a time. Start with the ones.

script.say: "These subtraction problems are written one number under the other. Subtract one place at a time. Start on the right with the ones. Then subtract the tens."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board, one number under the other. Subtract the ones first, then the tens, and write each digit under its column. Tell the children to check the sign before they start.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens column with a finger and subtract only the ones, then cover the ones and subtract the tens. Counting back on fingers is fine for the small differences.

blocks.title: Jump Puzzles: Follow the Arrows
blocks.instruction: Start at the number and follow the arrows: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, right is 1 more. Write where you land.

script.say: "Each puzzle starts at a number and has three arrows. Every arrow changes the number: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, and right is 1 more. Follow the arrows and write the number where you land."
script.first: Point to the key at the top of the page and read it aloud together. Do the first puzzle on the board, one arrow at a time, and write the number after each arrow: for example, "30, one less is 29, ten more is 39, one less is 38."
script.stuck: Have the child write the new number above each arrow before going on to the next one. If the classroom has a hundreds chart, the child can put a finger on the starting number and move one square for each arrow.

blocks.title: Parts of a Plant We Eat
blocks.instruction: Look at each food. Circle the part of the plant that we eat.

script.say: "We eat different parts of plants: roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds. Look at each food and circle the part of the plant we eat."
script.first: Draw a plant on the board and label its parts. Name the first food on the page together and ask, "Does it grow under the ground, is it the stem, a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or a seed?" Circle the word.
script.stuck: Ask the child where the food grows: under the ground (roots), the long part that holds the plant up (stem), the flat green part (leaf), the part bees visit (flower), the part with seeds inside (fruit), or the seed itself. Let the child choose and say why.

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

blocks.title: The Other Half
blocks.instruction: Trace the dashed half so both sides of each picture look the same.

script.say: "Each picture is the same on both sides of the line, but one side is dashed. Trace the dashed half so both sides look the same."
script.first: Fold a sheet of paper in half and show that both halves match. Point to the dashed half of the first picture and trace a few dashes together, slowly.
script.stuck: Have the child trace one part of the dashed half at a time and compare it with the same part on the solid side: the two must look like a picture and its reflection.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 2
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 2
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 2 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Rounding Up or Down? Sort the Numbers
blocks.instruction: Does each number round up or down to the nearest ten? Write it in the right bin.

script.say: "Rounding to the nearest ten: look at the ones digit. 0 to 4 round down, 5 to 9 round up. Write each number in the right bin: round down or round up."
script.first: Read the box at the top: 0 to 4 round down, 5 to 9 round up. Do the first number together: look at its ones digit and write it in the right bin.
script.stuck: Have the child cover every digit but the ones digit with a finger and check it against the box at the top: 0 to 4 down, 5 to 9 up.

blocks.title: What Is the Lesson?
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write its lesson. Then write what a character does that shows the lesson.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write its lesson, the thing a reader learns from it, and what a character does that shows the lesson."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. After reading, ask, "What does the story teach us?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Base Words and Suffixes
blocks.instruction: A suffix at the end changes the word: kind + ness = kindness.

script.say: "A suffix at the end changes a word: kind and -ness make kindness. Read each word, circle the base word, and underline the suffix. Then do the rest of the page."
script.first: Write kindness on the board: circle kind, underline -ness. Ask what it means: being kind. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then read the whole word and ask what it means.

blocks.title: Match the Verb to Its Past Tense
blocks.instruction: Read each verb on the left. Draw a line to its past tense (the yesterday form) on the right — one line for each verb.

script.say: "Read each verb on the left. Draw a line to its past tense, the yesterday form, on the right."
script.first: Write jump and jumped on the board: "Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped." Read the first verb aloud and find its yesterday form together. Some verbs change: sing, sang.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud with the verb and listen. If the sentence has "yesterday," the verb tells about the past (jumped). With one person and "today" or "every day," the verb gets an s (runs, sings).

blocks.title: Rows and Columns
blocks.instruction: Count the rows and columns. Finish the multiplication sentence.

script.say: "Count the rows and the columns of each array. Finish the multiplication sentence: rows times columns."
script.first: Draw an array of 3 rows of 4 dots on the board. Count the rows and the columns together, then add the rows: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Show that 3 × 4 means 3 rows of 4. Do the first picture on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child run a finger along each row of an array and count the rows first, then count the things in the top row. On this page the first number is the number of rows and the second number is how many are in each row.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot: Count by Fives
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Count by fives from 5 to 50 and connect the dots. Part of the picture is already drawn.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot, and you count by fives. Start at the orange dot at 5. Draw a line to 10, then to 15, and keep going to 50."
script.first: Count by fives from 5 to 50 together. Find the orange dot at 5 together and draw the line to 10. Part of the picture is already drawn; the dots finish it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and add five; that is the dot to look for. The numbers in the row at the bottom can be crossed off one by one.

blocks.title: My Habitat Report
blocks.instruction: In the picture, draw three animals that live there, write their names and a plant that grows there, and circle the word that fits this habitat.

script.say: "This is your habitat report. In the picture, draw three animals that live there and write their names. Then write a plant that grows there, and circle whether the habitat is wet or dry."
script.first: Read the name of the habitat on the page aloud and talk about it: "What animals live in the ocean?" Let a few children say ideas. Each child draws and labels three animals.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Which animals have you seen at an aquarium, in a book, or in a movie about the sea?" Any animal that lives in the ocean is right, and the drawing does not have to be neat. Point to the board for the spelling.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates
blocks.instruction: Find each square by its letter and number, like B2. Color it with the color of its group to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Read the first square, for example B2: go across to B and down to 2. Color it in its color together. Tell the children to cross off each square on the list as they color it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

blocks.title: Find the Symmetric Picture
blocks.instruction: Circle the picture that is the same on both sides.

script.say: "Circle the picture in each row that is the same on both sides."
script.first: Draw a heart with a line down the middle: "Both sides match." Look at the first row together and ask which picture would match if you folded it in the middle.
script.stuck: Have the child cover one side of each picture with a hand, look at the other side, and then switch. The picture whose two sides match is the one to circle.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 3
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 3
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 3 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count by Threes
blocks.instruction: Skip count by 3. Write each missing number.

script.say: "On this page we count by threes: 3, 6, 9, 12. Some numbers are missing. Count by threes and write each missing number. The rows do not start at 3."
script.first: Count by threes together to 60. Read the first row aloud and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. Tell the children that a row does not always start at 3.
script.stuck: Have the child add three to the number before the gap with fingers: say the number, then count three more. To check, the next printed number must be three more than the number the child wrote.

blocks.title: How a Character Meets a Challenge
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then write the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Ask the class, "What is the character's problem? What does the character do about it?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Closed or Open? Sort Long Words
blocks.instruction: A closed syllable has a short vowel; an open syllable has a long vowel.

script.say: "A closed syllable ends with a consonant, and its vowel is short: rab in rabbit. An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name: ro in robot. Read each word and write it under its heading, closed or open first syllable, with a line between its syllables. Then answer each sentence with yes or no."
script.first: Read the two headings aloud. Write tiger and napkin on the board and split them together: ti|ger has an open first syllable with a long i, nap|kin a closed one with a short a. Read the first word on the page together and write it under its heading.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the letters between the two vowels. Two consonants: split between them. One consonant: split after the first vowel and say it long; if that is not a word, split after the consonant and say it short. A part that ends with a vowel is open, a part that ends with a consonant is closed. For your own reference, on this page the words with a closed first syllable are hel|met, sig|nal, rib|bon, mod|el, grav|el, and trav|el; the words with an open first syllable are ro|bot, fo|cus, mu|sic, and mo|tel. The answers to the sentences are yes, no, no, yes, no, no.

blocks.title: Fix the Sentence: Where Does It End?
blocks.instruction: Two sentences ran together. Write them as two sentences.

script.say: "Two sentences ran together. Find where the first one ends and write them as two sentences, each with a capital letter and a period."
script.first: Read the first line aloud and stop where the first idea ends. Write it on the board as two sentences together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the first word, then on every name, then on the end of the sentence, and ask at each place, "Capital letter? End mark?" The three small pictures above the first sentence show the three things to check.

blocks.title: Addition and Subtraction with Regrouping
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem. Regroup when you need to carry or borrow.

script.say: "Look at the sign of each problem first. Work one place at a time, starting with the ones: carry when a sum is ten or more, borrow when the top digit is too small."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board, one number under the other. Point to the sign first. Work the ones column first: if it is 10 or more, carry a ten; if you cannot take away, borrow a ten. Then the tens and the hundreds.
script.stuck: Have the child cover all but one column and work it aloud. If a sum is ten or more, carry the ten; if the top digit is too small, borrow a ten. Check the sign of each problem first.

blocks.title: Expanded Form Both Ways
blocks.instruction: Put the parts together, or break each number into hundreds, tens and ones. Write the numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Every digit in a number is worth something. In 479, the 4 is worth 400, the 7 is worth 70, and the 9 is worth 9. This page goes both ways. When the parts are printed, put them together and write the number in the box. When the number is printed, break it into its hundreds, its tens, and its ones."
script.first: Write 257 on the board and break it up together: 200 + 50 + 7. Then go the other way: 400 + 30 + 2 = 432. Point out that some problems put the parts together and others break the number up. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the number aloud slowly and write what each part says: "two hundred" is 200, "forty" is 40, "two" is 2. A child who writes 2 + 4 + 2 for 242 has copied the digits; point to the first 2 and ask, "Is this 2 ones or 2 hundreds?" The right three parts in another order are still correct.

blocks.title: Family Relationships: Riddles
blocks.instruction: Read each riddle and write the right family word from the box on the line; one word can fit more than one riddle.

script.say: "Now it is time to read and think. Each sentence is a riddle about one child's family. Read the riddle and work it out step by step. Then write the right family word from the box on the line. Some words fit more than one riddle."
script.first: Draw a family tree on the board with stick people: the child the riddles are about at the bottom; the mom and the dad above the child; a grandma and a grandpa above each parent; an aunt or an uncle beside each parent; and a cousin under the aunt. Read the first riddle aloud and follow it on the tree together, one step at a time, and write the word. Keep to the family on the page, not the children's own families.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the end of the riddle and say who its first part names ("the dad"), then add the last word ("his brother"). Following the riddle on the tree on the board helps. The children of an aunt or an uncle are cousins.

blocks.title: Help the Rabbit Pick Up Every Carrot
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

blocks.title: Read the Calendar
blocks.instruction: Look at the calendar. Use it to answer every question.

script.say: "This is a calendar page for one month. The questions under it ask you to find things on the calendar. Read each question and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the month and the days of the week across the top. Read the first question aloud and find the answer on the calendar together: put one finger on the date and slide up the column to its day.
script.stuck: For a question about a day of the week, have the child find the date and move a finger straight up its column to the day's name. For a question about a picture, the child looks for the little picture inside the calendar.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 4
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 4
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 4 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Going Down!
blocks.instruction: The numbers go down by the same amount. Write the missing numbers.

script.say: "The numbers in each row go down by the same amount. Find how much, and write the missing numbers."
script.first: Read the first row aloud. Look at two numbers next to each other and ask, "How much less is the second?" Count back by that amount to fill the empty boxes together.
script.stuck: Have the child find two numbers next to each other with no gap and count down from one to the other: that is the step. Where one box is empty between two numbers, the jump is two steps.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: A Card for Mom
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow; then they read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Which sentence helps us?" Circle the answer together. Question 3 asks the children to write their own answer on the lines: tell them to use a full sentence.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question.

blocks.title: Which Word Fits? Suffixes in Sentences
blocks.instruction: -ness and -ment make nouns: soft, softness; move, movement.

script.say: "A suffix at the end changes a word: kind and -ness make kindness. Read each word, circle the base word, and underline the suffix. Then do the rest of the page."
script.first: Write kindness on the board: circle kind, underline -ness. Ask what it means: being kind. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then read the whole word and ask what it means.

blocks.title: Parts of a Friendly Letter
blocks.instruction: A friendly letter has a date, a greeting, a body, a closing, and a signature.

script.say: "A friendly letter has five parts: the date, the greeting, the body, the closing, and the signature. Write the name of each part on its line, using the word bank."
script.first: Read the five parts in the word bank aloud and find each one in the letter on the page together: the date at the top, "Dear…" is the greeting, the long middle is the body, "Your friend" is the closing, and the name at the end is the signature. Do the first one together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Where does a letter start? Who is it to? Who wrote it?" Point to each part as you ask.

blocks.title: Shopping Math: Two Stories
blocks.instruction: Read each story and use the shelf prices to answer it.

script.say: "Read each story and use the prices on the shelf to answer it."
script.first: Read the prices on the shelf aloud. Read the first story aloud and find the prices of the things in it; add them together on the board.
script.stuck: Have the child circle the two things on the shelf that the question shows, then write the two prices one under the other and add the ones first. Coins or drawn dimes and pennies help a child who cannot add the numbers yet.

blocks.title: Thirds and Quarters
blocks.instruction: Color the fraction of each shape.

script.say: "Each shape is cut into equal parts. Read the fraction and color that many parts."
script.first: Draw a rectangle cut into four equal parts on the board and color three: "three fourths: three of four equal parts." Do the first shape on the page together: read the fraction, count the parts, and color.
script.stuck: Have the child count the equal parts of the shape and color as many as the top number of the fraction says: any parts, all the way to their edges. A child who colors the whole shape counts the parts again with you.

blocks.title: Civic Virtues at School
blocks.instruction: Read each situation. Write the virtue it calls for. Use each word one time. Then write what a good citizen would do.

script.say: "Read each situation. Write the virtue it calls for, using each word in the word box one time. Then write what a good citizen would do."
script.first: Read the word box aloud: each virtue and what it means. Read the first situation aloud and ask, "Which virtue does this call for?" Find the word that fits and write it together. Then finish "A good citizen would" together with something kind and true to do, such as "tell the truth" or "give everyone a turn." If your page asks for a situation of your own for a partner, any real school moment is right.
script.stuck: Read the meanings in the word box with the child, one at a time, and ask, "Does this one fit?" A tight stomach, a fast heart, or shaking hands in the situation means it takes courage. Owning up to something you did: honesty. A job or a promise you said you would do: responsibility. Sharing turns or things with others: fairness. Someone new or different (new words, a new lunch, an idea unlike your own): respect.

blocks.title: Find 7 Differences at the Pond
blocks.instruction: Circle the 7 differences, 4 in the left pair of pictures and 3 in the right pair, and check a box for each.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle. There are two pairs of pictures. The pictures in each pair look the same, but they are not. Find 4 differences in the left pair and 3 in the right pair, and circle each one."
script.first: Find one difference in the left pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Show how to circle it and check off one box, so that everyone can see how many are still left to find.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom.

blocks.title: Quarter Hours
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Every clock on this page shows a quarter hour: something o'clock, quarter past, half past, or quarter to. Read each clock and circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Show quarter past (the long hand on 3), half past (on 6), and quarter to (on 9). Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, the minutes from the long hand, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then look at the long hand: on the 12 is o'clock, on the 3 quarter past, on the 6 half past, on the 9 quarter to.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 5
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 5
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 5 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Odd Number Hunt
blocks.instruction: Circle every ODD number. Look at the last digit to decide.

script.say: "Even numbers can be split into two equal groups. Odd numbers always have one left over. You only need to look at the last digit. If a number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9, it is odd. Circle every odd number."
script.first: Write 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 on the board and leave it there. Do the first few numbers together: point to the last digit and ask, "Is it on our list?" Circle the number if it is: it is odd.
script.stuck: Have the child cover every digit but the last one with a finger and check it against the list on the board.

blocks.title: What Is the Lesson?
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write its lesson. Then write what a character does that shows the lesson.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write its lesson, the thing a reader learns from it, and what a character does that shows the lesson."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. After reading, ask, "What does the story teach us?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Split the Compound: Find the Two Words
blocks.instruction: The whole word is printed letter by letter next to its picture. Draw one line where the second word starts.

script.say: "A compound word is made of two smaller words, like sun and flower in sunflower. Each word on this page is printed letter by letter. Draw one line where the second word starts."
script.first: Read every word on the page aloud with the class. Then read the first word again and look at its picture. Ask, "Which two words make it?" Draw one line where the second word starts, together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the whole word and clap once for each of the two small words, then cover the end of the word with a finger and move it until a real word shows.

blocks.title: The Irregular Verbs: be, have, do, go
blocks.instruction: These verbs change a lot. Write the today form and the yesterday form of each one in the dashed boxes.

script.say: "Be, have, do, and go change a lot. Write the today form and the yesterday form of each one in the dashed boxes. Then finish the sentences."
script.first: Say the verbs with the class: go, goes, went; have, has, had; be, is, was; do, does, did. Do the first row together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud with the verb and listen. If the sentence has "yesterday," the verb tells about the past (jumped). With one person and "today" or "every day," the verb gets an s (runs, sings).

blocks.title: Big Arrays
blocks.instruction: Count all the pictures. Write how many there are in all.

script.say: "Count the equal groups and how many are in each group. Finish the multiplication: the number of groups times the number in each group."
script.first: Draw 3 groups of 4 dots on the board. Count the groups and the dots in one group: 3 groups of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child count by the number in each group: 4, 8, 12. The number of groups is how many times they count.

blocks.title: Story Problems Within 100: Question, Equation, Answer
blocks.instruction: Read each story. If the question is missing, write a question that fits. Then write the equation and the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Write the question if it is missing, then the equation and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "What do we need to find out?" Write the equation on the board together and solve it with tens and ones. Then the children read the other stories on their own.
script.stuck: Read the story with the child and underline the numbers. Ask, "Are things put together, or taken away?" Draw a quick bar to show the parts and the whole.

blocks.title: Label the Butterfly Life Cycle
blocks.instruction: Write the four stage names from the word bank on the lines under their pictures, then cross out the name that does not belong.

script.say: "A butterfly grows in four stages. Write the four stage names from the word bank on the lines under their pictures. Then cross out the name that is not part of a butterfly's life."
script.first: Read the word bank aloud together. Ask, "What does a butterfly start as?" An egg. Find the egg picture and write egg under it together. Talk through the order: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A tadpole is a baby frog.
script.stuck: Have the child follow the arrows from the egg and name what each picture shows.

blocks.title: Draw It Twice as Big
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big.

script.say: "Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big."
script.first: Find the top-left colored square on the small grid together and count which row and which column it is in. Find the same row and column on the big grid and color that square. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Rounding to the Nearest 10 and 100
blocks.instruction: Round each number twice: to the nearest ten in the first box and to the nearest hundred in the second.

script.say: "Round each number two times: first to the nearest ten, then to the nearest hundred. Look at the digit to the right of the place you round to: 0 to 4, round down; 5 to 9, round up."
script.first: Read the example at the top together; the wavy equal sign means "is about." Do the first number on the board: underline its tens digit and look at the ones digit to round to the nearest ten; then underline its hundreds digit and look at the tens digit to round to the nearest hundred. Tell the children to start from the number on the page both times.
script.stuck: Have the child say the two tens the number is between and ask which one is closer; then the two hundreds. A 5 always rounds up.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 6
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 6
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 6 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 100 More, 100 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 100 less and the number that is 100 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 100 less. On the right, write the number that is 100 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "A hundred more: which digit changes? Which two stay the same?" Show that only the hundreds digit changes. Count by hundreds from another number together.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens and the ones with a finger and look only at the hundreds digit: one less for 100 less, one more for 100 more. The two covered digits are copied as they are.

blocks.title: Show Where the Story Says It
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write each answer. In the box, write the number of the paragraph that proves your answer.

script.say: "Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. Then write each answer. In the box, write the number of the paragraph that proves your answer."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Show the children the small numbers at the start of the paragraphs.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the story. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Suffixes -ful, -less, and -ly
blocks.instruction: -ful means full of, and -less means without.

script.say: "A suffix is a word part at the end. -ful means full of, -less means without, and -ly tells how. Circle the base word in each word and underline the suffix. Then match each word to its meaning."
script.first: Write playful on the board: circle play, underline -ful. Ask, "What does playful mean? Full of play." Do the same with toothless. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then add the suffix and ask what the whole word means.

blocks.title: Write About the Picture
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture. Use the word bank to help you write about what you see.

script.say: "Look at the picture. Use the words in the word bank to help you write about what you see. The sentence starters help you begin."
