script.first: Look at the picture together and read the word bank and the sentence starters aloud. Say one sentence together using the first starter, and write it on the board. Tell the children to finish each sentence with their own words and to end it with a period.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "What do you see? What is happening?" Have the child say the sentence aloud before writing it. A child who finishes early writes one more sentence on the last lines.

blocks.title: Subtracting Across Zeros
blocks.instruction: Subtract one place at a time. Regroup when you need to borrow.

script.say: "These are subtraction problems, written one number under the other. Work one place at a time, starting with the ones, and borrow when the top digit is too small. Where the tens digit is 0, borrow from the hundreds first."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board. The top number has a zero in the tens place, so to borrow for the ones you first borrow from the hundreds: the 0 becomes 10, then 9. Work it through together.
script.stuck: Have the child work one column at a time. Where the tens digit is 0, the child borrows from the hundreds first: the 0 becomes 10, then gives one ten to the ones and becomes 9.

blocks.title: More Than Nine of a Kind
blocks.instruction: Count the blocks. Ten ones make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Write the number.

script.say: "Count the blocks in each picture. Ten small cubes make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Write the number they show."
script.first: Draw a flat (a hundred), two rods, and four small cubes on the board. Count together: "one hundred, one hundred ten, one hundred twenty, and four more: one hundred twenty-four." Tell the children that when there are ten or more cubes of one kind, they bundle ten into the next place. Do the first picture together.
script.stuck: Have the child count each kind first: hundreds, tens, ones. If there are more than nine ones, circle ten of them: that is one more ten.

blocks.title: Make Clay Float: A Change the Shape Experiment
blocks.instruction: Color the ring where each clay shape ends up, circle the thing that floats, then draw your own clay boat in the big tank.

script.say: "The same clay can sink or float: a ball of clay sinks, a clay boat floats. Color the ring where each clay shape ends up, circle the thing that floats, then draw your own clay boat."
script.first: Talk about the pictures: a ball and a flat boat made of the same clay. Ask, "Which one floats? Why?" Do the first part together.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is it flat and wide like a boat, or a tight ball?"

blocks.title: Mystery Number: Two Arrows, One Square
blocks.instruction: Follow both arrows. They point to the same square of the chart. Write the mystery number.

script.say: "Each puzzle has two numbers, and each number has an arrow. The key at the top tells what the arrows do: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, and right is 1 more. Both arrows lead to the same number. Find that mystery number and write it in the box."
script.first: Point to the key at the top: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, right is 1 more. Do the first puzzle on the board: follow the first number's arrow, then the second number's arrow, and check that both land on the same number.
script.stuck: Have the child say what the arrow does before using it, and follow only one arrow at first. Then the child follows the second arrow; if the two answers are not the same, one of them needs another look.

blocks.title: Find 10 Differences in the Garden
blocks.instruction: Circle the 10 differences, 5 in each pair of pictures, and check a box under the pair for every one you find.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle with two pairs of pictures. In each pair, the picture on the right is different in 5 places. Circle each difference, and check a box under the pair for every one you find."
script.first: Find one difference in the top pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Circle it in the picture on the right and check off one box.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom. Things can be missing, added, or changed.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 7
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 7
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 7 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: The 2 Times Table
blocks.instruction: Multiply. Write each product in the box.

script.say: "Multiply. Write each product in the box. All the problems on this page use the same times table."
script.first: Count by the table's number together to ten times it. Do the first two problems together and show that each answer is the one before plus one more group.
script.stuck: Have the child count by the table's number on fingers, one finger for each group, or start from a fact the child knows: 5 times the number, then count on by one more group.

blocks.title: The Central Message
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write its central message and three things in the story that show it.

script.say: "Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. Then write its central message, the lesson it teaches, and three things in the story that show it."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. After reading, ask, "What does this story teach us?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the story. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Describing Words in Real Life
blocks.instruction: Describing words tell what real things are like: a warm hat, a cold drink.

script.say: "Describing words tell what real things are like: hot soup, a soft blanket. Read each sentence and do what the page asks."
script.first: Read the first part of the page aloud with the class and do its first item together. Ask, "What is this thing really like? Which word fits?"
script.stuck: Ask the child to think of a real one: "Have you touched one? Is it hard or soft, hot or cold?"

blocks.title: Fix the Sentence: Where Does It End?
blocks.instruction: Two sentences ran together. Write them as two sentences.

script.say: "Two sentences ran together. Find where the first one ends and write them as two sentences, each with a capital letter and a period."
script.first: Read the first line aloud and stop where the first idea ends. Write it on the board as two sentences together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the first word, then on every name, then on the end of the sentence, and ask at each place, "Capital letter? End mark?" The three small pictures above the first sentence show the three things to check.

blocks.title: Tricky Groups
blocks.instruction: Count the equal groups. Finish the multiplication.

script.say: "Count the equal groups and how many are in each group. Finish the multiplication: the number of groups times the number in each group."
script.first: Draw 3 groups of 4 dots on the board. Count the groups and the dots in one group: 3 groups of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child count by the number in each group: 4, 8, 12. The number of groups is how many times they count.

blocks.title: Tally to Graph
blocks.instruction: Read the tally chart. Color one bar for each count.

script.say: "Read the tally chart. Color one box of the bar graph for each tally mark."
script.first: Count the tally marks of the first row together: a bundle with a line across is five. Color that many boxes in its bar, from the bottom up.
script.stuck: Have the child write the number next to each tally first: five for each bundle, then the single marks. For the bar, the child puts a finger on that number at the side of the graph and colors up to its line.

blocks.title: Continents and Oceans
blocks.instruction: Find each continent and ocean on the map. Write its number in the box next to its name.

script.say: "The map shows the continents and the oceans, each with a number. If your page has names, write each number in the box next to its name. If it has numbered lines, write each name on the line with its number."
script.first: Point to North America: "This is where the United States is." Find its number together, then write it in its box, or write "North America" on its line. The oceans are the big shaded areas around the white land.
script.stuck: Give clues: "The Pacific is the biggest ocean, on the left and right. Antarctica is the icy land at the bottom." Let the child find each one.

blocks.title: The Other Half
blocks.instruction: Trace the dashed half so both sides of each picture look the same.

script.say: "Each picture is the same on both sides of the line, but one side is dashed. Trace the dashed half so both sides look the same."
script.first: Fold a sheet of paper in half and show that both halves match. Point to the dashed half of the first picture and trace a few dashes together, slowly.
script.stuck: Have the child trace one part of the dashed half at a time and compare it with the same part on the solid side: the two must look like a picture and its reflection.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates on a 10 × 10 Grid
blocks.instruction: Find each square on the big grid by its letter and number. Color it to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the lists name. Show how to find a square: put one finger on the letter at the top and one finger on the number at the side, and move them until they meet. Find the first square of the first list together and color it. Tell the children to cross out each code once its square is colored.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 8
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 8
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 8 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Machines
blocks.instruction: Each machine uses its rule on every number. Fill in the missing ones.

script.say: "Each number machine has a rule, printed at the top. A number goes in on the left, the machine uses its rule, and a new number comes out on the right. Fill in the missing numbers. Watch out: sometimes the number that went in is the one that is missing."
script.first: Read the rule of the first machine aloud, for example "+9." Do the first number together: put it in, use the rule, and write what comes out. If the number that comes out is given, go backward: use the opposite rule.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is the missing number before the arrow or after it?" After the arrow, the child uses the rule. Before the arrow, the child does the opposite, then checks by putting the number through the machine.

blocks.title: Answer with Evidence
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write each answer. In the box, write the number of the paragraph that proves your answer.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write each answer. In the box, write the number of the paragraph that proves your answer."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Show the children the small numbers at the start of the paragraphs.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Split the Compound: Find the Two Words
blocks.instruction: The whole word is printed letter by letter next to its picture. Draw one line where the second word starts.

script.say: "A compound word is made of two smaller words, like sun and flower in sunflower. Each word on this page is printed letter by letter. Draw one line where the second word starts."
script.first: Read every word on the page aloud with the class. Then read the first word again and look at its picture. Ask, "Which two words make it?" Draw one line where the second word starts, together.
script.stuck: Have the child say the whole word and clap once for each of the two small words, then cover the end of the word with a finger and move it until a real word shows.

blocks.title: Match the Verb to Its Past Tense
blocks.instruction: Read each verb on the left. Draw a line to its past tense (the yesterday form) on the right — one line for each verb.

script.say: "Read each verb on the left. Draw a line to its past tense, the yesterday form, on the right."
script.first: Write jump and jumped on the board: "Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped." Read the first verb aloud and find its yesterday form together. Some verbs change: sing, sang.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud with the verb and listen. If the sentence has "yesterday," the verb tells about the past (jumped). With one person and "today" or "every day," the verb gets an s (runs, sings).

blocks.title: 3-Digit Numbers in Columns
blocks.instruction: Add or subtract one place at a time. Start with the ones.

script.say: "Add or subtract one place at a time: ones, then tens, then hundreds. Look at the sign of each problem first."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board, one number under the other. Point to the sign. Work the ones column first, then the tens, then the hundreds. Tell the children to check the sign of every problem, because the page mixes them.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens column with a finger and add only the ones, then cover the ones and add the tens. Fingers or dots are fine for the small sums.

blocks.title: Read the Line Plot
blocks.instruction: Count the X marks above each number. Write how many.

script.say: "A line plot shows how many with X marks above each number. Count the X marks above each number and write how many."
script.first: Draw a short number line on the board with a few X marks above the numbers. Count the X marks above one number together and write the count. Do the first question on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the number and count the X marks straight above it, from the bottom up.

blocks.title: Name the Moon Phases
blocks.instruction: Look at each moon. Write its name on the lines. Use each word in the word bank twice.

script.say: "Look at each moon. Write its name on the lines: new moon, first quarter, full moon, or last quarter. Use each word in the word bank twice."
script.first: Read the word bank aloud. Draw a full moon (all bright) and a new moon (dark) on the board. A quarter moon shows half of the circle bright. Do the first moon on the page together.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is it all bright, all dark, or half bright?" A half-bright moon is a quarter: first quarter when the right side is bright, last quarter when the left side is.

blocks.title: Line of Symmetry?
blocks.instruction: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry? Circle the check mark or the X.

script.say: "A mirror line cuts a picture into two halves that match exactly, like a picture and its reflection in a mirror. Look at the dashed line on each picture. If both sides match, circle the check. If they do not match, circle the X."
script.first: Draw a heart with a dashed line down the middle: "If I fold here, both sides match: a line of symmetry." Look at the first picture and its dashed line together: would the two sides match? Circle the check mark or the X.
script.stuck: Have the child cover one side of the picture with a hand, look at the other side, and then switch. Ask, "Is this part on the other side, too?" If both sides match along the dashed line, it is a line of symmetry.

blocks.title: Help the Orangutan Find the Banana Tree
blocks.instruction: Look at the whole maze first. Then draw the orangutan's way to the banana tree.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 9
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 9
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 9 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 40 to 60
blocks.instruction: This line does not start at zero. Count on from the nearest printed number and write the number each arrow points to.

script.say: "These number lines do not start at zero. They start at 40 and go to 60. Each arrow points to a number. Find out which number it is and write it in the box."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Point out that it does not start at zero. Count the small marks from the nearest printed number to the arrow and write the number.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the nearest printed number and count the small marks one by one to the arrow, saying the numbers. An answer such as 3 means the child wrote the number of steps, not the number on the line; an answer that is too small means the child counted from the left end as if it were zero.

blocks.title: Main Idea and Key Details
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the main idea of the whole text and three key details that support it.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write the main idea of the whole text and three key details that support it."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Ask, "What is the whole text mostly about?" before the children write.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Closed and Open Syllables
blocks.instruction: An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name: ro | bot.

script.say: "A closed syllable ends with a consonant, and its vowel is short: rab in rabbit. An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name: ro in robot. Read each word, draw a line between its syllables, and write C or O for each one."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write robot and rabbit on the board, split them together (ro|bot, rab|bit), and mark each part C or O. Read the first word on the page together and do it.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the letters between the two vowels. Two consonants: split between them. One consonant: split after the first vowel and say it long; if that is not a word, split after the consonant and say it short. A part that ends with a vowel is open, a part that ends with a consonant is closed. For your own reference, on this page the splits are cac|tus, si|lo, e|mu, mo|ment, mo|tel, si|lent, ro|dent, pic|nic, ba|con, hu|mid, si|ren, dol|phin, to|ken, ten|nis, po|lo, and ra|ven; a part that ends with a vowel gets O, a part that ends with a consonant gets C. The sentences take program, frozen, broken, pupil, halo, and label.

blocks.title: Parts of a Friendly Letter
blocks.instruction: A friendly letter has a date, a greeting, a body, a closing, and a signature.

script.say: "A friendly letter has five parts: the date, the greeting, the body, the closing, and the signature. Write the name of each part on its line, using the word bank."
script.first: Read the five parts in the word bank aloud and find each one in the letter on the page together: the date at the top, "Dear…" is the greeting, the long middle is the body, "Your friend" is the closing, and the name at the end is the signature. Do the first one together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Where does a letter start? Who is it to? Who wrote it?" Point to each part as you ask.

blocks.title: The Missing Factor
blocks.instruction: Look at the array. Write the missing factor.

script.say: "Count the rows of each array and the things in one row. Write the missing factor."
script.first: Draw an array on the board, for example 2 rows of 7. Write ? × 7 = 14 and ask, "How many rows of 7 make 14?" Count the rows together. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child count the rows and the shapes in one row of the array. The missing factor is the number that is not printed: rows times shapes in a row makes the total.

blocks.title: Share the Set
blocks.instruction: Circle the fraction of the pictures. Write how many that is.

script.say: "Each row shows a group of pictures and a fraction. Circle that part of the group, and write how many that is."
script.first: Draw 8 circles on the board. Say, "One half means two equal groups. Half of 8 is 4." Circle 4. For one fourth, make four equal groups and circle one group. Do the first row together.
script.stuck: Have the child share the pictures into as many equal groups as the bottom number says, one picture at a time. Then circle as many groups as the top number says.

blocks.title: Why Do We Have Day and Night?
blocks.instruction: Look where the Sun is. At each numbered pin, is it day or night? Circle the word in the table.

script.say: "Look where the Sun is. The side of Earth that faces the Sun has day; the other side has night. At each numbered pin, is it day or night? Circle the word in the table."
script.first: Point from the Sun on the page to Earth and show the side that faces it. Do the first pin together: "Does it face the Sun?" Circle day or night.
script.stuck: Have the child trace a line from the Sun to the pin: if Earth is in the way, it is night there.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

blocks.title: Read the Calendar: A Busy Month
blocks.instruction: Find the date one week later, and count the days from one sticker to another.

script.say: "This is a calendar page for one month. Some days have a little picture on them, like a sticker. The questions ask you to find dates, to go one week ahead, and to count the days from one sticker to another."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the month and the days of the week across the top. Read the first question aloud and find the answer together. For "one week later," move straight down one row: seven days.
script.stuck: For a day of the week, have the child find the date and move a finger straight up its column. To count the days from one sticker to another, the child starts on the day after the first sticker and counts every day up to and including the second sticker.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 10
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 10
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 10 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Walls with Two-Digit Answers
blocks.instruction: The numbers go past 20. Add each pair of bricks and write the sum in the brick above.

script.say: "This is a number wall. Each brick is the sum of the two bricks right under it. Start at the bottom and build every wall to the top. The numbers get bigger than twenty, so you may add on paper."
script.first: Draw the first wall on the board. Point to two bricks next to each other at the bottom and add them aloud, tens and ones; write the sum in the brick above them. Tell the children to work up the wall one row at a time.
script.stuck: Put two fingers on the two bricks under the empty brick and have the child add those two numbers on scrap paper, tens and ones. A wrong brick lower down makes every brick above it wrong, so check the rows from the bottom up.

blocks.title: Events in Order
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Then write the four events or steps in order.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write the four events or steps in order."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Look for time words like first, then, and later together.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Base Words and Suffixes
blocks.instruction: A suffix at the end changes the word: kind + ness = kindness.

script.say: "A suffix at the end changes a word: kind and -ness make kindness. Read each word, circle the base word, and underline the suffix. Then do the rest of the page."
script.first: Write kindness on the board: circle kind, underline -ness. Ask what it means: being kind. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then read the whole word and ask what it means.

blocks.title: The Irregular Verbs: be, have, do, go
blocks.instruction: These verbs change a lot. Write the today form and the yesterday form of each one in the dashed boxes.

script.say: "Be, have, do, and go change a lot. Write the today form and the yesterday form of each one in the dashed boxes. Then finish the sentences."
script.first: Say the verbs with the class: go, goes, went; have, has, had; be, is, was; do, does, did. Do the first row together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence aloud with the verb and listen. If the sentence has "yesterday," the verb tells about the past (jumped). With one person and "today" or "every day," the verb gets an s (runs, sings).

blocks.title: Divide It Up
blocks.instruction: Share the pile equally into the bins. Write how many each gets.

script.say: "Share the pile equally into the bins. Write how many each bin gets. That is division: 12 ÷ 3 means 12 shared into 3 equal groups."
script.first: Draw 12 dots and 3 circles on the board. Share the dots one at a time into the circles and count each circle: 4. Write 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Do the first problem on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child share the pictures one by one, crossing each off, until none is left. Then count one bin.

blocks.title: Dot-to-Dot: Count by Fives
blocks.instruction: Start at the orange dot. Count by fives from 5 to 50 and connect the dots. Part of the picture is already drawn.

script.say: "This is a dot-to-dot, and you count by fives. Start at the orange dot at 5. Draw a line to 10, then to 15, and keep going to 50."
script.first: Count by fives from 5 to 50 together. Find the orange dot at 5 together and draw the line to 10. Part of the picture is already drawn; the dots finish it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the number they are on and add five; that is the dot to look for. The numbers in the row at the bottom can be crossed off one by one.

blocks.title: Where People Live and Why
blocks.instruction: Find each letter on both maps. Circle many people or few people. Use the land map to write a reason.

script.say: "Find each letter on both maps. Circle many people or few people, then use the land map to write a reason."
script.first: Read the keys under the maps aloud: one dot is 100,000 people; then mountains (the little peaks), desert (the dashes), plains (flat land), and other land. Do the first letter together: find it on the map of where people live and ask, "Are the dots crowded here or far apart?" Circle many or few. Then find it on the land map: "Is there water nearby? What is the land like?" Write the reason together; if your page has reason words, use them. Every letter by the ocean or a Great Lake has many people; every letter in the mountains or the desert has few.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the letter on the dot map: many dots close by means many people. On the land map: by an ocean or a lake there is water and a port; a desert is dry; mountains are cold and steep. If your page asks where many people live in our state, any true place and reason is right.

blocks.title: Find 10 Differences: In the Park
blocks.instruction: Circle the 10 differences, 5 in each pair of pictures, and check a box under the pair for every one you find.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle with two pairs of pictures. In each pair, the picture on the right is different in 5 places. Circle each difference, and check a box under the pair for every one you find."
script.first: Find one difference in the top pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Circle it in the picture on the right and check off one box.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom. Things can be missing, added, or changed.

blocks.title: What Time Is It?
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour, and the long hand shows the minutes: count by fives. Circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Count by fives around the numbers with the class: 5, 10, 15… Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, count the minutes by fives, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then have the child count by fives from the 12 to the long hand: 5, 10, 15.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 11
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 11
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 11 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count by Fours
blocks.instruction: Skip count by 4. Write each missing number.

script.say: "On this page we count by fours: 4, 8, 12, 16. Some numbers are missing. Count by fours and write each missing number. The rows do not start at 4."
script.first: Count by fours together to 60. Read the first row aloud and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. Tell the children that a row does not always start at 4.
script.stuck: Have the child add four to the number before the gap with fingers: say the number, then count four more. To check, the next printed number must be four more than the number the child wrote.

blocks.title: Ask and Answer
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Each sentence in a box is from the text. Write the question that the sentence answers. The first word is given.

script.say: "Read the text. Each sentence in a box comes from the text. Write the question that the sentence answers. The first one is started for you."
script.first: Read the text aloud with the class. Read the first sentence in a box and ask, "What question does this answer?" Look at how the first one is started and finish it together. A question ends with a question mark.
script.stuck: Have the child find the sentence in the text and ask, "What would someone ask to get this answer: who, what, where, when, why, or how?"

blocks.title: Suffixes -ful, -less, and -ly
blocks.instruction: -ful means full of, and -less means without.

script.say: "A suffix is a word part at the end. -ful means full of, -less means without, and -ly tells how. Circle the base word in each word and underline the suffix. Then match each word to its meaning."
script.first: Write playful on the board: circle play, underline -ful. Ask, "What does playful mean? Full of play." Do the same with toothless. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then add the suffix and ask what the whole word means.

blocks.title: Plan Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Plan before you write: an opinion and reasons that tell why.

script.say: "Plan your opinion piece before you write: choose a question, write your opinion, and give reasons that tell why."
script.first: Read the questions aloud and let a few children say their opinion and one reason. Each child circles a question and fills in the plan.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Multiply and Divide Fact Families
blocks.instruction: Use the three numbers on the roof. Complete the four related facts.

script.say: "Use the three numbers on the roof of each house to finish two multiplications and two divisions."
script.first: Draw a house with 2, 9, and 18 on the roof. Write the four facts together: 2 × 9, 9 × 2, 18 ÷ 2, 18 ÷ 9. The biggest number is the product. Do the first house on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child find the biggest number on the roof: it is the product. The two smaller numbers are the factors: they multiply to the product, and the product divided by one factor gives the other.

blocks.title: Expanded Form Both Ways
blocks.instruction: Put the parts together, or break each number into hundreds, tens and ones. Write the numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Every digit in a number is worth something. In 479, the 4 is worth 400, the 7 is worth 70, and the 9 is worth 9. This page goes both ways. When the parts are printed, put them together and write the number in the box. When the number is printed, break it into its hundreds, its tens, and its ones."
script.first: Write 257 on the board and break it up together: 200 + 50 + 7. Then go the other way: 400 + 30 + 2 = 432. Point out that some problems put the parts together and others break the number up. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child read the number aloud slowly and write what each part says: "two hundred" is 200, "forty" is 40, "two" is 2. A child who writes 2 + 4 + 2 for 242 has copied the digits; point to the first 2 and ask, "Is this 2 ones or 2 hundreds?" The right three parts in another order are still correct.

blocks.title: Towns Grow Near Resources
blocks.instruction: Look at the sample state. Write what each site has. Then write which site is the worst place for a town, and why.

script.say: "This is a sample state, made up for the page. Look at its land and water, and decide where a town could start and grow."
script.first: Read the words on the map aloud together: forest, mine, dry, rocky land, farmland, river, harbor, sea. Find each lettered site and ask, "What is near it?" Say, "A town needs water first." If your page asks for the better place, it is the site that is not in the dry, rocky land; then circle what that site has. If your page asks what each site has, do the first site together; the worst place is the site in the dry, rocky land, because it has no water. If your page asks about our own town, any true resource is right, such as a river or farmland.
script.stuck: Point to one site at a time and ask, "Is there water here? Could people grow food? Is there a harbor?" The site by the river has river water and rich soil for farms; the site by the harbor has a harbor.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates on a 6 × 6 Grid
blocks.instruction: Find each square by its letter and number. Color it to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the lists name. Show how to find a square: put one finger on the letter at the top and one finger on the number at the side, and move them until they meet. Find the first square of the first list together and color it. Tell the children to cross out each code once its square is colored.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

blocks.title: Rounding to the Nearest 10 and 100
blocks.instruction: Round each number twice: to the nearest ten in the first box and to the nearest hundred in the second.

script.say: "Round each number two times: first to the nearest ten, then to the nearest hundred. Look at the digit to the right of the place you round to: 0 to 4, round down; 5 to 9, round up."
script.first: Read the example at the top together; the wavy equal sign means "is about." Do the first number on the board: underline its tens digit and look at the ones digit to round to the nearest ten; then underline its hundreds digit and look at the tens digit to round to the nearest hundred. Tell the children to start from the number on the page both times.
script.stuck: Have the child say the two tens the number is between and ask which one is closer; then the two hundreds. A 5 always rounds up.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 12
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 12
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 12 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Big Skip Counting
blocks.instruction: Find the counting rule. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Find the counting rule of each row: what is added each time? Write each missing number."
script.first: Read the first row aloud and look at two numbers next to each other: how much is added? Count on by that amount to fill the empty boxes together.
script.stuck: Have the child find two numbers next to each other with no gap and count up from one to the other: that is the step. Where one box is empty between two numbers, the jump is two steps.

blocks.title: Cause and Effect
blocks.instruction: Read the text. A cause makes something happen. An effect is what happens. Write the missing cause or effect.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write the missing cause or effect. A cause makes something happen; an effect is what happens."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Write "Because it rained, the game was canceled" on the board: the rain is the cause, the canceled game the effect.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Describing Words in Real Life
blocks.instruction: Describing words tell what real things are like: a warm hat, a cold drink.

script.say: "Describing words tell what real things are like: hot soup, a soft blanket. Read each sentence and do what the page asks."
script.first: Read the first part of the page aloud with the class and do its first item together. Ask, "What is this thing really like? Which word fits?"
script.stuck: Ask the child to think of a real one: "Have you touched one? Is it hard or soft, hot or cold?"

blocks.title: Choose the Linking Word
blocks.instruction: Because and since tell why. Therefore tells what happens as a result.

script.say: "Linking words join an opinion to its reasons. Because and since tell why. Therefore tells what happens as a result. For example gives an example. Circle the linking word that fits each sentence."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Read the first sentence aloud with each linking word and circle the one that fits together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Does the second part give a reason, a result, or an example?" Then find the word for it in the box.

blocks.title: Divide It Up
blocks.instruction: Share the pile equally into the bins. Write how many each gets.

script.say: "Share the pile equally into the bins. Write how many each bin gets. That is division: 12 ÷ 3 means 12 shared into 3 equal groups."
script.first: Draw 12 dots and 3 circles on the board. Share the dots one at a time into the circles and count each circle: 4. Write 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Do the first problem on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child share the pictures one by one, crossing each off, until none is left. Then count one bin.

blocks.title: Multiplication and Division Word Problems
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Use the picture to help you. Write the answer in the box, then finish the answer sentence.

script.say: "Read each story. Are equal groups put together? Then you multiply. Is a total shared or split into equal groups? Then you divide. Write the number sentence and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "Is it equal groups put together (multiply), or a total shared into equal groups (divide)?" Use the picture and write the answer and the answer sentence together.
script.stuck: Ask the child to underline the two numbers in the story and to say what each number counts: the groups, or how many are in each group. The picture shows the groups, and counting them is fine as a check.

blocks.title: Sort the Animals
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to the group it belongs to.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Mammals, Birds, and Reptiles. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Does it have fur, feathers, or scales? Does it lay eggs or feed its babies milk?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. Mammals have fur or hair, birds have feathers, and reptiles have dry scales.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Mystery Number: Two Arrows, One Square
blocks.instruction: Follow both arrows. They point to the same square of the chart. Write the mystery number.

script.say: "Each puzzle has two numbers, and each number has an arrow. The key at the top tells what the arrows do: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, and right is 1 more. Both arrows lead to the same number. Find that mystery number and write it in the box."
script.first: Point to the key at the top: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, right is 1 more. Do the first puzzle on the board: follow the first number's arrow, then the second number's arrow, and check that both land on the same number.
script.stuck: Have the child say what the arrow does before using it, and follow only one arrow at first. Then the child follows the second arrow; if the two answers are not the same, one of them needs another look.

blocks.title: Line of Symmetry?
blocks.instruction: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry? Circle the check mark or the X.

script.say: "A mirror line cuts a picture into two halves that match exactly, like a picture and its reflection in a mirror. Look at the dashed line on each picture. If both sides match, circle the check. If they do not match, circle the X."
script.first: Draw a heart with a dashed line down the middle: "If I fold here, both sides match: a line of symmetry." Look at the first picture and its dashed line together: would the two sides match? Circle the check mark or the X.
script.stuck: Have the child cover one side of the picture with a hand, look at the other side, and then switch. Ask, "Is this part on the other side, too?" If both sides match along the dashed line, it is a line of symmetry.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 13
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 13
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 13 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Odd or Even? Write Two Equal Addends
blocks.instruction: Circle the dots two by two. Then write the number as two equal parts and write what is left over in the small box.

script.say: "Circle the dots two by two. Then write the number as two equal parts, and write what is left over in the small box."
script.first: Draw 7 dots on the board and circle them in pairs: three pairs and one left over. Write 7 = 3 + 3 + 1 left over. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child circle the dots two by two and count the pairs: that is each equal part. A dot left over goes in the small box, and the number is odd; no dot left over means it is even.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: Scout Learns to Sit
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence. When you finish, turn the page over and write three sentences that tell what happens next in the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow; then they read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Which sentence helps us?" Circle the answer together. Question 3 asks the children to write their own answer on the lines: tell them to use a full sentence.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question.

blocks.title: Label the Parts of Speech
blocks.instruction: Every word has a job. Label each word by the job it does in its sentence.

script.say: "Every word has a job. A noun names something, a pronoun takes its place, a verb shows an action or being, an adjective tells about a noun, and an adverb tells how. Label each word by its job."
script.first: Read the box with the letters for each job aloud. Read the first sentence on the page aloud and label its first word together: "What job does this word do here?"
script.stuck: Ask the questions one by one: "Is it a thing? Does it replace a name? Is it something you do? Does it describe a thing? Does it tell how?" For your own reference, on this page: 1 playful Adj, kittens N, chased V, it P; 2 cookies N, were V, crunchy Adj; 3 Omar N, built V, huge Adj, castle N; 4 noisy Adj, parrot N, repeated V, funny Adj, words N; 5 She P, waved V, sadly Adv; 6 We P, happily Adv, shared V, warm Adj, bread N; 7 ocean N, was V, calm Adj; 8 Rosa N, carefully Adv, painted V, tiny Adj, shell N.

blocks.title: Plan Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Plan before you write: an opinion and reasons that tell why.

script.say: "Plan your opinion piece before you write: choose a question, write your opinion, and give reasons that tell why."
script.first: Read the questions aloud and let a few children say their opinion and one reason. Each child circles a question and fills in the plan.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Rows and Columns
blocks.instruction: Count the rows and columns. Finish the multiplication sentence.

script.say: "Count the rows and the columns of each array. Finish the multiplication sentence: rows times columns."
script.first: Draw an array of 3 rows of 4 dots on the board. Count the rows and the columns together, then add the rows: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Show that 3 × 4 means 3 rows of 4. Do the first picture on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child run a finger along each row of an array and count the rows first, then count the things in the top row. On this page the first number is the number of rows and the second number is how many are in each row.

blocks.title: Thirds and Quarters
blocks.instruction: Color the fraction of each shape.

script.say: "Each shape is cut into equal parts. Read the fraction and color that many parts."
script.first: Draw a rectangle cut into four equal parts on the board and color three: "three fourths: three of four equal parts." Do the first shape on the page together: read the fraction, count the parts, and color.
script.stuck: Have the child count the equal parts of the shape and color as many as the top number of the fraction says: any parts, all the way to their edges. A child who colors the whole shape counts the parts again with you.

blocks.title: Where Do Animals Live?
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each animal to where it lives.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Land, Water, and Air. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Where does this animal spend most of its time: on land, in the water, or in the air?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. An animal that flies lives on land too, so Air and Land are both right for it, and a crab lives in the water and on land, so Water and Land are both right for it, when the child can say why.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Bring the Polar Bear Home Safely
blocks.instruction: Help the polar bear get to the igloo. Do not take a road with a walrus or a hole in the ice.

script.say: "Help the animal get home safely. Look at the whole maze first. Do not take a road with one of the dangers the page names."
script.first: Read the title aloud and show the start and the goal. Point to the dangers on the page and say that a road with a danger is closed. Trace a way with your finger and stop at each fork: "Is there a danger on this road?" Tell the children to find the whole way with a finger before they draw.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: The Other Half
blocks.instruction: Trace the dashed half so both sides of each picture look the same.

script.say: "Each picture is the same on both sides of the line, but one side is dashed. Trace the dashed half so both sides look the same."
script.first: Fold a sheet of paper in half and show that both halves match. Point to the dashed half of the first picture and trace a few dashes together, slowly.
script.stuck: Have the child trace one part of the dashed half at a time and compare it with the same part on the solid side: the two must look like a picture and its reflection.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 14
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 14
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 14 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: The 5 Times Table
blocks.instruction: Multiply. Write each product in the box.

script.say: "Multiply. Write each product in the box. All the problems on this page use the same times table."
script.first: Count by the table's number together to ten times it. Do the first two problems together and show that each answer is the one before plus one more group.
script.stuck: Have the child count by the table's number on fingers, one finger for each group, or start from a fact the child knows: 5 times the number, then count on by one more group.

blocks.title: How a Character Meets a Challenge
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then write the answer to each question.

script.say: "Read the text at the top of the page carefully. Then write the answer to each question."
script.first: Read the title and the first part of the text aloud while the children follow. Then the children read it again on their own. Read the first question aloud together and ask, "Where in the text can we find this?" Find the sentence together and write the first answer together. Ask the class, "What is the character's problem? What does the character do about it?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text together. Point to the part that has the answer and have the child read it aloud before writing.

blocks.title: Plural Nouns: Spelling Rules
blocks.instruction: Plural nouns name more than one. Each one follows a spelling rule.

script.say: "A plural noun names more than one. Its spelling follows a rule: add -s; add -es after s, x, z, ch, or sh; change y to i and add -es; some words change completely. Read the rules at the top and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the rule box aloud and write one example of each rule on the board: cats, boxes, babies, leaves. Do the first item on the page together and say which rule it follows.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the last letter or letters of the word and find the matching rule in the box.

blocks.title: Draft Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Write your opinion and reasons. Join them with linking words.

script.say: "Write your opinion piece. Choose one question, state your opinion, give reasons, and join them with linking words. End with a closing sentence."
script.first: Read the questions aloud and let a few children say an opinion and a reason. Write a frame on the board: In my opinion … because … Also, … For example, … That is why … Each child circles one question and writes.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Shopping Math: Is There Enough Money?
blocks.instruction: Compare the money with the price. Circle yes or no, then write the total.

script.say: "Compare the money with the price. Circle yes if there is enough money, or no if there is not. Then write the total."
script.first: Read the prices aloud. Read the first question aloud, add the two prices on the board, and compare with the money the child has.
script.stuck: Have the child circle the two things on the shelf that the question shows, then write the two prices one under the other and add the ones first. Coins or drawn dimes and pennies help a child who cannot add the numbers yet.

blocks.title: Find the Start: Story Problems Within 100
blocks.instruction: Read each story. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the number you need. Write an equation. Then write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. In the bar model, write the two numbers you know and a question mark for the number you need. Then solve."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "Do we know the start? The change? The end?" Write the two numbers you know in the bar and a question mark where the missing number goes. Solve it together.
script.stuck: Read the story with the child and underline the numbers. Ask, "Are things put together, or taken away?" Draw a quick bar to show the parts and the whole.

blocks.title: Three Levels of Government
blocks.instruction: Read each card. Write each leader and each service in the right column: local, state or national.

script.say: "Read each card and write it in the right column: local, state, or national."
script.first: Read the three column names aloud and say, "Local means our town or city. State means our state. National means our whole country." Read the cards aloud and do the first one together. Answers: local: the mayor, the city council, a city park, the fire department, trash pickup; state: the governor, the state legislature, a state highway, a driver's license; national: the president, Congress, the mail, a national park, coins and paper money. If your page asks which level to ask about something broken in a city park, the answer is local, because the city takes care of its parks.
script.stuck: Have the child look for a clue word on the card, such as city, state, or national. With no clue word, ask, "Does it lead or serve one town, one state, or the whole country?"

blocks.title: Copy the Picture on an 8 × 8 Grid
blocks.instruction: A bigger grid: find each square by its letter and number, then copy.

script.say: "A bigger grid: find each square by its letter and number, and copy the picture onto the empty grid."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Find one colored square together, say its letter and number, and color the same square on the empty grid. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 15
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 15
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 15 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: 100 More, 100 Less
blocks.instruction: Write the number that is 100 less and the number that is 100 more.

script.say: "Look at the number in the middle. On the left, write the number that is 100 less. On the right, write the number that is 100 more."
script.first: Do the first one on the board: read the number in the middle and ask, "A hundred more: which digit changes? Which two stay the same?" Show that only the hundreds digit changes. Count by hundreds from another number together.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens and the ones with a finger and look only at the hundreds digit: one less for 100 less, one more for 100 more. The two covered digits are copied as they are.

blocks.title: Ask and Answer About a Story
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Each sentence in a box is from the story. Write the question that the sentence answers. The first word is given.

script.say: "Read the story. Each sentence in a box comes from the story. Write the question that the sentence answers. The first one is started for you."
script.first: Read the story aloud with the class. Read the first sentence in a box and ask, "What question does this answer?" Look at how the first one is started and finish it together.
script.stuck: Have the child find the sentence in the story and ask, "What would someone ask to get this answer: who, what, where, when, why, or how?"

blocks.title: Past Tense: Regular and Irregular Verbs
blocks.instruction: Regular verbs add -ed in the past. Irregular verbs change: go, went.

script.say: "Regular verbs add -ed in the past: walk, walked. Irregular verbs change: go, went. Read the rules at the top and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the rule box aloud with an example of each rule. Do the first item on the page together and say which rule it follows.
script.stuck: Ask the child to say the verb in a sentence with "yesterday": "Yesterday I…" The word they say is often the past tense; then check its spelling with the rules.

blocks.title: Plan Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Plan before you write: an opinion and reasons that tell why.

script.say: "Plan your opinion piece before you write: choose a question, write your opinion, and give reasons that tell why."
script.first: Read the questions aloud and let a few children say their opinion and one reason. Each child circles a question and fills in the plan.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: To the Minute
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock to the minute. The short hand shows the hour. Count the minutes by fives, then by ones. Circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board with the long hand two marks after the 4. Count by fives to the 4 (20) and then by ones (21, 22): 22 minutes. Do the first clock on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child count by fives to the number before the long hand, then count each small mark by ones.

blocks.title: Division Word Problems: Making Groups
blocks.instruction: Circle the equal groups in the picture, then write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Are equal groups put together? Then you multiply. Is a total shared or split into equal groups? Then you divide. Write the number sentence and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Circle equal groups in the picture together and count the groups: that is the answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child to underline the two numbers in the story and to say what each number counts: the groups, or how many are in each group. The picture shows the groups, and counting them is fine as a check.

blocks.title: Three Branches
blocks.instruction: Read each card. Write it under its branch, for our national government and for our state government. Write the three job cards in the national chart.

script.say: "Our government has three branches: legislative makes the laws, executive carries them out, judicial decides what laws mean. Write each card under its branch."
script.first: Read the sentence that says what check means, then the cards. Do the first card together. Answers: legislative: Congress, makes the laws, the state legislature; executive: the president, carries out laws, the governor; judicial: the Supreme Court, decides what laws mean, the state courts. If your page has a chart for our state, the three job cards go in the national chart. If your page asks for another way one branch can check another (the veto is printed), help with one: "Congress can pass a bill again over a veto," or "The courts can decide a law goes against the Constitution."
script.stuck: Read the card with the child and ask, "Does it make laws, carry them out, or decide what they mean?" Then find that branch's box.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates: Write the Codes
blocks.instruction: The picture is colored in. Write the code of each square in the list for its color.

script.say: "This grid already has a picture colored in. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. Write the name of each colored square in the list for its color."
script.first: Show how to name a square: go straight up from the square to its letter and straight to the side to its number, and write the letter first. Do the first colored square together and write its code in the first box of the list. Tell the children to put a small dot on each square once its code is written.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on the square and move it straight up to read the letter, then straight to the left to read the number. The order of the codes in the list does not matter, as long as every colored square is there once.

blocks.title: Read the Calendar
blocks.instruction: Look at the calendar. Use it to answer every question.

script.say: "This is a calendar page for one month. The questions under it ask you to find things on the calendar. Read each question and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the month and the days of the week across the top. Read the first question aloud and find the answer on the calendar together: put one finger on the date and slide up the column to its day.
script.stuck: For a question about a day of the week, have the child find the date and move a finger straight up its column to the day's name. For a question about a picture, the child looks for the little picture inside the calendar.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 16
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 16
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 16 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Label the Number Line
blocks.instruction: Use the numbers you see to find what the line counts by. Write the missing numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Use the numbers you see to find what the line counts by. Then write the missing numbers in the boxes."
script.first: Draw the first line on the board. Ask, "How far is it from one printed number to the next? How many marks are in between?" Find the step together, then count on to each box.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the nearest printed number and count the small marks one by one to the arrow. An answer such as 3 or 7 means the child counted from the left end as if it were zero; point to the 40.

blocks.title: Retell the Story
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Then retell it: write the four main events in order.

script.say: "Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. Then retell it: write the four main events in order."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Ask the class, "What happens first? What is the most important thing that happens next?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the story. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Sort the Parts of Speech
blocks.instruction: A word’s job makes it a noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, or adverb.

script.say: "Every word has a job. A noun names something, a pronoun takes its place, a verb shows an action or being, an adjective tells about a noun, and an adverb tells how, when, or how often. Write each word in the column of its job and cross it out. Then write two more words of your own for each job."
script.first: Read the box with the letters for each job aloud. Read the first sentence on the page aloud and label its first word together: "What job does this word do here?"
script.stuck: Ask the questions one by one: "Is it a thing? Does it replace a name? Is it something you do? Does it describe a thing? Does it tell how?" For your own reference, on this page the nouns are planet and aunt; the pronouns you, I, he, and they; the verbs hid and drank; the adjectives hungry, huge, and shiny; the adverbs neatly, now, sadly, and soon.

blocks.title: Choose the Linking Word
blocks.instruction: Because and since tell why. Therefore tells what happens as a result.

script.say: "Linking words join an opinion to its reasons. Because and since tell why. Therefore tells what happens as a result. For example gives an example. Circle the linking word that fits each sentence."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Read the first sentence aloud with each linking word and circle the one that fits together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Does the second part give a reason, a result, or an example?" Then find the word for it in the box.

blocks.title: Regrouping Review
blocks.instruction: Solve each problem. Regroup when you need to carry or borrow.

script.say: "Look at the sign of each problem first: some add and some take away. Work one place at a time, starting with the ones: carry when a sum is ten or more, borrow when the top digit is too small."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board, one number under the other. Point to the sign first: the page mixes adding and taking away. Work the ones column first and carry or borrow when you need to.
script.stuck: Have the child cover all but one column and work it aloud. If a sum is ten or more, carry the ten; if the top digit is too small, borrow a ten. Check the sign of each problem first.

blocks.title: More Than Nine of a Kind
blocks.instruction: Count the blocks. Ten ones make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Write the number.

script.say: "Count the blocks in each picture. Ten small cubes make a ten, and ten tens make a hundred. Write the number they show."
script.first: Draw a flat (a hundred), two rods, and four small cubes on the board. Count together: "one hundred, one hundred ten, one hundred twenty, and four more: one hundred twenty-four." Tell the children that when there are ten or more cubes of one kind, they bundle ten into the next place. Do the first picture together.
script.stuck: Have the child count each kind first: hundreds, tens, ones. If there are more than nine ones, circle ten of them: that is one more ten.

blocks.title: Where Taxes Go
blocks.instruction: Follow the arrows. Draw or write a service in each box and the level of government that pays for it. Then finish the sentence.

script.say: "People and businesses pay taxes. Each level of government collects its own and uses it for services."
script.first: Read the labels on the three buildings: "local: our town," "state: our state," "national: our country." If your page shows three services with pictures, read each one and ask, "Who pays for this?" Answers, for the services your page shows: a fire truck, new books for the library, trash pickup: local; highway patrol cars: state; soldiers who keep us safe, astronauts exploring space: national. If your page has empty service boxes, children draw or write any three real services and their levels, such as a fire station, local; a state park, state; the army, national. Police and schools are mostly local.
script.stuck: Read the building labels with the child again and ask, "Who takes care of this?" For the last sentence, help with a true one: "Without taxes, the town would not have money for its library." If your page asks what our town should spend more on, every honest answer is right.

blocks.title: Write What Is Different
blocks.instruction: Circle the 3 differences (something may be gone), then write one sentence about each one on the lines, using the words in the two strips.

script.say: "Here are two pictures that look almost the same. Picture 2 is different in 3 places. Circle each difference in picture 2. Then write one sentence about each difference on the lines. The words in the two strips under the pictures help you."
script.first: Show the two pictures and find one difference together. Circle it in picture 2. Read the two strips of words aloud and build the first sentence together about the thing you circled, for example "In picture 2, the … is bigger." The children find the other two and write a sentence for each.
script.stuck: Have the child compare one small part of the two pictures at a time, from top to bottom. For the sentence, ask, "Which thing is it? What happened to it?" The child picks one word from each strip and says the sentence aloud before writing it.

blocks.title: Hot or Cold?
blocks.instruction: Read each thermometer. Write the temperature it shows.

script.say: "A thermometer shows how hot or cold it is. Find where the red line stops on the scale and write that temperature in degrees Fahrenheit."
script.first: Look at the scale of the first thermometer together: the numbers go up by tens, and each small mark between two numbers is 2 more degrees. Put a finger on the top of the red line, find the number just below it, and count up by twos to the top of the line. Write the number in the box.
script.stuck: Have the child find the number just below the top of the red line and count the small marks up by twos: "80, 82, 84, 86, 88." The top of the red line is the temperature, never the number above it.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 17
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 17
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 17 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Machines
blocks.instruction: Each machine uses its rule on every number. Fill in the missing ones.

script.say: "Each number machine has a rule, printed at the top. A number goes in on the left, the machine uses its rule, and a new number comes out on the right. Fill in the missing numbers. Watch out: sometimes the number that went in is the one that is missing."
script.first: Read the rule of the first machine aloud, for example "+9." Do the first number together: put it in, use the rule, and write what comes out. If the number that comes out is given, go backward: use the opposite rule.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is the missing number before the arrow or after it?" After the arrow, the child uses the rule. Before the arrow, the child does the opposite, then checks by putting the number through the machine.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: The Class Trip
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence. When you finish, turn the page over and write three sentences that tell what happens next in the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow; then they read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Which sentence helps us?" Circle the answer together. Question 3 asks the children to write their own answer on the lines: tell them to use a full sentence.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question.

blocks.title: Rewrite the Story in the Past Tense
blocks.instruction: To tell a story about the past, change every verb to the past tense.

script.say: "This little story is told in the present. Rewrite it in the past tense: change every numbered verb to its yesterday form."
script.first: Read the story aloud. Do the first numbered verb together: "make… yesterday we made." Write it on the line. Remind the children that some verbs just add -ed and some change.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence with "yesterday" at the start and say the verb that sounds right.

blocks.title: Plan Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Plan before you write: an opinion and reasons that tell why.

script.say: "Plan your opinion piece before you write: choose a question, write your opinion, and give reasons that tell why."
script.first: Read the questions aloud and let a few children say their opinion and one reason. Each child circles a question and fills in the plan.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: To the Minute
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock to the minute. The short hand shows the hour. Count the minutes by fives, then by ones. Circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board with the long hand two marks after the 4. Count by fives to the 4 (20) and then by ones (21, 22): 22 minutes. Do the first clock on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child count by fives to the number before the long hand, then count each small mark by ones.

blocks.title: Round to the Hundred
blocks.instruction: Look at the dot. Circle the hundred it is closer to.

script.say: "Rounding means finding the nearest round number. Each number line on this page goes from one hundred to the next. Look at the dot. Is it closer to the hundred on the left or to the hundred on the right? Circle the hundred it is closer to."
script.first: Draw a number line from 400 to 500 with the dot near 470. Ask, "Is the dot closer to 400 or to 500?" Do the first one on the page together and circle the closer hundred.
