script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dot and count the small steps to each end of the line; the end with fewer steps is closer. Each small step is 10.

blocks.title: Parts of a Plant We Eat
blocks.instruction: Look at each food. Circle the part of the plant that we eat.

script.say: "We eat different parts of plants: roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds. Look at each food and circle the part of the plant we eat."
script.first: Draw a plant on the board and label its parts. Name the first food on the page together and ask, "Does it grow under the ground, is it the stem, a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or a seed?" Circle the word.
script.stuck: Ask the child where the food grows: under the ground (roots), the long part that holds the plant up (stem), the flat green part (leaf), the part bees visit (flower), the part with seeds inside (fruit), or the seed itself. Let the child choose and say why.

blocks.title: Find the Symmetric Picture
blocks.instruction: Circle the picture that is the same on both sides.

script.say: "Circle the picture in each row that is the same on both sides."
script.first: Draw a heart with a line down the middle: "Both sides match." Look at the first row together and ask which picture would match if you folded it in the middle.
script.stuck: Have the child cover one side of each picture with a hand, look at the other side, and then switch. The picture whose two sides match is the one to circle.

blocks.title: Help the Ant Reach Its Raspberry
blocks.instruction: Help the ant go down and up through the tunnels to the raspberry. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 18
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 18
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 18 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count by Threes
blocks.instruction: Skip count by 3. Write each missing number.

script.say: "On this page we count by threes: 3, 6, 9, 12. Some numbers are missing. Count by threes and write each missing number. The rows do not start at 3."
script.first: Count by threes together to 60. Read the first row aloud and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. Tell the children that a row does not always start at 3.
script.stuck: Have the child add three to the number before the gap with fingers: say the number, then count three more. To check, the next printed number must be three more than the number the child wrote.

blocks.title: The Main Idea of Each Paragraph
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write what each paragraph is mostly about.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write what each paragraph is mostly about."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Do the first paragraph together: read it and say in a few words what it is mostly about.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Closed or Open? Sort Long Words
blocks.instruction: A closed syllable has a short vowel; an open syllable has a long vowel.

script.say: "A closed syllable ends with a consonant, and its vowel is short: rab in rabbit. An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name: ro in robot. Read each word and write it under its heading, closed or open first syllable, with a line between its syllables. Then answer each sentence with yes or no."
script.first: Read the two headings aloud. Write tiger and napkin on the board and split them together: ti|ger has an open first syllable with a long i, nap|kin a closed one with a short a. Read the first word on the page together and write it under its heading.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the letters between the two vowels. Two consonants: split between them. One consonant: split after the first vowel and say it long; if that is not a word, split after the consonant and say it short. A part that ends with a vowel is open, a part that ends with a consonant is closed. For your own reference, on this page the words with a closed first syllable are ab|sent, in|vent, mag|ic, tun|nel, pet|al, and rob|in; the words with an open first syllable are lo|go, ro|dent, u|nit, and li|lac. The answers to the sentences are yes, no, no, yes, no, no.

blocks.title: Join Sentences with Joining Words
blocks.instruction: A joining word shows how two ideas go together.

script.say: "A joining word shows how two ideas go together. And adds another idea, because tells why, but shows a difference, and so tells the result. Join the sentences with a word from the box."
script.first: Read the box aloud. Read the first two sentences aloud and try each joining word between them. Ask which one makes sense and write the joined sentence together.
script.stuck: Read the two sentences with each joining word and ask, "Which one tells how they go together?"

blocks.title: Area of a Rectangle: Multiply the Side Lengths
blocks.instruction: Multiply the two side lengths. Write the equation and the area.

script.say: "To find the area of a rectangle, multiply its two side lengths. Write the equation and the area with its unit."
script.first: Draw a rectangle on the board with sides 4 and 3 and fill it with a grid: count the squares, 12. Show that 4 × 3 = 12 square units. Do the first rectangle on the page together and write the unit.
script.stuck: Have the child find the two side lengths and multiply them. A child who does not know the fact adds one side as many times as the other side says. The unit is "square" and the unit of the sides.

blocks.title: How Far Apart? Count the Jumps
blocks.instruction: Count how many jumps down and how many jumps right take you from the first number to the second. Write both numbers.

script.say: "Count how many jumps down and how many jumps right take you from the first number to the second. Write both numbers."
script.first: Point to the key: down is 10 more, right is 1 more. Do the first one on the board: from 4 to 35, count the tens: 14, 24, 34: three jumps down; then 35: one jump right.
script.stuck: Have the child count by tens first until the tens digit matches, then by ones.

blocks.title: Family Relationships: Riddles
blocks.instruction: Read each riddle and write the right family word from the box on the line; one word can fit more than one riddle.

script.say: "Now it is time to read and think. Each sentence is a riddle about one child's family. Read the riddle and work it out step by step. Then write the right family word from the box on the line. Some words fit more than one riddle."
script.first: Draw a family tree on the board with stick people: the child the riddles are about at the bottom; the mom and the dad above the child; a grandma and a grandpa above each parent; an aunt or an uncle beside each parent; and a cousin under the aunt. Read the first riddle aloud and follow it on the tree together, one step at a time, and write the word. Keep to the family on the page, not the children's own families.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the end of the riddle and say who its first part names ("the dad"), then add the last word ("his brother"). Following the riddle on the tree on the board helps. The children of an aunt or an uncle are cousins.

blocks.title: The Other Half
blocks.instruction: Trace the dashed half so both sides of each picture look the same.

script.say: "Each picture is the same on both sides of the line, but one side is dashed. Trace the dashed half so both sides look the same."
script.first: Fold a sheet of paper in half and show that both halves match. Point to the dashed half of the first picture and trace a few dashes together, slowly.
script.stuck: Have the child trace one part of the dashed half at a time and compare it with the same part on the solid side: the two must look like a picture and its reflection.

blocks.title: How Much Time Passed?
blocks.instruction: Compare the two clocks. Write how much time passed.

script.say: "Each row shows a start clock and an end clock. Read both and write how much time passed. The word next to the box tells you to answer in hours or in minutes."
script.first: Read the two clocks of the first row together and write both times on the board. Count on from the start time to the end time: by hours when the box says hours, by fives when it says minutes. Write the answer in the box.
script.stuck: Have the child write both times first. For hours, count the hours on from the first clock: "9 o'clock, 10, 11, 12: three hours." For minutes, count by fives from where the first minute hand points to where the second one points, going past the 12 if it has to.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 19
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 19
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 19 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Going Down!
blocks.instruction: The numbers go down by the same amount. Write the missing numbers.

script.say: "The numbers in each row go down by the same amount. Find how much, and write the missing numbers."
script.first: Read the first row aloud. Look at two numbers next to each other and ask, "How much less is the second?" Count back by that amount to fill the empty boxes together.
script.stuck: Have the child find two numbers next to each other with no gap and count down from one to the other: that is the step. Where one box is empty between two numbers, the jump is two steps.

blocks.title: Answer with Evidence
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write each answer. In the box, write the number of the paragraph that proves your answer.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write each answer. In the box, write the number of the paragraph that proves your answer."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Show the children the small numbers at the start of the paragraphs.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Possessive Nouns: One Owner or More
blocks.instruction: One owner: the bee’s hive. More than one owner: the bees’ hives.

script.say: "An apostrophe shows who owns something. One owner: add apostrophe s, the bee's hive. More than one owner that ends in s: add the apostrophe after the s, the bees' hives. Read the box and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write the bee's hive and the bees' hives on the board and ask how many bees there are in each. Do the first item together: "How many owners?"
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is there one owner or more than one?" Then point to the matching rule in the box.

blocks.title: Draft Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Write your opinion and reasons. Join them with linking words.

script.say: "Write your opinion piece. Choose one question, state your opinion, give reasons, and join them with linking words. End with a closing sentence."
script.first: Read the questions aloud and let a few children say an opinion and a reason. Write a frame on the board: In my opinion … because … Also, … For example, … That is why … Each child circles one question and writes.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Measuring Cups and Scales
blocks.instruction: Read each measuring cup and balance scale. Write the amount with its unit.

script.say: "Read each measuring cup and balance scale. Write the amount with its unit: grams for the scale, milliliters for the cup."
script.first: Point to the numbers on the first cup or scale and count the marks between them together. Read where the line or the pointer is and write the amount with its unit.
script.stuck: Have the child find the printed number just below the line and count the marks up to it.

blocks.title: Tally to Graph
blocks.instruction: Read the tally chart. Color one bar for each count.

script.say: "Read the tally chart. Color one box of the bar graph for each tally mark."
script.first: Count the tally marks of the first row together: a bundle with a line across is five. Color that many boxes in its bar, from the bottom up.
script.stuck: Have the child write the number next to each tally first: five for each bundle, then the single marks. For the bar, the child puts a finger on that number at the side of the graph and colors up to its line.

blocks.title: Sort by Food Group
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each food to its food group.

script.say: "At the top of the page there are pictures. At the bottom there are boxes: Fruits, Vegetables, Grains, and Protein. Draw a line from each picture to the box where it belongs."
script.first: Read the words on the boxes aloud and point to each box. Name every picture together, so that everyone knows what it shows. Do the first picture together: ask, "Is this a fruit, a vegetable, a grain like bread or pasta, or a protein like eggs, meat, or fish?" Draw the line from the dot under the picture to its box. If a food fits two groups, either box is right when the child can say why.
script.stuck: Point to one picture at a time and ask the question of the page about it. If the child is not sure, ask about something the child knows: "Have you ever seen one? What is it like?" Then let the child choose the box.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates on a 10 × 10 Grid
blocks.instruction: Find each square on the big grid by its letter and number. Color it to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the lists name. Show how to find a square: put one finger on the letter at the top and one finger on the number at the side, and move them until they meet. Find the first square of the first list together and color it. Tell the children to cross out each code once its square is colored.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

blocks.title: Quarter Hours
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Every clock on this page shows a quarter hour: something o'clock, quarter past, half past, or quarter to. Read each clock and circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Show quarter past (the long hand on 3), half past (on 6), and quarter to (on 9). Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, the minutes from the long hand, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then look at the long hand: on the 12 is o'clock, on the 3 quarter past, on the 6 half past, on the 9 quarter to.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 20
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 20
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 20 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: The 10 Times Table
blocks.instruction: Multiply. Write each product in the box.

script.say: "Multiply. Write each product in the box. All the problems on this page use the same times table."
script.first: Count by the table's number together to ten times it. Do the first two problems together and show that each answer is the one before plus one more group.
script.stuck: Have the child count by the table's number on fingers, one finger for each group, or start from a fact the child knows: 5 times the number, then count on by one more group.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: Breakfast for Mom
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence. When you finish, turn the page over and write three sentences that tell what happens next in the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow; then they read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Which sentence helps us?" Circle the answer together. Question 3 asks the children to write their own answer on the lines: tell them to use a full sentence.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question.

blocks.title: Which Word Fits? Suffixes in Sentences
blocks.instruction: -ness and -ment make nouns: soft, softness; move, movement.

script.say: "A suffix at the end changes a word: kind and -ness make kindness. Read each word, circle the base word, and underline the suffix. Then do the rest of the page."
script.first: Write kindness on the board: circle kind, underline -ness. Ask what it means: being kind. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then read the whole word and ask what it means.

blocks.title: Plan Your Story
blocks.instruction: Plan the beginning, the middle, and the end of your story.

script.say: "Plan your story: choose a story idea, then plan the beginning, the middle, and the end."
script.first: Read the story ideas aloud and let a few children say what could happen. Each child circles an idea and fills in the plan: who and where at the beginning, the problem in the middle, how it is solved at the end.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Perimeter: Find the Missing Side
blocks.instruction: The perimeter of each shape is given. Write an equation with n for the missing side. Then find n.

script.say: "The perimeter of each shape is given. Write an equation with n for the missing side. Then find n."
script.first: Draw a rectangle on the board with sides 5, 5, 10, and n and the perimeter 30. Add the sides you know (20) and ask, "What more makes 30?" n = 10. Do the first shape on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child add the sides that are given and take that sum away from the perimeter: what is left is n. Check by adding all the sides, n too: the sum must be the perimeter.

blocks.title: Read the Line Plot
blocks.instruction: Count the X marks above each number. Write how many.

script.say: "A line plot shows how many with X marks above each number. Count the X marks above each number and write how many."
script.first: Draw a short number line on the board with a few X marks above the numbers. Count the X marks above one number together and write the count. Do the first question on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the number and count the X marks straight above it, from the bottom up.

blocks.title: A Community Problem
blocks.instruction: Read about the problem. Write three solutions, with a cost and a benefit for each. Then write a letter to the city council.

script.say: "In this sample town, a busy street runs between the homes and the park, and there is no crosswalk. Choose a way to make crossing safe, then write a letter to the city council."
script.first: Read the problem aloud and look at the picture together. Talk about three ways to fix it: a sign that says SLOW costs the least; a guard who helps children cross is paid each day and helps before and after school; a crosswalk with a light costs the most to build but stops cars whenever people need to cross, all day and night. If your page lists the three solutions, circle one; if it has an empty table, write three solutions with a cost and a benefit for each. Start the letter together: "We noticed there is no crosswalk by the park." Any solution is right when its reason fits. If your page asks who would carry out the plan, it is city workers.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which way would you choose, and why?" Have the child say it aloud, then write it after "We suggest" and "because."

blocks.title: Find 7 Differences: On the Farm
blocks.instruction: Circle the 7 differences, 4 in the left pair of pictures and 3 in the right pair, and check a box for each.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle. There are two pairs of pictures. The pictures in each pair look the same, but they are not. Find 4 differences in the left pair and 3 in the right pair, and circle each one."
script.first: Find one difference in the left pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Show how to circle it and check off one box, so that everyone can see how many are still left to find.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom.

blocks.title: Read the Calendar: A Busy Month
blocks.instruction: Find the date one week later, and count the days from one sticker to another.

script.say: "This is a calendar page for one month. Some days have a little picture on them, like a sticker. The questions ask you to find dates, to go one week ahead, and to count the days from one sticker to another."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the month and the days of the week across the top. Read the first question aloud and find the answer together. For "one week later," move straight down one row: seven days.
script.stuck: For a day of the week, have the child find the date and move a finger straight up its column. To count the days from one sticker to another, the child starts on the day after the first sticker and counts every day up to and including the second sticker.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 21
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 21
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 21 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Odd Number Hunt
blocks.instruction: Circle every ODD number. Look at the last digit to decide.

script.say: "Even numbers can be split into two equal groups. Odd numbers always have one left over. You only need to look at the last digit. If a number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9, it is odd. Circle every odd number."
script.first: Write 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 on the board and leave it there. Do the first few numbers together: point to the last digit and ask, "Is it on our list?" Circle the number if it is: it is odd.
script.stuck: Have the child cover every digit but the last one with a finger and check it against the list on the board.

blocks.title: Events in Order
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Then write the four events or steps in order.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write the four events or steps in order."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Look for time words like first, then, and later together.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Add the Apostrophe: Fix the Possessives
blocks.instruction: Look at how many owners there are before you write the apostrophe.

script.say: "An apostrophe shows who owns something. One owner: add apostrophe s, the bee's hive. More than one owner that ends in s: add the apostrophe after the s, the bees' hives. Read the box and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write the bee's hive and the bees' hives on the board and ask how many bees there are in each. Do the first item together: "How many owners?"
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is there one owner or more than one?" Then point to the matching rule in the box.

blocks.title: Show Feelings in a Story
blocks.instruction: An action can show how a character feels.

script.say: "Quotation marks go around the exact words someone says. A comma or an end mark goes inside the closing quotation mark: “We won,” said Kim. Read the box and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write a line of dialogue on the board and point to each mark. Do the first item on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the words the person says: they go inside the quotation marks, and the comma or end mark goes in with them.

blocks.title: Area of an L-Shape
blocks.instruction: Cut each shape into two rectangles with one straight line. Find the area of each part. Then add the two areas.

script.say: "Draw one straight line to split each L-shape into two rectangles. Find the area of each part. Then add the two areas."
script.first: Draw an L-shape on the board and split it with one line into two rectangles. Find each area and add them. Do the first shape on the page together.
script.stuck: Help the child draw the line where the L bends, so that two rectangles show. Then find the two side lengths of each rectangle; a missing length is the long side take away the short side.

blocks.title: Share the Set
blocks.instruction: Circle the fraction of the pictures. Write how many that is.

script.say: "Each row shows a group of pictures and a fraction. Circle that part of the group, and write how many that is."
script.first: Draw 8 circles on the board. Say, "One half means two equal groups. Half of 8 is 4." Circle 4. For one fourth, make four equal groups and circle one group. Do the first row together.
script.stuck: Have the child share the pictures into as many equal groups as the bottom number says, one picture at a time. Then circle as many groups as the top number says.

blocks.title: Primary or Secondary?
blocks.instruction: Read each source. Write its name in the right column: primary or secondary.

script.say: "A primary source is made at the time by someone who was there. A secondary source is made later by someone who studied the past. Write each source in the right column."
script.first: Write those two sentences on the board: not every page prints them. Read the first source and its line aloud and ask, "When was it made? Was the maker there?" Write it in its column together. Answers, for the sources your page shows: primary: the diary, the photograph of the new school, the soldier's letter, the map drawn in 1870, the newspaper from the day the bridge opened. Secondary: the textbook page, the encyclopedia article, the museum sign. If your page asks which source best tells what school was like in 1900, it is the diary, because the girl was there in 1900.
script.stuck: Ask the two questions again. Old does not mean primary: the encyclopedia article was written in 1955, long after the town began, by someone who studied it.

blocks.title: Help the Rabbit Find the Cabbage
blocks.instruction: Look at the whole maze first. Then draw the orangutan's way to the banana tree.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: Find 10 Differences: In the Forest
blocks.instruction: Circle the 10 differences, 5 in each pair of pictures, and check a box under the pair for every one you find.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle with two pairs of pictures. In each pair, the picture on the right is different in 5 places. Circle each difference, and check a box under the pair for every one you find."
script.first: Find one difference in the top pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Circle it in the picture on the right and check off one box.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom. Things can be missing, added, or changed.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 22
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 22
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 22 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Rounding to the Nearest 100
blocks.instruction: Round each number to the nearest hundred and write it in the box. Look at the tens digit.

script.say: "Round each number to the nearest hundred and write it in the box. Look at the tens digit: 0 to 4 round down, 5 to 9 round up."
script.first: Read the box at the top: look at the tens digit; 0 to 4 round down, 5 to 9 round up. Do the first number together on the board: 462 has 6 tens, so it rounds up to 500.
script.stuck: Have the child point to the tens digit and check it against the box at the top. Rounding down keeps the hundreds digit; rounding up adds one to it; the tens and ones become zeros.

blocks.title: Read and Answer
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow; then they read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Which sentence helps us?" Circle the answer together. Question 3 asks the children to write their own answer on the lines: tell them to use a full sentence.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question.

blocks.title: Which Plural Is Right?
blocks.instruction: A plural noun names more than one. Its spelling follows a rule.

script.say: "A plural noun names more than one. Its spelling follows a rule: add -s; add -es after s, x, z, ch, or sh; change y to i and add -es; some words change completely. Read the rules at the top and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the rule box aloud and write one example of each rule on the board: cats, boxes, babies, leaves. Do the first item on the page together and say which rule it follows.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the last letter or letters of the word and find the matching rule in the box.

blocks.title: Time Words in a Story
blocks.instruction: Time words such as “later that day” tell when things happen.

script.say: "Time words like first, later that day, and finally tell when things happen in a story. Read the box at the top and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box of time words aloud. Do the first item on the page together and say where the time word goes.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Does this happen at the start, in the middle, or at the end?" Then pick a time word from that part of the box.

blocks.title: Perimeter: Find the Missing Side
blocks.instruction: The perimeter of each shape is given. Write an equation with n for the missing side. Then find n.

script.say: "The perimeter of each shape is given. Write an equation with n for the missing side. Then find n."
script.first: Draw a rectangle on the board with sides 5, 5, 10, and n and the perimeter 30. Add the sides you know (20) and ask, "What more makes 30?" n = 10. Do the first shape on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child add the sides that are given and take that sum away from the perimeter: what is left is n. Check by adding all the sides, n too: the sum must be the perimeter.

blocks.title: Division Word Problems: Two Ways
blocks.instruction: One story shares things equally, the other makes equal groups. Both are division. Solve each story and write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Are equal groups put together? Then you multiply. Is a total shared or split into equal groups? Then you divide. Write the number sentence and the answer."
script.first: Read both stories aloud. One shares things equally, the other makes equal groups; both are division. Solve the first one together with a quick drawing.
script.stuck: Ask the child to underline the two numbers in the story and to say what each number counts: the groups, or how many are in each group. The picture shows the groups, and counting them is fine as a check.

blocks.title: A Double Timeline
blocks.instruction: Write each event's letter above its year on its timeline. Then draw a line between each two events, one on each timeline, that happened within five years of each other.

script.say: "Write each event's letter above its year on its own timeline: the sample town or the United States. Then join the events, one on each timeline, that happened within five years of each other."
script.first: Read the events and their years aloud. Show the marks: each long mark with a number is ten years, and each short mark between is five. Do the first event together: find its year on its own timeline and write the letter above it. The two joining lines: the railroad (1869) with the town's first school (1870), and the vote (1920) with the town library (1920). If your page asks for two events from our town, any true event with its year is right, such as the year our school opened if the class knows it.
script.stuck: Have the child find the ten years first: 1869 is just before the 1870 mark, almost on it: one year short. Then check which timeline the event belongs on, the town or the United States, and write the letter there.

blocks.title: Copy the Picture Using Letters and Numbers
blocks.instruction: Use the letter and number of each square to copy the picture.

script.say: "Use the letter and number of each square to copy the picture onto the empty grid."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Find one colored square together, say its letter and number, and color the same square on the empty grid. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates
blocks.instruction: Find each square by its letter and number, like B2. Color it with the color of its group to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Read the first square, for example B2: go across to B and down to 2. Color it in its color together. Tell the children to cross off each square on the list as they color it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 23
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 23
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 23 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Where on the Number Line? 40 to 60
blocks.instruction: This line does not start at zero. Count on from the nearest printed number and write the number each arrow points to.

script.say: "These number lines do not start at zero. They start at 40 and go to 60. Each arrow points to a number. Find out which number it is and write it in the box."
script.first: Draw the first number line on the board. Point out that it does not start at zero. Count the small marks from the nearest printed number to the arrow and write the number.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the nearest printed number and count the small marks one by one to the arrow, saying the numbers. An answer such as 3 means the child wrote the number of steps, not the number on the line; an answer that is too small means the child counted from the left end as if it were zero.

blocks.title: Show Where the Story Says It
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write each answer. In the box, write the number of the paragraph that proves your answer.

script.say: "Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. Then write each answer. In the box, write the number of the paragraph that proves your answer."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Show the children the small numbers at the start of the paragraphs.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the story. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Label the Parts of Speech
blocks.instruction: Every word has a job. Label each word by the job it does in its sentence.

script.say: "Every word has a job. A noun names something, a pronoun takes its place, a verb shows an action or being, an adjective tells about a noun, and an adverb tells how. Label each word by its job."
script.first: Read the box with the letters for each job aloud. Read the first sentence on the page aloud and label its first word together: "What job does this word do here?"
script.stuck: Ask the questions one by one: "Is it a thing? Does it replace a name? Is it something you do? Does it describe a thing? Does it tell how?" For your own reference, on this page: 1 I P, always Adv, wash V, dishes N; 2 He P, gladly Adv, shared V, juicy Adj, apples N; 3 Ella N, quietly Adv, closed V, door N; 4 They P, hugged V, me P; 5 He P, quickly Adv, finished V, tricky Adj, puzzle N; 6 friendly Adj, nurse N, often Adv, helped V, us P; 7 You P, laugh V, often Adv; 8 Thirsty Adj, horses N, drank V, cool Adj, water N.

blocks.title: Quotation Marks in Dialogue
blocks.instruction: A comma or a question mark goes inside the closing quotation mark.

script.say: "Quotation marks go around the exact words someone says. A comma or an end mark goes inside the closing quotation mark: “We won,” said Kim. Read the box and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write a line of dialogue on the board and point to each mark. Do the first item on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the words the person says: they go inside the quotation marks, and the comma or end mark goes in with them.

blocks.title: Shade the Fraction
blocks.instruction: Color the right number of parts to show each fraction.

script.say: "Each shape is cut into equal parts. Read the fraction next to it and color that many parts: the top number tells how many to color, the bottom number how many equal parts the whole has."
script.first: Draw a rectangle cut into four equal parts and color three: "three fourths." Do the first shape on the page together: read the fraction, count the equal parts, and color as many as the top number says.
script.stuck: Have the child count the equal parts of the shape and check them against the bottom number. Then color one part at a time, counting up to the top number.

blocks.title: Two-Step Story Problems Within 100
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Do the first step, then the second step. Write the numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Each story has two steps. Do the first step, then the second step. Write the numbers in the boxes."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "What happens first? What happens next?" Do step a together, then step b with the answer of step a.
script.stuck: Read the story with the child and underline the numbers. Ask, "Are things put together, or taken away?" Draw a quick bar to show the parts and the whole.

blocks.title: Life Then and Now
blocks.instruction: Read about life around 1900 and look at each photo. Write what it is like today. Then finish the sentences.

script.say: "These sample photos are drawings of life around 1900, more than 100 years ago. Read about each one and write what it is like today."
script.first: Read the first row's title and its "About 1900" text aloud and look at its photo. Ask, "What is it like today?" and write it together on the Today lines. Then finish the two sentences under the rows: what changed most, and something that stayed the same. Any true answer about life today is right; children write about most places today, not about their own homes. If your page asks which change mattered most, every honest reason is right.
script.stuck: Read the "About 1900" text again and ask, "Do we still do that? What do we use now?" For what stayed the same, say, "People still walk, write letters, and learn with a teacher."

blocks.title: Line of Symmetry?
blocks.instruction: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry? Circle the check mark or the X.

script.say: "A mirror line cuts a picture into two halves that match exactly, like a picture and its reflection in a mirror. Look at the dashed line on each picture. If both sides match, circle the check. If they do not match, circle the X."
script.first: Draw a heart with a dashed line down the middle: "If I fold here, both sides match: a line of symmetry." Look at the first picture and its dashed line together: would the two sides match? Circle the check mark or the X.
script.stuck: Have the child cover one side of the picture with a hand, look at the other side, and then switch. Ask, "Is this part on the other side, too?" If both sides match along the dashed line, it is a line of symmetry.

blocks.title: What Time Is It?
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock. The short hand shows the hour, and the long hand shows the minutes: count by fives. Circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board. Count by fives around the numbers with the class: 5, 10, 15… Do the first clock on the page together: read the hour from the short hand, count the minutes by fives, and circle the time.
script.stuck: Ask, "Which number has the short hand just passed?" That is the hour, even when the short hand is close to the next number. Then have the child count by fives from the 12 to the long hand: 5, 10, 15.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 24
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 24
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 24 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Count by Fours
blocks.instruction: Skip count by 4. Write each missing number.

script.say: "On this page we count by fours: 4, 8, 12, 16. Some numbers are missing. Count by fours and write each missing number. The rows do not start at 4."
script.first: Count by fours together to 60. Read the first row aloud and clap at each empty box. Ask, "What number goes here?" Write it in. Tell the children that a row does not always start at 4.
script.stuck: Have the child add four to the number before the gap with fingers: say the number, then count four more. To check, the next printed number must be four more than the number the child wrote.

blocks.title: The Central Message
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Write its central message and three things in the story that show it.

script.say: "Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. Then write its central message, the lesson it teaches, and three things in the story that show it."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. After reading, ask, "What does this story teach us?"
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the story. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Past Tense: Regular and Irregular Verbs
blocks.instruction: Regular verbs add -ed in the past. Irregular verbs change: go, went.

script.say: "Regular verbs add -ed in the past: walk, walked. Irregular verbs change: go, went. Read the rules at the top and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the rule box aloud with an example of each rule. Do the first item on the page together and say which rule it follows.
script.stuck: Ask the child to say the verb in a sentence with "yesterday": "Yesterday I…" The word they say is often the past tense; then check its spelling with the rules.

blocks.title: Write with Time Words
blocks.instruction: Time words help a reader follow the events in order.

script.say: "Write a short story with time words, so a reader can follow the events in order. Read the example first."
script.first: Read the example story aloud and point to its time words. Let a few children say a story idea. Each child writes a story with at least three time words.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: 2-Digit Column Subtraction
blocks.instruction: Subtract one place at a time. Start with the ones.

script.say: "These subtraction problems are written one number under the other. Subtract one place at a time. Start on the right with the ones. Then subtract the tens."
script.first: Write the first problem on the board, one number under the other. Subtract the ones first, then the tens, and write each digit under its column. Tell the children to check the sign before they start.
script.stuck: Have the child cover the tens column with a finger and subtract only the ones, then cover the ones and subtract the tens. Counting back on fingers is fine for the small differences.

blocks.title: Jump Puzzles: Follow the Arrows
blocks.instruction: Start at the number and follow the arrows: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, right is 1 more. Write where you land.

script.say: "Each puzzle starts at a number and has three arrows. Every arrow changes the number: up is 10 less, down is 10 more, left is 1 less, and right is 1 more. Follow the arrows and write the number where you land."
script.first: Point to the key at the top of the page and read it aloud together. Do the first puzzle on the board, one arrow at a time, and write the number after each arrow: for example, "30, one less is 29, ten more is 39, one less is 38."
script.stuck: Have the child write the new number above each arrow before going on to the next one. If the classroom has a hundreds chart, the child can put a finger on the starting number and move one square for each arrow.

blocks.title: Resources at the Bakery
blocks.instruction: Look at the bakery. Write each card in its column: natural, human or capital resources.

script.say: "A bakery needs resources to make bread. Natural resources come from nature, human resources are people and their work, and capital resources are things people made that help make goods. Write each card in its column."
script.first: Look at the bakery picture together and read the cards aloud. Do the first card together: "Is it from nature, a person's work, or a thing people made?" Answers, for the cards your page shows: natural: wheat grown on a farm, the water for the dough, salt; human: the skill of the baker, a cashier's work; capital: an oven, the mixer, a van that delivers bread, the bakery building. If your page asks about a business in our town, any business works; one true example under each kind is enough.
script.stuck: Ask the three questions one at a time: "Does it come from nature? Is it a person and their work? Is it a thing people made to help make goods?" The oven and the van were made by people, so they are capital.

blocks.title: Help the Earthworm Reach the Leaf
blocks.instruction: Help the ant go down and up through the tunnels to the raspberry. Draw a line along the way.

script.say: "Time for a maze. Before you pick up your pencil, look at the whole picture and find the start and the end."
script.first: Hold up the page and show the start and the end. Tell the children to trace the way with a finger first and to draw only when the finger has found a way.
script.stuck: Suggest starting from the end and working backward. A wrong turn does not need to be erased; tell the child to go back to the last place where the path split and try the other way.

blocks.title: To the Minute
blocks.instruction: Read each clock. Circle the matching time.

script.say: "Read each clock to the minute. The short hand shows the hour. Count the minutes by fives, then by ones. Circle the time that matches."
script.first: Draw a clock on the board with the long hand two marks after the 4. Count by fives to the 4 (20) and then by ones (21, 22): 22 minutes. Do the first clock on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child count by fives to the number before the long hand, then count each small mark by ones.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 25
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 25
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 25 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Number Machines
blocks.instruction: Each machine uses its rule on every number. Fill in the missing ones.

script.say: "Each number machine has a rule, printed at the top. A number goes in on the left, the machine uses its rule, and a new number comes out on the right. Fill in the missing numbers. Watch out: sometimes the number that went in is the one that is missing."
script.first: Read the rule of the first machine aloud, for example "+9." Do the first number together: put it in, use the rule, and write what comes out. If the number that comes out is given, go backward: use the opposite rule.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is the missing number before the arrow or after it?" After the arrow, the child uses the rule. Before the arrow, the child does the opposite, then checks by putting the number through the machine.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: The Snowman
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence. When you finish, turn the page over and write three sentences that tell what happens next in the story."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow; then they read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Which sentence helps us?" Circle the answer together. Question 3 asks the children to write their own answer on the lines: tell them to use a full sentence.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question.

blocks.title: Closed and Open Syllables
blocks.instruction: An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name: ro | bot.

script.say: "A closed syllable ends with a consonant, and its vowel is short: rab in rabbit. An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name: ro in robot. Read each word, draw a line between its syllables, and write C or O for each one."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write robot and rabbit on the board, split them together (ro|bot, rab|bit), and mark each part C or O. Read the first word on the page together and do it.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the letters between the two vowels. Two consonants: split between them. One consonant: split after the first vowel and say it long; if that is not a word, split after the consonant and say it short. A part that ends with a vowel is open, a part that ends with a consonant is closed. For your own reference, on this page the splits are lo|go, pho|to, si|ren, o|val, to|tal, i|tem, si|lo, pup|pet, pic|nic, ha|lo, to|ken, ro|dent, e|mu, pen|cil, u|nit, and pro|gram; a part that ends with a vowel gets O, a part that ends with a consonant gets C. The sentences take even, broken, solo, human, raven, and minus.

blocks.title: Choose the Joining Word
blocks.instruction: Pick the joining word that makes sense with both ideas.

script.say: "A joining word shows how two ideas go together. And adds another idea, because tells why, but shows a difference, and so tells the result. Join the sentences with a word from the box."
script.first: Read the box aloud. Read the first two sentences aloud and try each joining word between them. Ask which one makes sense and write the joined sentence together.
script.stuck: Read the two sentences with each joining word and ask, "Which one tells how they go together?"

blocks.title: Twin Fractions
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the fraction that shows the same amount.

script.say: "Some fractions look different but show the same amount, like one half and two fourths. Draw a line from each picture to the fraction that shows the same amount."
script.first: Draw two bars of the same length: one with one half shaded, one with two fourths shaded. Show that the shaded parts are the same length. Do the first picture on the page together: count the parts and the shaded parts.
script.stuck: Have the child count the equal parts (the bottom number) and the shaded parts (the top number) of the picture, then find the fraction that matches.

blocks.title: Multiply and Group: Word Problems
blocks.instruction: One story makes equal groups, the other splits a total into equal groups. Solve each story and write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Are equal groups put together? Then you multiply. Is a total shared or split into equal groups? Then you divide. Write the number sentence and the answer."
script.first: Read both stories aloud. One makes equal groups (multiply), the other splits a total into equal groups (divide). Solve the first one together with a quick drawing.
script.stuck: Ask the child to underline the two numbers in the story and to say what each number counts: the groups, or how many are in each group. The picture shows the groups, and counting them is fine as a check.

blocks.title: North, East, South, West: Label the Four Directions
blocks.instruction: The orange tip on each compass rose points north; write the three missing letters in the empty boxes.

script.say: "The four directions are north, east, south, and west. On these compass roses the orange tip always points north, even when it does not point up. Write the three missing letters in the empty boxes."
script.first: Draw a compass rose on the board: N at the top, S at the bottom, E on the right, W on the left. Say "Never Eat Soggy Waffles" going around clockwise from N. On the page, north is wherever the orange tip points, and on some roses it points down, left, or right. Do the first rose together: put a finger on the orange tip, say "north," then go around clockwise and say east, south, west, writing each missing letter where it falls.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the orange tip and say north, then go around clockwise: east, south, west.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

blocks.title: Hot or Cold?
blocks.instruction: Read each thermometer. Write the temperature it shows.

script.say: "A thermometer shows how hot or cold it is. Find where the red line stops on the scale and write that temperature in degrees Fahrenheit."
script.first: Look at the scale of the first thermometer together: the numbers go up by tens, and each small mark between two numbers is 2 more degrees. Put a finger on the top of the red line, find the number just below it, and count up by twos to the top of the line. Write the number in the box.
script.stuck: Have the child find the number just below the top of the red line and count the small marks up by twos: "80, 82, 84, 86, 88." The top of the red line is the temperature, never the number above it.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 26
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 26
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 26 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: The 3 Times Table
blocks.instruction: Multiply. Write each product in the box.

script.say: "Multiply. Write each product in the box. All the problems on this page use the same times table."
script.first: Count by the table's number together to ten times it. Do the first two problems together and show that each answer is the one before plus one more group.
script.stuck: Have the child count by the table's number on fingers, one finger for each group, or start from a fact the child knows: 5 times the number, then count on by one more group.

blocks.title: Main Idea and Key Details
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Write the main idea of the whole text and three key details that support it.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write the main idea of the whole text and three key details that support it."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Ask, "What is the whole text mostly about?" before the children write.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Possessive Nouns: One Owner or More
blocks.instruction: One owner: the bee’s hive. More than one owner: the bees’ hives.

script.say: "An apostrophe shows who owns something. One owner: add apostrophe s, the bee's hive. More than one owner that ends in s: add the apostrophe after the s, the bees' hives. Read the box and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write the bee's hive and the bees' hives on the board and ask how many bees there are in each. Do the first item together: "How many owners?"
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Is there one owner or more than one?" Then point to the matching rule in the box.

blocks.title: Plan Your Story
blocks.instruction: Plan the beginning, the middle, and the end of your story.

script.say: "Plan your story: choose a story idea, then plan the beginning, the middle, and the end."
script.first: Read the story ideas aloud and let a few children say what could happen. Each child circles an idea and fills in the plan: who and where at the beginning, the problem in the middle, how it is solved at the end.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Which Is Bigger?
blocks.instruction: Look at both bars. Circle the bigger fraction.

script.say: "Each row has two fraction bars. Look at both bars. Circle the bigger fraction."
script.first: Draw two bars of the same length on the board, one cut into halves and one into fourths. Shade one half and one fourth and ask which is bigger. Do the first row on the page together: compare how much of each bar is shaded.
script.stuck: Have the child compare the shaded parts of the two bars side by side. When the bars are the same size, the longer shaded part is the bigger fraction.

blocks.title: Round to the Hundred
blocks.instruction: Look at the dot. Circle the hundred it is closer to.

script.say: "Rounding means finding the nearest round number. Each number line on this page goes from one hundred to the next. Look at the dot. Is it closer to the hundred on the left or to the hundred on the right? Circle the hundred it is closer to."
script.first: Draw a number line from 400 to 500 with the dot near 470. Ask, "Is the dot closer to 400 or to 500?" Do the first one on the page together and circle the closer hundred.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the dot and count the small steps to each end of the line; the end with fewer steps is closer. Each small step is 10.

blocks.title: Label the Continents
blocks.instruction: Write the name of each numbered continent on its line. Use the names in the box.

script.say: "The map shows the seven continents, each with a number. Write the name of each continent on its line. If your page has a box of names, use it."
script.first: Say the seven names together: North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania, Antarctica (if your page has a box of names, read them from it). Point to North America on the map: "This is where the United States is." Find its number together and write North America on that line. The children do the rest; with a box, they cross out each name when they use it.
script.stuck: Give clues: "Antarctica is the icy one at the bottom. South America is under North America. Africa is the big one in the middle." Let the child find each one on the map.

blocks.title: Find 10 Differences in the Garden
blocks.instruction: Circle the 10 differences, 5 in each pair of pictures, and check a box under the pair for every one you find.

script.say: "Here is a spot-the-difference puzzle with two pairs of pictures. In each pair, the picture on the right is different in 5 places. Circle each difference, and check a box under the pair for every one you find."
script.first: Find one difference in the top pair together: ask a child to point to it and say what changed. Circle it in the picture on the right and check off one box.
script.stuck: Have the child cover part of both pictures of a pair with a hand and compare one small part at a time, from top to bottom. Things can be missing, added, or changed.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates on a 10 × 10 Grid
blocks.instruction: Find each square on the big grid by its letter and number. Color it to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Make sure every child has the crayons the lists name. Show how to find a square: put one finger on the letter at the top and one finger on the number at the side, and move them until they meet. Find the first square of the first list together and color it. Tell the children to cross out each code once its square is colored.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 27
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 27
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 27 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Read the Calendar: Days of the Week
blocks.instruction: Read down the columns to answer the questions about the days.

script.say: "This is a calendar page for one month. The questions under it ask you to find things on the calendar. Read each question and write the answer in the box."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the month and the days of the week across the top. Read the first question aloud: put a finger on the date and slide up the column to read its day. Read down a column to find all the dates of one day.
script.stuck: For a question about a day of the week, have the child find the day's name at the top and move a finger straight down its column. For one date, the child moves up from the date to the day's name.

blocks.title: Ask and Answer
blocks.instruction: Read the text. Each sentence in a box is from the text. Write the question that the sentence answers. The first word is given.

script.say: "Read the text. Each sentence in a box comes from the text. Write the question that the sentence answers. The first one is started for you."
script.first: Read the text aloud with the class. Read the first sentence in a box and ask, "What question does this answer?" Look at how the first one is started and finish it together. A question ends with a question mark.
script.stuck: Have the child find the sentence in the text and ask, "What would someone ask to get this answer: who, what, where, when, why, or how?"

blocks.title: Base Words and Suffixes
blocks.instruction: A suffix at the end changes the word: kind + ness = kindness.

script.say: "A suffix at the end changes a word: kind and -ness make kindness. Read each word, circle the base word, and underline the suffix. Then do the rest of the page."
script.first: Write kindness on the board: circle kind, underline -ness. Ask what it means: being kind. Do the first word on the page together.
script.stuck: Cover the suffix with a finger and read the base word. Then read the whole word and ask what it means.

blocks.title: Choose the Linking Word
blocks.instruction: Because and since tell why. Therefore tells what happens as a result.

script.say: "Linking words join an opinion to its reasons. Because and since tell why. Therefore tells what happens as a result. For example gives an example. Circle the linking word that fits each sentence."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Read the first sentence aloud with each linking word and circle the one that fits together.
script.stuck: Ask, "Does the second part give a reason, a result, or an example?" Then find the word for it in the box.

blocks.title: Right-Angle Hunt
blocks.instruction: Circle every right angle (a square corner).

script.say: "A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a sheet of paper. Circle every right angle on the page."
script.first: Hold up a sheet of paper and show its square corner. Show the children how to check a corner on the page with the corner of a sheet of paper or an index card. Find one right angle together and circle it.
script.stuck: Give the child a scrap of paper and have them hold its corner in each angle: if it fits exactly, it is a right angle.

blocks.title: How Far Apart? Count the Jumps
blocks.instruction: Count how many jumps down and how many jumps right take you from the first number to the second. Write both numbers.

script.say: "Count how many jumps down and how many jumps right take you from the first number to the second. Write both numbers."
script.first: Point to the key: down is 10 more, right is 1 more. Do the first one on the board: from 4 to 35, count the tens: 14, 24, 34: three jumps down; then 35: one jump right.
script.stuck: Have the child count by tens first until the tens digit matches, then by ones.

blocks.title: Road Safety Quiz: Which Sign Fits?
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and circle the one road sign that fits it.

script.say: "Read each sentence. Circle the one road sign that fits it."
script.first: Read the first sentence aloud and look at the three signs next to it. Ask, "Which sign tells drivers about this?" Circle it together. Read each sentence aloud for children who need it.
script.stuck: Read the sentence again and name the three signs; ask which one would help in that place.

blocks.title: Help the Bee Pick Up Every Sunflower
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

blocks.title: How Much Time Passed?
blocks.instruction: Compare the two clocks. Write how much time passed.

script.say: "Each row shows a start clock and an end clock. Read both and write how much time passed. The word next to the box tells you to answer in hours or in minutes."
script.first: Read the two clocks of the first row together and write both times on the board. Count on from the start time to the end time: by hours when the box says hours, by fives when it says minutes. Write the answer in the box.
script.stuck: Have the child write both times first. For hours, count the hours on from the first clock: "9 o'clock, 10, 11, 12: three hours." For minutes, count by fives from where the first minute hand points to where the second one points, going past the 12 if it has to.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 28
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 28
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 28 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Big Skip Counting
blocks.instruction: Find the counting rule. Write each missing number.

script.say: "Find the counting rule of each row: what is added each time? Write each missing number."
script.first: Read the first row aloud and look at two numbers next to each other: how much is added? Count on by that amount to fill the empty boxes together.
script.stuck: Have the child find two numbers next to each other with no gap and count up from one to the other: that is the step. Where one box is empty between two numbers, the jump is two steps.

blocks.title: Reading Comprehension: Camping in the Backyard
blocks.instruction: Read the story carefully. Then circle the best answer to each question.

script.say: "Now it is time to read. Read the story carefully, all the way to the end. You will not find the answers to questions 1 and 2 word for word in the story: look for clues and think about what the story tells you. Circle the best answer to questions 1 and 2. Then write your answer to question 3 on the lines, in a whole sentence."
script.first: Read the title and the story aloud while the children follow; then they read it again on their own. Read the first question and its choices aloud and ask, "Which sentence helps us?" Circle the answer together. Question 3 asks the children to write their own answer on the lines: tell them to use a full sentence.
script.stuck: Read the question to the child and ask, "Which sentence in the story gives you a clue?" For the written answer, have the child say the answer aloud first and start it with part of the question.

blocks.title: Plural Nouns: Spelling Rules
blocks.instruction: Plural nouns name more than one. Each one follows a spelling rule.

script.say: "A plural noun names more than one. Its spelling follows a rule: add -s; add -es after s, x, z, ch, or sh; change y to i and add -es; some words change completely. Read the rules at the top and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the rule box aloud and write one example of each rule on the board: cats, boxes, babies, leaves. Do the first item on the page together and say which rule it follows.
script.stuck: Have the child look at the last letter or letters of the word and find the matching rule in the box.

blocks.title: Plan Your Opinion Piece
blocks.instruction: Plan before you write: an opinion and reasons that tell why.

script.say: "Plan your opinion piece before you write: choose a question, write your opinion, and give reasons that tell why."
script.first: Read the questions aloud and let a few children say their opinion and one reason. Each child circles a question and fills in the plan.
script.stuck: Have the child tell you the idea aloud first; then say, "Write that." Help with the first words of a sentence, and let the child spell words as well as they can. A short, finished piece is better than a long, unfinished one.

blocks.title: Equal Partners
blocks.instruction: Draw a line from each picture to the fraction that shows the same amount.

script.say: "Some fractions look different but show the same amount, like one half and two fourths. Draw a line from each picture to the fraction that shows the same amount."
script.first: Draw two bars of the same length: one with one half shaded, one with two fourths shaded. Show that the shaded parts are the same length. Do the first picture on the page together: count the parts and the shaded parts.
script.stuck: Have the child count the equal parts (the bottom number) and the shaded parts (the top number) of the picture, then find the fraction that matches.

blocks.title: Multiplication and Division Word Problems
blocks.instruction: Read each story. Use the picture to help you. Write the answer in the box, then finish the answer sentence.

script.say: "Read each story. Are equal groups put together? Then you multiply. Is a total shared or split into equal groups? Then you divide. Write the number sentence and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "Is it equal groups put together (multiply), or a total shared into equal groups (divide)?" Use the picture and write the answer and the answer sentence together.
script.stuck: Ask the child to underline the two numbers in the story and to say what each number counts: the groups, or how many are in each group. The picture shows the groups, and counting them is fine as a check.

blocks.title: Fix the Arrow Program
blocks.instruction: Follow the arrows from the flag: each arrow is one step. One arrow is wrong: the path does not end on the star. Circle the wrong arrow and draw the correct arrow in the box under it.

script.say: "Follow the arrows from the flag: each arrow is one step. One arrow is wrong: the path does not end on the star. Find the wrong arrow and fix it."
script.first: Do the first puzzle on the board: put a finger on the flag and move one square for each arrow, saying "up, right, right." See where you land. Then find the arrow that takes the path the wrong way and cross it out.
script.stuck: Have the child move a finger one square per arrow and stop when the path goes off course: that arrow is the wrong one.

blocks.title: Find the Symmetric Picture
blocks.instruction: Circle the picture that is the same on both sides.

script.say: "Circle the picture in each row that is the same on both sides."
script.first: Draw a heart with a line down the middle: "Both sides match." Look at the first row together and ask which picture would match if you folded it in the middle.
script.stuck: Have the child cover one side of each picture with a hand, look at the other side, and then switch. The picture whose two sides match is the one to circle.

blocks.title: Mirror Pictures: Fold and Check
blocks.instruction: Picture 2 is flipped like a mirror; circle the 4 things or empty places that still differ, check a box for each, then fold on the line to check.

script.say: "This page has two pairs of pictures. In each pair, picture 2 is picture 1 flipped over, the way a mirror would show it. But some things are still different: four in all. Circle them in picture 2 and check a box for each one. Then fold the page on the dashed line to check."
script.first: Hold the page up and show how picture 2 is flipped: what is on the left in picture 1 is on the right in picture 2. Find one difference together and circle it. Show how to fold the page on the line at the end, so that the two pictures lie on top of each other.
