script.stuck: Have the child pick one thing in picture 1 and find it in picture 2 on the other side. Folding the page on the line and holding it up to the window shows what does not match.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 29
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 29
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 29 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Odd or Even? Write Two Equal Addends
blocks.instruction: Circle the dots two by two. Then write the number as two equal parts and write what is left over in the small box.

script.say: "Circle the dots two by two. Then write the number as two equal parts, and write what is left over in the small box."
script.first: Draw 7 dots on the board and circle them in pairs: three pairs and one left over. Write 7 = 3 + 3 + 1 left over. Do the first one on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child circle the dots two by two and count the pairs: that is each equal part. A dot left over goes in the small box, and the number is odd; no dot left over means it is even.

blocks.title: Cause and Effect
blocks.instruction: Read the text. A cause makes something happen. An effect is what happens. Write the missing cause or effect.

script.say: "Read the text carefully, all the way to the end. Then write the missing cause or effect. A cause makes something happen; an effect is what happens."
script.first: Read the title and the first paragraph aloud while the children follow; they read the rest on their own. Read the first question aloud and ask, "Which paragraph tells us?" Find it together and write the first answer together. Write "Because it rained, the game was canceled" on the board: the rain is the cause, the canceled game the effect.
script.stuck: Read the question with the child and look for its key words in the text. Have the child put a finger on the paragraph that answers it and read it aloud before writing. A short answer in the child's own words is fine.

blocks.title: Sort the Parts of Speech
blocks.instruction: A word’s job makes it a noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, or adverb.

script.say: "Every word has a job. A noun names something, a pronoun takes its place, a verb shows an action or being, an adjective tells about a noun, and an adverb tells how, when, or how often. Write each word in the column of its job and cross it out. Then write two more words of your own for each job."
script.first: Read the box with the letters for each job aloud. Read the first sentence on the page aloud and label its first word together: "What job does this word do here?"
script.stuck: Ask the questions one by one: "Is it a thing? Does it replace a name? Is it something you do? Does it describe a thing? Does it tell how?" For your own reference, on this page the nouns are teacher and zoo; the pronouns it, them, and we; the verbs hid, dug, and grabbed; the adjectives curly, hungry, and cozy; the adverbs always, slowly, soon, and calmly.

blocks.title: Quotation Marks in Dialogue
blocks.instruction: A comma or a question mark goes inside the closing quotation mark.

script.say: "Quotation marks go around the exact words someone says. A comma or an end mark goes inside the closing quotation mark: “We won,” said Kim. Read the box and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box at the top aloud. Write a line of dialogue on the board and point to each mark. Do the first item on the page together.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the words the person says: they go inside the quotation marks, and the comma or end mark goes in with them.

blocks.title: Bars That Count by 5
blocks.instruction: Careful — the scale counts by 5! Write the value of each bar.

script.say: "Careful: on this graph each line of the scale counts by five, not by one. Read the value of each bar and write it."
script.first: Point to the scale on the side and count it together: 0, 5, 10, 15. Read the first bar together: slide a finger from its top across to the scale. If it stops between two lines, it is halfway between them.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the top of the bar and move it straight across to the scale, then count by fives from zero up to that line.

blocks.title: Story Problems Within 100: Question, Equation, Answer
blocks.instruction: Read each story. If the question is missing, write a question that fits. Then write the equation and the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Write the question if it is missing, then the equation and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Ask, "What do we need to find out?" Write the equation on the board together and solve it with tens and ones. Then the children read the other stories on their own.
script.stuck: Read the story with the child and underline the numbers. Ask, "Are things put together, or taken away?" Draw a quick bar to show the parts and the whole.

blocks.title: Metamorphosis: Which Animal Will It Become?
blocks.instruction: Look at each stage and write its letter in a box under the animal it will grow into; some boxes stay empty.

script.say: "Look at each stage, like an egg, a tadpole, or a caterpillar. Write its letter in a box under the animal it will grow into. Some boxes stay empty."
script.first: Name the grown-up animals together, then look at the first stage and ask, "What will this become?" Write its letter in a box under that animal.
script.stuck: Ask the child which animal the stage looks a little like, or say what the stage is called: a tadpole becomes a frog, a caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

blocks.title: Grid Coordinates
blocks.instruction: Find each square by its letter and number, like B2. Color it with the color of its group to reveal the picture.

script.say: "This grid hides a picture. Every square has a name made of a letter and a number, like B2. The lists at the bottom tell you which squares to color and in which color."
script.first: Point to the letters across the top and the numbers down the side. Read the first square, for example B2: go across to B and down to 2. Color it in its color together. Tell the children to cross off each square on the list as they color it.
script.stuck: Have the child say the code aloud, letter first, then find the letter's column and slide a finger down to the number's row. A square in the wrong place shows in the picture; the child can check its code again.

blocks.title: Help the Crab Pick Up Every Shell
blocks.instruction: Help the rabbit get to the bucket and pick up every carrot, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each carrot.

script.say: "Read the title with me. Help the animal reach its goal and pick up every one of its things on the way, without using a path twice. Fill in a circle for each one you pick up."
script.first: Hold up the page and read the title and the directions aloud. Show the animal, its goal, and the things it must pick up, and count the things together. Tell the children to plan the whole way with a finger before they draw, because the first way they see may miss one.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on each thing to pick up and look at which paths lead to it. If the way is blocked because a path was already used, the child starts again with a finger and picks up the things in another order.

packs.title: Third Grade Sub Plans: Week 30
packs.metaTitle: Third Grade Emergency Sub Plans: Week 30
packs.metaDescription: No-prep emergency sub plans for week 30 of third grade: 9 review blocks in reading, word work, writing, and math, with a script for the guest teacher.

blocks.title: Label the Number Line
blocks.instruction: Use the numbers you see to find what the line counts by. Write the missing numbers in the boxes.

script.say: "Use the numbers you see to find what the line counts by. Then write the missing numbers in the boxes."
script.first: Draw the first line on the board. Ask, "How far is it from one printed number to the next? How many marks are in between?" Find the step together, then count on to each box.
script.stuck: Have the child put a finger on the nearest printed number and count the small marks one by one to the arrow. An answer such as 3 or 7 means the child counted from the left end as if it were zero; point to the 40.

blocks.title: Ask and Answer About a Story
blocks.instruction: Read the story. Each sentence in a box is from the story. Write the question that the sentence answers. The first word is given.

script.say: "Read the story. Each sentence in a box comes from the story. Write the question that the sentence answers. The first one is started for you."
script.first: Read the story aloud with the class. Read the first sentence in a box and ask, "What question does this answer?" Look at how the first one is started and finish it together.
script.stuck: Have the child find the sentence in the story and ask, "What would someone ask to get this answer: who, what, where, when, why, or how?"

blocks.title: Rewrite the Story in the Past Tense
blocks.instruction: To tell a story about the past, change every verb to the past tense.

script.say: "This little story is told in the present. Rewrite it in the past tense: change every numbered verb to its yesterday form."
script.first: Read the story aloud. Do the first numbered verb together: "make… yesterday we made." Write it on the line. Remind the children that some verbs just add -ed and some change.
script.stuck: Have the child read the sentence with "yesterday" at the start and say the verb that sounds right.

blocks.title: Time Words in a Story
blocks.instruction: Time words such as “later that day” tell when things happen.

script.say: "Time words like first, later that day, and finally tell when things happen in a story. Read the box at the top and do each part of the page."
script.first: Read the box of time words aloud. Do the first item on the page together and say where the time word goes.
script.stuck: Ask the child, "Does this happen at the start, in the middle, or at the end?" Then pick a time word from that part of the box.

blocks.title: Right-Angle Hunt
blocks.instruction: Circle every right angle (a square corner).

script.say: "A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a sheet of paper. Circle every right angle on the page."
script.first: Hold up a sheet of paper and show its square corner. Show the children how to check a corner on the page with the corner of a sheet of paper or an index card. Find one right angle together and circle it.
script.stuck: Give the child a scrap of paper and have them hold its corner in each angle: if it fits exactly, it is a right angle.

blocks.title: Division Word Problems: Making Groups
blocks.instruction: Circle the equal groups in the picture, then write the answer.

script.say: "Read each story. Are equal groups put together? Then you multiply. Is a total shared or split into equal groups? Then you divide. Write the number sentence and the answer."
script.first: Read the first story aloud. Circle equal groups in the picture together and count the groups: that is the answer.
script.stuck: Ask the child to underline the two numbers in the story and to say what each number counts: the groups, or how many are in each group. The picture shows the groups, and counting them is fine as a check.

blocks.title: Floating Facts: Sink or Float True or False
blocks.instruction: Read each sentence and circle true or false.

script.say: "Read each sentence about things that sink and float, and circle true or false."
script.first: Name the pictures at the top together. Read the first sentence aloud and ask, "Is that true?" Talk about it, then circle.
script.stuck: Ask the child what happens to that thing in a bathtub or a pool.

blocks.title: Draw It Twice as Big
blocks.instruction: Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big.

script.say: "Look at the picture on the small grid. Color the same squares on the big grid, where every square is twice as big."
script.first: Find the top-left colored square on the small grid together and count which row and which column it is in. Find the same row and column on the big grid and color that square. Tell the children to do one row at a time.
script.stuck: Have the child put one finger on a colored square and another on the same row and column of the empty grid.

blocks.title: Rounding to the Nearest 10 and 100
blocks.instruction: Round each number twice: to the nearest ten in the first box and to the nearest hundred in the second.

script.say: "Round each number two times: first to the nearest ten, then to the nearest hundred. Look at the digit to the right of the place you round to: 0 to 4, round down; 5 to 9, round up."
script.first: Read the example at the top together; the wavy equal sign means "is about." Do the first number on the board: underline its tens digit and look at the ones digit to round to the nearest ten; then underline its hundreds digit and look at the tens digit to round to the nearest hundred. Tell the children to start from the number on the page both times.
script.stuck: Have the child say the two tens the number is between and ask which one is closer; then the two hundreds. A 5 always rounds up.
